children.title: Coupling-Structure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Problem structures distinguished by whether cross-block dependence resides in constraints, variables, or both.

children.title: Complicating Constraints
children.top_down_role: Block-separable models joined by a comparatively small coupling-constraint system.

assumptions_latex: \(m\ge 2\), \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\), and \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\).
\(A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n_i}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^r\), with \(r\) comparatively small.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\) is the complicating-constraint subsystem whose removal separates the model by blocks.

notation.meaning: Decision vector and local feasible set for block i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-linked continuous block-separable formulation; inequalities may be converted using slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}\ \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i\in X_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b.\] The final equality system is called the system of complicating constraints when deleting it leaves \(m\) independent optimization problems, one in each \(x_i\). Its dimension \(r\), rather than the total number of local constraints, determines the dimension of the associated Lagrangian multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complicating constraints are a small set of linking rows whose removal leaves independent optimization problems over the local variable blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Complicating Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, and the formulation is mathematically coherent, but no inspectable authoritative citation supports the terminology or multiplier-dimension claim.

children.title: Complicating Variables
children.top_down_role: Models that separate after a coordinating variable block is fixed.

assumptions_latex: \(Z\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\), \(X_i(z)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\), and \(m\ge2\).
For every fixed \(z\in Z\), each block objective and feasible set depends only on \((x_i,z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixing \(z\) yields \(m\) mutually independent subproblems with value functions \(v_i(z)\).

notation.meaning: Local decision vector for block i.
Optimal value of local block i at fixed z.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared-variable formulation of primal or resource decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(z\in Z\) is a block of complicating variables for \[\inf_{z\in Z,\,x_i\in X_i(z)}\ g(z)+\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i,z)\] if fixing \(z\) removes every dependence between distinct local vectors \(x_i\) and \(x_j\). Equivalently, for fixed \(z\), the residual optimal value is \(g(z)+\sum_{i=1}^m v_i(z)\), where \[v_i(z)=\inf_{x_i\in X_i(z)} f_i(x_i,z).\] Thus coordination occurs only through the common choice of \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complicating variables are shared coordinates whose fixation makes all remaining local optimization blocks independent.
knowledge_statements.title: Complicating Variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly captures separation after fixing a shared variable block and fits the leaf, but it has no authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Hybrid Coupling Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Structures supporting hybrid relaxation and projection decompositions.

children.title: Constraint Coupling Component
children.top_down_role: The globally linking constraints present in hybrid decomposable structures.

assumptions_latex: \(z\in Z\) is shared and \(x_i\in X_i\) are local block variables.
\(A_i\) and \(B\) have a common row dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint-coupling component is \(\sum_i A_i x_i+Bz=b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint portion of a hybrid variable-and-row coupled model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a hybrid block model with local vectors \(x_i\) and shared vector \(z\), define the global residual by \[r(x,z)=\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i+Bz-b.\] The constraint coupling component is the requirement \(r(x,z)=0\), or its componentwise inequality analogue. It is global because one feasibility test simultaneously involves multiple local blocks, even after the common variable \(z\) has been assigned a value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constraint-coupling component is the global row system that simultaneously contains contributions from several local blocks and possibly the shared variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Coupling Component

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the constraint component of hybrid coupling, but the equality/inequality formulation and claimed residual interpretation lack cited support.

children.title: Variable Coupling Component
children.top_down_role: The shared or complicating variables present in hybrid decomposable structures.

assumptions_latex: \(z\in Z\) occurs in at least two local block objectives or feasible-set mappings.
Distinct local vectors \(x_i\) have no direct cross-block occurrence once \(z\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The variable-coupling component is the repeated occurrence of the same \(z\) across the local terms \(\Phi_i(x_i,z)\).

notation.meaning: Extended-real local objective encoding objective and feasibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable portion of a hybrid variable-and-row coupled model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the local contribution of block \(i\), including its local constraints through an extended-real function, as \(\Phi_i(x_i,z)\). The variable coupling component is the use of one common vector \(z\) in two or more terms of \[g(z)+\sum_{i=1}^m\Phi_i(x_i,z).\] It is precisely the coupling removed by fixing \(z\): after that fixation, each term can be optimized with respect to its own \(x_i\) independently of all other local vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable coupling is the repeated use of one shared decision block in otherwise local objectives or feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Coupling Component

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The extended-real formulation accurately describes shared-variable coupling and the definition fits the terminal container, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Hybrid Coupling Interaction
children.top_down_role: The interface between constraint relaxation and variable projection within one decomposition.

assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is nonempty, and the displayed extended-real infima are well-defined.
Each \(A_i\) and \(B\) maps into the same finite-dimensional coupling space.
No equality between a conditional primal value and its Lagrangian dual value is asserted without an appropriate strong-duality qualification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(z,\lambda)=g(z)+\langle\lambda,Bz-b\rangle+\sum_{i=1}^m\inf_{x_i}\{\Phi_i(x_i,z)+\langle A_i x_i,\lambda\rangle\}\text{ is separable in the }x_i\text{ for fixed }(z,\lambda).

notation.meaning: Multiplier for the global linking equality.
Conditional Lagrangian value after eliminating the local variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional separation statement for simultaneous shared-variable and affine row coupling; it does not assert an unconditional min-max master equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the hybrid problem \[P=\inf_{z\in Z,\,x_i}\left\{g(z)+\sum_{i=1}^m\Phi_i(x_i,z):\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i+Bz=b\right\},\] define, for fixed \((z,\lambda)\), \[q(z,\lambda)=g(z)+\langle\lambda,Bz-b\rangle+\sum_{i=1}^m\inf_{x_i}\bigl(\Phi_i(x_i,z)+\langle A_i x_i,\lambda\rangle\bigr).\] Evaluation of \(q(z,\lambda)\) separates into independent local infima. If \(P(z)\) denotes the conditional primal value at fixed \(z\), then \(\sup_{\lambda}q(z,\lambda)\le P(z)\); equality requires an appropriate strong-duality qualification for that conditional problem. Thus local separation requires joint conditioning on the shared variable and the linking-row multiplier, without implying an unconditional interchange of \(\inf_z\) and \(\sup_\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing the shared variable and pricing the linking rows separates the local infima, but conditional dual exactness and any global min-max interchange require additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Lagrangian Separation

assumptions_latex: The model contains both \(\sum_i A_i x_i+Bz=b\) and local terms \(\Phi_i(x_i,z)\).
The shared variable \(z\) occurs in at least two local terms, and at least two matrices \(A_i\) are nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither fixing \(z\) nor dualizing the linking rows alone removes both forms of coordination.

notation.meaning: Multiplier of the global linking constraint.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interaction of simultaneous shared-variable and linking-row coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the hybrid model \[\inf_{z\in Z,\,x_i}\ g(z)+\sum_{i=1}^m\Phi_i(x_i,z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i+Bz=b,\] fixing \(z\) removes shared-variable coupling but leaves the linking constraint among the \(x_i\). Dualizing that constraint with multiplier \(\lambda\) separates the \(x_i\) conditional on \((z,\lambda)\), but the common \(z\) still coordinates their value functions. Hence a complete decomposition must coordinate both \(z\) and \(\lambda\), or apply an equivalent joint master mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hybrid coupling persists through both shared variables and linking rows, so eliminating only one form does not fully separate the blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Coupling Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property appropriately describes the interaction of variable and row coupling, but the assertion about complete decomposition and joint coordination is unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Block-Angular Linear Program Interface
children.top_down_role: Canonical linear structures connecting block decomposition to Dantzig-Wolfe and Benders representations.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Dantzig-Wolfe Reformulation of Problems with Block Diagonal Structure

children.title: Row-Linked Block-Angular Models
children.top_down_role: Independent local blocks coordinated by common linking rows.

assumptions_latex: For each \(i\), \(A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{q_i\times n_i}\), \(D_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times n_i}\), and \(x_i\ge0\).
All local row systems are independent except for the common linking-row system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint matrix has diagonal local blocks \(A_i\) and one common row block \([D_1\ \cdots\ D_m]\).

notation.meaning: Local constraint matrix of block i.
Contribution of block i to the linking rows.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical equality-form row-linked linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A row-linked block-angular linear program has the form \[\min\ \sum_{i=1}^m c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_i x_i=b_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\qquad\sum_{i=1}^m D_i x_i=d,\qquad x_i\ge0.\] After ordering local rows first and linking rows last, its matrix is \[\begin{bmatrix}A_1&0&\cdots&0\\0&A_2&\cdots&0\\\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\0&0&\cdots&A_m\\D_1&D_2&\cdots&D_m\end{bmatrix}.\] Removing the final row block leaves independent linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A row-linked block-angular program has diagonal local constraint blocks plus a small final block of rows linking all local variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Row-Linked Block-Angular Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is a coherent row-linked block-angular equality form and matches the leaf, but it lacks an authoritative block-angular-programming citation.

children.title: Column-Linkage Dual-Angular Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Subsystems coordinated through shared variables or the dual counterpart of row-linked structure.

children.title: Column-Linked Model Structure
children.top_down_role: Block systems coordinated through variables shared across local column structures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical equality-form column-linked linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A column-linked linear program has the form \[\min\ d^{\mathsf T}z+\sum_{i=1}^m c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad B_i z+A_i x_i=b_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\qquad z\ge0,\quad x_i\ge0.\] Its constraint matrix is \[\begin{bmatrix}B_1&A_1&0&\cdots&0\\B_2&0&A_2&\cdots&0\\\vdots&\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots\\B_m&0&0&\cdots&A_m\end{bmatrix}.\] The columns associated with \(z\) cross otherwise independent row blocks. Fixing \(z\) leaves separate local systems in the variables \(x_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A column-linked model contains a shared variable block whose columns cross otherwise independent local row blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(z\ge0\) is shared and each \(x_i\ge0\) is local.
The displayed constraints are equality rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The vertically stacked \(B_i\) blocks are the shared columns, and fixing \(z\) separates the local systems.

notation.meaning: Incidence of the shared variables in row block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Linked Model Structure

children.title: Dual-Angular Model Structure
children.top_down_role: The dual structural counterpart associated with row-linked block-angular organization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-angular representation associated with the canonical equality-form column-linked primal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the column-linked primal with equality rows and nonnegative variables, the dual is \[\max_{y_1,\ldots,y_m}\sum_{i=1}^m b_i^{\mathsf T}y_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_i^{\mathsf T}y_i\le c_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\qquad\sum_{i=1}^mB_i^{\mathsf T}y_i\le d.\] Each \(y_i\) is unrestricted because its primal row is an equality. The \(A_i^{\mathsf T}y_i\le c_i\) inequalities are block-local, whereas the inequality involving the sum of \(B_i^{\mathsf T}y_i\) links all dual blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-angular model has local dual inequalities and a shared-column-induced inequality linking all dual blocks.
assumptions_latex: The associated primal uses equality constraints and nonnegative variables.
Each equality-row multiplier \(y_i\) is unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual contains local inequalities \(A_i^{\mathsf T}y_i\le c_i\) and the linking inequality \(\sum_iB_i^{\mathsf T}y_i\le d\).

notation.meaning: Dual vector for primal row block i.
Shared-column coefficient matrix in row block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Angular Model Structure

children.title: Column-Linkage Duality Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Navigation between the primal column-linked view and its dual-angular counterpart.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional LP correspondence between shared primal columns and a dual linking inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min\ d^{\mathsf T}z+\sum_{i=1}^m c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i\quad\text{s.t.}\quad B_i z+A_i x_i=b_i,\ z\ge0,\ x_i\ge0.\] Its linear-programming dual is \[\max_{y_1,\ldots,y_m}\sum_{i=1}^m b_i^{\mathsf T}y_i\quad\text{s.t.}\quad A_i^{\mathsf T}y_i\le c_i,\qquad\sum_{i=1}^mB_i^{\mathsf T}y_i\le d,\] with each \(y_i\) unrestricted. Thus local primal columns generate local dual inequalities, whereas the shared columns of \(z\) generate the inequality linking all dual blocks. Reversing the LP-duality construction restores the column-linked form, subject to the corresponding sign conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LP duality transposes shared primal columns into a linking dual inequality while leaving local columns local.
assumptions_latex: The primal has equality rows and nonnegative variables as displayed.
Ordinary finite-dimensional linear-programming dual construction applies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Shared primal columns correspond to the dual linking inequality \(\sum_iB_i^{\mathsf T}y_i\le d\), while local columns correspond to \(A_i^{\mathsf T}y_i\le c_i\).

notation.meaning: Dual vector for primal row block i.
Shared-column coefficient matrix in row block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Linkage Duality Correspondence

children.title: Replicated Block-Scenario Pattern Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Replicated local structures whose stochastic specialization is owned by the stochastic-programming route.

children.title: Repeated-Block Patterns
children.top_down_role: Replicated local structures with a common block template.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coefficient replication across distinct deterministic blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A row-linked block-angular linear program has an exact repeated-block pattern when common data \((A,D,b,c)\) satisfy \[(A_i,D_i,b_i,c_i)=(A,D,b,c)\qquad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] It can then be written as \[\min\sum_{i=1}^m c^{\mathsf T}x_i\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax_i=b\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\qquad\sum_{i=1}^mDx_i=d,\qquad x_i\ge0.\] Replication concerns the coefficient template; the decision vectors \(x_i\) remain distinct and need not have equal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repeated-block pattern uses identical local and linking data for distinct replica decision blocks.
assumptions_latex: All blocks have common dimensions and identical data \((A,D,b,c)\).
The replica variables \(x_i\) remain distinct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact replication means \((A_i,D_i,b_i,c_i)=(A,D,b,c)\) for every block i, not \(x_i=x_j\).
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-Block Patterns

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural consequence of exact deterministic replication with a common convex local set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min\sum_{i=1}^m c^{\mathsf T}x_i\quad\text{s.t.}\quad x_i\in X:=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad\sum_{i=1}^mDx_i=d,\] every permutation of a feasible tuple is feasible with the same objective value. If \(\bar x=m^{-1}\sum_i x_i\), then \((\bar x,\ldots,\bar x)\) is also feasible with the same value. Consequently, whenever an optimum exists, a symmetric optimum exists, although feasible or optimal replica decisions need not all be identical.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact repeated-block LPs are permutation invariant and admit an equally valued symmetric representative for every feasible tuple.
assumptions_latex: All replicas use the common convex set \(X=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
The objective and linking equation use identical \(c\) and \(D\) in every block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible tuple has an equally valued symmetric representative \((\bar x,\ldots,\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Arithmetic mean of the replica decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Permutation Symmetry and Symmetric Representatives

children.title: Scenario-Indexed Patterns
children.top_down_role: Replicated local structures organized by scenario indices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic finite-scenario two-stage linear deterministic-equivalent structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite-scenario two-stage linear model may be represented as \[\min_{z,(y_s)_{s\in S}}c^{\mathsf T}z+\sum_{s\in S}p_s q_s^{\mathsf T}y_s\quad\text{subject to}\quad T_s z+W_s y_s=h_s\ (s\in S),\qquad z\in Z,\quad y_s\ge0.\] The first-stage vector \(z\) is common to every scenario row block, while \(y_s\) is scenario-local. Scenario indexing permits \(T_s,W_s,h_s,q_s\) to vary with \(s\); it does not imply exact repeated data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario-indexed deterministic equivalent combines a common first-stage block with weighted, potentially heterogeneous scenario-local recourse blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(p_s\ge0\) with \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
The vector \(z\) is common, while \(y_s\) and recourse data may depend on s.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model has shared columns from \(z\) and scenario-local columns from \(y_s\), without requiring identical scenario data.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Indexed Patterns

children.title: Stochastic Specialization Boundary
children.top_down_role: The handoff from generic repeated-block structure to stochastic-programming treatment.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between generic indexed block models and scenario-based stochastic-programming formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Calling blocks scenarios, or assigning them arbitrary weights, does not by itself make an indexed block model stochastic. A scenario-based stochastic specialization requires the indices to represent realizations under a specified probability model and requires the objective or constraints to use that probabilistic interpretation, for example through expectation, a risk functional, or probability constraints. Whenever decisions are made before some uncertainty is revealed, copies associated with the same available information must additionally satisfy the corresponding common-decision or nonanticipativity restrictions. Without these ingredients, the formulation remains a deterministic indexed or repeated-block model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario labels and weights are insufficient: stochastic specialization requires a probability model used by the formulation and information-consistent decisions whenever uncertainty is not yet observed.
assumptions_latex: The model has finitely many indexed blocks.
No probabilistic interpretation is inferred solely from the block labels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A generic indexed-block model crosses into scenario-based stochastic programming only when its indices, criterion or constraints, and any pre-revelation decisions have the required probabilistic and information-structure semantics.

notation.meaning: Finite block or scenario index set.
Probability assigned to scenario s when a probability model is present.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Specialization Boundary

children.title: Master Representation Routes
children.top_down_role: Global coordination representations induced by relaxing, convexifying, or projecting local structure.

children.title: Multiplier-Space Representation
children.top_down_role: Coordination through prices associated with relaxed coupling.

assumptions_latex: For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(E_i\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space, \(X_i\subseteq E_i\) is nonempty, and \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
The coupling space \(Y\) is finite-dimensional, \(A_i:E_i\to Y\) is linear, \(b\in Y\), and \(p^*=\inf\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in Y^*}g(\lambda)\le p^*\).

notation.meaning: Multiplier in the dual of the coupling space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional separable minimization with an affine coupling equality relaxed into multiplier space.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\in Y^*\), define \[g(\lambda)=\inf_{x_i\in X_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+\left\langle\lambda,\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i-b\right\rangle\right\}.\] With \(A_i^*:Y^*\to E_i^*\) denoting the adjoint map, separability yields \[g(\lambda)=-\langle\lambda,b\rangle+\sum_{i=1}^m\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\langle A_i^*\lambda,x_i\rangle\bigr).\] Thus coordination is represented by the multiplier-space master problem \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in Y^*}g(\lambda)\), and each evaluation of \(g\) decomposes into independent block infima.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing the coupling equality produces a dual master over multipliers, and evaluating a multiplier separates into independent block problems.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Space Representation

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224
source_witnesses.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

assumptions_latex: The Lagrangian is affine in the multiplier.
At the multiplier under consideration, every block infimum is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s(\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i(\lambda)-b\in\partial^+g(\lambda).

notation.meaning: Concave superdifferential of the dual function.
Coupling residual produced by minimizing block responses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order geometry of the multiplier-space value function under attained block infima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(g(\lambda)=\inf_x L(x,\lambda)\), with \(L(x,\cdot)\) affine, is concave. If each block infimum is finite and attained at \(x_i(\lambda)\), then \[s(\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i(\lambda)-b\] is a supergradient of \(g\): for every multiplier \(\mu\), \[g(\mu)\le g(\lambda)+\langle s(\lambda),\mu-\lambda\rangle.\] Different minimizing block selections can produce different supergradients, so the multiplier master can be nonsmooth even when the underlying primal functions are smooth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual master is concave, and the coupling residual of minimizing block responses is a supergradient; nonunique responses can make the master nonsmooth.
knowledge_statements.title: Concavity and Residual Supergradients

children.title: Convex-Combination Representation
children.top_down_role: Coordination through generated representations of local extreme structures.

assumptions_latex: For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) is a nonempty compact polytope whose extreme points are \(v_{ik}\), indexed by a finite set \(K_i\).
The objective is linear with \(c_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\), and the coupling data satisfy \(A_i\in\mathbb R^{q\times n_i}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The block-angular linear program and the displayed full convex-combination master problem have the same feasible solutions and optimal value under the substitution \(x_i=\sum_{k\in K_i}\theta_{ik}v_{ik}\).

notation.meaning: Extreme point of block polytope i.
Convex weight assigned to an extreme point.
Finite index set of block extreme points.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Dantzig-Wolfe representation for compact polyhedral blocks.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Separable Strictly Convex Programming p. 229
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every \(x_i\in X_i\) admits a representation \[x_i=\sum_{k\in K_i}\theta_{ik}v_{ik},\qquad \sum_{k\in K_i}\theta_{ik}=1,\qquad \theta_{ik}\ge0.\] Consequently, \[\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i:\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b,\ x_i\in X_i\right\}\] is equivalently represented by \[\min_{\theta}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{k\in K_i}(c_i^{\mathsf T}v_{ik})\theta_{ik}:\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{k\in K_i}A_i v_{ik}\theta_{ik}=b,\ \sum_{k\in K_i}\theta_{ik}=1\ \text{for every }i,\ \theta_{ik}\ge0\right\}.\] Replacing each full set \(K_i\) by a generated subset produces a restricted master problem whose columns can be enlarged iteratively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each local polytope is represented by convex weights on its extreme points, producing an equivalent full master problem and restricted masters over generated subsets of columns.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Combination Representation

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.2 Separable Strictly Convex Programming p. 229
source_witnesses.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

assumptions_latex: Each \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
The objective and coupling constraints are linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X_i=\operatorname{conv}\{v_{ik}:k\in K_i\}+\operatorname{cone}\{r_{i\ell}:\ell\in R_i\},\text{ so an exact master includes both point and recession-generator columns whenever }\operatorname{rec}(X_i)\ne\{0\}.

notation.meaning: Finite point generator of local polyhedron i.
Finite generator of the recession cone of local polyhedron i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minkowski-Weyl extension of the compact-polytope seed to general nonempty polyhedra, including nonpointed blocks through recession generators for lineality directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonempty polyhedron \(X_i\), there are finite sets of point generators \(\{v_{ik}:k\in K_i\}\) and recession-cone generators \(\{r_{i\ell}:\ell\in R_i\}\) such that \[X_i=\operatorname{conv}\{v_{ik}:k\in K_i\}+\operatorname{cone}\{r_{i\ell}:\ell\in R_i\}.\] Hence every \(x_i\in X_i\) has a representation \[x_i=\sum_{k\in K_i}\theta_{ik}v_{ik}+\sum_{\ell\in R_i}\mu_{i\ell}r_{i\ell},\qquad \sum_{k\in K_i}\theta_{ik}=1,\qquad \theta_{ik},\mu_{i\ell}\ge0.\] Substitution yields an exact block-angular master with point columns contributing to the convexity equation and recession columns contributing zero to it. For a pointed polyhedron the generators may be chosen as extreme points and extreme rays. For a nonpointed polyhedron, recession generators must also span both directions of its lineality space, and an extreme-point-only description need not exist. A point-only master is therefore not exact for an unbounded block and can miss an improving recession direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact master for a general polyhedral block uses convex weights on finite point generators and conic weights on recession generators; lineality requires generators in both directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Point-and-Recession-Generator Representation

assumptions_latex: \(X_i=\operatorname{conv}(V_i)\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), and \(x_i\in X_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i\text{ can be represented using at most }\dim(\operatorname{aff}X_i)+1\text{ points of }V_i.

notation.meaning: Affine hull of the represented convex set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematically sound generic convex-geometric sparsity theorem, deferred because its primary canonical home is Caratheodory theory rather than this decomposition representation leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X_i=\operatorname{conv}(V_i)\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), then every \(x_i\in X_i\) is a convex combination of at most \(\dim(\operatorname{aff}X_i)+1\) points of \(V_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Caratheodory's theorem bounds a convex representation by affine dimension plus one points.
knowledge_statements.title: Caratheodory Sparsity of Convex Representations

intermediate_metadata.reason: The locally owned inventory comprises the accepted compact-polytope extreme-point master and the accepted general-polyhedron point-and-recession-generator extension, including the lineality and point-only failure boundaries. The generic Caratheodory theorem is deferred to convex geometry. Multiplier-space and value-function projection are excluded as sibling master routes; pricing algorithms and certificates are excluded as downstream scopes.

children.title: Value-Function Projection Representation
children.top_down_role: Coordination through outer representations of subordinate value functions and feasibility domains.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\times Y\) is nonempty and \(f:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
For the conjugate formula, \(Q\) is proper, closed, and convex on a finite-dimensional space \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{(x,y)\in F}f(x,y)=\inf_{x\in D}Q(x)\), with \(\operatorname{epi}Q\) represented by its affine minorants.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the value function.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection onto coordinating variables with a closed-convex epigraph formula.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the projected domain and subordinate value function by \[D=\{x\in X:\exists y\in Y,\ (x,y)\in F\},\qquad Q(x)=\inf\{f(x,y):(x,y)\in F\}.\] Then \(\inf_{(x,y)\in F}f(x,y)=\inf_{x\in D}Q(x)\). If \(Q\) is proper, closed, and convex, Fenchel-Moreau representation gives \[Q(x)=\sup_{s\in X^*}\{\langle s,x\rangle-Q^*(s)\},\] so \(\operatorname{epi}Q\) is the intersection of the halfspaces \(\eta\ge\langle s,x\rangle-Q^*(s)\). Finite subsets of these inequalities form outer master approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting out subordinate variables yields a value function and feasibility domain; affine lower supports provide outer master approximations of its epigraph.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Function Projection Representation

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimizer Recovery from a Projected Value Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery of a joint optimizer from a projected master solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)=\inf\{f(x,y):(x,y)\in F\}\) and \(D=\operatorname{proj}_X F\). A feasible pair \((x^*,y^*)\in F\) is jointly optimal if and only if \(x^*\in\arg\min_{x\in D}Q(x)\) and \(f(x^*,y^*)=Q(x^*)\). Thus recovery from a master optimizer additionally requires attainment of its subordinate infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible pair is jointly optimal exactly when its projected point minimizes the value function and its subordinate variable attains that value.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\times Y\) is nonempty.
The asserted master minimizer and subordinate attainment exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^*,y^*)\in\arg\min_F f\iff x^*\in\arg\min_DQ\ \text{and}\ f(x^*,y^*)=Q(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Optimizer Recovery from a Projected Value Function

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epigraph Projection, Attainment, and Closedness Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relationship between marginal epigraphs, projected joint epigraphs, and closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q(x)=\inf_y\varphi(x,y)\), put \(P=\operatorname{proj}_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}\varphi)\). In finite dimensions, \[P\subseteq\operatorname{epi}Q\subseteq\operatorname{cl}P.\] Equality \(P=\operatorname{epi}Q\) holds exactly when the infimum defining \(Q(x)\) is attained for every \(x\) with \(Q(x)\in\mathbb R\). Closed convexity of \(\varphi\) alone does not make \(Q\) closed: for \(C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x>0,\ y\ge 1/x\}\) and \(\varphi=\iota_C\), the set \(C\) is closed and convex but \(Q=\iota_{(0,\infty)}\) is not lower semicontinuous. Hence an unqualified closed-epigraph or Fenchel--Moreau representation requires closedness of \(Q\), or replacement by its lower-semicontinuous hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The marginal epigraph lies between the projected joint epigraph and its closure; exact projection requires boundary attainment, and closed joint data can still yield a nonclosed value function.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(\varphi:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\subseteq\operatorname{epi}Q\subseteq\operatorname{cl}P\), and closedness of \(\varphi\) alone does not imply closedness of \(Q\).

notation.meaning: Projection of the joint epigraph onto value-function variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Projection, Attainment, and Closedness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity inherited by the projected value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be convex and define \(Q(x)=\inf_y\varphi(x,y)\). If \(Q\) never takes the value \(-\infty\), then \(Q\) is convex. This applies to \(\varphi=f+\iota_F\) when \(F\) is convex and the extended-real constrained objective is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial minimization preserves convexity provided the marginal value never equals minus infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are real vector spaces.
\(\varphi\) is convex.
\(Q(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity under Partial Minimization

children.title: Relaxed Coupling Structure
children.top_down_role: The coupling relations transferred from direct enforcement to multiplier pricing.

assumptions_latex: For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(X_i\) is a nonempty local domain and \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).

The product variable is \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in\prod_{i=1}^m X_i\), the equality coupling map is \(C:\prod_iX_i\to Y\), and the inequality coupling map is \(H:\prod_iX_i\to\mathbb R^r\), where \(Y\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After relaxing \(C(x)=0\) and \(H(x)\le0\), the explicit domain is \(\prod_{i=1}^mX_i\), and coupling violations enter the objective through \(\lambda\in Y^*\) and \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition relative to a partition in which all global coupling equalities and inequalities are relaxed while local block domains are retained.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The relaxed coupling structure is the collection of coupling constraints removed from explicit feasibility and inserted into the objective through multipliers. For the constraints \(C(x)=0\) and \(H(x)\le0\), the partial Lagrangian is \[L(x,\lambda,\mu)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda,C(x)\rangle+\mu^{\mathsf T}H(x),\qquad \lambda\in Y^*,\quad\mu\in\mathbb R_+^r.\] The associated relaxed subproblem minimizes \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)\) over \(x\in\prod_{i=1}^mX_i\), without explicitly imposing the relaxed coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxed coupling constraints are removed from explicit feasibility and priced in the objective, leaving the product of the retained local block domains.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Coupling Structure

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224
source_witnesses.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

assumptions_latex: The explicit relaxed domain is a product \(\prod_iX_i\).
Coupling constraints are inserted into the objective through fixed admissible multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independent block minimization follows only when the complete priced objective is additively separable across blocks; removal of coupling constraints from explicit feasibility is not sufficient by itself.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between merely pricing coupling constraints and obtaining a decomposable relaxed subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Relaxing coupling constraints leaves a product explicit domain, but it yields independent block minimizations only if the full priced objective can be written as \[L(x,\lambda,\mu)=\sum_i\ell_i(x_i;\lambda,\mu).\] For example, with scalar blocks and relaxed equality \(C(x_1,x_2)=x_1x_2=0\), the priced term \(\lambda x_1x_2\) remains cross-block coupled whenever \(\lambda\ne0\). Thus removal from explicit feasibility alone does not imply Lagrangian separability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing a coupling constraint does not by itself create independent block subproblems; the complete priced objective must also separate additively.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relaxation Does Not Alone Imply Separability
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Does Not Alone Imply Separability

children.title: Retained Local Structure
children.top_down_role: The block-local relations that remain enforced within decomposed subproblems.

assumptions_latex: Variables are partitioned as \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\).
Each block has a local feasible set \(X_i=\{x_i:R_i(x_i)=0,\ S_i(x_i)\le0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Retaining \(x_i\in X_i\) preserves block feasibility while permitting independent block minimization whenever the Lagrangian objective separates.

notation.meaning: Local feasible set for block i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-local constraints retained explicitly in every relaxed subproblem.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The retained local structure consists of all domain and constraint conditions imposed explicitly inside each Lagrangian subproblem. With \[X_i=\{x_i:R_i(x_i)=0,\ S_i(x_i)\le0\},\] these conditions remain enforced when coupling constraints are relaxed. If the partial Lagrangian has the form \(L(x,\lambda)=\alpha(\lambda)+\sum_i L_i(x_i,\lambda)\), then \[\inf_{x\in\prod_i X_i}L(x,\lambda)=\alpha(\lambda)+\sum_i\inf_{x_i\in X_i}L_i(x_i,\lambda).\] Thus retention preserves local feasibility and determines the independently solvable block domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retained local constraints remain explicitly enforced in every subproblem and define the feasible domain of each independently solved block.
knowledge_statements.title: Retained Local Structure

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224
source_witnesses.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of independent block minimization when the retained domain is not a Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Objective separability alone does not imply independent block minimization. Let \(X=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1=x_2\}\), \(L_1(x_1)=(x_1-1)^2\), and \(L_2(x_2)=(x_2+1)^2\). Then \[\inf_{(x_1,x_2)\in X}\bigl(L_1(x_1)+L_2(x_2)\bigr)=2,\qquad \inf_{x_1}L_1(x_1)+\inf_{x_2}L_2(x_2)=0.\] Thus the independent-infimum identity requires the retained feasible domain to separate as \(X=\prod_iX_i\), not merely the Lagrangian objective to be additive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A retained cross-block constraint can prevent independent minimization even when the Lagrangian objective is additive.
assumptions_latex: \(L(x,\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^mL_i(x_i,\lambda)\).
Independent block minimization is claimed over the retained feasible domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The product-domain condition \(X=\prod_iX_i\) is essential for the general independent-infimum identity.

notation.meaning: Retained feasible domain of block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure Under Retained Cross-Block Coupling

children.title: Relaxation-Retention Partition
children.top_down_role: Structural choices governing the boundary between priced coupling and local enforcement.

assumptions_latex: The minimization problem has an ambient domain \(X\), objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), equality constraints \(G_j(x)=0\) for \(j\in J_{=}\), and inequality constraints \(G_j(x)\le0\) for \(j\in J_{\le}\), where \(J=J_{=}\mathbin{\dot\cup}J_{\le}\).
A subset \(R\subseteq J\) is selected for relaxation, and \(T=J\setminus R\) is retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J=R\mathbin{\dot\cup}T\) specifies exactly which constraints are priced and which remain explicitly imposed.

notation.meaning: Admissible multiplier set determined by equality and inequality senses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-index partition defining a partial Lagrangian interface for equalities and inequalities written in nonpositive form.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A relaxation-retention partition is a disjoint decomposition \[J=R\mathbin{\dot\cup}T.\] Constraints indexed by \(R\) are removed from explicit feasibility and assigned multipliers, while constraints indexed by \(T\) remain explicitly imposed. Define \[\Lambda_R=\{\lambda_R:\lambda_j\in\mathbb R\ \text{for }j\in R\cap J_{=},\ \lambda_j\ge0\ \text{for }j\in R\cap J_{\le}\}.\] For \(\lambda_R\in\Lambda_R\), the partial Lagrangian and retained domain are \[L_R(x,\lambda_R)=f(x)+\sum_{j\in R}\lambda_jG_j(x),\qquad X_T=\{x\in X:G_j(x)=0\ \text{for }j\in T\cap J_{=},\ G_j(x)\le0\ \text{for }j\in T\cap J_{\le}\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation-retention partition divides equality and nonpositive inequality constraints into those priced by admissible multipliers and those imposed directly in every subproblem.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Retention Partition

children.title: Partial Lagrangian Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxations that price only a selected portion of the available coupling structure.

assumptions_latex: A minimization problem has ambient domain \(X\), objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), equality index set \(J_{=}\), inequality index set \(J_{\le}\), and constraints \(G_j(x)=0\) for \(j\in J_{=}\) and \(G_j(x)\le0\) for \(j\in J_{\le}\).
The full index set \(J=J_{=}\mathbin{\dot\cup}J_{\le}\) is partitioned as \(J=R\mathbin{\dot\cup}T\), with equality multipliers unrestricted and inequality multipliers nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_R=\sup_{\lambda_R\in\Lambda_R}\inf_{x\in X_T}L_R(x,\lambda_R)\le p^*\).

notation.meaning: Partial Lagrangian for relaxed index set R.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial relaxation of a selected subset of equality and nonpositive inequality constraints in minimization.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[X_T=\{x\in X:G_j(x)=0\ \text{for }j\in T\cap J_{=},\ G_j(x)\le0\ \text{for }j\in T\cap J_{\le}\}\] and \[\Lambda_R=\{\lambda_R:\lambda_j\in\mathbb R\ \text{for }j\in R\cap J_{=},\ \lambda_j\ge0\ \text{for }j\in R\cap J_{\le}\}.\] The partial Lagrangian relaxation associated with \(R\) is \[L_R(x,\lambda_R)=f(x)+\sum_{j\in R}\lambda_jG_j(x),\qquad g_R(\lambda_R)=\inf_{x\in X_T}L_R(x,\lambda_R),\] with optimized bound \[d_R=\sup_{\lambda_R\in\Lambda_R}g_R(\lambda_R)\le p^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial Lagrangian prices only the selected equality and inequality constraints, retains all others explicitly, and defines a valid optimized lower bound for minimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial Lagrangian Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224
source_witnesses.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

assumptions_latex: \(L_R(x,\lambda_R)=f(x)+\langle\lambda_R,G_R(x)\rangle\) is the partial Lagrangian on the retained domain \(X_T\).
\(\Lambda_R\) is the convex admissible multiplier set determined by the relaxed constraint senses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_R\) is concave on \(\Lambda_R\); if \(x_\lambda\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X_T}L_R(x,\lambda)\), then \(G_R(x_\lambda)\in\partial^+g_R(\lambda)\) relative to \(\Lambda_R\).

notation.meaning: vector of constraint functions indexed by the relaxed set R
superdifferential of a concave function on the admissible multiplier set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concave multiplier-space geometry of a partial Lagrangian relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The partial dual function \[g_R(\lambda_R)=\inf_{x\in X_T}\bigl(f(x)+\langle\lambda_R,G_R(x)\rangle\bigr)\] is concave on \(\Lambda_R\). If the inner infimum at \(\lambda\) is attained by \(x_\lambda\), then for every \(\eta\in\Lambda_R\), \[g_R(\eta)\le g_R(\lambda)+\langle G_R(x_\lambda),\eta-\lambda\rangle,\] so the relaxed-constraint residual is a supergradient relative to the admissible multiplier set. If the infimum is not attained, no residual from an actual minimizing primal point is available by this formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The partial dual function is concave, and an attained relaxed subproblem exposes its relaxed-constraint residual as a dual supergradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Dual Concavity and Residual Supergradients

children.title: Nested Lagrangian Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxation structures organized across multiple decomposition levels.

assumptions_latex: A minimization problem has equality constraints \(G_j(x)=0\) for \(j\in J_{=}\) and inequality constraints \(G_j(x)\le0\) for \(j\in J_{\le}\), with \(J=J_{=}\mathbin{\dot\cup}J_{\le}\).

The relaxed index sets satisfy \(R_1\subseteq R_2\subseteq J\); at level \(k\), constraints in \(R_k\) are assigned admissible multipliers and constraints in \(J\setminus R_k\) remain explicitly imposed.

notation.meaning: Relaxed constraint set at hierarchy level k.
Optimized partial-Lagrangian bound at level k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound ordering for nested partial Lagrangian relaxations of a fixed minimization problem.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\in\{1,2\}\), let \(d_{R_k}\) denote the optimized partial-Lagrangian lower bound obtained by relaxing exactly the constraints in \(R_k\) and retaining those in \(J\setminus R_k\). If \(R_1\subseteq R_2\), then \[d_{R_2}\le d_{R_1}\le p^*.\] Thus, in this nested construction, relaxing additional constraints cannot increase the optimized lower bound, although it can increase block separability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nested relaxed sets in a fixed minimization problem, relaxing more constraints cannot increase the optimized lower bound, although it can improve separability.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Lagrangian Relaxations

children.title: Coupling-Scale Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: The allocation of coupling structures across successive relaxation layers.

assumptions_latex: A fixed minimization problem has constraint index set \(J\), ambient domain \(X\), objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), equality constraints \(G_j(x)=0\), and inequalities \(G_j(x)\le0\).
The relaxed sets form a finite chain \(R_0\subseteq R_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq R_K\subseteq J\), and level \(k\) retains exactly the constraints indexed by \(J\setminus R_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{R_K}\le\cdots\le d_{R_1}\le d_{R_0}\le p^*\).

notation.meaning: Relaxed constraint set at scale k.
Optimized partial-Lagrangian bound at scale k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite hierarchy ordered by inclusion of relaxed coupling sets in a fixed minimization problem.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(k\in\{0,\ldots,K\}\), let \(X_{J\setminus R_k}\) be the subset of \(X\) satisfying all constraints indexed by \(J\setminus R_k\), let \(\Lambda_{R_k}\) contain unrestricted multipliers for relaxed equalities and nonnegative multipliers for relaxed inequalities, and define \[L_{R_k}(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\sum_{j\in R_k}\lambda_jG_j(x),\qquad d_{R_k}=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda_{R_k}}\inf_{x\in X_{J\setminus R_k}}L_{R_k}(x,\lambda).\] The nested chain \[R_0\subseteq R_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq R_K\subseteq J\] represents a coupling-scale hierarchy, with bound ordering \[d_{R_K}\le\cdots\le d_{R_1}\le d_{R_0}\le p^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested relaxed constraint sets represent coupling scales whose optimized lower bounds cannot increase as additional coupling constraints are relaxed.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupling-Scale Hierarchy

children.title: Strengthened Lagrangian Formulations
children.top_down_role: Equivalent reformulations and redundant structure used to improve the resulting bound.

assumptions_latex: A base minimization formulation has primal value \(p^*\), Lagrangian dual function \(g_{\mathrm{base}}(\lambda)\), and optimized bound \(d_{\mathrm{base}}=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}g_{\mathrm{base}}(\lambda)\).

An equivalent strengthened formulation adds inequalities \(r_q(x)\le0\), indexed by \(q\in Q\), without changing the primal feasible set or objective values; these inequalities are dualized with multipliers \(\nu_q\ge0\), and \(g_{\mathrm{str}}(\lambda,0)=g_{\mathrm{base}}(\lambda)\) for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\mathrm{base}}\le d_{\mathrm{str}}\le p^*\).

notation.meaning: Optimized bound from the base formulation.
Optimized bound from the strengthened formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound strengthening by dualizing added valid structure in an equivalent minimization formulation, with zero added multipliers reproducing the base dual function.

source_refs.locator: 3.4 Parallelization and Decomposition of Optimization Problems p. 224
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the strengthened optimized bound by \[d_{\mathrm{str}}=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda,\ \nu\in\mathbb R_+^{Q}}g_{\mathrm{str}}(\lambda,\nu).\] If the strengthened formulation is primal-equivalent to the base formulation and satisfies \(g_{\mathrm{str}}(\lambda,0)=g_{\mathrm{base}}(\lambda)\) for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), then \[d_{\mathrm{base}}\le d_{\mathrm{str}}\le p^*.\] The first inequality can be strict, but strict improvement is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing valid added structure cannot worsen the optimized lower bound when zero added multipliers exactly reproduce the base Lagrangian dual function.
knowledge_statements.title: Strengthened Lagrangian Formulations

Added nonpositive inequalities use nonnegative multipliers.

children.title: Lagrangian Bound Validity
children.top_down_role: The universal bounding role of feasible multiplier choices.

assumptions_latex: The ambient set is \(X\), the objective is \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), the equality map is \(h:X\to\mathbb R^q\), and the inequality map is \(c:X\to\mathbb R^r\).
The minimization value is \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ h(x)=0,\ c(x)\le0\}\), with equality multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^q\) unrestricted and inequality multiplier \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \((\lambda,\mu)\in\mathbb R^q\times\mathbb R_+^r\), \(g(\lambda,\mu)\le p^*\), and hence \(d^*\le p^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak Lagrangian duality for minimization with finite-dimensional equality and componentwise nonpositive inequality constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}h(x)+\mu^{\mathsf T}c(x),\qquad g(\lambda,\mu)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda,\mu).\] For every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^q\) and \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^r\), weak Lagrangian duality gives \[g(\lambda,\mu)\le p^*.\] Consequently, \[d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^q,\ \mu\in\mathbb R_+^r}g(\lambda,\mu)\le p^*.\] This bound validity does not require convexity or a constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every unrestricted equality multiplier and nonnegative inequality multiplier gives a lower bound for the minimization problem, and optimizing over those multipliers preserves validity.
knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Bound Validity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Wrong-Sign Inequality Multipliers Destroy Bound Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp sign boundary for minimization inequalities written as \(c(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{-1\}\), \(f(-1)=0\), and \(c(-1)=-1\le0\). Then \(p^*=0\). If the sign restriction is violated by choosing \(\mu=-1\), \[g(\mu)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\mu c(x)\}=1>p^*.\] Thus nonnegativity of inequality multipliers is necessary for universal lower-bound validity under the convention \(c(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative multiplier on a nonpositive minimization constraint can make the Lagrangian value exceed the primal optimum.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
The inequality convention is \(c(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu<0\) can yield \(g(\mu)>p^*\); universal validity therefore requires \(\mu\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Wrong-Sign Inequality Multipliers Destroy Bound Validity

children.title: Exact Lagrangian Relaxation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural settings in which the optimized relaxation closes the relevant duality gap.

assumptions_latex: For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(E_i\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space, \(X_i\subseteq E_i\) is nonempty and convex, and \(f_i:E_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex with \(X_i\cap\operatorname{dom}f_i\neq\varnothing\).
The equality data are linear maps \(A_i:E_i\to\mathbb R^q\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^q\); for \(j\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\), each \(c_{ji}:E_i\to\mathbb R\) is convex, and \(p^*\) is finite.

There exists \(\bar x=(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_m)\in\operatorname{ri}(\prod_i(X_i\cap\operatorname{dom}f_i))\) such that \(\sum_iA_i\bar x_i=b\) and \(\sum_i c_{ji}(\bar x_i)<0\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^q,\ \mu\in\mathbb R_+^r}g(\lambda,\mu)=p^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex strong duality and dual attainment under an explicit relative-interior Slater condition.

source_refs.locator: 3.4.2 Separable Strictly Convex Programming p. 229

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[p^*=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i):\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b,\ \sum_{i=1}^m c_{ji}(x_i)\le0\ \text{for }j=1,\ldots,r,\ x_i\in X_i\right\}.\] Define \[g(\lambda,\mu)=\inf_{x_i\in X_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}\left(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i-b\right)+\sum_{j=1}^r\mu_j\sum_{i=1}^m c_{ji}(x_i)\right\}.\] Under the stated relative-interior Slater condition, \[\max_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^q,\ \mu\in\mathbb R_+^r}g(\lambda,\mu)=p^*.\] Thus the optimized Lagrangian relaxation is exact and an optimal multiplier pair exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated finite-dimensional convex separable problem, the relative-interior Slater condition gives equality of the primal and optimized Lagrangian values and guarantees optimal multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Lagrangian Relaxation Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong Lagrangian duality for feasible finite-valued polyhedral convex programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite-dimensional minimization problem whose objective, including the indicator of its explicit feasible set, is proper, closed, and polyhedral convex, and whose relaxed constraints are affine equalities and affine inequalities written in nonpositive form. If the primal problem is feasible and has finite optimal value \(p^*\), then its Lagrangian dual attains the same value at some unrestricted equality multiplier and nonnegative inequality multiplier. No strict inequality point is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible finite-valued polyhedral convex program has an attained exact Lagrangian dual even when strict Slater feasibility fails.
assumptions_latex: The ambient spaces are finite dimensional.
The objective plus explicit-set indicator is proper, closed, and polyhedral convex.
All relaxed constraints are affine.
The primal problem is feasible and \(p^*\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{\lambda,\,\mu\ge0}g(\lambda,\mu)=p^*\), and the maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Exactness Without Strict Feasibility

children.title: Lagrangian Duality-Gap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Nonconvex or weakly formulated settings with persistent bound gaps.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite nonconvex equality-constrained family exhibiting an arbitrary prescribed positive Lagrangian gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a>0\) and \(\gamma>0\), let \(X=\{0,a,2a\}\), impose \(x=a\), and set \(f(0)=f(2a)=0\), \(f(a)=\gamma\). Then \(p^*=\gamma\), while \(q(\lambda)=\min\{-a\lambda,\gamma,a\lambda\}=-a|\lambda|\), so \(d^*=0\) and \(p^*-d^*=\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A three-point nonconvex problem can have any prescribed positive Lagrangian duality gap.
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*=\gamma,\qquad d^*=0,\qquad p^*-d^*=\gamma.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Three-Point Positive-Gap Family

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perturbation-Function Characterization of the Lagrangian Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained minimization represented by its constraint-perturbation value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(u)=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax-b=u\}\), \(p^*=v(0)\), and \(d^*=\sup_\lambda\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\}\). With \(v^*(y)=\sup_u\{y^{\mathsf T}u-v(u)\}\), one has \(d^*=v^{**}(0)\). Hence \(p^*-d^*=v(0)-v^{**}(0)\ge0\), with a strict gap exactly when the lower-semicontinuous convex envelope of \(v\) is strictly below \(v\) at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimized Lagrangian value is the closed convex envelope of the perturbation value at zero, so the gap is its closure-convexification defect there.
assumptions_latex: \(v(0)\in\mathbb R\)
\(v\) and \(v^*\) are proper on the finite-dimensional perturbation space

notation.meaning: lower-semicontinuous convex envelope of the perturbation value function

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation-Function Characterization of the Lagrangian Gap
Lagrangian Duality-Gap Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional minimization with potentially nonconvex local domains or objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal value \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax=b\}\), define \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\}\) and \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda}q(\lambda)\). Weak duality gives \(d^*\le p^*\), while nonconvexity may produce \(p^*-d^*>0\). Concretely, let \(X=\{0,1,2\}\), impose \(x=1\), and set \(f(0)=f(2)=0\), \(f(1)=1\). Then \(p^*=1\), whereas \(q(\lambda)=\min\{-\lambda,1,\lambda\}=-|\lambda|\), so \(d^*=0\) and the duality gap equals \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lagrangian bounds remain valid without convexity, but optimizing them can leave a positive gap; a three-point example has primal value 1 and dual value 0.
assumptions_latex: \(X\ne\varnothing\) and the primal equality-constrained problem has finite value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^*\le p^*\), and strict inequality can occur in nonconvex problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Equivalent Convexifications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional separable equality coupling represented through proper closed-convexified block value functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\ge1\), let \(b\in\mathbb R^r\), and for each \(i\) let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), \(A_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^r\), and \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). Define \(h_i:\mathbb R^r\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) by \(h_i(y)=\inf\{f_i(x):x\in X_i,\ A_ix=y\}\). Assume every \(h_i\) and \(h_i^{**}\) is proper and \(b\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h_1^{**}+\cdots+\operatorname{dom}h_m^{**})\). Then the optimized Lagrangian bound equals the value of the closed-convexified resource formulation: \[\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^r}\left\{-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b-\sum_{i=1}^m h_i^*(-\lambda)\right\}=\inf_{\substack{y_i\in\mathbb R^r\\\sum_{i=1}^m y_i=b}}\sum_{i=1}^m h_i^{**}(y_i).\] Thus replacing the block value functions by their biconjugates preserves the optimized Lagrangian bound under the stated qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the block value functions and their closed convex envelopes are proper and the convexified domains satisfy the stated relative-interior qualification, the optimized Lagrangian bound equals the resource-allocation problem formed from those closed convex envelopes.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge1\), \(b\in\mathbb R^r\), \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), and \(A_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^r\).
Each \(h_i\) and \(h_i^{**}\) is proper.
\(b\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h_1^{**}+\cdots+\operatorname{dom}h_m^{**})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^r}\{-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b-\sum_i h_i^*(-\lambda)\}=\inf_{\sum_i y_i=b}\sum_i h_i^{**}(y_i)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Dual Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-coupled finite-dimensional block minimization evaluated independently at a shared multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\ge1\), \(b\in\mathbb R^r\), \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), \(A_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^r\), and \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). Consider \(\inf\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^m A_ix_i=b\}\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^r\), define \(q_i(\lambda)=\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\{f_i(x_i)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_ix_i\}\). Whenever all \(q_i(\lambda)\) are finite, the dual function separates as \[q(\lambda)=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_{i=1}^m q_i(\lambda).\] If each block infimum is attained at \(x_i(\lambda)\), the blocks can be solved independently and \(s(\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^m A_ix_i(\lambda)-b\) belongs to \(\partial^+q(\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a shared finite-dimensional multiplier, finite block dual values sum to the dual value. If every block minimum is attained, the blocks can be solved independently and their aggregate coupling residual is a dual supergradient.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge1\), \(b\in\mathbb R^r\), \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), and \(A_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^r\).
\(q_i(\lambda)\in\mathbb R\) for every block at the multiplier being evaluated.
Each block infimum is attained when the supergradient formula is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\lambda)=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_iq_i(\lambda)\), and under attainment \(\sum_iA_ix_i(\lambda)-b\in\partial^+q(\lambda)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the accepted finite-dimensional equality-coupled setting, suppose \(q\) is finite near \(\bar\lambda\), every local argmin mapping is nonempty and compact near \(\bar\lambda\), and the hypotheses of Danskin's theorem hold. If every block has a unique minimizer \(x_i(\bar\lambda)\), then \(q\) is differentiable at \(\bar\lambda\) and \[\nabla q(\bar\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i(\bar\lambda)-b.\] Without uniqueness, distinct minimizing responses may yield distinct residual supergradients, so differentiability need not hold.

knowledge_statements.title: Centralized Price Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous projected dual ascent with one coordinator and parallel block responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(m\ge1\), block sets \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), functions \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), maps \(A_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^r\), a coupling vector \(b\in\mathbb R^r\), a nonempty closed convex multiplier set \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R^r\), an initial multiplier \(\lambda^0\in\Lambda\), and steps \(\alpha_k>0\). At iteration \(k\), the coordinator broadcasts \(\lambda^k\). In parallel, block \(i\) returns \(x_i^k\in\arg\min_{x_i\in X_i}\{f_i(x_i)+(\lambda^k)^{\mathsf T}A_ix_i\}\) and its attained local value. The coordinator computes \(q(\lambda^k)=-({\lambda^k})^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_i[f_i(x_i^k)+({\lambda^k})^{\mathsf T}A_ix_i^k]\), forms \(s^k=\sum_iA_ix_i^k-b\), and updates \[\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_ks^k).\] Stop according to a prescribed iteration or progress criterion, and output the best evaluated dual value and an associated multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinator broadcasts a common multiplier, receives independently optimized block responses and values, aggregates their coupling residual, and performs projected dual ascent while retaining the best evaluated dual bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), \(A_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^r\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^r\).
Every block response problem attains a finite minimum at each evaluated multiplier.
\(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R^r\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(\alpha_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k(\sum_iA_ix_i^k-b))\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence of Centralized Projected Dual Ascent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard diminishing-step convergence for the synchronous centralized coordination seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q:\Lambda\to\mathbb R\) be finite, upper semicontinuous, and concave on a nonempty closed convex set \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R^r\), with \(\Lambda^*=\arg\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\neq\varnothing\). For \(s^k\in\partial^+q(\lambda^k)\), set \(\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_ks^k)\). If \(\|s^k\|\le G\), \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), then \(\max_{0\le t\le k}q(\lambda^t)\to q^*\), and \((\lambda^k)\) converges to a point of \(\Lambda^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With an attained upper-semicontinuous concave dual objective, bounded supergradients, and square-summable but nonsummable steps, the best dual value converges to optimum and the centralized multiplier sequence converges to an optimal multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is finite, upper semicontinuous, and concave on the nonempty closed convex set \(\Lambda\).
\(\Lambda^*\neq\varnothing\) and \(s^k\in\partial^+q(\lambda^k)\) with \(\|s^k\|\le G<\infty\).
\(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{0\le t\le k}q(\lambda^t)\to q^*\) and \(\lambda^k\to\lambda^\infty\in\Lambda^*\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Navigation boundary between common-price dual decomposition and network-governed distributed optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Price coordination crosses from centralized dual decomposition into distributed optimization when agents maintain local multiplier copies \(\lambda_i\), update them using only local data and neighbor messages, and must enforce agreement of those copies through a communication graph. Correctness then requires both optimization hypotheses and a mixing or consensus condition that contracts disagreement; connectedness and double stochasticity of one fixed mixing matrix alone do not exclude periodic noncontractive behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local price copies coordinated through neighbor messages make the method distributed, and convergence additionally requires genuine disagreement contraction rather than graph connectedness alone.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Price-Coordination Interface
Distributed Price Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus-plus-supergradient coordination over a fixed connected communication network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let agents communicate through a nonnegative doubly stochastic matrix \(W\) whose graph is connected. Agent \(i\) initializes \(\lambda_i^0\in\Lambda\). At iteration \(k\), it receives neighboring prices, forms \(v_i^k=\sum_jW_{ij}\lambda_j^k\), computes a local dual supergradient \(s_i^k\) at \(v_i^k\), and updates \[\lambda_i^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(v_i^k+\alpha_k s_i^k).\] With bounded supergradients, \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), the standard synchronous method targets both price consensus and maximization of the aggregate concave dual objective. Output the local prices and best aggregate dual value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each agent averages neighboring prices, adds its local dual supergradient, and projects; connected mixing and standard diminishing steps drive consensus and dual optimization.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is doubly stochastic and its communication graph is connected.
Local dual supergradients are uniformly bounded.
\(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_i^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\sum_jW_{ij}\lambda_j^k+\alpha_ks_i^k)\), targeting consensus at a dual optimizer.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility domain for assigning right-hand-side shares to blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For block sets \(X_i\) and linear maps \(A_i\), define \(Y_i=A_iX_i=\{A_ix_i:x_i\in X_i\}\). The equality-coupled system \(x_i\in X_i\), \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\) is feasible if and only if \(b\in\sum_iY_i\). Equivalently, the allocation master admits shares \(y_i\in Y_i\) with \(\sum_i y_i=b\) exactly when the original coupled system is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The original coupling is feasible exactly when the right-hand side belongs to the Minkowski sum of the attainable block-resource sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Allocation-Master Feasibility Domain

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate Representation of the Allocation Value Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-dual representation of the convex right-hand-side allocation master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\Phi(b)=\inf_{\sum_i y_i=b}\sum_{i=1}^m\phi_i(y_i).\] For proper convex \(\phi_i:\mathbb R^r\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), \[\Phi^*(\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^m\phi_i^*(\lambda).\] If \(\Phi\) is proper and lower semicontinuous at \(b\), then \[\Phi(b)=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^r}\left\{\lambda^{\mathsf T}b-\sum_{i=1}^m\phi_i^*(\lambda)\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The allocation value's conjugate is the sum of the block conjugates, yielding the common-price dual when biconjugacy holds at the requested resource.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\phi_i\) is proper and convex.
The allocation value is interpreted in the extended-real sense.
For the displayed dual equality, \(\Phi\) is proper and lower semicontinuous at \(b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi^*=\sum_i\phi_i^*,\qquad \Phi(b)=\sup_\lambda\{\lambda^{\mathsf T}b-\sum_i\phi_i^*(\lambda)\}\text{ under the stated closedness condition}.

notation.meaning: Optimal allocation value as a function of total resource
Fenchel conjugate of block i's resource-value function

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Reconstruction from an Optimal Resource Allocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery of a coupled primal optimizer from attained block value-function minima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y^*=(y_1^*,\ldots,y_m^*)\) solve \(\inf\{\sum_i\phi_i(y_i):\sum_i y_i=b\}\), where \(\phi_i(y_i)=\inf\{f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ A_ix_i=y_i\}\). If for every \(i\) there exists \(x_i^*\in X_i\) with \(A_ix_i^*=y_i^*\) and \(f_i(x_i^*)=\phi_i(y_i^*)\), then \((x_i^*)_{i=1}^m\) is feasible and optimal for the original equality-coupled problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal allocated shares reconstruct an optimal coupled primal solution whenever every block value is attained at its assigned share.
assumptions_latex: The allocation master has an optimal solution \(y^*\).
Every block infimum defining \(\phi_i(y_i^*)\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_iA_ix_i^*=b,\qquad \sum_if_i(x_i^*)=\inf_{x_i\in X_i,\,\sum_iA_ix_i=b}\sum_if_i(x_i).

notation.meaning: Optimal resource share assigned to block i
Block optimizer attaining the value at its assigned share
