knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Resource-Value Function Need Not Be Closed
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp closedness boundary for partial minimization over a block fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:u>0,\ v\ge 1/u\}\), let \(f(u,v)=0\), and let \(A(u,v)=u\). Then \(X\) is closed and convex, while \[\phi(y)=\inf\{f(u,v):(u,v)\in X,\ u=y\}=\begin{cases}0,&y>0,\\+\infty,&y\le0.\end{cases}\] Thus \(\phi\) is convex but is not lower semicontinuous at \(y=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a closed convex block set and convex objective can yield a convex but nonclosed resource-value function after projection.
assumptions_latex: Resource values are interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi\text{ is convex but not lower semicontinuous at }0.

notation.meaning: Resource-value function induced by projection onto u

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Resource-Value Function Need Not Be Closed

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Block Resource Value Need Not Be Attained
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp attainment boundary for reconstructing a primal block from an allocated share.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:u>0,\ v\ge1/u\}\), let \(f(u,v)=u\), and let the resource map be \(A(u,v)=0\). At the only attainable share \(y=0\), \[\phi(0)=\inf_{(u,v)\in X}u=0,\] but no point of \(X\) attains this value because every feasible point has \(u>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite resource-value infimum can fail to be attained, preventing primal reconstruction from the allocated share.
assumptions_latex: Resource values are interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi(0)=0\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname*{argmin}_{(u,v)\in X}u=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Block value at the sole attainable share

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Block Resource Value Need Not Be Attained

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real primal decomposition of a separable equality-coupled problem into block resource-value functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block define \(\phi_i(y_i)=\inf\{f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ A_ix_i=y_i\}\), taking \(+\infty\) for an empty fiber. Then, in the extended-real sense, \[\inf_{\substack{x_i\in X_i\\\sum_iA_ix_i=b}}\sum_i f_i(x_i)=\inf_{\substack{y_i\in\mathbb R^r\\\sum_i y_i=b}}\sum_i\phi_i(y_i).\] The identity requires neither convexity nor attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coupled primal value equals allocation of the total right-hand side among independent block value functions.
assumptions_latex: Values are interpreted in the extended-real sense.
The displayed interblock coupling is \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x_i\in X_i,\,\sum_iA_ix_i=b}\sum_i f_i(x_i)=\inf_{\sum_i y_i=b}\sum_i\phi_i(y_i).

notation.meaning: Right-hand-side share assigned to block i

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Right-Hand-Side Allocation Identity
Right-Hand-Side Allocation Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal decomposition of an equality-coupled separable problem by resource shares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block define the resource-value function \(\phi_i(y_i)=\inf\{f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ A_ix_i=y_i\}\), with value \(+\infty\) when no such \(x_i\) exists. Then the equality-coupled problem admits the exact representation \[\inf_{\substack{x_i\in X_i\\\sum_iA_ix_i=b}}\sum_i f_i(x_i)=\inf_{\sum_i y_i=b}\sum_i\phi_i(y_i).\] Thus a master problem allocates right-hand-side shares \(y_i\), while each block independently evaluates its cost of meeting its assigned share. No convexity is required for this value identity, although convexity affects master-problem tractability and duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coupled problem equals a master allocation of resource shares whose objective sums independent block value functions; the identity itself does not require convexity.
assumptions_latex: Optimization values are interpreted in the extended-real sense.
The coupling constraint is \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x_i\in X_i,\,\sum_iA_ix_i=b}\sum_i f_i(x_i)=\inf_{\sum_i y_i=b}\sum_i\phi_i(y_i)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Diminishing Step Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Step-size classification for projected subgradient optimization of a concave dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A positive step sequence \((\alpha_k)_{k\ge0}\) is diminishing when \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\alpha_k=0\). For projected dual supergradient ascent \(\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k s^k)\), diminishing steps make the magnitude of bounded-supergradient corrections vanish asymptotically. Diminishing alone imposes neither \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) nor \(\sum_k\alpha_k<\infty\); therefore it does not by itself provide the persistent movement condition commonly used in subgradient convergence results.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diminishing positive step tends to zero. This condition alone says nothing about whether cumulative movement is finite or infinite.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha_k>0\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\alpha_k)\text{ is diminishing}\iff\lim_{k\to\infty}\alpha_k=0\).

notation.meaning: subgradient step size at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes diminishing steps from summability conditions and fits the terminal container, but no targeted source with a locator is supplied.

children.title: Nonsummable Step Regimes
children.top_down_role: Step families classified by persistent cumulative movement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-value convergence for exact projected supergradient ascent on a concave dual objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k s^k)\), where \(s^k\in\partial^+q(\lambda^k)\), \(\|s^k\|\le G\), and \(\lambda^*\in\arg\max_\Lambda q\). If \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), then for every \(N\ge1\), \[0\le q^*-q_{\mathrm{best},N}\le\frac{\|\lambda^0-\lambda^*\|^2+G^2\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k^2}{2\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k},\qquad q_{\mathrm{best},N}=\max_{0\le k<N}q(\lambda^k).\] Hence \(q_{\mathrm{best},N}\to q^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infinite total movement and finite accumulated squared movement force the best dual value to the optimum under bounded exact supergradients.
assumptions_latex: q\text{ is concave on a nonempty closed convex set }\Lambda
\lambda^*\in\arg\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)
s^k\in\partial^+q(\lambda^k),\quad \|s^k\|\le G
\alpha_k>0,\quad \sum_k\alpha_k=\infty,\quad \sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le q^*-q_{\mathrm{best},N}\le\frac{\|\lambda^0-\lambda^*\|^2+G^2\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k^2}{2\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k},\qquad q_{\mathrm{best},N}\to q^*

notation.meaning: best dual value among the first N iterates

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsummable Square-Summable Step Convergence
Nonsummable Step Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent-movement condition for positive diminishing subgradient steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A positive step sequence \((\alpha_k)_{k\ge0}\) is nonsummable when \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\). In the diminishing nonsummable regime one simultaneously has \(\alpha_k\to0\) and infinite cumulative step length. The frequently used square-summable-but-not-summable condition strengthens this to \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k^2<\infty.\] Under standard bounded-subgradient and solution-existence assumptions, the first condition prevents prematurely finite travel, while the second controls accumulated squared perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsummable steps have infinite total length. The standard convergence regime combines this with vanishing steps and a finite sum of squared steps.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha_k>0\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), optionally together with \(\alpha_k\to0\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nonsummability condition and content kind fit the node, but the convergence interpretation about persistent travel and squared perturbations has no cited source.

children.title: Step-Summability Boundary
children.top_down_role: The distinction between useful long-run movement and overly rapid step decay.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp finite-travel failure for exact one-dimensional supergradient ascent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(\lambda)=-|\lambda|\) on \(\mathbb R\), with unique maximizer \(\lambda^*=0\). Choose positive steps satisfying \(A=\sum_{k=0}^\infty\alpha_k<\infty\) and initialize at \(\lambda^0>A\). Every iterate remains positive and exact supergradient ascent gives \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k-\alpha_k\). Consequently \(\lambda^k\to\lambda^0-A>0\) and \(q(\lambda^k)\not\to q^*=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A summable step sequence can provide too little total travel to reach the optimizer, even with exact one-dimensional supergradients.
assumptions_latex: q(\lambda)=-|\lambda|
\alpha_k>0,\quad A=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k<\lambda^0
\Lambda=\mathbb R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda^k\to\lambda^0-A>0,\qquad q(\lambda^k)\not\to q^*=0
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Total-Step Stagnation
Step-Summability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp exponent thresholds for polynomially diminishing step sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha_k=c(k+1)^{-p}\) with \(c>0\) and \(p>0\). Then \(\alpha_k\to0\) for every \(p>0\). The sequence is nonsummable exactly when \(0<p\le1\), because \(\sum_k\alpha_k\) is a \(p\)-series. Its squares are summable exactly when \(p>\tfrac12\). Consequently, the square-summable-but-not-summable regime is precisely \(\tfrac12<p\le1\); \(p=1\) is the boundary for total-step summability, and \(p=\tfrac12\) is the boundary for square summability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For polynomial steps, infinite total length requires exponent at most 1, while finite squared length requires exponent above one half.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\iff p\le1\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\iff p>\tfrac12\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial-step thresholds are mathematically consistent and the property kind fits the boundary leaf, but no inspectable source locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic Lagrangian Dual Ascent with Exact Line Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual multiplier ascent for a finite-scenario stochastic program using projected constraint-residual directions and exact line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\pi^0\geq0\) and \(v=0\). Given \(\pi^v\), solve the Lagrangian subproblem to obtain \((x^v,y_1^v,\ldots,y_K^v)\), and define each direction component by \(\widehat\pi_i^k=0\) when \(\pi_i^{v,k}=0\) and \(g_i^2(x^v,y_k^v,k)\leq0\), and by \(\widehat\pi_i^k=g_i^2(x^v,y_k^v,k)\) otherwise. If \(\widehat\pi^k=0\) for every \(k\), stop. Otherwise choose \(\lambda^v\) maximizing \(\theta(\pi^v+\lambda\widehat\pi)\) over \(\lambda\geq0\) subject to \(\pi^v+\lambda\widehat\pi\geq0\), set \(\pi^{v+1}=\pi^v+\lambda^v\widehat\pi\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start with nonnegative multipliers, solve the Lagrangian subproblem, and use constraint residuals as the ascent direction except where an inactive nonnegativity boundary requires a zero component. Stop when every direction vanishes; otherwise maximize the dual objective exactly along the feasible ascent ray and update the multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \pi^0\geq0
\text{At each iteration the Lagrangian subproblem and the stated feasible line-search maximization are solved.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\pi=0\Rightarrow\text{stop};\qquad \pi^{v+1}=\pi^v+\lambda^v\widehat\pi,\quad \lambda^v\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda\geq0,\,\pi^v+\lambda\widehat\pi\geq0}\theta(\pi^v+\lambda\widehat\pi).

children.title: Polyak Step Regimes
children.top_down_role: Multiplier step families organized around target-value information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected concave maximization using the attained optimal value as an exact target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the exact-target Polyak update \(\alpha_k=\beta_k(q^*-q(\lambda^k))/\|s^k\|^2\), every \(\lambda^*\in\arg\max_\Lambda q\) satisfies \[\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^*\|^2\le\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|^2-\beta_k(2-\beta_k)\frac{(q^*-q(\lambda^k))^2}{\|s^k\|^2}.\] If \(0<\underline\beta\le\beta_k\le\overline\beta<2\), \(\|s^k\|\le G\), and \(q\) is upper semicontinuous on \(\Lambda\), then \(q(\lambda^k)\to q^*\), \(\operatorname{dist}(\lambda^k,\Lambda^*)\to0\), and in finite dimensions \(\lambda^k\) converges to a maximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the exact target and relaxation bounded strictly between zero and two, Polyak steps decrease distance to every maximizer and force the dual gap to zero.
assumptions_latex: q\text{ is concave and upper semicontinuous on a nonempty closed convex set }\Lambda
\Lambda^*=\arg\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\ne\varnothing
s^k\in\partial^+q(\lambda^k),\quad 0<\|s^k\|\le G\text{ whenever }q(\lambda^k)<q^*
0<\underline\beta\le\beta_k\le\overline\beta<2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(\lambda^k)\to q^*,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(\lambda^k,\Lambda^*)\to0

notation.meaning: uniform lower and upper relaxation bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Target Polyak Fejér Convergence
Polyak Step Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Target-exact Polyak steps for projected maximization of a concave dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\) be concave on a closed convex set \(\Lambda\), suppose its attained optimum \(q^*\) is known, and initialize \(\lambda^0\in\Lambda\). At iteration \(k\), choose \(s^k\in\partial^+q(\lambda^k)\). If \(s^k=0\), stop; otherwise choose \(\beta_k\in(0,2)\), set \[\alpha_k=\beta_k\frac{q^*-q(\lambda^k)}{\|s^k\|^2},\qquad \lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_ks^k).\] Stop at zero target gap or a prescribed tolerance, and output the best multiplier and dual value encountered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Polyak rule scales a dual supergradient by the known optimality gap divided by its squared norm, with relaxation strictly between zero and two.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is concave and attains the known finite value \(q^*\) on \(\Lambda\).
\(\Lambda\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(s^k\in\partial^+q(\lambda^k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k=\beta_k(q^*-q(\lambda^k))/\|s^k\|^2\) for \(0<\beta_k<2\).

children.title: Primal-Bound-Guided Step Regimes
children.top_down_role: Multiplier step families guided by available primal bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition of a feasible-incumbent target's excess over the ideal dual target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(U_k=f(x^k)\) for a feasible point of a primal minimization problem, weak duality gives \(q(\lambda^k)\le q^*\le p^*\le U_k\), and \[U_k-q(\lambda^k)=\bigl(q^*-q(\lambda^k)\bigr)+\bigl(p^*-q^*\bigr)+\bigl(U_k-p^*\bigr).\] Thus the excess over the exact Polyak numerator consists of the primal-dual gap and incumbent suboptimality. Primal feasibility verifies target validity but not target accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent supplies a valid upper target, but its excess over the ideal target contains both duality-gap and incumbent errors.
assumptions_latex: x^k\text{ is feasible for a primal minimization problem}
U_k=f(x^k)
q^*\le p^*\le U_k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_k-q(\lambda^k)=[q^*-q(\lambda^k)]+[p^*-q^*]+[U_k-p^*]\ge0

notation.meaning: objective value of a feasible primal incumbent

review_flags: validity of the bound alone gives no convergence guarantee
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Bound Target-Gap Decomposition
Primal-Bound-Guided Step Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyak-type dual steps using an available primal upper bound as target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(U_k\) be a valid primal upper bound satisfying \(U_k\ge p^*\ge q(\lambda^k)\). Given \(s^k\in\partial^+q(\lambda^k)\) with \(s^k\ne0\) and \(\beta_k>0\), define \[\alpha_k=\beta_k\frac{U_k-q(\lambda^k)}{\|s^k\|^2},\qquad \lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_ks^k).\] Update \(U_k\) whenever a better feasible primal point is found. Stop using prescribed primal-dual gap, residual, or iteration criteria; output the best primal bound, dual bound, and multiplier. Because \(U_k\) may exceed the optimal dual value, safeguards or target reduction may be necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible primal value can replace the unknown optimal dual value in a Polyak-like step, but an overly loose bound can cause oversized persistent steps.
assumptions_latex: \(U_k\) is the objective value of a feasible primal point or another valid primal upper bound.
\(s^k\in\partial^+q(\lambda^k)\) and \(s^k\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k=\beta_k(U_k-q(\lambda^k))/\|s^k\|^2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the primal-bound-guided leaf, but unrestricted positive relaxation and the unspecified safeguard or target-reduction mechanism make the reliable algorithmic regime source-dependent. No source is supplied.

children.title: Target-Quality Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Reliability limits caused by inaccurate, stale, or unattainable target information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an unsafeguarded Polyak-type ascent rule when its target lies below the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(\lambda)=-|\lambda|\) on \(\mathbb R\), let \(q^*=0\) and use the underestimated target \(T=-1\). At \(\lambda^0=1\), \(q(\lambda^0)=T\), so \(\alpha_0=\beta(T-q(\lambda^0))/\|s^0\|^2=0\) although \(\lambda^0\) is not optimal. More generally, whenever \(q(\lambda^k)>T\), the nominal step is negative and reverses the ascent direction. Clipping negative steps prevents reversal but can still stagnate on the nonoptimal target level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A target below the optimum can make a Polyak step vanish at a nonoptimal point or become negative after the target level is exceeded.
assumptions_latex: q(\lambda)=-|\lambda|,\quad \Lambda=\mathbb R,\quad q^*=0
\alpha_k=\beta(T-q(\lambda^k))/\|s^k\|^2,\quad \beta>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(\lambda^k)=T\Rightarrow\alpha_k=0,\qquad q(\lambda^k)>T\Rightarrow\alpha_k<0
knowledge_statements.title: Underestimated-Target Stagnation and Sign Reversal
Target-Quality Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step sensitivity of Polyak-type dual ascent to target overestimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\) be concave with maximizer \(\lambda^*\) and value \(q^*\). For \(s^k\in\partial^+q(\lambda^k)\), set \(\delta_k=q^*-q(\lambda^k)\), choose target \(T_k=q^*+e_k\), and use \(\alpha_k=\beta_k(T_k-q(\lambda^k))/\|s^k\|^2\). Nonexpansiveness of projection and the supergradient inequality give \[\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^*\|^2\le\|\lambda^k-\lambda^*\|^2-\frac{\beta_k(\delta_k+e_k)\bigl(2\delta_k-\beta_k(\delta_k+e_k)\bigr)}{\|s^k\|^2}.\] For \(e_k=0\) and \(0<\beta_k<2\), the correction is nonnegative; persistent overestimation can reverse its sign near optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact target yields a distance decrease for relaxation below two. A persistently high target can make the same bound increase near the optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is concave, \(\lambda^*\in\arg\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\), and \(\Lambda\) is closed convex.
\(s^k\in\partial^+q(\lambda^k)\) and \(s^k\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_k=0\) and \(0<\beta_k<2\) ensure the displayed distance correction is nonnegative; sufficiently large \(e_k>0\) need not.

notation.meaning: target error relative to the optimal dual value
target value used by the step rule

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive Aggregation of Block Solution Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable Lagrangian evaluation with independently certified inexact block minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(L(x,\lambda)=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_iL_i(x_i,\lambda)\). If \(L_i(\widehat x_i,\lambda)\le\inf_{x_i\in X_i}L_i(x_i,\lambda)+\varepsilon_i\), then \(L(\widehat x,\lambda)\le q(\lambda)+\sum_i\varepsilon_i\), and \(\widehat g=\sum_iA_i\widehat x_i-b\) is a \((\sum_i\varepsilon_i)\)-supergradient of \(q\) at \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent block-solution errors add, and their sum is the aggregate dual-supergradient error.
assumptions_latex: \(L(x,\lambda)=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_iL_i(x_i,\lambda)\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Moreau-Envelope Representation of the Augmented Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex equality-constrained problem under a qualification supporting the augmented-dual envelope identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(\mu)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\mu^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\}\). Under the stated convex interchange qualification, \(q_\rho(\lambda)=\sup_{\mu\in\mathbb R^m}\{q(\mu)-\|\mu-\lambda\|^2/(2\rho)\}\). Thus \(q_\rho\) is concave and continuously differentiable, \(\nabla q_\rho(\lambda)=(\mu_\rho(\lambda)-\lambda)/\rho\), and \(\nabla q_\rho\) is \(1/\rho\)-Lipschitz. If the dual supremum is finite, \(\sup_\lambda q_\rho(\lambda)=\sup_\mu q(\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic augmented dual is the concave Moreau envelope of the ordinary dual, smoothing multiplier dependence without changing a finite best dual bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity properties and feasibility convergence of step-size-weighted primal averages under the equality-multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_k\) and \(\bar x^K=S_K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_kx^k\). Convexity gives \(\bar x^K\in X\) and \(f(\bar x^K)\le S_K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_kf(x^k)\). If \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_k(Ax^k-b)\), then \[A\bar x^K-b=\frac{\lambda^K-\lambda^0}{S_K}.\] Consequently, \(\|\lambda^K-\lambda^0\|=o(S_K)\) implies \(A\bar x^K-b\to0\); bounded multipliers give \(\|A\bar x^K-b\|=O(1/S_K)\). Individual responses need not converge or become feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted averaging preserves convex feasibility and Jensen bounds, while its coupling residual equals total multiplier displacement divided by cumulative step size.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex and \(x^k\in X\).
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is convex and finite at every averaged iterate under consideration.
\(\alpha_k>0\), \(S_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_k\), and \(S_K\to\infty\).
\(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_k(Ax^k-b)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x^K\in X,\quad f(\bar x^K)\le\frac1{S_K}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_kf(x^k),\quad A\bar x^K-b=\frac{\lambda^K-\lambda^0}{S_K}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex averaging of primal Lagrangian minimizers generated along a multiplier sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(S_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_k\) and \(\bar x^K=S_K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_kx^k\). Convexity gives \(\bar x^K\in X\), linearity gives \(A\bar x^K-b=S_K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_k(Ax^k-b)\), and convexity of \(f\) gives \(f(\bar x^K)\le S_K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\alpha_kf(x^k)\). Consequently, bounds on cumulative weighted residuals and objective values transfer directly to the recovered primal average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging primal iterates preserves convex-set membership, averages their coupling residuals exactly, and cannot exceed their weighted average objective value.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\), \(x^0=0\), \(x^1=1\), \(w_0=-1\), and \(w_1=2\). Although \(w_0+w_1=1>0\) and both iterates lie in \(X\), the normalized affine average is \(\bar x=(-1)0+2(1)=2\notin X\). Thus positive total weight is insufficient: nonnegativity of every normalized weight is essential for universal preservation of convex feasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w_k\ge0\), \(W_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}w_k>0\), and \(\bar x_w^K=W_K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}w_kx^k\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Streaming recurrence equivalent to the offline weighted average, including leading zero weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(W_0=0\) and leave the average undefined. For each \(k\), set \(W_{k+1}=W_k+w_k\). If \(W_{k+1}=0\), store no average. If \(W_k=0<W_{k+1}\), set \(\bar x_w^{k+1}=x^k\). If \(W_k>0\), update \[\bar x_w^{k+1}=\bar x_w^k+\frac{w_k}{W_{k+1}}(x^k-\bar x_w^k).\] Whenever \(W_{k+1}>0\), this equals \(W_{k+1}^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^kw_jx^j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Skip leading zero weights, initialize at the first positive weight, and thereafter maintain the exact normalized weighted average.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose nonnegative weights \(w_k\) with \(W_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}w_k>0\), and output \(\bar x_w^K=W_K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}w_kx^k\). Equivalently, initialize \(W_0=0\) and, whenever \(W_{k+1}=W_k+w_k>0\), update \(\bar x_w^{k+1}=(W_k\bar x_w^k+w_kx^k)/W_{k+1}\). Stop at the selected recovery horizon. Because the normalized weights are convex coefficients, \(\bar x_w^K\in X\); its linear coupling residual is the same weighted average of the iterate residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative normalized weights combine primal iterates into a feasible-domain point whose coupling residual is their identically weighted residual average.

children.title: Averaging-Horizon Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Recovery behavior associated with aggregation windows and response histories.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Divergence of the trailing-window length alone does not transfer full-history feasibility convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^k=1\) when \(n^3\le k<n^3+n\) for some integer \(n\ge1\), and let \(x^k=0\) otherwise. Then the full-history averages satisfy \(K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}x^k\to0\). At \(K_n=n^3+n\), however, choose \(H_{K_n}=n\). The trailing window consists entirely of ones, so \[\frac1{H_{K_n}}\sum_{k=K_n-H_{K_n}}^{K_n-1}x^k=1.\] Thus even \(H_{K_n}\to\infty\) does not ensure trailing-average feasibility without a uniform cumulative-error condition over the selected windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse but increasingly long blocks can have vanishing full-history averages while selected growing trailing windows remain maximally infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(x^k=1\) on each block \([n^3,n^3+n)\) and is zero otherwise.
The target equality is \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac1K\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}x^k\to0,\qquad H_{K_n}=n\to\infty,\qquad \frac1{H_{K_n}}\sum_{k=K_n-H_{K_n}}^{K_n-1}x^k=1.

notation.meaning: end of the nth nonzero block

Hence \(H_K\to\infty\) implies \(\widetilde x^K\to0\) for this sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Growing trailing windows restore feasibility for perfectly alternating responses, with residual at most the reciprocal window length.

notation.meaning: number of most recent iterates retained

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed trailing windows need not inherit feasibility convergence of full-history ergodic averages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(X=[-1,1]\), the equality constraint \(x=0\), and iterates \(x^k=(-1)^k\). The full-history average satisfies \(K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}x^k\to0\). For any fixed odd window length \(H\), however, the trailing average is \(H^{-1}\sum_{k=K-H}^{K-1}x^k=(-1)^{K-H}/H\), which oscillates and never becomes feasible. Thus replacing an expanding ergodic horizon by a fixed recent window can destroy residual convergence, even for bounded iterates whose full averages converge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed odd trailing window of an alternating sequence remains infeasible, although the corresponding full-history averages converge to feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Averaging-Horizon Sensitivity

children.title: Resource Repair
children.top_down_role: Restoration of violated global resource relations in assembled local solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) are nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(\bar x_i\in X_i\).
Shared-resource relations are \(\sum_iA_ix_i=b\) and, when present, \(\sum_iB_ix_i\le d\) componentwise.
Each repair metric satisfies \(M_i\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the admissible correction set \(D\) is nonempty, the weighted minimum-change repair has a unique minimizer and its corrected blocks satisfy all declared local and shared-resource relations; if \(D=\varnothing\), exact repair within the local domains is impossible.

correction applied to primal block i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted minimum-change restoration of equality balances and componentwise resource capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the admissible correction set \[D=\left\{\delta:\bar x_i+\delta_i\in X_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\quad \sum_iA_i(\bar x_i+\delta_i)=b,\quad \sum_iB_i(\bar x_i+\delta_i)\le d\right\},\] omitting either resource relation when it is absent. If \(D\ne\varnothing\), compute \[\delta^\star=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\delta\in D}\frac12\sum_i\delta_i^{\mathsf T}M_i\delta_i,\qquad x_i^{\mathrm{rep}}=\bar x_i+\delta_i^\star.\] The minimizer exists and is unique. The output satisfies every local block domain and declared shared-resource relation. If \(D=\varnothing\), report restoration failure; no correction preserving all \(X_i\) can restore those relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find the unique weighted minimum-change correction that preserves local block domains and restores shared-resource balances or capacities, or report that no such repair exists.

children.title: Feasibility Projection
children.top_down_role: Projection-based restoration of coordinated primal feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection of a dual-derived primal candidate onto a closed convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a candidate \(\widehat{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and a nonempty closed convex feasible set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), compute
\[x^{+}=P_C(\widehat{x}):=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in C}\frac12\lVert x-\widehat{x}\rVert_2^2.\]
The minimizer exists and is unique. It satisfies \(x^{+}\in C\) and the variational inequality \(\langle \widehat{x}-x^{+},z-x^{+}\rangle\le 0\) for every \(z\in C\). Thus projection restores feasibility while making the smallest Euclidean displacement from the recovered candidate. The output is \(x^{+}\); an implementation may stop when its projection subproblem residual meets a prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the recovered candidate onto the closed convex feasible region. The unique result is feasible and has minimum Euclidean distance from the candidate.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(\widehat{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{+}=P_C(\widehat{x})\in C\) is uniquely defined and minimizes \(\lVert x-\widehat{x}\rVert_2\) over \(C\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the feasible set
primal candidate obtained from dual information

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and approximate feasibility certification by Euclidean distance to the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The distance function \(d_C(x)=\inf_{z\in C}\lVert x-z\rVert_2\) satisfies \[d_C(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in C.\] If \(C\) is also convex, then \(d_C(x)=\lVert x-P_Cx\rVert_2\). Hence \(\lVert x-P_Cx\rVert_2\le\varepsilon\) certifies that the candidate is within Euclidean distance \(\varepsilon\) of feasibility, while \(P_Cx\) itself is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to a closed feasible set is zero exactly at feasible points; for a convex set, projection displacement equals that distance.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Distance Feasibility Certificate

assumptions_latex: Euclidean projection means minimizing distance over \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Emptiness or nonclosedness can destroy existence, while nonconvexity can destroy uniqueness and firm nonexpansiveness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp structural boundary for existence, uniqueness, and stability of Euclidean feasibility projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C=\varnothing\), no projection exists. If \(C\) is not closed, the distance infimum need not be attained; projecting \(0\) onto \((0,1)\) has no minimizer. If \(C\) is closed but nonconvex, a nearest point can exist without being unique; projecting \(0\) onto \(\{-1,1\}\) has two minimizers. Thus the single-valued firmly nonexpansive projector for closed convex sets does not extend in general beyond that class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Empty or nonclosed sets can destroy projection existence, while nonconvex sets can destroy uniqueness and firm nonexpansiveness.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence and Uniqueness Failure Boundary

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(u,v\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert P_Cu-P_Cv\rVert_2^2\le\langle P_Cu-P_Cv,u-v\rangle\), hence \(\lVert P_Cu-P_Cv\rVert_2\le\lVert u-v\rVert_2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric stability of Euclidean feasibility restoration on a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(u,v\in\mathbb R^n\), the Euclidean projector satisfies \[\lVert P_Cu-P_Cv\rVert_2^2\le\langle P_Cu-P_Cv,u-v\rangle.\] Consequently \(P_C\) is nonexpansive and continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a nonempty closed convex set is firmly nonexpansive and therefore cannot enlarge Euclidean distances.
knowledge_statements.title: Firm Nonexpansiveness of Feasibility Projection

children.title: Primal Construction Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Heuristic construction of coordinated primal candidates from decomposed responses.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Construction Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic greedy construction of a feasible block solution from dual prices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For block sets \(X_i\), coupling requirement \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\), multiplier \(\lambda\), and penalty \(\rho>0\), initialize an empty partial solution and residual \(r_0=b\). At stage \(i\), select
\[x_i\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X_i}\bigl(c_i^{\mathsf T}x+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_i x+\rho\lVert r_{i-1}-A_i x\rVert\bigr),\qquad r_i=r_{i-1}-A_i x_i.\]
After all blocks are selected, apply any prescribed repair move that remains inside the product set. Stop with a feasible incumbent when \(r_m=0\); otherwise return the constructed point together with \(\lVert r_m\rVert\) as its infeasibility measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select block decisions greedily using dual prices and residual penalties, then repair them. Return a feasible incumbent or the final coupling violation.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\neq\varnothing\) and each displayed block minimization attains a solution.
\(\rho>0\) and \(\lambda\) are fixed during construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns \(x\in\prod_iX_i\), with coupling feasibility certified when \(r_m=0\).

notation.meaning: remaining coupling residual after selecting blocks through index i

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Relaxation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative weakness condition for a Lagrangian relaxation of a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p^*\in\mathbb{R}\) be the primal optimum and let \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\) be the optimum of a valid Lagrangian dual relaxation, so \(d^*\le p^*\). For a prescribed tolerance \(\eta>0\) and scale \(s>0\), the relaxation is weak at level \(\eta\) when
\[\frac{p^*-d^*}{s}\ge\eta.\]
A scale-independent convention may take \(s=\max\{1,|p^*|\}\). Under this condition, even exact optimization of the relaxation cannot produce a lower bound whose normalized gap from the primal optimum is below \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation is weak when its best dual bound remains separated from the primal optimum by at least a prescribed normalized gap.
assumptions_latex: \(p^*\) and \(d^*\) are finite.
\(q\) is a valid lower-bounding dual function for a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((p^*-d^*)/s\ge\eta\), so exact dual solution cannot close the prescribed normalized gap.
review_flags: A source is needed for the selected quantitative convention for relaxation weakness.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf and the inequality is internally coherent, but the threshold and normalization convention define a particular notion of relaxation weakness without cited support. A source is needed for that convention and its interpretation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise dual-bound dominance is general strengthening theory, not a pathology specific to weak-relaxation regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If two valid dual relaxations satisfy \(q_2(\lambda)\ge q_1(\lambda)\) on a common multiplier domain, then \(\sup_\lambda q_2(\lambda)\ge\sup_\lambda q_1(\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise dominance cannot worsen an optimized lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(q_1\) and \(q_2\) are valid lower-bounding dual functions on a common admissible multiplier domain.
\(q_2(\lambda)\ge q_1(\lambda)\) for every admissible \(\lambda\).

children.title: Bound Stagnation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Multiplier progress patterns with little improvement in the global bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational stagnation diagnostic based on retained rather than current dual bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For valid lower bounds \(\ell_k=q(\lambda^k)\), define \(B_K=\max_{0\le k<K}\ell_k\). Then \((B_K)\) is nondecreasing and \(B_K\to\sup_{k\ge0}\ell_k\le d^*\). Thus the generated search never attains a bound strictly above \(d^*-\varepsilon\) exactly when \(B_K\le d^*-\varepsilon\) for every \(K\). This all-history diagnostic differs from the tail criterion \(\limsup_k\ell_k\le d^*-\varepsilon\): an early strong bound remains recorded by \(B_K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The running maximum converges to the best generated bound, but it is an all-history diagnostic rather than an equivalent form of tail-value stagnation.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_k=q(\lambda^k)\le d^*<\infty\) for every \(k\).
\(B_K=\max_{0\le k<K}\ell_k\).
\(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_K\uparrow\sup_{k\ge0}\ell_k,\qquad \bigl(\forall K,\ B_K\le d^*-\varepsilon\bigr)\Longleftrightarrow \sup_{k\ge0}\ell_k\le d^*-\varepsilon.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-So-Far Bound Stagnation
Bound Stagnation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary defined by nonvanishing distance between generated bounds and the best dual value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\ell_k=q(\lambda^k)\) be valid lower bounds for a minimization problem and let \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)<\infty\). For tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), the bound sequence is in an \(\varepsilon\)-stagnation regime when
\[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\ell_k\le d^*-\varepsilon.\]
Equivalently, the generated multipliers fail asymptotically to attain any bound within \(\varepsilon\) of the strongest value available from the chosen relaxation. This criterion distinguishes algorithmic bound stagnation from relaxation weakness: stagnation concerns failure to approach \(d^*\), whereas weakness concerns a gap between \(d^*\) and the primal optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds stagnate when their asymptotic values remain at least epsilon below the best bound attainable from the same relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(q(\lambda^k)\) is a valid lower bound for every \(k\).
\(d^*<\infty\) and \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}q(\lambda^k)\le d^*-\varepsilon\).

children.title: Relaxation-Strength Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Structural indicators separating poor model relaxation from poor multiplier progress.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact attribution of an observed gap into incumbent, relaxation, and dual-search components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Whenever \(L\le d^*\le p^*\le U\), the observed gap decomposes as \[U-L=(U-p^*)+(p^*-d^*)+(d^*-L).\] The nonnegative terms are primal-incumbent suboptimality, structural relaxation weakness, and failure of the evaluated multiplier to attain the best value of that relaxation. Thus a large \(U-L\) cannot identify its cause without additional information about \(p^*\) or \(d^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The observed gap is the sum of incumbent error, structural relaxation gap, and dual-search error.
assumptions_latex: \(U=f(x^{\mathrm F})<\infty\) for a primal-feasible point \(x^{\mathrm F}\).
\(L=q(\lambda)>-\infty\) is a valid lower bound.
\(L\le d^*\le p^*\le U\).

knowledge_statements.title: Three-Way Relaxation-Gap Diagnostic
Relaxation-Strength Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori diagnostic using a feasible primal value and a valid dual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^{\mathrm F}\) be primal feasible for a minimization problem, let \(U=f(x^{\mathrm F})\), and let \(L=q(\lambda)\) be a valid Lagrangian lower bound. Define
\[G_{\mathrm{abs}}=U-L,\qquad G_{\mathrm{rel}}=\frac{U-L}{\max\{1,|U|\}}.\]
Weak duality gives \(L\le p^*\le U\), hence \(0\le U-p^*\le G_{\mathrm{abs}}\). Therefore \(G_{\mathrm{abs}}\le\varepsilon\), or respectively \(G_{\mathrm{rel}}\le\varepsilon\), certifies an absolute, or normalized, primal optimality gap no larger than \(\varepsilon\). A large observed gap diagnoses only the combined relaxation and primal-incumbent quality; by itself it does not identify which component is weak.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare a feasible objective value with a valid dual bound. A small gap certifies near-optimality; a large gap alone does not isolate its cause.
assumptions_latex: \(x^{\mathrm F}\) is primal feasible.
\(q(\lambda)\le p^*\) is a valid lower bound.
The problem is a minimization problem with finite \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le f(x^{\mathrm F})-p^*\le f(x^{\mathrm F})-q(\lambda)\).
review_flags: A direct source for the diagnostic convention and interpretation is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind is appropriate, and the absolute primal-dual gap certificate follows from weak duality. A direct source is still required for the chosen relative-gap normalization and for the diagnostic interpretation of a large observed gap.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-value convergence does not certify multiplier convergence when the optimal dual set is non-singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(\lambda)=0\) for \(|\lambda|\le1\) and \(q(\lambda)=1-|\lambda|\) otherwise. Then \(q\) is concave and every point of \([-1,1]\) is dual optimal. For \(\lambda^k=(-1)^k\), the dual values are identically optimal, but the multiplier sequence has accumulation points \(-1\) and \(1\) and does not converge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An alternating sequence on a flat optimal dual face has constant optimal values but two multiplier limit points.
assumptions_latex: \(q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is defined by \(q(\lambda)=0\) for \(|\lambda|\le1\) and \(q(\lambda)=1-|\lambda|\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(\lambda^k)=\sup_\lambda q(\lambda)=0,\qquad \operatorname{acc}(\lambda^k)=\{-1,1\}.

notation.meaning: concave dual objective with a non-singleton optimal face

knowledge_statements.title: Flat-Dual-Face Oscillation
Multiplier Oscillation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic oscillation criterion for a multiplier sequence in finite-dimensional dual space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A bounded multiplier sequence \((\lambda^k)_{k\ge0}\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) exhibits persistent oscillation when it has at least two distinct accumulation points. Equivalently, there exist subsequences \((k_j)\) and \((r_j)\) and vectors \(\bar\lambda\ne\widetilde\lambda\) such that
\[\lambda^{k_j}\to\bar\lambda,\qquad \lambda^{r_j}\to\widetilde\lambda.\]
This condition implies that \((\lambda^k)\) does not converge, although its objective values may converge. A stronger stepwise oscillation diagnostic is \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\lVert\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\rVert>0\), which implies nonconvergence but is not necessary for multiple accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multipliers oscillate persistently when a bounded iterate sequence approaches at least two different limit points, even if dual values converge.
assumptions_latex: \((\lambda^k)\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The existence of distinct accumulation points implies that \((\lambda^k)\) is nonconvergent.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the selected oscillation criterion.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf and the finite-dimensional accumulation-point criterion is mathematically coherent. No source is supplied for adopting this particular criterion, or the stronger stepwise test, as the intended multiplier-oscillation regime.

children.title: Persistent Primal Infeasibility
children.top_down_role: Sustained incompatibility among local primal responses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent infeasibility of raw responses need not be inherited by their convex averages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=[-1,1]\), coupling equality \(x=0\), and \(x^k=(-1)^k\), every raw iterate is locally feasible and has coupling-residual norm one. Nevertheless, \(\bar x^K=K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}x^k\) satisfies \(|\bar x^K|\le1/K\) and converges to feasibility. Thus persistent infeasibility of generated responses is not inherited automatically by ergodic primal recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating raw responses stay one unit from feasibility while their full averages converge to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(X=[-1,1]\) and the coupling equality is \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \liminf_{k\to\infty}|x^k|=1,\qquad \left|K^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}x^k\right|\le K^{-1}\to0.
knowledge_statements.title: Raw Persistence Versus Averaged Feasibility
Persistent Primal Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic failure of recovered block solutions to satisfy coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For recovered block decisions \(x^k=(x_1^k,\ldots,x_m^k)\) satisfying their local constraints, define the coupling residual
\[r^k=\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i^k-b.\]
The sequence has persistent primal infeasibility at level \(\delta>0\) when
\[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\lVert r^k\rVert\ge\delta.\]
Consequently, no sufficiently late recovered iterate satisfies the coupling constraint within tolerance smaller than \(\delta\). This definition concerns the generated primal sequence; it does not imply that the original optimization problem itself is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovered iterates remain persistently infeasible when their coupling residual stays bounded away from zero, despite satisfaction of local block constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i^k\in X_i\) for every block \(i\) and iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\lVert\sum_iA_ix_i^k-b\rVert\ge\delta\).

notation.meaning: coupling-constraint residual of the recovered primal iterate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, and the positive-liminf formulation correctly distinguishes persistent generated-iterate infeasibility from infeasibility of the original problem. A source is required for the selected persistence convention.

children.title: Oscillation-Infeasibility Linkage
children.top_down_role: The association between unstable prices and failure to coordinate local responses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent infeasibility need not produce multiplier oscillation when step sizes vanish summably.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(r^k=1\), \(\alpha_k=(k+1)^{-2}\), and \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_kr^k\). The residual remains nonzero, but \(\lambda^k=\lambda^0+\sum_{j=1}^k j^{-2}\) converges. Hence persistent primal infeasibility does not imply multiplier oscillation when step sizes may vanish; any converse based on \(\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\|=\alpha_k\|r^k\|\) requires at least control preventing vanishing steps on the relevant indices, and boundedness is additionally needed to infer multiple accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constant infeasibility with summable step sizes produces convergent multipliers, so the residual-to-oscillation converse fails.
assumptions_latex: \(r^k=1\) for all \(k\ge0\).
\(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_kr^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \liminf_{k\to\infty}|r^k|=1,\qquad \lambda^k\to\lambda^0+\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}j^{-2}.
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing-Step Converse Failure
Oscillation-Infeasibility Linkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linkage induced by the standard equality-multiplier subgradient update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose equality-coupling multipliers are updated by
\[\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_k r^k,\qquad r^k=\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i^k-b,\qquad \alpha_k>0.\]
Then the primal residual and multiplier displacement satisfy the exact identity
\[\lVert r^k\rVert=\frac{\lVert\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\rVert}{\alpha_k}.\]
If \(\alpha_k\le\overline\alpha<\infty\) and \(\limsup_k\lVert\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\rVert\ge\gamma>0\), then \(\limsup_k\lVert r^k\rVert\ge\gamma/\overline\alpha\). Thus persistent stepwise multiplier oscillation forces recurrent primal infeasibility under bounded step sizes, though it need not imply a positive residual limit inferior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the standard multiplier update, scaled multiplier motion equals primal residual. Persistent multiplier jumps therefore force recurrent infeasibility when step sizes are bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_kr^k\) with \(\alpha_k>0\).
\(\alpha_k\le\overline\alpha<\infty\).
\(\limsup_k\lVert\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\rVert\ge\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\lVert r^k\rVert\ge\gamma/\overline\alpha>0\).
review_flags: The algebraic identity is direct, but a source is needed for its interpretation as an instability linkage.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the linkage leaf, and the displayed identity and limsup implication are algebraically correct under the stated update and bounded step sizes. A source is needed for interpreting this identity as the intended instability linkage in Lagrangian decomposition.

children.title: Inexact Subproblem Contamination
children.top_down_role: Loss of reliable dual and primal information under uncontrolled local error.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine-in-multiplier Lagrangian dual oracle generated by a certified approximate primal response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\langle\lambda,h(x)\rangle\}\), and suppose \(\widetilde x^k\) satisfies \(L(\widetilde x^k,\lambda^k)\le q(\lambda^k)+\varepsilon_k\). Then \(\widetilde s^k=h(\widetilde x^k)\) obeys \[q(\mu)\le q(\lambda^k)+\langle\widetilde s^k,\mu-\lambda^k\rangle+\varepsilon_k\quad\text{for every }\mu.\] Thus \(\widetilde s^k\) is an \(\varepsilon_k\)-supergradient. For independent blocks with certified errors \(\varepsilon_i^k\), the aggregate residual is an \(\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k\)-supergradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified approximately optimal Lagrangian response produces an epsilon-supergradient, and separable block errors add.

knowledge_statements.title: Convergence Under Summably Controlled Subproblem Error
Inexact Subproblem Contamination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of certified dual bounds when approximate block values have uncontrolled positive error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a separable dual function \(q(\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^m q_i(\lambda)+\beta(\lambda)\), suppose block \(i\) returns \(\widetilde q_i^k\) satisfying
\[q_i(\lambda^k)\le\widetilde q_i^k\le q_i(\lambda^k)+\varepsilon_i^k.\]
Then the assembled value obeys
\[q(\lambda^k)\le\widetilde q^k\le q(\lambda^k)+\sum_i\varepsilon_i^k.\]
Hence \(\widetilde q^k\) is not necessarily a valid lower bound for the primal minimization problem. If the aggregate errors lack a known bound or fail to vanish, reported dual progress and subgradient-based primal information can remain contaminated; certification requires subtracting a valid aggregate error bound or solving the blocks exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate block minima can overstate the dual value. Without controlled aggregate error, reported bounds and derived primal information lose certification.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) decomposes into independently minimized block terms and \(\beta\).
\(0\le\varepsilon_i^k<\infty\) whenever an error bound is claimed.

knowledge_statements.title: Carathéodory Sparse Block Representation
Bounded Block-Polytope Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convex-combination representation used for bounded Dantzig-Wolfe blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) be a nonempty bounded polyhedron with vertex set \(V_i=\{v_i^1,\ldots,v_i^{N_i}\}\). Then
\[P_i=\operatorname{conv}(V_i)=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^{N_i}\theta_{ij}v_i^j:\ \theta_{ij}\ge0,\ \sum_{j=1}^{N_i}\theta_{ij}=1\right\}.\]
Thus every block decision \(x_i\in P_i\) admits a convex-combination representation by finitely many extreme points. Conversely, every coefficient vector satisfying the nonnegativity and convexity equations produces a point of \(P_i\). Substitution of this representation yields the standard bounded-block master variables in a Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every point of a bounded polyhedral block is a convex combination of its finitely many vertices, and every such combination remains in the block.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-value and attainment test for a linear objective on a pointed unbounded block polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\) be a nonempty pointed polyhedron. Then \(\inf_{x\in P}c^{\mathsf T}x> -\infty\) if and only if \(c^{\mathsf T}r\ge0\) for every \(r\in R\). When this condition holds, \(\min_{x\in P}c^{\mathsf T}x=\min_{v\in V}c^{\mathsf T}v\), so an optimum is attained at a vertex. If some \(r\in R\) satisfies \(c^{\mathsf T}r<0\), that ray certifies value \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear block problem is bounded below exactly when no recession ray has negative objective slope; when bounded, a vertex is optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Ray Boundedness Certificate
Unbounded Block-Polyhedron Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minkowski-Weyl representation for a nonempty pointed unbounded block polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) be a nonempty pointed polyhedron with vertices \(V_i=\{v_i^1,\ldots,v_i^{N_i}\}\) and extreme recession rays \(R_i=\{r_i^1,\ldots,r_i^{M_i}\}\). Then
\[P_i=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^{N_i}\theta_{ij}v_i^j+\sum_{h=1}^{M_i}\mu_{ih}r_i^h:\ \theta_{ij}\ge0,\ \sum_j\theta_{ij}=1,\ \mu_{ih}\ge0\right\}.\]
The convexity equation applies only to point coefficients; recession coefficients are nonnegative and need not sum to one. Conversely, every displayed combination lies in \(P_i\). This point-and-ray form supplies both column types required by an unbounded-block Dantzig-Wolfe master representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointed unbounded polyhedral block consists of convex combinations of vertices plus nonnegative combinations of its extreme recession rays.
assumptions_latex: \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) is nonempty, pointed, and polyhedral.
\(V_i\) and \(R_i\) list its vertices and extreme recession rays.

children.title: Block Lineality Regimes

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
\(c\in\mathbb R^n\).

notation.meaning: lineality space of the block polyhedron
recession cone of the block polyhedron

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundedness condition for linear optimization over a polyhedral block containing two-sided recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, let \(L=\operatorname{lin}(P)\), and consider \(\inf_{x\in P}c^{\mathsf T}x\). This infimum is finite if and only if \(c^{\mathsf T}d\ge 0\) for every \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(P)\). Since \(L\subseteq\operatorname{rec}(P)\) and \(-L=L\), finiteness forces \(c^{\mathsf T}\ell=0\) for every \(\ell\in L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear objective has finite value on the block exactly when it has nonnegative slope on every recession direction; consequently it must be constant along every lineality direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Objective Compatibility with Block Lineality
Block Lineality Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation boundary for polyhedral blocks containing nontrivial two-sided recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty polyhedron \(P_i\), define its lineality space by
\[L_i=\operatorname{lin}(P_i):=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}:x+td\in P_i\text{ for every }x\in P_i\text{ and }t\in\mathbb{R}\}.\]
A block is in a lineality regime when \(L_i\ne\{0\}\), equivalently when its recession cone contains a nonzero vector together with its negative. In that case a point-and-one-sided-ray formula alone is incomplete. Choosing a finite point set \(V_i\), pointed recession generators \(R_i\), and a basis \(B_i\) of \(L_i\), the complete form is
\[P_i=\operatorname{conv}(V_i)+\operatorname{cone}(R_i)+\operatorname{span}(B_i),\]
whenever these sets generate the corresponding quotient representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block has lineality when it contains complete lines. Its representation must include unrestricted lineality directions in addition to points and one-sided rays.
assumptions_latex: \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
\(V_i\), \(R_i\), and \(B_i\) generate its pointed quotient, recession cone modulo lineality, and lineality space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L_i\ne\{0\}\), a complete representation includes the term \(\operatorname{span}(B_i)\).

notation.meaning: generators of the pointed recession component

children.title: Nonpointed Block Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local block structures lacking the pointed geometry used by standard representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonpointed Block Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for extreme-generator reformulations of polyhedral blocks with nonzero lineality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n: Dx\le d\}\) be nonempty, and let its lineality space be \(L(P)=\{z:Dz=0\}\). The block is nonpointed exactly when \(L(P)\ne\{0\}\). Then every \(x\in P\) lies on the affine line \(x+\mathbb R z\subseteq P\) for each nonzero \(z\in L(P)\), so \(P\) has no extreme points. Consequently, a Dantzig--Wolfe representation using only extreme-point and extreme-ray columns is incomplete; it must retain lineality variables or first pass to the quotient by \(L(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral block with nonzero lineality has no extreme points, so an extreme-generator master must explicitly represent lineality or use a pointed quotient.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(P)\ne\{0\}\Rightarrow \operatorname{ext}(P)=\varnothing\), and extreme-point/ray columns alone do not represent \(P\).

notation.meaning: lineality space of the block polyhedron
set of extreme points of the block polyhedron

children.title: Extreme-Structure Representation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Representation limits arising when extreme points or rays do not provide the expected block description.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\text{ is pointed}\iff \operatorname{ext}(P)\ne\varnothing\iff \operatorname{rec}(P)\cap(-\operatorname{rec}(P))=\{0\}.\)

notation.meaning: set of extreme points of P

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact geometric boundary determining whether a nonempty polyhedron possesses an extreme point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonempty polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), the following are equivalent: \(P\) is pointed; \(P\) contains no affine line; \(\operatorname{rec}(P)\cap(-\operatorname{rec}(P))=\{0\}\); and \(\operatorname{ext}(P)\ne\varnothing\). Thus nonzero lineality eliminates all extreme points, whereas pointedness guarantees at least one extreme point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty polyhedron has an extreme point exactly when it is pointed, equivalently when it contains no line and its recession cone has zero lineality.
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Point Existence and Pointedness
Extreme-Structure Representation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp pointedness boundary for the usual extreme-point and extreme-ray representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron. If \(P\) is pointed, it has finite sets \(V\) of extreme points and \(R\) of extreme recession directions satisfying \[P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R).\] If \(P\) is not pointed, then \(P\) has nonzero lineality and no extreme points; hence this representation with \(V\) equal to the extreme points fails. A complete generator representation must additionally include the lineality space or use representatives in a pointed quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard extreme-point/ray representation applies to pointed polyhedra; nonzero lineality destroys extreme points and requires an added lineality representation.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pointedness permits \(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\) with extreme generators; nonpointedness invalidates the extreme-point-only part.

notation.meaning: finite set of extreme recession directions

children.title: Linking Row Families

knowledge_statements.title: Linking Row Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rows coupling otherwise independent blocks in a Dantzig–Wolfe master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider block variables \(x_i\in P_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). A linking-row family is a system \[\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i\ \mathrel{\bowtie}\ b,\] where each component of \(\bowtie\) is one of \(=\), \(\le\), or \(\ge\), and at least one row contains nonzero coefficients from two or more blocks. After substituting block generator representations, these rows become master constraints whose coefficients are the images of block generators under \(A_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linking rows contain coefficients from multiple blocks and become master constraints after block generators replace the original variables.
assumptions_latex: \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) is the local feasible region of block \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i A_i x_i\mathrel{\bowtie}b\) is retained as a coupling constraint in the master formulation.

notation.meaning: linking-row coefficient matrix for block i
local feasible region of block i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits Linking Row Families, and the variables and row relation are introduced consistently. No cited source with a specific locator supports the Dantzig-Wolfe terminology or transformation.

children.title: Convexity Row Families
children.top_down_role: Master rows governing the representation of local block combinations.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexity Row Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization rows attached to convex combinations of block point generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block \(i\) represented by point generators \(v_{ik}\in P_i\) and nonnegative weights \(\lambda_{ik}\), its convexity row is \[\sum_{k\in K_i}\lambda_{ik}=1.\] Together with \(\lambda_{ik}\ge0\), this row makes \(\sum_{k\in K_i}v_{ik}\lambda_{ik}\) a convex combination. Ray or lineality variables are not included in this normalization because they enter conically or freely rather than as convex weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each block’s point-pattern weights are nonnegative and sum to one; ray and lineality variables are excluded from this normalization.
assumptions_latex: \(P_i\) is represented using point generators indexed by \(K_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{ik}\ge0\) and \(\sum_{k\in K_i}\lambda_{ik}=1\) make the point contribution a convex combination.

notation.meaning: point generator k of block i
weight assigned to point generator k of block i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits Convexity Row Families, and the normalization statement correctly distinguishes point, ray, and lineality coefficients. A specific Dantzig-Wolfe source locator is absent.

children.title: Master-Row Role Separation
children.top_down_role: The division of global coordination from local representation within the master.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Row Role Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural distinction between global coupling rows and block normalization rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a Dantzig--Wolfe master with point-pattern variables \(\lambda_{ik}\), linking rows have coefficients \(A_i v_{ik}\) and enforce the original cross-block system, whereas the convexity row for block \(i\) has coefficient \(1\) on every \(\lambda_{ik}\) of that block and \(0\) on other blocks. Thus linking-row dual multipliers alter pattern reduced costs through \(A_i v_{ik}\), while convexity-row multipliers contribute block-specific constant offsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linking rows enforce cross-block feasibility, while convexity rows normalize one block’s weights; their dual multipliers affect reduced costs differently.
assumptions_latex: Each block has point generators \(v_{ik}\) and weights \(\lambda_{ik}\).
The master retains the original linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Linking and convexity rows have distinct coefficient structures and distinct terms in each pattern's reduced cost.

notation.meaning: linking-column image of block pattern k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the role-separation leaf, and the stated coefficient and reduced-cost distinctions are internally consistent. No inspectable source supports the master-row taxonomy and dual interpretation.

children.title: Block Columns

knowledge_statements.title: Block Columns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master columns induced by feasible point or recession generators of one block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the block objective \(c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i\) and linking map \(A_i x_i\), a point generator \(v_{ik}\in P_i\) induces the master column whose linking entries are \(A_i v_{ik}\), whose block convexity entry is \(1\), and whose objective coefficient is \(c_i^{\mathsf T}v_{ik}\). A recession generator \(r_{i\ell}\in\operatorname{rec}(P_i)\) analogously induces entries \(A_i r_{i\ell}\), convexity entry \(0\), and objective coefficient \(c_i^{\mathsf T}r_{i\ell}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block generator becomes a master column through its linking image, convexity coefficient, and objective value.
assumptions_latex: Block \(i\) has objective vector \(c_i\), linking matrix \(A_i\), and polyhedral feasible region \(P_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Point and recession generators induce master columns \((A_i v_{ik},1;c_i^{\mathsf T}v_{ik})\) and \((A_i r_{i\ell},0;c_i^{\mathsf T}r_{i\ell})\), respectively.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits Block Columns, and the point and recession column data are stated consistently. A source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is required.

children.title: Pattern Variables

knowledge_statements.title: Pattern Variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-master variables weighting individual block generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given point generators \(v_{ik}\) and recession generators \(r_{i\ell}\) for block \(i\), point-pattern variables satisfy \(\lambda_{ik}\ge0\) and \(\sum_k\lambda_{ik}=1\), while ray-pattern variables satisfy \(\mu_{i\ell}\ge0\). They parameterize the block vector by \[x_i=\sum_k v_{ik}\lambda_{ik}+\sum_\ell r_{i\ell}\mu_{i\ell}.\] If lineality generators are present, their coefficients are free variables and are not included in the convexity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pattern variables weight point and ray generators so that their aggregate reconstructs a feasible block vector.
assumptions_latex: The supplied point, ray, and any lineality generators give a complete representation of \(P_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pattern variables parameterize every represented \(x_i\in P_i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits Pattern Variables, and the reconstruction formula is appropriately conditioned on completeness of the generators. No cited locator supports the extended-master parameterization.

children.title: Column-Variable Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Variable Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-to-one indexing of generated master columns and their extended variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every retained block point generator \(v_{ik}\), introduce exactly one master variable \(\lambda_{ik}\) multiplying the column \((A_i v_{ik},1)\) with objective coefficient \(c_i^{\mathsf T}v_{ik}\). For every retained recession generator \(r_{i\ell}\), introduce exactly one variable \(\mu_{i\ell}\) multiplying \((A_i r_{i\ell},0)\) with objective coefficient \(c_i^{\mathsf T}r_{i\ell}\). Under this indexing, selecting a generator coefficient in the reconstruction is identical to selecting its associated master column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every retained block generator has one master column and one matching variable whose value is the generator’s reconstruction coefficient.
assumptions_latex: Duplicate generated columns are either retained with distinct indices or explicitly identified before forming the correspondence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Generator indices, master-column indices, and pattern-variable indices coincide.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward reconstruction validity versus completeness of the extended representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the master use arbitrary subsets of valid point, recession, and lineality generators of each \(P_i\). Every coefficient vector satisfying the associated sign, convexity, and linking constraints reconstructs an original-space feasible tuple, with the same objective value when generator costs are exact. Completeness is unnecessary for this forward implication but is required in general for every original-space feasible tuple to have a master representation. With incomplete generators, the restricted master may omit feasible or optimal points and its minimization value may exceed the full problem value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid retained generators always reconstruct feasible solutions, but incomplete generator sets may omit feasible or optimal original-space points.

Original-Space Reconstruction

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block \(i\), let a feasible master solution provide point weights \(\lambda_{ik}\), ray coefficients \(\mu_{i\ell}\), and, when needed, free lineality coefficients \(\eta_{iq}\). Reconstruct \[x_i=\sum_k v_{ik}\lambda_{ik}+\sum_\ell r_{i\ell}\mu_{i\ell}+\sum_q z_{iq}\eta_{iq}.\] If the generator representation is complete, the convexity rows hold, and all master linking rows hold, then \(x_i\in P_i\) for every block and the reconstructed tuple satisfies the original linking constraints with the same objective value.

children.title: Dantzig-Wolfe Master-Pricing Equivalence
children.top_down_role: The relationship between omitted master columns and local optimization under master dual prices.

children.title: Blockwise Pricing Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Independent pricing interfaces induced by separable local feasible regions.

assumptions_latex: The pricing feasible region retains a constraint involving more than one block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\neq\prod_iP_i\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{independent block minimizers need not form a feasible or optimal global pricing point}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp structural boundary for independent block pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0\le x_1,x_2\le1\), retain the coupling equation \(x_1+x_2=1\), and minimize \(q(x)=-x_1-x_2\). Each isolated block problem minimizes at \(x_i=1\), but the concatenated choice \((1,1)\) violates the retained coupling equation. Thus additive reduced cost alone does not justify unrelated block solves when the pricing feasible region is not a Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual coupling constraint can make independently optimal block choices mutually infeasible, so objective separability alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Cross-Block Constraints Destroy Independent Pricing
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Cross-Block Constraints Destroy Independent Pricing

\(q(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m q_i(x_i)\), with each \(q_i\) real-valued on \(P_i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\prod_{i=1}^mP_i\) and \(q(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m q_i(x_i)\). Then \[\inf_{x\in P}q(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\inf_{x_i\in P_i}q_i(x_i).\] If every block infimum is attained, every concatenation of block minimizers is a global minimizer. If one block infimum is \(-\infty\), the global infimum is \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Cartesian-product feasible set and additive reduced-cost objective make global pricing exactly equal to independent block pricing.
knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian-Product Pricing Separability
Blockwise Pricing Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent pricing oracles produced by separable block feasible regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization master, let \(\pi\) be the linking-row dual vector and \(\sigma_i\) the convexity-row dual value for block \(i\). Independently for each block, solve \[\theta_i=\inf_{x_i\in P_i}\bigl(c_i^{\mathsf T}-\pi^{\mathsf T}A_i\bigr)x_i-\sigma_i.\] If an optimizer \(x_i^*\) has \(\theta_i<0\), return its induced column; if every \(\theta_i\ge0\), report no improving point column. If a block objective is unbounded below along a recession direction, return the associated ray column. Stop when all blocks return nonnegative finite optima.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given master duals, solve one independent reduced-cost problem per block and add any negative-cost point or improving ray column.
assumptions_latex: The original objective and local feasible set are separable by block.
Blocks interact only through the retained linking rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global pricing separates into \(m\) independent block problems, and any negative block optimum supplies an improving master column.

minimum reduced cost in block i
