children.title: Reduced-Cost Pricing Equivalence
children.top_down_role: The certificate relationship between master prices and block improvement.

children.title: Reduced-Cost Certificates
children.top_down_role: Master-side improvement information associated with absent block columns.

assumptions_latex: The restricted minimization master has an optimal primal-dual pair with value \(z_R\).
For each block, \(\theta_i\) is a certified lower bound on the reduced cost of every full-master point column.
Every full-master ray column has certified nonnegative reduced cost at \(\bar\pi\).
The full master has a finite optimum \(z_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le z_R-z_*\le-\sum_i\min\{\theta_i,0\}.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound on every point-column reduced cost of block i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori full-master bound obtained from certified block pricing bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\bar\lambda,\bar\pi,\bar\alpha)\) be an optimal primal-dual pair for a feasible bounded restricted minimization master with value \(z_R\). For each block, let \(\theta_i\) be a certified lower bound on the reduced cost of every full-master point column, and suppose every ray-indexed reduced cost is certified nonnegative. Replacing \(\bar\alpha_i\) by \(\bar\alpha_i+\min\{\theta_i,0\}\) then gives a full-master dual-feasible vector. Consequently, \[z_R+\sum_i\min\{\theta_i,0\}\le z_*\le z_R,\qquad 0\le z_R-z_*\le-\sum_i\min\{\theta_i,0\}.\] In particular, \(\theta_i\ge-\varepsilon_i\) for all \(i\) implies \(z_R-z_*\le\sum_i\varepsilon_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified point-column reduced-cost lower bounds, together with nonnegative ray checks, give a computable upper bound on the restricted-master optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Quantitative Pricing-Gap Certificate
Reduced-Cost Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-and-oracle certificate that no omitted point column improves a minimization master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\pi,\sigma_i)\) be dual multipliers from a feasible restricted master, and define \(q_i(x)=(c_i^{\mathsf T}-\pi^{\mathsf T}A_i)x-\sigma_i\). Exact pricing values \(\theta_i=\inf_{x\in P_i}q_i(x)\) form a reduced-cost certificate. If \(\theta_i\ge0\) for every block and every feasible recession direction \(r\in\operatorname{rec}(P_i)\) satisfies \((c_i^{\mathsf T}-\pi^{\mathsf T}A_i)r\ge0\), then no omitted point or ray column has negative reduced cost. With primal and dual feasibility, the current master solution is optimal for the full reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative exact pricing bounds, recession checks, and feasible master primal-dual solutions certify full-master optimality.
assumptions_latex: The master is a minimization linear program.
Pricing is exact over every block feasible region.
Restricted-master primal and dual solutions are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No omitted column has negative reduced cost, so the restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind exactly fits Reduced-Cost Certificates. The certificate is internally coherent, but its reduced-cost sign convention and full-master optimality conclusion require an authoritative, specifically located source.

children.title: Pricing Outcomes
children.top_down_role: Block-oracle outcomes identifying improving columns or their absence.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive exact-oracle outcomes for a block pricing problem in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For block \(i\), minimize \(q_i(x)=(c_i^{\mathsf T}-\pi^{\mathsf T}A_i)x-\sigma_i\) over \(P_i\). Exact pricing has three relevant outcomes: if a finite optimum satisfies \(q_i(x_i^*)<0\), return the improving point column induced by \(x_i^*\); if the finite optimum is nonnegative, certify that the block has no improving point column; if the objective is unbounded below, return a recession direction \(r\in\operatorname{rec}(P_i)\) satisfying \((c_i^{\mathsf T}-\pi^{\mathsf T}A_i)r<0\), which induces an improving ray column.

A ray master variable has objective coefficient \(c_i^{\mathsf T}r\), linking column \(A_ir\), and coefficient zero in the block convexity row. Its reduced cost at linking multiplier \(\pi\) is therefore \[\bar c_{ir}=c_i^{\mathsf T}r-\pi^{\mathsf T}A_ir.\] Hence \(\bar c_{ir}<0\) is exactly a violated full-master ray inequality, while nonnegative reduced cost for every recession generator is equivalent to feasibility of all ray-indexed dual inequalities.

Consequently, absence of a negative-reduced-cost column certifies optimality of the restricted solution for the full master.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition by allowing block-specific spaces, feasible sets, costs, and linking maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A heterogeneous Dantzig–Wolfe block family is a finite indexed collection \(\{(X_i,P_i,c_i,A_i)\}_{i\in I}\), where \(X_i\) is a finite-dimensional real vector space, \(P_i\subseteq X_i\) is a nonempty polyhedron, \(c_i\in X_i^*\), and \(A_i:X_i\to Y\) maps into a common coordination space \(Y\). No common local dimension, feasible-set description, cost functional, or linking map is required across indices. The associated block-angular problem couples otherwise separate decisions only through a constraint such as \(\sum_{i\in I}A_ix_i=b\), with \(x_i\in P_i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{(x_1,x_2)\in[0,1]^2:x_1=x_2\}\) and let \(r(x_1,x_2)=-x_1+x_2\). Independent minimization over the projections \(P_1=P_2=[0,1]\) selects \(x_1=1\) and \(x_2=0\), producing the spurious value \(-1\), although that pair is infeasible for \(P\). On the coupled domain, \(r(x_1,x_2)=0\) everywhere. Thus pricing separation requires both a separable reduced-cost expression and a Cartesian candidate domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled-Feasibility Pricing Counterexample
Cross-Block Pricing Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of heterogeneous pricing under blockwise local feasibility and additive reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_i\) be independent local feasible sets, let \(\pi\) price the common linking equation, and let \(\alpha_i\) price block \(i\)'s convexity equation. The reduced cost of a block column \(v\in P_i\) is \(r_i(v)=c_i^{\mathsf T}v-\pi^{\mathsf T}A_iv-\alpha_i\). Because neither feasibility nor this reduced-cost expression contains another block's decision, pricing separates as \[q_i=\inf_{v\in P_i}r_i(v),\qquad i\in I.\] Thus the global search for an improving column is equivalent to computing the independent block values and testing \(\min_{i\in I}q_i<0\). knowledge_statements.title: Algorithm-State Symmetry Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbitwise pricing reuse under a symmetry-compatible algorithmic state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the block action preserves local costs and linking contributions and every additional term in the current pricing model is equivariant. In particular, let convexity multipliers satisfy \(\alpha_{gi}=\alpha_i\). Then the reduced cost of \(T_{g,i}x\) in block \(gi\) equals that of \(x\) in block \(i\). Hence blocks in one orbit have equal pricing optima, and a representative optimizer transports throughout the orbit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When both block data and the current pricing state respect the symmetry, one pricing solve per block orbit suffices.
assumptions_latex: The immutable group-action conditions hold.
Convexity multipliers and all stabilization or restriction terms are equivariant.
Pricing minima are attained for optimizer transport.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_{gi}^*=\rho_i^*,\quad x_i^*\mapsto T_{g,i}x_i^*.

notation.meaning: Transformation from block i to block gi.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivariant Pricing on Block Orbits
Symmetric Block Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block equivalence induced by transformations preserving the coordinated optimization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A block family indexed by \(I\) is symmetric under a group \(G\) if each \(g\in G\) induces a permutation \(i\mapsto g i\) and bijections \(T_{g,i}:P_i\to P_{g i}\) satisfying \(c_{g i}^{\mathsf T}T_{g,i}x=c_i^{\mathsf T}x\) and \(A_{g i}T_{g,i}x=A_ix\) for every \(x\in P_i\). The transformations must compose consistently: \(T_{gh,i}=T_{g,h i}\circ T_{h,i}\) and \(T_{e,i}\) is the identity. Thus applying any group element to block labels and local decisions preserves feasibility contributions and objective contributions, although blocks need not be literally identical in their original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block family is symmetric when a group permutes blocks through compatible transformations that preserve local feasibility, cost, and linking contributions.
assumptions_latex: A group \(G\) acts on the finite index set \(I\).
Each \(T_{g,i}\) is a bijection from \(P_i\) to \(P_{g i}\).
The transformations satisfy the stated composition law.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The action preserves \(c_i^{\mathsf T}x\) and \(A_ix\), and therefore preserves the coordinated block model.

notation.meaning: Transformation carrying block i to block gi
Image of block index i under group element g

children.title: Symmetry-Based Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Shared or aggregated representations enabled by repeated symmetric structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to dropping copy-specific restrictions during aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two copies satisfy \(\lambda_{ia}+\lambda_{ib}=1\), with additional restrictions \(\lambda_{1a}=1\) and \(\lambda_{2b}=1\). Their only aggregate is \((y_a,y_b)=(1,1)\). The naive aggregate system \(y_a,y_b\ge0\), \(y_a+y_b=2\) also admits \((2,0)\), which cannot be disaggregated subject to the copy-specific restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing column weights while discarding copy-specific restrictions can create aggregate points with no feasible disaggregation.
assumptions_latex: Each copy has a unit convexity equation.
The stated copy-specific restrictions are part of the original master.
The naive aggregate retains only nonnegativity and total weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (2,0)\text{ satisfies the naive aggregate but has no feasible original disaggregation.}

notation.meaning: Aggregate weights of columns a and b.

knowledge_statements.title: Naive Aggregation Can Lose Disaggregability

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Aggregation of Identical Convexity Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact aggregation for repeated interchangeable convexity families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\) identical families with common column set \(V\), define \(y_v=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_{iv}\). If every copy has only \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_v\lambda_{iv}=1\), and column \(v\) has common cost \(d_v\) and linking vector \(a_v\), then the exact aggregate system is \[y\ge0,\qquad \sum_{v\in V}y_v=m.\] Objective and linking contributions become \(\sum_vd_vy_v\) and \(\sum_va_vy_v\). Every aggregate point disaggregates, for example by \(\lambda_{iv}=y_v/m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interchangeable identical convexity families can be replaced exactly by total column weights summing to the number of copies.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many identical copies and a common column set \(V\).
Costs and linking columns are copy-independent.
No copy-specific constraint remains beyond nonnegativity and unit convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{y:y_v=\sum_i\lambda_{iv}\}=\{y\ge0:\sum_vy_v=m\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Aggregation of Identical Convexity Families

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence of invariant solutions for convex symmetric masters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act linearly and preserve a nonempty convex feasible set \(F\) and linear objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\). For every \(x\in F\), \[\bar x=|G|^{-1}\sum_{g\in G}gx\] is feasible, is fixed by \(G\), and has the same objective value. Therefore, whenever an optimum exists, an invariant optimum exists. Restriction to aggregate variables is exact only if those variables describe the invariant feasible set without losing disaggregability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex symmetric master with invariant linear objective has an invariant optimum, but an aggregate formulation must still describe the invariant feasible set exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acts linearly.
\(F\) is nonempty, convex, and invariant.
The linear objective is invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\in F,\quad g\bar x=\bar x,\quad c^{\mathsf T}\bar x=c^{\mathsf T}x.
knowledge_statements.title: Group-Averaged Invariant Optimum
Symmetry-Based Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbit aggregation for columns having identical objective and linking coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a symmetry group partition the full-master column indices \((i,v)\) into orbits \(O\). Assume every index in an orbit has the same objective coefficient \(d_O
eq	ext{undefined}\), the same linking column \(a_O\), and interchangeable convexity participation after aggregating equivalent block equations. Define \(y_O=\sum_{(i,v)\in O}\lambda_{iv}\). Then each orbit contributes \(d_Oy_O\) to the objective and \(a_Oy_O\) to the linking equations. Replacing orbit members by \(y_O\geq0\), together with the induced aggregate convexity constraints and orbit-capacity bounds when required, gives the projection of the symmetric master onto invariant variables. Any disaggregation of \(y_O\) satisfying the original convexity equations recovers an equivalent master solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Columns in one symmetry orbit can be replaced by their total weight when their costs, linking columns, and convexity participation are interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: The group action preserves all master coefficients.
Orbit members are interchangeable in the convexity constraints.
Any necessary orbit-capacity bounds are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_O=\sum_{(i,v)\in O}\lambda_{iv}\) preserves objective and linking contributions and yields the invariant projection of the master.

notation.meaning: Aggregate weight of columns in orbit O
Common objective and linking coefficients of orbit O

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the appropriate content kind, but the exact aggregation is not reliably specified. The expression d_O\neq\text{undefined} is nonstandard, and phrases such as 'interchangeable convexity participation,' 'induced aggregate convexity constraints,' and capacity bounds 'when required' do not state checkable sufficient conditions. An authoritative symmetry-reduction source is needed before the correct mathematical version can be fixed.

children.title: Partial Dantzig-Wolfe Reformulation
children.top_down_role: Selective convexification of only part of the block structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pricing interface created only for blocks selected for reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each reformulated block \(i\in D\), dual multipliers \((\pi,\alpha_i)\) induce \[\rho_i^*=\min_{v\in V_i}\{(c_i-A_i^{\mathsf T}\pi)^{\mathsf T}v-\alpha_i\}.\] A negative attained value supplies a dual-violating omitted column. Exact nonnegative minima for every selected block exclude omitted selected-block violations. Blocks in \(E\) remain explicit and receive no Dantzig--Wolfe pricing problem from this reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only selected blocks are priced; exact nonnegative reduced-cost minima for all selected blocks exclude omitted improving columns.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is solved with linking multiplier \(\pi\) and convexity multipliers \(\alpha_i\).
Pricing is exact and its minimum is attained when a column is returned.
The sign convention is minimization with nonnegative column variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_i^*<0\text{ identifies a violated omitted-column constraint; }\rho_i^*\ge0\ \forall i\in D\text{ excludes all such violations.}
knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Block Pricing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for unbounded selected blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an unbounded selected polyhedron, an exact substitution generally requires \[x_i=\sum_{v\in V_i}v\lambda_{iv}+\sum_{r\in R_i}r\mu_{ir},\qquad \sum_{v\in V_i}\lambda_{iv}=1,\quad \lambda_{iv},\mu_{ir}\ge0.\] Omitting a required recession direction makes the partial reformulation a restriction. A point-only convex-combination representation is exact for a polytope or when all necessary recession behavior remains represented elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected unbounded blocks require necessary ray columns; point columns alone need not preserve their feasible sets.
assumptions_latex: \(P_i\) is a selected polyhedron.
\(V_i\) and \(R_i\) contain the point and recession generators used by the substitution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Exactness requires every necessary point and recession direction to be represented.}
knowledge_statements.title: Point-and-Ray Completeness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound and exactness behavior for finite selected-block column subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing each complete selected-block column set \(V_i\) by \(W_i\subseteq V_i\) restricts the partial master. For feasible minimization masters, \[z_{\mathrm{PRM}}\ge z_{\mathrm{partial\ full}}=z_{\mathrm{original}}.\] Under master strong duality, equality is certified when a restricted-master optimum has exact nonnegative minimum reduced cost for every selected block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible partial restricted master gives an upper bound in minimization; exact pricing exhaustion restores full partial-master optimality.
assumptions_latex: The complete selected-block representations are exact.
The partial restricted master is feasible.
The equality certificate assumes applicable master strong duality and exact pricing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_{\mathrm{PRM}}\ge z_{\mathrm{original}},\text{ with equality under exact pricing exhaustion.}

notation.meaning: Current generated subset for selected block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Partial-Master Bound
Partial Dantzig-Wolfe Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selective convexification of chosen blocks while retaining the remaining variables explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the block indices as \(I=D\mathbin{\dot\cup}E\). For each reformulated block \(i\in D\), suppose \(P_i=\operatorname{conv}(V_i)\) and substitute \(x_i=\sum_{v\in V_i}v\lambda_{iv}\), with \(\sum_{v\in V_i}\lambda_{iv}=1\) and \(\lambda_{iv}\geq0\). Retain \(x_j\in P_j\) explicitly for \(j\in E\). The partial master has linking equation \[\sum_{i\in D}\sum_{v\in V_i}A_iv\lambda_{iv}+\sum_{j\in E}A_jx_j=b\] and objective \(\sum_{i\in D}\sum_{v\in V_i}c_i^{\mathsf T}v\lambda_{iv}+\sum_{j\in E}c_j^{\mathsf T}x_j\). This formulation is equivalent to the original problem when every selected block uses its complete representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial reformulation replaces selected blocks by column weights while leaving all other block variables and constraints explicit.
assumptions_latex: \(I=D\mathbin{\dot\cup}E\) is a partition.
\(P_i=\operatorname{conv}(V_i)\) for each \(i\in D\).
Unreformulated constraints \(x_j\in P_j\) are retained for \(j\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complete column representations for \(i\in D\) make the partial master objective-preserving and feasible-set equivalent to the original formulation.

notation.meaning: Indices of blocks reformulated by columns
Complete column set for selected block i

children.title: Nested Dantzig-Wolfe Reformulation
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical master-pricing interfaces for multilevel block structures.

assumptions_latex: Each inner formulation represents its outer block \(P_i\) exactly.
The outer reduced cost is a linear functional on each \(P_i\).
The outer restricted master satisfies primal-dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(q_i\ge0\text{ for every }i\bigr)\) together with outer restricted-master primal-dual optimality certifies optimality of the complete nested master.

notation.meaning: outer reduced-cost functional restricted to outer block i
globally optimal inner pricing value for outer block i

review_flags: The claim concerns exact finite-dimensional linear inner and outer formulations; no convergence claim is made for inexact nested column generation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined inner-and-outer oracle condition certifying optimality of an exact nested Dantzig-Wolfe master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an outer restricted-master dual solution, let \(\rho_i(x_i)\) be the reduced cost of an outer-block decision \(x_i\in P_i\), and define \(q_i=\min_{x_i\in P_i}\rho_i(x_i)\). If every \(q_i\) is computed globally through an exact inner Dantzig-Wolfe representation of \(P_i\), then \(q_i\ge0\) for every outer block, together with primal-dual optimality of the outer restricted master, certifies optimality for the complete nested master. If an inner solve supplies neither an exact optimum nor a valid lower bound proving \(q_i\ge0\), failure to find an improving outer column is not an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested column generation is certified only when every inner pricing problem proves that its true outer reduced-cost minimum is nonnegative; merely failing to find an improving inner column is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Nested Pricing-Exhaustion Certificate
Nested Dantzig-Wolfe Reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-level exact representation with outer columns generated by inner Dantzig–Wolfe masters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each outer block \(P_i\) itself have a block-angular description \(P_i=\{x_i=(x_{ik})_k:\sum_kB_{ik}x_{ik}=d_i,\ x_{ik}\in P_{ik}\}\), where \(P_{ik}=\operatorname{conv}(V_{ik})\). The inner Dantzig–Wolfe master represents \(P_i\) using weights on \(V_{ik}\) and the local equations \(\sum_kB_{ik}x_{ik}=d_i\). Its feasible extreme solutions form outer columns \(W_i\). An outer master then represents \(x_i=\sum_{w\in W_i}w\mu_{iw}\), imposes \(\sum_{w\in W_i}\mu_{iw}=1\), and coordinates blocks through \(\sum_i\sum_{w\in W_i}A_iw\mu_{iw}=b\). With complete inner and outer column sets, this hierarchy is equivalent to the original multilevel block-angular problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested reformulation solves inner block-angular representations to generate outer columns, which a higher-level master coordinates through the global linking equations.
assumptions_latex: Every inner set satisfies \(P_{ik}=\operatorname{conv}(V_{ik})\).
Each outer block \(P_i\) is exactly represented by its inner master.
\(W_i\) contains all outer columns required for \(P_i=\operatorname{conv}(W_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complete inner sets \(V_{ik}\) and outer sets \(W_i\) yield an objective-preserving representation of the original multilevel problem.

notation.meaning: Inner columns for subblock k of outer block i
Feasible outer columns generated by block i's inner master
Outer-master weight assigned to column w

review_flags: nested formulation depends on whether outer columns are vertices, extreme solutions, or general generated points

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the nested-reformulation topic, but a source is required to determine whether W_i should consist of projected vertices, images of inner-master extreme points, or a broader generated set. The stated completeness assumption asserts P_i=conv(W_i), yet the preceding construction and multilevel equivalence need authoritative support with a precise locator.

children.title: Strong Block-Convexification Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings in which local convex hull structure materially strengthens the master.

assumptions_latex: \(F_H\) and \(F_R\) are nonempty compact sets.
\(F_H\subseteq F_R\), and both problems use the same linear objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\).

notation.meaning: Feasible region using exact block convex hulls and the common linking constraints.
Feasible region using weaker block relaxations and the same linking constraints.
Optimal values over the exact-hull and weaker regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp objective-specific characterization of strict strengthening by exact block convexification when both minima are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_H\subseteq F_R\) be the nonempty compact feasible regions obtained, respectively, from exact block convex hulls and weaker block relaxations under identical linking constraints. For a linear minimization objective, set \(v_H=\min_{x\in F_H}c^{\mathsf T}x\) and \(v_R=\min_{x\in F_R}c^{\mathsf T}x\). Then \(v_H>v_R\) if and only if no optimizer of the weaker relaxation belongs to \(F_H\). Equivalently, equality holds if and only if the weaker optimal face intersects the exact block-hull region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact block convexification improves an attained bound strictly exactly when every optimizer of the weaker relaxation is excluded by the block-hull formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Block-Convexification Criterion
Strong Block-Convexification Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength comparison between exact block convexification and a conventional block relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For blocks \(k=1,\ldots,K\), let \(X_k\) be the original feasible sets and let \(R_k\supseteq X_k\) be tractable convex relaxations. Under the same linking constraints, denote by \(v_{\mathrm{DW}}\) and \(v_R\) the minimization bounds obtained from \(\prod_k\operatorname{conv}(X_k)\) and \(\prod_k R_k\), respectively. Then \(v_{\mathrm{DW}}\ge v_R\). The strengthening is material whenever the linking constraints and objective expose a point feasible in \(\prod_k R_k\) but excluded by some \(\operatorname{conv}(X_k)\); in that case strict inequality can occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact convexification of each block gives at least the relaxation bound, and can give a strictly stronger bound when linking constraints expose missing block-hull inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(X_k\neq\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{conv}(X_k)\subseteq R_k\) for every \(k\).
Both formulations use identical linear objectives and linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[v_{\mathrm{DW}}\ge v_R,\quad\text{with strict inequality possible if some block-hull exclusion is exposed.}\]

notation.meaning: Original feasible set of block k.
Conventional convex relaxation of block k.
