children.title: Weak or Redundant Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Extended representations that add little useful strength.

assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(R\) are nonempty compact sets with \(S\subseteq R\).
The same linear minimization objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) is used on both sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min_{x\in S}c^{\mathsf T}x=\min_{x\in R}c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S\cap\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in R}c^{\mathsf T}x\neq\varnothing.\]

notation.meaning: Projected feasible region of the stronger extended formulation.
Feasible region of the weaker original relaxation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-specific redundancy despite a potentially strict strengthening of the projected feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq R\) be nonempty compact projected relaxation regions, where \(S\) is supplied by an extended formulation, and minimize the same linear objective over both. The extension is bound-redundant for that objective if and only if the optimal face of \(R\) contains a point of \(S\). Consequently, strict containment \(S\subsetneq R\) does not by itself imply a stronger bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly smaller projected relaxation can have the same bound; equality holds exactly when it contains an optimizer of the weaker relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Specific Bound Redundancy
Weak or Redundant Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary at which a block extended formulation provides no projected relaxation strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block \(k=1,\ldots,K\), let \(Q_k\) be an extended formulation in variables \((x_k,y_k)\), let \(P_k=\operatorname{proj}_{x_k}(Q_k)\), and let \(R_k\) be the block set used by the original relaxation. Let \(Q\) be the coupled extended feasible region obtained from the sets \(Q_k\) and common linking constraints in \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_K)\), and let \(R\) be the corresponding region obtained from the sets \(R_k\). If \(P_k=R_k\) for every block and the objective depends only on \(x\), then \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=R\), so the two relaxations have the same optimal value whenever that value is well-defined. The extension is therefore bound-redundant, although it may alter sparsity, degeneracy, or computational behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every extended block projects exactly onto the block relaxation it replaces, while the linking constraints and objective use only the original variables, then the coupled projected feasible region and relaxation value are unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k=\operatorname{proj}_{x_k}(Q_k)=R_k\) for every \(k=1,\ldots,K\).
The objective and common linking constraints depend only on \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_K)\).
The compared optimal values are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=R\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v_Q=v_R.\]

notation.meaning: Projection of the extended block formulation onto its original variables.
Coupled extended region and corresponding original-variable relaxation region.
Optimal relaxation values of the extended and original formulations.

children.title: Extended-Master Size Explosion
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial growth of block representations motivating dynamic generation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implicit Columns Do Not Imply Tractable Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between avoiding enumeration and solving pricing efficiently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Column generation avoids simultaneous storage of all columns, but exact iterations require optimization of reduced cost over the implicit block set. That problem may itself be computationally hard. Therefore, a compact block description and small restricted master do not imply polynomial total work without a tractable pricing oracle, an oracle-complexity assumption, and control of the number of iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Implicit generation avoids full storage but does not make hard pricing easy or bound the iteration count.
assumptions_latex: Columns are generated through exact pricing.
No tractable pricing-oracle or iteration-bound assumption is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Implicit storage alone gives no polynomial-time guarantee.}

notation.meaning: Implicit local feasible set used by pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Columns Do Not Imply Tractable Pricing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit point-and-ray column count across separately represented blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If block \(i\) is represented by point columns \(V_i\) and ray columns \(R_i\), explicit enumeration introduces \[N_{\mathrm{col}}=\sum_i(|V_i|+|R_i|)\] block-column variables, together with linking rows and required convexity rows. The count is additive across blocks but can be exponential because one compactly described block can have exponentially many generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full separate-block master has the sum of all point and ray counts as column variables, and one block can already make that count exponential.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many separately represented polyhedral blocks.
\(V_i\) and \(R_i\) are the enumerated point and ray generators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{col}}=\sum_i(|V_i|+|R_i|).
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Master Enumeration Size
Extended-Master Size Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit enumeration can be exponential even when the original block description is compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a Dantzig--Wolfe block whose column set contains one column for every extreme point of \(X_n=[0,1]^n\). The block has the compact description \(0\le x_i\le1\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), but \(X_n\) has \(2^n\) extreme points. Hence an explicitly enumerated master requires \(2^n\) column variables for this block, plus its convexity constraint. Column generation avoids storing all columns by maintaining a finite active subset and generating an omitted column through pricing when needed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact n-dimensional block may have exponentially many extreme-point columns, so full master enumeration can require 2^n variables and motivates dynamic column generation.
assumptions_latex: The master uses one variable for each extreme point of \(X_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[|\operatorname{ext}(X_n)|=2^n,\qquad\text{so explicit master size is exponential in }n.\]

notation.meaning: Set of extreme points of the block polytope.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hypercube example correctly demonstrates exponential explicit-column growth and fits the failure-boundary leaf, but it has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Reformulation-Induced Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Redundant block representations and broad master faces that impair progress.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear certificate for a continuum of equivalent extended-master representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\lambda=b\), \(\lambda\ge0\), objective \(c^{\mathsf T}\lambda\), and original-space projection \(x=P\lambda\), let \(d\ne0\) satisfy \[Ad=0,\qquad Pd=0,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}d=0.\] Every \(\lambda+\tau d\ge0\) is feasible, has the same objective, and projects to the same \(x\). A nontrivial admissible interval at an optimum certifies a nontrivial segment of equivalent optimal representations. Duplicate-column splitting is the two-coordinate special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direction annihilated by constraints, projection, and objective certifies equivalent master representations whenever nonnegativity permits movement along it.
assumptions_latex: The extended master and projection are linear.
\(d\ne0\) satisfies the three homogeneous conditions.
The admissible values of \(\tau\) preserve nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A(\lambda+\tau d)=b,\quad P(\lambda+\tau d)=P\lambda,\quad c^{\mathsf T}(\lambda+\tau d)=c^{\mathsf T}\lambda.
knowledge_statements.title: Nullspace Certificate for Representation Redundancy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted-Master Row Redundancy and Dual Nonuniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual nonuniqueness from row redundancy and its boundary for omitted-column pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a restricted master with column matrix \(A_R\), suppose \(q\ne0\) satisfies \(A_R^{\mathsf T}q=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}q=0\). If \(y\) is restricted-dual feasible, then \(y+\tau q\) is restricted-dual feasible with the same value for every \(\tau\). For an omitted column \(a\), however, its reduced cost changes by \(-\tau q^{\mathsf T}a\). Thus restricted-master row redundancy can make omitted-column pricing depend on the chosen dual representative unless \(q^{\mathsf T}a=0\) for every admissible full-master column. If that latter condition holds, dual multipliers remain nonunique but all full reduced costs are invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A redundant restricted-master row direction creates nonunique duals; omitted-column reduced costs vary only when that direction is not redundant for the full column family.
assumptions_latex: The restricted primal is \(A_R\lambda=b\), \(\lambda\ge0\).
\(q\ne0\) satisfies \(A_R^{\mathsf T}q=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}q=0\).
A restricted-dual feasible multiplier exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y+\tau q\text{ has equal restricted-dual value, and }\bar c_a(y+\tau q)=\bar c_a(y)-\tau q^{\mathsf T}a.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Row Redundancy and Dual Nonuniqueness
Reformulation-Induced Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicate columns create nonunique master representations and can contribute to degeneracy or stalling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose two columns in the same convexity family have identical linking vectors, costs, and projected block vectors: \(a_1=a_2\), \(c_1=c_2\), and \(p_1=p_2\). If a feasible master point satisfies \(\lambda_1+[0m\lambda_2=t>0\), then for every \(\theta\in[0,1]\), replacing \((\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\) by \((\theta t,(1-\theta)t)\) preserves all master constraints, the objective value, and the projected block solution. At an optimal point, these representations form a nontrivial segment contained in the optimal set. This representation redundancy can contribute to degeneracy and equivalent pivots, but the segment alone does not prove simplex primal degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fully duplicate columns allow the same total weight to be split continuously without changing constraints, cost, or the projected solution. This creates nonunique optimal representations and may contribute to degeneracy, though it does not alone prove simplex primal degeneracy.
assumptions_latex: Both columns belong to the same convexity family.
A feasible master solution satisfies \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2=t>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bigl\{(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)=(\theta t,(1-\theta)t):\theta\in[0,1]\bigr\}\] preserves feasibility, objective value, and the projected solution; when the original point is optimal, this segment is contained in the optimal set.

notation.meaning: Linking vector, cost, and projected block vector of column j.
Master weight assigned to column j.
Combined weight of the duplicate columns.

children.title: Column Generation Workflow
children.top_down_role: Continuous master-pricing workflow and its improvement, termination, stabilization, and failure interfaces.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: A Primer in Column Generation; Implementing Mixed Integer Column Generation

children.title: Restricted-Master Pricing System
children.top_down_role: The paired finite master, dual-price interface, and implicit column oracle.

children.title: Restricted Master Problem
children.top_down_role: The active finite restriction of an implicit full master.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal feasibility boundary between a feasible full master and an arbitrary active-column restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the full master satisfy \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1\), \(0\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1\), and \(\lambda\ge0\). It is feasible at \((0,1)\). For the nonempty active set \(J^R=\{1\}\), the restricted master requires both \(\lambda_1=1\) and \(0\lambda_1=1\), hence is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full master may be feasible while a nonempty active-column restriction is infeasible because omitted columns are needed to satisfy the linking equations.
assumptions_latex: The full family contains columns with linking coefficients \(a_1=0\) and \(a_2=1\).
The linking right-hand side is one and the column weights satisfy one convexity equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{MP}\text{ feasible}\not\Longrightarrow\operatorname{RMP}(J^R)\text{ feasible}.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Feasibility Can Fail

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual LP and strong duality for the finite equality-form restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dual of the restricted master is \[\max_{\pi,\sigma}\ b^{\mathsf T}\pi+\sum_{k=1}^K\sigma_k\quad\text{subject to}\quad a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi+\sigma_k\le c_{kj}\quad(k=1,\ldots,K,\ j\in J_k^R),\] where \(\pi\) and each \(\sigma_k\) are unrestricted because their primal rows are equalities. If the restricted primal is feasible and has a finite optimum, finite-dimensional LP strong duality gives equal attained primal and dual values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The restricted-master dual has one inequality per active column; feasibility and a finite optimum give equal attained primal and dual optima.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master has the equality-form primal stated in the immutable seed.
The restricted master is feasible and has finite objective coefficients and a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_R=b^{\mathsf T}\pi^*+\sum_k\sigma_k^*=\sum_{k,j\in J_k^R}c_{kj}\lambda_{kj}^*.

notation.meaning: Dual multiplier for the linking equality
Dual multiplier for family k's convexity equality

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Dual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective ordering induced by nested finite active-column restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization full master, fixing omitted nonnegative column variables to zero restricts its feasible region. Hence every feasible restricted-master solution is full-master feasible and \(v_{\mathrm{MP}}\le v_R\). If \(J_k^R\subseteq J_k^{R'}\) for every \(k\), enlarging the active sets relaxes the restriction and \(v_{R'}\le v_R\). Therefore \(v_{\mathrm{MP}}\le v_{R'}\le v_R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible restricted master gives an upper bound on the minimization full master, and adding columns can only lower or preserve its optimum.
assumptions_latex: The full master is a minimization problem.
The active sets satisfy \(J_k^R\subseteq J_k^{R'}\subseteq J_k\) for every family.
The compared restricted masters are feasible and have finite optima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_{\mathrm{MP}}\le v_{R'}\le v_R.

notation.meaning: Optimum over enlarged active sets J^{R'}

knowledge_statements.title: Restriction Bound and Monotonicity
Restricted Master Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite active-column restriction of a block-angular full master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J_k\) be the full column index set for family \(k\), and choose finite nonempty active sets \(J_k^R\subseteq J_k\). The restricted master problem is
\[\min_{\lambda}\ \sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{j\in J_k^R}c_{kj}\lambda_{kj}\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{j\in J_k^R}a_{kj}\lambda_{kj}=b,\quad \sum_{j\in J_k^R}\lambda_{kj}=1\ \ (k=1,\ldots,K),\quad \lambda_{kj}\ge0.\]
Its variables are only the currently generated columns; feasibility requires the selected columns to satisfy the linking and convexity equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The restricted master is the full block-angular master limited to finite active column subsets, with the original linking and per-family convexity constraints retained.
assumptions_latex: \(J_k^R\subseteq J_k\) is finite and nonempty for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{RMP}=\operatorname{MP}\big|_{\lambda_{kj}=0\text{ for }j\notin J_k^R}.\]

notation.meaning: Linking vector and objective coefficient of a column.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally consistent and appropriately specializes a block-angular restricted master, but no source locator is supplied.

children.title: Dual-Price Interface
children.top_down_role: Transfer of restricted-master dual information into pricing objectives.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on interpreting transferred multipliers as reduced-cost and dual-feasibility information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pricing value is a dual slack only when row orientation, multiplier sign, and scaling agree with the restricted-master dual. For example, with \(c_j=0\), \(a_j=1\), and the true multiplier \(\pi=1\), the true reduced cost is \(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j\pi=-1\). Transferring \(-\pi\) while retaining the same formula gives \(\widehat{\bar c}_j=1\), falsely reporting the improving column as nonimproving. Arbitrary stale or dual-infeasible prices may define search objectives but do not certify full-master dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced costs certify dual inequalities only when pricing uses the restricted master's row orientation, multiplier sign, and scaling; mismatched or uncertified prices can invalidate or reverse the test.
assumptions_latex: The master is a minimization LP with nonnegative column variables.
Pricing is intended to evaluate slacks of the restricted-master dual convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat{\bar c}_j\text{ is a valid dual slack only when the transferred multipliers use the master convention}.

notation.meaning: True reduced cost under the master convention
Reduced cost computed by the pricing implementation

knowledge_statements.title: Price-Convention Consistency
Dual-Price Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost transformation from restricted-master dual multipliers to pricing objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the restricted master, let \(\pi\) be the unrestricted multiplier of the linking equation and \(\sigma_k\) the unrestricted multiplier of family \(k\)'s convexity equation. A candidate column \(j\in J_k\) has reduced cost
\[\bar c_{kj}=c_{kj}-a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma_k.\]
Thus pricing family \(k\) computes \(z_k(\pi)=\inf_{j\in J_k}\{c_{kj}-a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma_k\}\). A negative value identifies a violated full-master dual inequality; a nonnegative value means every column in that family satisfies its dual inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted-master dual multipliers enter each pricing objective through reduced cost; negative family minimum violates a full-master dual constraint, while a nonnegative minimum validates that family.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is feasible and has a finite optimum.
The linking and convexity equations use the sign convention displayed in the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[z_k(\pi)<0\iff \exists j\in J_k:\ a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi+\sigma_k>c_{kj}.\]

notation.meaning: Dual multiplier for the linking equation.
Dual multiplier for family k's convexity equation.
Reduced cost of a candidate column.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost interface and dual-inequality interpretation are correct under the displayed sign convention, but they lack inspectable source support.

children.title: Pricing Subproblem Family
children.top_down_role: Optimization interfaces that search the implicit master-variable space.

children.title: Single-Family Pricing
children.top_down_role: One oracle representing a common master column family.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-column insertion within one common pricing family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Instead of adding only a minimum-reduced-cost column, a single-family iteration may return a finite batch \(B_t\subseteq J\) with \(\bar c_j<-\tau\) for every \(j\in B_t\), add all columns in \(B_t\), and reoptimize once. The batch need not contain every negative-reduced-cost column for the augmentation to be valid. Failure of a nonexhaustive batch generator to return a column is not a stopping certificate; stopping still requires a certified global family minimum of at least \(-\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-family oracle may add several certified improving columns before reoptimization, but only a certified global family minimum can justify stopping.
assumptions_latex: Every inserted object is a valid member of the common family \(J\).
Every inserted column has reduced cost below the chosen negative threshold at the current dual solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B_t\ne\varnothing\Longrightarrow\text{all columns in }B_t\text{ may be added before reoptimization}.

notation.meaning: Batch of improving columns returned at iteration t

knowledge_statements.title: Batch Single-Family Pricing
Single-Family Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pricing iteration when all omitted columns belong to one common family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an optimal restricted-master dual pair \((\pi,\sigma)\), solve the single-family oracle
\[j^*\in\arg\min_{j\in J}\{c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma\}.\]
If its value is below a prescribed negative tolerance \(-\tau\), add column \(j^*\) to the active set and reoptimize the restricted master. Otherwise stop and report that no column has reduced cost below \(-\tau\). For exact pricing with \(\tau=0\), stopping supplies the full-family dual-feasibility test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One oracle minimizes reduced cost over the common column family; add a sufficiently negative column and reoptimize, or stop when the family minimum meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The pricing oracle globally minimizes reduced cost over \(J\).
The restricted master supplies optimal dual multipliers \((\pi,\sigma)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bar c_{j^*}<-\tau\Rightarrow j^*\text{ is added};\qquad \bar c_{j^*}\ge-\tau\Rightarrow\text{stop}.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches single-family pricing and correctly distinguishes tolerance stopping from exact pricing, but no source locator is provided.

children.title: Multiple-Block Pricing
children.top_down_role: Separate pricing oracles for heterogeneous column families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selective family scheduling with an exhaustive all-family termination test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), a multi-block scheme may price only \(I_t\subseteq\mathcal K\), add certified negative-reduced-cost columns returned there, and reoptimize. Such a partial sweep cannot certify termination. Before stopping, every required family must be priced at the same current restricted-master dual solution and satisfy \(\min_{j\in J_k}\bar c_{kj}\ge-\tau_k\). Passing the tests only for \(I_t\) is insufficient whenever an unpriced family contains a column of reduced cost below its threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blocks may be priced selectively during progress iterations, but termination requires an exhaustive all-family test at one current restricted-master dual solution.
assumptions_latex: Every required family is included in the sweep used to declare termination.
Each terminating family test globally minimizes reduced cost or supplies an equivalent certified lower bound over its complete family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{termination requires }\min_{j\in J_k}\bar c_{kj}\ge-\tau_k\quad\forall k\in\mathcal K.
knowledge_statements.title: Selective and Exhaustive Multi-Block Pricing
Multiple-Block Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent reduced-cost minimization for heterogeneous block families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given restricted-master dual multipliers \((\pi,\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_K)\), solve for every required family
\[j_k^*\in\arg\min_{j\in J_k}\{c_{kj}-a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma_k\},\qquad k=1,\ldots,K.\]
Add one or more returned columns whose reduced costs are below \(-\tau_k\), then reoptimize the restricted master. Stop only when every family satisfies \(\bar c_{k j_k^*}\ge-\tau_k\). Exact global pricing and \(\tau_k=0\) yield a full-master dual-feasibility test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each heterogeneous family solves its own reduced-cost problem; columns may be added in parallel, and stopping requires every family to pass its pricing test.
assumptions_latex: Each oracle globally minimizes reduced cost over its full family \(J_k\).
All column families required by the full master are priced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min_{j\in J_k}\bar c_{kj}\ge-\tau_k\quad\text{for every }k\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{all tolerance-adjusted family tests pass}.\]

notation.meaning: Full column set of family k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiple-family pricing algorithm and exhaustive stopping condition fit the leaf, but the record lacks an inspectable citation.

children.title: Structured Combinatorial Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing delegated to network, dynamic-programming, or other specialized optimization engines.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity transfer from a native combinatorial optimization problem to exact pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact structured pricing computes \(\min_{y\in Y_k}w_\pi(y)\), where \(w_\pi(y)=c_k(y)-a_k(y)^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma_k\). If this modified native problem is solvable in time \(T_k(n)\), pricing is solvable in \(T_k(n)\) plus the cost of forming modified weights and mapping an optimizer to a column. Conversely, the column-generation wrapper does not remove the hardness of globally optimizing \(w_\pi\); when that represented native optimization problem is NP-hard, exact pricing is NP-hard absent additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structured pricing inherits the tractability or hardness of globally optimizing its dual-modified native objective.
assumptions_latex: The object-to-column mapping represents the complete family.
Modified weights and the returned object-to-column mapping have explicitly accounted computational overhead.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{time}(\text{pricing})=T_k(n)+\operatorname{overhead}(\text{modified weights and column mapping}).

notation.meaning: Running time for globally optimizing the modified native problem

knowledge_statements.title: Inherited Pricing Complexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Heuristic Pricing Is Not an Exhaustion Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between heuristic column discovery and exact pricing certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a heuristic returns \(\widehat y\in Y_k\) with \(w_\pi(\widehat y)<0\), then \(\widehat y\) yields a valid improving master column. If it returns no such object, full-family dual feasibility does not follow unless it also certifies \(\min_{y\in Y_k}w_\pi(y)\ge0\). An unsearched object may still have negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heuristic can validly discover an improving column, but failure to find one cannot certify pricing exhaustion without a global bound.
assumptions_latex: The heuristic searches only part of \(Y_k\) or lacks a valid global lower bound on the pricing optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w_\pi(\widehat y)<0\Longrightarrow\text{valid improving column},\qquad w_\pi(\widehat y)\ge0\not\Longrightarrow\min_{y\in Y_k}w_\pi(y)\ge0.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Pricing Is Not an Exhaustion Certificate
Structured Combinatorial Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of pricing to an exact specialized combinatorial optimization oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose family \(k\)'s columns are indexed by feasible combinatorial objects \(y\in Y_k\), with column cost \(c_k(y)\) and linking vector \(a_k(y)\). At dual prices \((\pi,\sigma_k)\), pricing is exactly
\[\min_{y\in Y_k}\bigl\{c_k(y)-a_k(y)^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma_k\bigr\}.\]
If this objective decomposes as an additive path, state-transition, matching, or analogous structured cost, any exact specialized solver for that combinatorial problem is a valid pricing oracle. Its optimizer maps back to the corresponding master column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When columns encode combinatorial objects, reduced-cost minimization can be solved by an exact network, dynamic-programming, matching, or other structure-specific engine.
assumptions_latex: The mapping \(y\mapsto(a_k(y),c_k(y))\) represents every column in family \(k\).
The specialized solver returns a global minimizer over \(Y_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[y^*\in\arg\min_{y\in Y_k}\{c_k(y)-a_k(y)^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma_k\}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y^*\text{ yields a minimum-reduced-cost column}.\]

notation.meaning: Feasible combinatorial objects indexing family k.
Linking vector generated by object y.
Master cost generated by object y.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly reduces column pricing to exact optimization over combinatorial objects, but no source locator supports the claim.

children.title: Reduced-Cost Certificate Family
children.top_down_role: Improvement and termination certificates connecting pricing outcomes to full-master optimality.

children.title: Negative Reduced-Cost Column Certificate
children.top_down_role: Certification that the current restricted master omits an improving column.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative Reduced-Cost Column Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate of a violated full-master dual inequality and, with a positive pivot step, strict improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\pi,\sigma_k)\) be optimal restricted-master dual multipliers. An omitted column \(j\in J_k\setminus J_k^R\) with
\[\bar c_{kj}=c_{kj}-a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma_k<0\]
certifies that the restricted dual solution violates the full-master inequality \(a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi+\sigma_k\le c_{kj}\). Therefore the current restricted-master dual solution cannot certify full-master optimality. If inserting the column admits a feasible simplex step of positive length, that step strictly decreases the minimization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-reduced-cost omitted column visibly violates a full-master dual constraint; if it supports a positive feasible pivot, it also gives strict primal improvement.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master and full master are linear minimization problems with the displayed reduced-cost convention.
The candidate column is absent from the active set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bar c_{kj}<0\Rightarrow a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi+\sigma_k>c_{kj},\] with strict primal improvement when a positive feasible entering step exists.

notation.meaning: Reduced cost of the omitted column.
Current active set for family k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The negative reduced-cost condition correctly certifies violation of a full-master dual inequality, with strict improvement properly conditioned on a positive feasible step. An inspectable source is missing.

children.title: No-Improving-Column Certificate
children.top_down_role: Full-master certification after every required pricing family has been resolved.

assumptions_latex: A restricted-master primal-dual pair satisfies the exact no-negative-reduced-cost certificate over every full column family.
At least one omitted column has zero reduced cost at the certifying dual solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global optimality remains certified, but uniqueness and irrelevance of every omitted column do not follow.

notation.meaning: Reduced cost of an omitted column.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretive boundary of the exact no-negative-reduced-cost certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The condition \(\bar c_{kj}\ge0\) for every omitted column certifies optimality but does not imply strict positivity. If an omitted column has \(\bar c_{kj}=0\), adding it cannot lower the objective below the certified optimum, but it may participate in an alternative optimal master solution or yield a different optimal primal decomposition. Thus no-improving-column means no strictly negative reduced cost; it does not mean that the optimum is unique or that every omitted column is irrelevant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No negative reduced costs certify optimality, but omitted zero-reduced-cost columns may participate in alternative optimal solutions. The certificate does not imply uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Reduced-Cost Boundary
No-Improving-Column Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact full-master optimality certificate obtained after exhaustive family pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a feasible restricted-master solution and its dual multipliers \((\pi,\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_K)\) be primal-dual optimal for the restricted master. If exact pricing over every full family establishes
\[\min_{j\in J_k}\{c_{kj}-a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma_k\}\ge0\qquad(k=1,\ldots,K),\]
then all full-master dual inequalities hold. The restricted primal solution is also feasible for the full master, and its value equals the feasible full-dual value; hence it is globally optimal for the full linear master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If exact pricing finds no negative reduced cost in any required family, restricted primal and dual solutions certify optimality for the full linear master.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master has a primal-dual optimal pair.
Pricing is exact and covers every column family of the full master.
The full master is the linear block-angular formulation represented by those families.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min_{j\in J_k}\bar c_{kj}\ge0\ \forall k\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v_{\mathrm{RMP}}=v_{\mathrm{MP}}.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact all-family pricing test correctly yields full-master dual feasibility and optimality, but no authoritative source locator is supplied.

children.title: Inexact-Pricing Bound Certificates
children.top_down_role: Qualified bounds and stopping information obtained from bounded pricing error.

assumptions_latex: A feasible pricing column \(\hat p_k\) has reduced cost \(r_k=\bar c_{k\hat p_k}\).
The pricing solver certifies \(r_k-v_k\le\varepsilon_k\), where \(v_k=\inf_{p\in P_k}\bar c_{kp}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle-gap certificate implies \(v_k\ge r_k-\varepsilon_k\), furnishing the global lower bound required for an inexact-pricing dual correction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a pricing-solver optimality-gap certificate into a master-valid pricing lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Feasibility gives \(v_k\le r_k\), while the certified additive gap gives \[r_k-\varepsilon_k\le v_k\le r_k.\] Therefore \(r_k-\varepsilon_k\) is a valid global lower bound for family \(k\) and can be used in the family dual-price correction. The returned value \(r_k\) alone, without a certified bound on \(r_k-v_k\), gives no lower bound on unsearched columns and cannot support termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified additive pricing-solver gap converts a returned feasible reduced cost into a global lower bound. A returned value without such a gap cannot certify termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Gap Conversion Certificate

assumptions_latex: Family \(k\) has the normalization equation \(\sum_{j\in J_k}\lambda_{kj}=d_k\) with \(d_k\ge0\).
The restricted-master dual prices satisfy \(\min_{j\in J_k}\bar c_{kj}\ge-\varepsilon_k\) for every family.
The restricted primal-dual pair is optimal and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Shifting \(\sigma_k\) to \(\sigma_k-\varepsilon_k\) yields a full-dual lower-bound loss of \(d_k\varepsilon_k\) for family k.

notation.meaning: Right-hand side of family k's normalization equation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonunit-normalization variant of the additive pricing-error certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The corrected prices \((\pi,\sigma_k-\varepsilon_k)\) satisfy every full-master column inequality. If the restricted-master value is \(U=b^{\mathsf T}\pi+\sum_k d_k\sigma_k\), then \[L=U-\sum_k d_k\varepsilon_k\] is a valid full-master lower bound, and \(U-L=\sum_k d_k\varepsilon_k\) bounds the loss attributable to the certified pricing errors. The unweighted sum is the special case \(d_k=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a nonunit family-normalization right-hand side, each additive pricing error is weighted by that right-hand side in the full-master lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Family-Error Dual Correction
Inexact-Pricing Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid full-master lower bound from certified additive errors in family pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a minimization master, let \((\pi,\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_K)\) be an optimal restricted-master dual solution. Suppose each pricing procedure certifies
\[\min_{j\in J_k}\{c_{kj}-a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma_k\}\ge-\varepsilon_k,\qquad \varepsilon_k\ge0.\]
Then \((\pi,\sigma_k-\varepsilon_k)\) is feasible for the full dual. Consequently
\[L=b^{\mathsf T}\pi+\sum_{k=1}^K(\sigma_k-\varepsilon_k)\]
is a valid full-master lower bound. If the restricted primal value is \(U\), then \(U-L\) is a certified optimality-gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified additive pricing errors can shift convexity dual prices into full-dual feasibility, yielding a valid lower bound and a computable primal-dual gap.
assumptions_latex: Each oracle supplies a valid global lower bound \(-\varepsilon_k\) on its family's minimum reduced cost.
The restricted primal-dual pair is optimal and has finite value \(U\).
Every full-master family is covered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[L\le v_{\mathrm{MP}}\le U,\qquad 0\le U-v_{\mathrm{MP}}\le U-L.\]

notation.meaning: Certified additive pricing error for family k.
Restricted-master primal value and full-master upper bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The familywise dual-price shifts and resulting lower bound are mathematically consistent, but this nontrivial inexact-pricing certificate requires an inspectable source.

children.title: Numerical Pricing-Certificate Boundary
children.top_down_role: Reliability boundaries arising from approximate prices and finite-precision reduced costs.

children.title: Pricing Tolerance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Acceptance regimes for approximate pricing outcomes near the improvement threshold.

assumptions_latex: The restricted master is a minimization problem with dual multipliers \(\pi\) for linking constraints and \(\sigma_j\) for block-\(j\) convexity.
Each column \(p\in P_j\) has cost \(c_{jp}\), linking vector \(a_{jp}\), and reduced cost \(\bar c_{jp}=c_{jp}-\pi^\top a_{jp}-\sigma_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reported nonimprovement result certifies only the tolerance level justified by the pricing oracle and its error bound.

notation.meaning: Exact minimum reduced cost over block j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive-error pricing regimes follow directly from reduced-cost lower bounds
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-error regimes for minimization-form column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the pricing routine returns \(\hat p_j\in P_j\) and a certified lower bound \(L_j\) satisfying \(L_j\le v_j\le \bar c_{j\hat p_j}\) and \(\bar c_{j\hat p_j}-L_j\le\varepsilon_j\). The regime is exact when \(\varepsilon_j=0\), certified \(\tau\)-pricing when \(\varepsilon_j\le\tau\), and heuristic when no valid \(L_j\) is available. A column is definitively improving when \(\bar c_{j\hat p_j}<0\). Block \(j\) is certified nonimproving to tolerance \(\tau\) when \(L_j\ge-\tau\); global \(\tau\)-termination requires this inequality for every block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing is exact at zero oracle error, tolerance-certified with a valid lower bound, and merely heuristic without one; termination requires every block lower bound to exceed the negative tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Tolerance Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically coherent and fits the tolerance-regime leaf, but no inspectable source supports the stated classification and global termination criterion.

children.title: Numerical Reduced-Cost Certification
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision reliability of reduced-cost signs and termination evidence.

assumptions_latex: The true reduced cost is \(\bar c=c-\pi^{\mathsf T}a-\sigma\), while \(\widehat{\bar c}=\hat c-\hat\pi^{\mathsf T}\hat a-\hat\sigma\).
Verified bounds satisfy \(|c-\hat c|\le\eta_c\), \(\|a-\hat a\|_*\le\eta_a\), \(\|\pi-\hat\pi\|\le\eta_\pi\), and \(|\sigma-\hat\sigma|\le\eta_\sigma\).
The computed dot product and final arithmetic have certified absolute error at most \(\eta_{\mathrm{fl}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid reduced-cost error radius is \(\eta_c+\|\hat\pi\|\eta_a+\|\hat a\|_*\eta_\pi+\eta_a\eta_\pi+\eta_\sigma+\eta_{\mathrm{fl}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of a rigorous reduced-cost interval from primitive data and arithmetic error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\delta=\eta_c+\|\hat\pi\|\eta_a+\|\hat a\|_*\eta_\pi+\eta_a\eta_\pi+\eta_\sigma+\eta_{\mathrm{fl}}.\] Then \(|\bar c-\widehat{\bar c}|\le\delta\), so \([\widehat{\bar c}-\delta,\widehat{\bar c}+\delta]\) encloses the true reduced cost. The cross term \(\eta_a\eta_\pi\) is required when both the column and multiplier are uncertain. An interval omitting any uncertified cost, column, multiplier, family-price, or arithmetic error is not a valid sign certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rigorous reduced-cost interval can be assembled from bounds on cost, column, multiplier, family-price, and arithmetic errors. Simultaneous column and multiplier uncertainty requires a cross term.
knowledge_statements.title: Compositional Reduced-Cost Error Radius

assumptions_latex: Reduced costs are evaluated for a minimization-form restricted master at computed dual multipliers \((\hat\pi,\hat\sigma_j)\).
Certified bounds \(e_{jp}\) and \(d_{jp}\) cover, respectively, column-data evaluation error and dual-arithmetic error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interval \([\widehat{\bar c}_{jp}-e_{jp}-d_{jp},\widehat{\bar c}_{jp}+e_{jp}+d_{jp}]\) is a verifiable enclosure of the true reduced cost.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: interval arithmetic converts bounded evaluation error into a sign certificate
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval certificate for a computed reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the exact reduced cost be \(\bar c_{jp}=c_{jp}-\pi^\top a_{jp}-\sigma_j\), and suppose verified error analysis gives \(|\bar c_{jp}-\widehat{\bar c}_{jp}|\le\delta_{jp}\). Then \(\widehat{\bar c}_{jp}+\delta_{jp}<0\) certifies that column \(p\) is improving, while \(\widehat{\bar c}_{jp}-\delta_{jp}\ge-\tau\) certifies that this column is not more than \(\tau\)-improving. If the interval intersects \((-\infty,-\tau)\) and \([-\tau,\infty)\), its sign relative to the tolerance is numerically unresolved and cannot certify either conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computed reduced cost is certified by an error interval: a wholly negative interval proves improvement, while an interval above the tolerance threshold proves nonimprovement.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Reduced-Cost Certification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interval certificate and its tolerance tests are internally consistent, and certificate is the correct content kind, but the record has no cited source.

children.title: Tolerance-Certification Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases where oracle tolerance or numerical error weakens pricing conclusions.

assumptions_latex: For each pricing block \(j\), a certified lower bound \(L_j\le v_j\) and an incumbent reduced cost \(U_j\ge v_j\) are available.
Termination tolerance satisfies \(\tau\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sharp certification boundary is \(L_j=-\tau\): values below it leave possible improving columns unresolved.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the boundary follows from an enclosing interval for the exact pricing optimum
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp interval boundary between tolerance certification and unresolved pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Block \(j\) is certified \(\tau\)-nonimproving exactly when its available information entails \(v_j\ge-\tau\); the sufficient interval test is \(L_j\ge-\tau\). If \(L_j<-\tau\le U_j\), both \(v_j<-\tau\) and \(v_j\ge-\tau\) are consistent with the certificate, so neither termination nor existence of a \(\tau\)-improving column follows. In particular, using only \(U_j\ge-\tau\) as a stopping test is invalid: an attained or approximate incumbent can be nonimproving while an unexamined column has reduced cost below \(-\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Termination is certified only when the pricing lower bound reaches the negative tolerance; a straddling interval leaves both improvement and nonimprovement possible.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Certification Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The straddling-interval failure boundary is precise and matches the leaf, but its sharpness and stopping-test claims lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Pricing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Oracle regimes balancing certification, column diversity, and computational effort.

children.title: Exact Pricing
children.top_down_role: Globally resolved pricing used for definitive improvement or termination certification.

assumptions_latex: The pricing set \(P_j\) is nonempty.
The reduced-cost infimum \(v_j=\inf_{p\in P_j}\bar c_{jp}\) is finite but need not be attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact knowledge of \(v_j\) can certify nonimprovement, but an oracle cannot return an exact minimizing column unless the infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment requirement for an exact-pricing oracle that must return a minimizing column.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(v_j\) is not attained, no \(p_j^\star\in P_j\) satisfies \(\bar c_{jp_j^\star}=v_j\), so an exact pricing oracle defined to return a global minimizer does not exist. A separately certified bound \(v_j\ge-\tau\) can nevertheless certify block nonimprovement. Conversely, \(v_j< -\tau\) guarantees the existence of at least one feasible column with reduced cost below \(-\tau\), although a search procedure must still produce it. For example, with \(P_j=(0,1]\) and \(\bar c_{jp}=p\), the exact value is \(v_j=0\), but no minimizing column exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact pricing requires attainment when the oracle must return a minimizer. A certified infimum can still prove nonimprovement even when no minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Value and Attainment Boundary

assumptions_latex: For block \(j\), the column set \(P_j\) is nonempty and the reduced-cost infimum is attained.
The current restricted-master dual multipliers are \((\pi,\sigma_j)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact pricing returns a global minimizer and therefore gives a definitive improvement or block-termination decision.

notation.meaning: Reduced cost of column p in block j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact pricing is global minimization of reduced cost in classical column generation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global block pricing for minimization-form column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact pricing oracle for block \(j\) returns \(p_j^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in P_j}\bar c_{jp}\) together with the value \(v_j=\bar c_{jp_j^\star}\). For tolerance \(\tau\ge0\), if \(v_j<-\tau\), the returned column is \(\tau\)-improving and may enter the restricted master. If \(v_j\ge-\tau\), no column in \(P_j\) has reduced cost below \(-\tau\). Exact pricing over every block therefore supplies the reduced-cost component of a definitive \(\tau\)-termination certificate for the current master dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact pricing globally minimizes reduced cost in a block, yielding either an improving column or a conclusive block nonimprovement certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly characterizes exact pricing under attainment and matches the stated node role, but no authoritative source with a locator is supplied.

children.title: Approximate Pricing Search Family
children.top_down_role: Restricted or approximate searches for inexpensive improving columns.

children.title: Heuristic Pricing
children.top_down_role: Approximate searches designed to find inexpensive improving columns.

assumptions_latex: A searchable column set \(P_j\), current dual multipliers, and a finite search budget \(B_j\) are given.
Every candidate returned by the search is feasible for the original block column set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Heuristic pricing may establish improvement through a found column but cannot establish global nonimprovement from search failure alone.

notation.meaning: Set of columns examined within the budget.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: heuristic pricing searches a feasible subset without a global optimality bound
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted feasible search without a global pricing bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(S_j(B_j)=\varnothing\), apply any budget-limited search rule to generate feasible columns in \(P_j\), evaluate their reduced costs, and retain \(\hat p_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in S_j(B_j)}\bar c_{jp}\) when the examined set is nonempty. Stop when \(\bar c_{j\hat p_j}< -\tau\), the budget is exhausted, or the search rule terminates. Output \(\hat p_j\) as an improving column only if its reduced cost is below \(-\tau\); otherwise output “not found,” which is not a certificate that \(\min_{p\in P_j}\bar c_{jp}\ge-\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heuristic pricing searches feasible columns within a budget. Finding a sufficiently negative reduced cost proves improvement, but finding none does not justify termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm appropriately distinguishes discovery of an improving column from certification of global nonimprovement, but it is unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Partial Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing restricted to selected blocks, column classes, or oracle regions.

assumptions_latex: The full pricing set is partitioned or covered by searchable subsets \(P_{j,1},\ldots,P_{j,m}\).
A selection rule chooses a nonempty subset of indices \(I_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) at pricing iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Partial pricing certifies only the searched subsets unless every omitted subset has a valid lower-bound certificate.

notation.meaning: Pricing subsets searched at iteration k.
Best reduced cost in subset i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: partial pricing restricts each search to selected column classes
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pricing selected column classes rather than the entire block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), select \(I_k\), solve or search each subproblem \(\inf_{p\in P_{j,i}}\bar c_{jp}\) for \(i\in I_k\), and add any returned columns whose reduced costs are below \(-\tau\). If none is found, update the selection rule and continue or invoke a global certification step. Termination for block \(j\) is valid only if the searched subsets cover \(P_j\) with certified lower bounds at least \(-\tau\), or if every omitted subset independently has such a bound. Exhausting only \(I_k\) does not certify the full pricing problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial pricing searches selected column classes. Failure on those classes cannot certify full nonimprovement unless all omitted classes also have valid lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial Pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The partial-pricing procedure and its certification limitation fit the terminal container, but no source supports the selected-subset workflow or termination condition.

children.title: Exact-Certification Handoff
children.top_down_role: The boundary at which restricted searches must yield to certification-capable pricing.

assumptions_latex: Heuristic or partial pricing has stopped without producing a new column below tolerance \(-\tau\).
An exact oracle or a certified global lower-bounding oracle is available for every pricing block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A definitive stopping decision is delegated to the certification oracle, not inferred from approximate-search failure.

notation.meaning: Certified global lower bound for block j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: approximate discovery and exact termination certification have distinct logical roles
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition from inexpensive discovery to globally valid pricing certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After approximate search fails to find a column with reduced cost below \(-\tau\), run the certification oracle at the current master dual multipliers. If it returns a column \(p\) with \(\bar c_{jp}< -\tau\), resume restricted-master optimization with that column. If it returns a valid bound \(L_j\ge-\tau\), mark block \(j\) certified. Terminate column generation only after all blocks are certified at the same accepted dual solution. Approximate-search history may warm-start certification but cannot replace its global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When approximate search stalls, exact or lower-bounding pricing either supplies a missed improving column or certifies the block before termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Certification Handoff

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The handoff principle is logically consistent and correctly separates approximate discovery from global certification, but it has no source.

children.title: Multiple-Column Pricing
children.top_down_role: Generation of several diverse improving columns during one pricing phase.

assumptions_latex: Reduced costs are fixed throughout the pricing phase.
Distinct feasible columns can be enumerated in nondecreasing reduced-cost order.
The batch limit is \(q\in\mathbb N\), and the acceptance tolerance is \(\tau\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The batch contains the first \(q\) improving columns, or all improving columns when fewer exist; only a certified bound on unseen columns proves exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact order-statistic variant of multiple-column pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Enumerate distinct feasible columns so that \(\bar c_{p_{(1)}}\le\bar c_{p_{(2)}}\le\cdots\), and return \[Q_q=\{p_{(i)}:1\le i\le q,\ \bar c_{p_{(i)}}< -\tau\}.\] Stop enumeration when \(|Q_q|=q\), or when a valid lower bound on every not-yet-enumerated reduced cost is at least \(-\tau\). The latter event certifies that \(Q_q\) contains every \(\tau\)-improving column when fewer than \(q\) exist; reaching the cardinality limit alone is not a pricing-exhaustion certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact k-best pricing returns the lowest-reduced-cost improving columns up to a batch limit. Only a bound on unseen columns can certify exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact K-Best Batch Pricing

assumptions_latex: The original active set is \(R\), and \(Q\) is a finite set of feasible columns.
Each comparison reoptimizes the same feasible, bounded minimization restricted master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adding the entire batch weakly dominates adding any subset, but strict improvement is not guaranteed.

notation.meaning: Restricted-master optimal value over active set S.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master-value monotonicity induced by multi-column batch insertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(Q'\subseteq Q\), \[v(R\cup Q)\le v(R\cup Q')\le v(R).\] Thus retaining more feasible returned columns cannot worsen the reoptimized restricted-master value. Either inequality can be an equality even when columns in \(Q\) had negative reduced cost at the pre-insertion dual solution, because the selected dual solution can be degenerate or the columns can become jointly redundant after reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reoptimizing with the full feasible column batch weakly dominates reoptimizing with any subset, although degeneracy can prevent strict improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Batch-Insertion Dominance

assumptions_latex: Pricing is performed at fixed restricted-master dual multipliers during one pricing phase.
Each returned column is feasible and has reduced cost below the acceptance threshold \(-\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pricing phase may add any finite accepted set; global termination still requires a lower bound over every ungenerated column.

notation.meaning: Maximum number of accepted columns per block.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: multiple-column pricing retains several feasible negative-reduced-cost columns from one dual vector
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch insertion of several improving columns from one pricing phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block \(j\), search the pricing set at the current dual multipliers and construct a finite set \(Q_j\) with \(|Q_j|\le q_j\) and \(\bar c_{jp}< -\tau\) for every \(p\in Q_j\). A selection rule may rank by reduced cost and may impose a diversity predicate on column vectors. Add \(\bigcup_j Q_j\) to the restricted master, remove duplicates, and reoptimize. If no column is accepted, output termination only when an accompanying global pricing bound establishes \(\inf_{p\in P_j}\bar c_{jp}\ge-\tau\) for every block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple-column pricing collects several feasible, sufficiently negative, optionally diverse columns at one dual solution, then adds the batch before reoptimizing the master.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Column Pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The batch-pricing algorithm matches the multiple-column leaf and preserves the need for global termination bounds, but no inspectable citation is provided.

children.title: Concurrent Pricing Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Concurrent pricing across blocks or oracle variants.

children.title: Parallel Pricing
children.top_down_role: Concurrent pricing across blocks or oracle variants under coordinated master information.

assumptions_latex: All block oracles are evaluated at the same restricted-master dual vector \(y\).
Each block oracle depends only on \(y\), its block data, and a fixed local state.
Oracle outputs are deterministic, or the realized randomness and local states are fixed for the comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Synchronous parallel execution and serial execution of the same block-oracle calls return the same aggregate set of columns and bounds.

notation.meaning: Columns returned by block oracle j at price y.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order equivalence of independent synchronous pricing calls evaluated at one common dual vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When each \(Q_j(y)\) depends only on the common vector \(y\), fixed block data, and fixed local state, evaluating all block oracles concurrently and synchronizing their results returns \(Q(y)=\bigcup_{j=1}^m Q_j(y)\), exactly as serial evaluation of the same calls in any order. The equivalence can fail if calls share mutable state, consume order-dependent randomness, or are evaluated at different dual vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent block oracles evaluated at one common dual vector return the same aggregate result in synchronous parallel execution as in any serial ordering of the same fixed calls.
knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Oracle Equivalence

assumptions_latex: Pricing blocks \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\) are conditionally independent once a common dual vector \(y^k\) is fixed.
All workers complete before the restricted master is updated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Synchronous parallel pricing is equivalent to evaluating the independent block oracles at the same dual vector.

notation.meaning: Restricted-master dual vector at phase k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous worker decomposition across independent pricing blocks.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Parallel computing p. 101
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Broadcast \(y^k\) to all workers. In parallel, worker \(j\) searches or solves its pricing problem and returns a finite set \(Q_j^k\) of feasible columns, their reduced costs evaluated at \(y^k\), and any claimed lower bound. After a synchronization barrier, validate the returned columns, add every column whose reduced cost is below \(-\tau\), and reoptimize the restricted master. Declare termination only when every worker supplies a valid global lower bound at least \(-\tau\) for the same \(y^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel pricing solves independent block subproblems simultaneously at one dual vector, synchronizes their results, adds accepted columns, and requires all blocks for termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Pricing

children.title: Asynchronous Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing in which block-oracle results return without synchronized completion.

assumptions_latex: Each worker prices block \(j\) using a tagged dual vector \(y^{s_j}\), where \(s_j\le k\) is its launch version.
Returned columns can be reevaluated at the current dual vector \(y^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Asynchronous results may supply columns after current-dual validation, but stale bounds cannot directly certify current-dual termination.

notation.meaning: Dual version used by worker j.
Maximum permitted delay in dual versions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonblocking pricing with versioned dual information.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Launch each worker with a version-tagged dual vector without waiting for other workers. On receiving a feasible column \(p\) computed from \(y^{s_j}\), discard it if \(k-s_j>D\) under a bounded-delay policy; otherwise recompute its reduced cost at \(y^k\) and accept it only if the current value is below \(-\tau\). Reoptimize according to the master update policy while other workers continue. For termination, cancel or join outstanding tasks and obtain current-version global lower bounds from every pricing block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous workers price with versioned dual vectors. Returned columns must be checked at the current dual vector, and termination requires fresh certification from every block.

children.title: Stale-Price Reliability
children.top_down_role: Reliability limits associated with delayed or outdated master-price information.

assumptions_latex: The reduced cost is \(\bar c_{jp}(y,\sigma_j)=c_{jp}-y^{\mathsf T}a_{jp}-\sigma_j\).
The chosen norm and dual norm satisfy Holder's inequality.
Every block-j column satisfies \(\|a_{jp}\|_*\le M_j<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The valid stale-price error radius is \(M_j\|y^k-y^s\|+|\sigma_j^k-\sigma_j^s|\), so both dual-price components must be controlled.

notation.meaning: Family-price dual component at time t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reliability margin for affine reduced costs evaluated at stale linking and family prices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(p\in P_j\), \[|\bar c_{jp}(y^k,\sigma_j^k)-\bar c_{jp}(y^s,\sigma_j^s)|\le M_j\|y^k-y^s\|+|\sigma_j^k-\sigma_j^s|=\Delta_{s,k}^{(j)}.\] Hence \(\bar c_{jp}(y^s,\sigma_j^s)+\Delta_{s,k}^{(j)}< -\tau\) certifies current \(\tau\)-improvement. If \(L_j^s\le\inf_p\bar c_{jp}(y^s,\sigma_j^s)\), then \(L_j^s-\Delta_{s,k}^{(j)}\) is a valid current lower bound, and current family nonimprovement follows when it is at least \(-\tau\). The coefficient \(M_j\) is sharp in general: a scalar column with \(|a_{jp}|=M_j\) aligned with the price change attains the linking-price term. Without a finite norm bound or control of both price components, stale and current reduced costs can have arbitrarily different signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stale reduced cost must be corrected for drift in both the linking dual and the family dual price. Without bounds on both contributions, even its sign is unreliable.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Dual-Price Drift Bound

assumptions_latex: A stale pricing result was computed at dual vector \(y^s\), while the current vector is \(y^k\).
Every column vector satisfies a known bound \(\|a_{jp}\|_*\le M_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stale reduced costs are reliable only within the drift margin \(M_j\|y^k-y^s\|\); stale lower bounds require the same correction.

notation.meaning: Reduced cost at dual vector y.
Uniform dual norm bound on block columns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-based validity margin for stale pricing information.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Synchronization Issues in Parallel and Distributed Algorithms p. 88
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(p\in P_j\), dual-norm compatibility gives \(|\bar c_{jp}(y^k)-\bar c_{jp}(y^s)|\le\Delta_{s,k}\). Hence a stale column is certainly \(\tau\)-improving at \(y^k\) if \(\bar c_{jp}(y^s)+\Delta_{s,k}< -\tau\). If \(L_j^s\le\inf_{p\in P_j}\bar c_{jp}(y^s)\), then \(L_j^s-\Delta_{s,k}\) is a valid current lower bound; current \(\tau\)-nonimprovement follows only when \(L_j^s-\Delta_{s,k}\ge-\tau\). Without a finite \(M_j\) or controlled dual drift, stale pricing information has no uniform reliability guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded column norms convert dual drift into a reduced-cost error margin. Stale improvement or termination claims remain valid only after applying that margin.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Price Reliability

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 Synchronization Issues in Parallel and Distributed Algorithms p. 88

children.title: Structural Seed Columns
children.top_down_role: Problem-derived columns used to establish an initial master.

assumptions_latex: The initial restricted master requires a finite column set whose master rows and block convexity requirements are well defined.
Selected seed columns are feasible for their respective block subproblems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Structural seeds initialize the restricted master exactly when their master representation satisfies the stated coverage and feasibility conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \((S_j^0)_j\) is a structural seed family when every \(S_j^0\) is finite and contains only valid columns from \(P_j\), and the restricted master formed from \(S^0\) represents all mandatory block equations, including \(\sum_{p\in S_j^0}\lambda_{jp}=1\) whenever block \(j\) has a convexity row. If no such weights exist, the seeds define a valid but infeasible restricted master and must be supplemented by feasibility columns or a phase-I construction.

children.title: Artificial-Variable Initialization
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary master structures based on artificial variables when natural seed feasibility is absent.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}(Kx+Ma)=\{(0,1)\}\text{ on }x+a=1,\ x,a\ge0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite example showing that feasibility alone does not make an arbitrary positive penalty exact.
