knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the artificial penalty is smaller than the structural cost of satisfying a row, the augmented optimum can retain an artificial despite structural feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Insufficient Big-M Penalty

assumptions_latex: The original equality-form linear program is feasible and has a finite attained optimum.
An optimal dual multiplier \(y^*\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a^+=a^-=0\quad\text{at every augmented optimum}.

notation.meaning: optimal multiplier for the original equality rows

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient finite penalty for eliminating artificials at augmented-master optima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^\top\lambda:A\lambda=b,\lambda\ge0\}\) with dual \(\max\{b^\top y:A^\top y\le c\}\). In the split-artificial augmentation with common penalty \(M\), if an optimal original dual multiplier \(y^*\) satisfies \(M>\|y^*\|_\infty\), then every augmented optimum has \(a^+=a^-=0\), and its structural component is optimal for the original master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty strictly larger than the infinity norm of an optimal equality-row multiplier is exact and forces all artificial variables to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Artificial-Penalty Threshold
Artificial-Variable Initialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Big-penalty initialization for an equality-form restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given structural columns indexed by \(J\), form \[\min_{\lambda,a^+,a^-}\; c_J^\top\lambda+M\mathbf 1^\top(a^++a^-)\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_J\lambda+a^+-a^-=b,\quad \lambda,a^+,a^-\geq0.\] Initialize with \(\lambda=0\), \(a^+=\max\{b,0\}\), and \(a^-=\max\{-b,0\}\), componentwise. The resulting restricted master is feasible. Here \(M>0\) is chosen sufficiently large that retaining a positive artificial variable is dominated whenever a structural feasible solution exists. Output the initialized master and its artificial-variable basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split artificial variables make every equality row initially feasible; a large objective penalty drives them to zero when structural feasibility is attainable.
assumptions_latex: \(A_J\in\mathbb R^{m\times |J|}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\lambda\geq0\).
\(M>0\) is a valid dominating penalty for the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\lambda,a^+,a^-)=(0,\max\{b,0\},\max\{-b,0\})\) is feasible for the augmented restricted master.

notation.meaning: nonnegative artificial variables for equality residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The split artificials give the stated feasible point, but a finite dominating value of M requires objective and feasible-region assumptions not supplied. The claimed artificial-variable basis also needs an explicit selection rule, especially for zero right-hand-side rows.

children.title: Feasibility-Phase Initialization
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary restricted-master phases focused on establishing an initially viable column set.

assumptions_latex: All full-master structural variables are nonnegative column weights.
The feasibility-pricing oracle globally maximizes \(a(p)^\top y\) over every admissible column.
Any convexity or type rows are included in \(a(p)\) with their declared normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_p a(p)^\top y\le0\ \land\ b^\top y>0\Longrightarrow b\notin\operatorname{cone}\{a(p)\}.

notation.meaning: linking-row vector of an admissible structural column

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Test distinguishing restricted infeasibility from a full-column Farkas certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\) satisfy \(A_J^\top y\le0\) and \(b^\top y>0\). If the full admissible column family contains a column \(a(p)\) with \(a(p)^\top y>0\), that column violates the restricted Farkas inequality and may be added to continue feasibility generation. If \(a(p)^\top y\le0\) for every admissible column, Farkas' alternative certifies infeasibility of the full conic master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A column with positive pairing against the Phase-I certificate can escape restricted infeasibility; exhaustive absence of such a column certifies full-master infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Pricing Escape Test

assumptions_latex: The finite-dimensional Phase-I linear program is solved to optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi_J>0\Longrightarrow\exists y:\ A_J^\top y\le0,\ \|y\|_\infty\le1,\ b^\top y>0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation and restricted-infeasibility certificate for split-residual Phase I.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dual of \[\min\{\mathbf1^\top(a^++a^-):A_J\lambda+a^+-a^-=b,\ \lambda,a^+,a^-\ge0\}\] is \[\max_y\{b^\top y:A_J^\top y\le0,\ -\mathbf1\le y\le\mathbf1\}.\] Hence \(\phi_J>0\) yields \(y\) with \(b^\top y=\phi_J>0\) and \(A_J^\top y\le0\), certifying infeasibility of \(A_J\lambda=b,\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Phase-I dual is a bounded Farkas alternative; a positive optimum certifies infeasibility of the current restricted column cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Phase-I Dual Alternative
Feasibility-Phase Initialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Phase-I initialization for an equality-form restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the auxiliary problem \[\phi_J=\min_{\lambda,a^+,a^-}\;\mathbf 1^\top(a^++a^-)\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_J\lambda+a^+-a^-=b,\quad\lambda,a^+,a^-\geq0.\] Start from the split-residual artificial solution. If \(\phi_J=0\), return an optimal \(\lambda\) as a feasible restricted-master initialization. If \(\phi_J>0\), report that the restricted master over \(J\) is infeasible and invoke a separately certified feasibility-pricing or column-generation step before making any conclusion about a larger master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phase I minimizes total artificial violation. A zero optimum supplies a structural feasible start for the current restricted master; a positive optimum proves only that the current column set is structurally infeasible, so conclusions about a larger master require certified feasibility pricing or column generation.
assumptions_latex: The restricted-master constraints are \(A_J\lambda=b\) with \(\lambda\geq0\).
The Phase-I auxiliary problem is solved to global optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi_J=0\) if and only if there exists \(\lambda\geq0\) satisfying \(A_J\lambda=b\).

notation.meaning: optimal Phase-I violation over the current columns

children.title: Auxiliary-Structure Removal
children.top_down_role: The transition from initialization devices to the original restricted-master representation.

assumptions_latex: The basis transformation is nonsingular and represents row-equivalent equality constraints.
All artificial variables are fixed to zero in the target structural master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar b_r=0\ \land\ \bar A_{r,J}=0\Longrightarrow\text{row }r\text{ may be deleted without changing the structural feasible set}.

notation.meaning: transformed row coefficients of all structural columns

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact tableau certificate permitting redundant-row deletion after artificials are fixed to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After basis transformation, suppose the row containing a zero basic artificial has zero right-hand side and zero coefficients for every structural variable: \(\bar b_r=0\) and \(\bar A_{r,J}=0\). After artificials are fixed to zero, the transformed equation is \(0=0\), so deleting it does not change the structural feasible set. Failure to find a pivot without this zero-row certificate does not establish redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero transformed row over all structural columns certifies redundancy after artificials are fixed to zero; mere absence of a convenient pivot does not.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Row Deletion Certificate

assumptions_latex: All variables are in nonnegative standard form.
The current basis is primal feasible.
The selected entering column and leaving row satisfy the standard primal-simplex minimum-ratio rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar b_r=0,\ \bar a_{rj}>0\text{ and valid minimum-ratio selection}\Longrightarrow\text{the pivot preserves primal feasibility and removes the basic artificial}.

notation.meaning: nonbasic columns in the current basis tableau

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-feasible pivot condition for replacing a zero-valued basic artificial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the current basis equations as \(x_B=\bar b-\bar A_Nx_N\). If a basic artificial occupies row \(r\) with \(\bar b_r=0\), a nonbasic structural column \(j\) with \(\bar a_{rj}>0\) can enter with that artificial leaving at ratio zero when row \(r\) is a valid minimum-ratio choice. The pivot is degenerate but preserves primal feasibility and removes that artificial from the basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero basic artificial can be pivoted out by a structural column with a positive tableau coefficient when the ordinary minimum-ratio conditions permit that zero-ratio pivot.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate-Artificial Pivot Criterion
Auxiliary-Structure Removal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe removal criterion after restricted-master Phase I.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Artificial columns may be removed after Phase I when \(\phi_J=0\) and a feasible basis can be formed entirely from structural columns, after deleting redundant equality rows if necessary. Pivot every zero-valued basic artificial variable out using a nonzero eligible structural coefficient; if no such coefficient exists, classify the associated row as redundant or retain the artificial column temporarily. The resulting structural basis must satisfy \(A_J\lambda=b\) and \(\lambda\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Remove artificials only after zero Phase-I violation and construction of a structural feasible basis, handling degenerate basic artificials by pivoting or redundant-row deletion.
assumptions_latex: Phase I terminates with \(\phi_J=0\).
Permitted row deletion preserves the structural feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After successful pivots and valid redundant-row deletions, the unaugmented restricted master retains a feasible starting basis.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the removal leaf, but zero Phase-I value alone does not certify that each degenerate artificial can be removed. The pivot eligibility and redundant-row classification require authoritative support and a precise certification rule.

children.title: Cross-Solve Column-Reuse Interface
children.top_down_role: Transfer of columns and master state across related solves.

children.title: Restricted-Master Warm Starts
children.top_down_role: Transfer of restricted-master state across related solves.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplex reoptimization choice after mapping a nonsingular basis into a compatible restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization LP in standard equality form, let the mapped partition be \((B,N)\), let \(x_B=B^{-1}b'\), and let \(\bar c_N=c_N'-A_N'^{\mathsf T}B^{-\mathsf T}c_B'\). If \(x_B\ge0\) and \(\bar c_N\ge0\), the mapped basis is optimal. If only \(x_B\ge0\) holds, start primal simplex; if only \(\bar c_N\ge0\) holds, start dual simplex. If neither holds, repair the basis or run a feasibility initialization before reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mapped basis that is both primal and dual feasible is already optimal; primal-only feasibility selects primal simplex, dual-only feasibility selects dual simplex, and failure of both tests requires repair or feasibility initialization.
assumptions_latex: The new restricted master is \(\min\{c'^{\mathsf T}x:A'x=b',\ x\ge0\}\).
The mapped basis matrix \(B\) is nonsingular and its rows, columns, costs, and bounds have the meanings used in the new master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_B\ge0\land\bar c_N\ge0\Longrightarrow B\text{ is optimal for the new restricted master}.
knowledge_statements.title: Mapped-Basis Reoptimization Branches
Restricted-Master Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis warm start between compatible restricted-master solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For consecutive restricted masters, retain the previous structural columns and basis \(B\). Map unchanged rows and columns into the new formulation, update the right-hand side or costs, and test primal feasibility \(B^{-1}b'\geq0\) and dual feasibility \(c_{N}'-A_N'^\top B^{-\top}c_B'\geq0\). If both hold, the mapped basis is optimal; if only one holds, initialize the corresponding primal or dual simplex reoptimization. Otherwise use basis repair or feasibility initialization. Output the reoptimized restricted-master solution and basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map a prior basis into the new restricted master, test primal and dual feasibility, then reoptimize with a suitable simplex start or repair.
assumptions_latex: The old basis columns and their row meanings admit an unambiguous mapping to the new master.
\(B\) remains nonsingular after mapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A mapped basis satisfying both feasibility tests is optimal for the new restricted master.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasibility tests are standard for a minimization LP in equality form, but that form and its sign conventions are not stated. It is also unclear whether B denotes the mapped new basis matrix when coefficients change. A restricted-master warm-start source is required.

children.title: Column Reuse
children.top_down_role: Transfer of previously generated columns into a related pricing context.

assumptions_latex: The minimization reduced-cost convention is \(\bar c=c-\pi^\top a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar c(0)>0\quad\text{but}\quad\bar c(2)<0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why historical reduced costs cannot permanently classify a reusable column.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization-master column with new cost \(c=1\) and linking coefficient \(a=1\), its reduced cost is \(\bar c(\pi)=1-\pi\). It is nonimproving at \(\pi=0\), where \(\bar c=1\), but improving at \(\pi=2\), where \(\bar c=-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced cost depends on the current dual multiplier, so historical reduced costs are not safe permanent reuse filters.
knowledge_statements.title: Stored Reduced-Cost Screening Failure

assumptions_latex: Column weights are nonnegative.
The columns have identical coefficients in every new master row, including convexity and type rows.
Both columns have the same declared point, ray, or other column semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a'(p)=a'(q),\ c'(p)\le c'(q)\Longrightarrow q\text{ is dominated by }p.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe deduplication and dominance after new-instance coefficients are evaluated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a minimization master with nonnegative weights, suppose compatible columns \(p,q\) have the same new master vector and the same column type, \(a'(p)=a'(q)\), but \(c'(p)\le c'(q)\). Weight on \(q\) can be transferred to \(p\) without changing feasibility or increasing cost. Thus \(q\) is dominated; if costs are equal, either is an exact duplicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among reused columns with identical new master coefficients and semantics, only a cheapest representative is needed.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent-Column Dominance in a Reuse Pool
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent-Column Dominance in a Reuse Pool
Column Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reusing generated columns across related decomposition solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a stored pool \(P\) and a new instance, retain every column \(p\in P\) that passes the new block-feasibility and representation tests. Recompute its master coefficient vector \(a'(p)\), cost \(c'(p)\), and reduced cost \(\bar c'(p)=c'(p)-\pi^\top a'(p)\); do not reuse stored reduced costs. Insert compatible columns into the initial restricted master, remove duplicates under the new representation, and apply feasibility initialization if their conic or convex hull does not satisfy the linking rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse only columns feasible and representable in the new instance, recomputing coefficients, costs, and reduced costs before constructing the initial restricted master.
assumptions_latex: Each stored column can be validated against the new block model.
The new master coefficient and cost mappings are evaluable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned initial pool contains only columns valid for the new formulation and uses newly evaluated master data.

notation.meaning: recomputed reduced cost in the new solve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The workflow fits the leaf, but the reduced-cost formula assumes a particular minimization and linking-row convention. Cross-instance column validity and representation tests are formulation-dependent and need a supporting source.

children.title: Cross-Solve Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Structural limits on reusing master state or columns after model changes.

assumptions_latex: The old-to-new object map \(T\) and the new coefficient and cost maps are explicitly defined.
The new formulation exposes all type-specific master semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(p)\in X'\ \land\ \text{all new semantic predicates hold}\Longrightarrow T(p)\text{ is a valid new-master column}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient compatibility predicate for safely transporting a column between related formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) map an old generated object \(p\) into the new block space. Transfer is structurally valid if \(T(p)\in X'\); its declared column type is preserved; every new master coefficient and cost is evaluated by \(a'(T(p))\) and \(c'(T(p))\); and all type-specific rows, bounds, signs, integrality declarations, and normalization coefficients are satisfied. These conditions suffice for insertion as a valid new-master variable, but do not preserve old reduced cost or basis status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Safe transport requires a feasible mapped object, preserved column semantics, and satisfaction of every new master mapping and type-specific rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Preserving Column Transport

assumptions_latex: The master distinguishes point weights from recession-ray weights through its convexity-row coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dim p=\dim q\not\Longrightarrow\text{cross-solve compatibility}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equal-dimensional example showing why coefficient dimensions do not establish compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a Dantzig-Wolfe master, point columns carry coefficient \(1\) in a convexity row \(\sum_p\lambda_p=1\), whereas recession-ray columns carry coefficient \(0\). A stored vector can have the same physical dimension and linking coefficients as a new point column yet represent a ray. Assigning it the point coefficient, or assigning a point the ray coefficient, changes the represented polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Points and recession rays may have identical vector dimensions but different convexity-row semantics, so dimension matching is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Point-Ray Semantic Incompatibility
Cross-Solve Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity predicate for transferring a generated column between solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stored column \(p\) is cross-solve compatible with a new decomposed formulation precisely when: \(p\) belongs to the new generating block's feasible set; its coordinates have the same declared semantic meaning and units; and the new mappings \(a'(p)\) and \(c'(p)\) into master rows and objective are defined. Basis transfer additionally requires a bijection between involved rows and columns that preserves coefficients and yields a nonsingular mapped basis. Matching dimensions alone is not sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer requires block feasibility, semantic coordinate agreement, and defined new master mappings; basis transfer also requires coefficient-preserving row-column correspondence and nonsingularity.
assumptions_latex: Old and new formulations expose explicit block, coordinate, row, and cost mappings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only columns satisfying all compatibility predicates may enter the new restricted master without reformulation.

notation.meaning: column coefficients in the new master
column cost in the new master

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated checks are useful necessary conditions, but “precisely when” is too strong for general decompositions: convexity weights, column types, bounds, integrality, and other master semantics may also matter. A formal cross-solve mapping source is needed to determine the correct predicate.

children.title: Dual Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Regularization families controlling unstable restricted-master prices.

children.title: Localized Dual Stabilization Family
children.top_down_role: Localization of dual movement around reference prices.

children.title: Box Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Dual localization through componentwise bounds around reference prices.

assumptions_latex: \(\Delta_i>0\) for every localized component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\) satisfies every componentwise stabilization bound if and only if \(\|W(\pi-\bar\pi)\|_\infty\le 1\).

notation.meaning: Diagonal matrix of reciprocal componentwise radii.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact geometric representation of componentwise dual localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For radii \(\Delta_i>0\), let \(W=\operatorname{diag}(\Delta_1^{-1},\ldots,\Delta_m^{-1})\). Then \[\{\pi:\bar\pi_i-\Delta_i\le\pi_i\le\bar\pi_i+\Delta_i\ \forall i\}=\{\pi:\|W(\pi-\bar\pi)\|_\infty\le1\}.\] Thus box stabilization is precisely an axis-aligned weighted \(\ell_\infty\)-localization of the dual multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A componentwise stabilization box is exactly a weighted infinity-norm ball around the dual center.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted-Infinity-Norm Representation of a Stabilization Box
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted-Infinity-Norm Representation of a Stabilization Box
Box Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinity-norm localization of restricted-master dual iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a concave restricted dual objective \(D_J\), center \(\bar\pi\), and radii \(\Delta_i>0\), compute \[\pi^+\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\pi}\{D_J(\pi):\bar\pi_i-\Delta_i\leq\pi_i\leq\bar\pi_i+\Delta_i\ \text{for all }i\}.\] Use \(\pi^+\) for pricing. Components fixed by dual sign or domain restrictions retain those restrictions in addition to the box. Update the center or radii only through the localization-management rule, and output \(\pi^+\) with its active bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize the restricted dual inside a componentwise box around a reference multiplier, then use the localized multiplier for pricing.
assumptions_latex: \(D_J\) is a proper concave restricted-dual objective.
The intersection of the dual domain with the stabilization box is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi^+\) lies in the prescribed box and maximizes \(D_J\) over that localized dual region.

The mathematical subproblem is coherent, but the specialized algorithm requires an appropriate source.

children.title: Trust-Region Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Dual localization through an aggregate neighborhood around reference prices.

assumptions_latex: \(D_J\) is differentiable and concave on the localized feasible set.
\(H\succ0\), \(\Delta>0\), and \(\Pi\) is closed and convex.
There exists \(\pi^0\in\operatorname{ri}(\Pi)\) with \((\pi^0-\bar\pi)^\top H(\pi^0-\bar\pi)<\Delta^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility, stationarity, nonnegative multiplier, and complementary slackness are necessary and sufficient for global optimality of \(\pi^+\).

notation.meaning: Multiplier of the ellipsoidal localization constraint.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate for a differentiable concave restricted dual localized by a positive-definite quadratic norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\succ0\), let \(\Pi\) be closed and convex, and maximize differentiable concave \(D_J\) over \(\Pi\cap\{\pi:(\pi-\bar\pi)^\top H(\pi-\bar\pi)\le\Delta^2\}\). Under the stated relative-interior Slater condition, \(\pi^+\) is optimal if and only if it is feasible and there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \[\nabla D_J(\pi^+)-2\lambda H(\pi^+-\bar\pi)\in N_\Pi(\pi^+),\qquad \lambda\big((\pi^+-\bar\pi)^\top H(\pi^+-\bar\pi)-\Delta^2\big)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A localized dual point is optimal exactly when its gradient is balanced by the trust-region and dual-domain normals, with feasibility and complementary slackness.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimality Conditions for Ellipsoidal Dual Localization
knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Conditions for Ellipsoidal Dual Localization
Trust-Region Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-ball localization of restricted-master dual iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a concave restricted dual objective \(D_J\), center \(\bar\pi\), norm \(\|\cdot\|_H\), and radius \(\Delta>0\), compute \[\pi^+\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\pi}\{D_J(\pi):\|\pi-\bar\pi\|_H\leq\Delta,\ \pi\in\Pi\}.\] Price columns at \(\pi^+\). Compare actual dual improvement with the improvement predicted by the restricted model; accept or reject the center update and enlarge or shrink \(\Delta\) according to fixed ratio thresholds. Output the localized pricing multiplier and updated radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize the restricted dual within a norm ball, price at that multiplier, and update the center and radius using actual-versus-predicted improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(D_J\) is proper and concave on the dual domain \(\Pi\).
The localized maximization problem has a solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pricing multiplier satisfies \(\pi^+\in\Pi\) and \(\|\pi^+-\bar\pi\|_H\leq\Delta\).

children.title: Localization-Region Management
children.top_down_role: Structural choices controlling the size and movement of the admissible price neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.title: Localization-Region Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance and radius updates for localized dual stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_k>0\) be predicted improvement, \(a_k\) actual improvement after pricing, and \(\rho_k=a_k/p_k\). For fixed \(0\leq\eta_1<\eta_2<1\), reject the trial center and shrink the region when \(\rho_k<\eta_1\); accept the trial center when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\); and enlarge the region when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\) and the trial point is near its boundary. Keep radii within \([\Delta_{\min},\Delta_{\max}]\). If \(p_k\leq0\), invoke a termination or model-repair test rather than forming the ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept centers and resize localization regions using actual-to-predicted improvement, with safeguards for radius bounds and nonpositive predictions.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\Delta_{\min}\leq\Delta_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated radius remains in \([\Delta_{\min},\Delta_{\max}]\), and center acceptance follows the stated ratio test.

children.title: Regularized Dual-Master Stabilization Family
children.top_down_role: Regularized dual master models designed to damp price oscillation.

children.title: Proximal Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Price stabilization through proximity to a reference dual point.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically regularized restricted-dual maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a proper concave restricted-dual objective \(D_J\), reference center \(\bar\pi\), parameter \(t>0\), and positive-definite matrix \(H\), compute \[\pi^+\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\pi\in\Pi}\left\{D_J(\pi)-\frac{1}{2t}\|\pi-\bar\pi\|_H^2\right\}.\] Use \(\pi^+\) for pricing. The quadratic term selects a localized dual solution even when the unregularized restricted dual has multiple maximizers. Output \(\pi^+\); update \(\bar\pi\) separately through the reference-center rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize the restricted dual minus a positive quadratic distance from a reference multiplier, then use the unique regularized solution for pricing.
assumptions_latex: \(D_J\) is proper, upper semicontinuous, and concave on closed convex \(\Pi\).
\(t>0\) and \(H\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized objective is strongly concave and therefore has at most one maximizer \(\pi^+\).

assumptions_latex: The proximal metric is allowed to be positive semidefinite rather than positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H\succeq0\not\Longrightarrow\text{uniqueness of the stabilized maximizer}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp uniqueness boundary for the proximal metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_J(\pi_1,\pi_2)=0\), \(\Pi=[-1,1]^2\), \(\bar\pi=0\), and \(H=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\). The regularized objective is \(-\pi_1^2/(2t)\), so every \((0,s)\) with \(s\in[-1,1]\) is a maximizer.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori optimality bound supplied by valid concave supergradient cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For exact supergradient cuts, define \(\widehat D_k(\pi)=\min_{i\in I_k}\{D(\pi^i)+(g^i)^\top(\pi-\pi^i)\}\) and \(B_k=\sup_{\pi\in\Pi}\widehat D_k(\pi)\). Then \(D(\pi)\le\widehat D_k(\pi)\) for every \(\pi\in\Pi\), hence \(D^*\le B_k\). For any feasible incumbent \(\bar\pi_k\), \(0\le D^*-D(\bar\pi_k)\le B_k-D(\bar\pi_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximized bundle upper model gives a valid dual upper bound, so its gap above the incumbent certifies dual suboptimality.

assumptions_latex: The model is intended to upper-model a concave maximization objective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating valid bundle cuts from arbitrary affine model fitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The bundle bounds require every stored affine function \(\ell_i\) to satisfy \(D(\pi)\le\ell_i(\pi)\) on \(\Pi\). For \(D(\pi)=-|\pi|\), the affine function formed at \(\pi=1\) using the incorrectly signed slope \(+1\) is \(\ell(\pi)=\pi-2\), and \(D(0)=0>\ell(0)=-2\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact concave bundle cycle retaining all generated supergradient cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be concave on closed convex \(\Pi\). Retain all exact supergradient cuts \(\ell_i\) and form \(\widehat D_k=\min_{i\in I_k}\ell_i\). Ensure that a cut generated at the current evaluated center \(\bar\pi_k\) is retained. For \(t_k\in[t_{\min},t_{\max}]\), compute \[\pi_k^+\in\arg\max_{\pi\in\Pi}\left\{\widehat D_k(\pi)-\frac{\|\pi-\bar\pi_k\|_2^2}{2t_k}\right\}.\] Set \(p_k=\widehat D_k(\pi_k^+)-D(\bar\pi_k)\), evaluate \(D(\pi_k^+)\) and an exact supergradient, and append its cut. For \(\eta\in(0,1)\), take \(\bar\pi_{k+1}=\pi_k^+\) when \(p_k>0\) and \(D(\pi_k^+)-D(\bar\pi_k)\ge\eta p_k\); otherwise retain \(\bar\pi_{k+1}=\bar\pi_k\). Keep \(t_k\) within its safeguards, allowing an increase after serious steps and a decrease after null steps. Stop when finite \(B_k=\sup_{\pi\in\Pi}\widehat D_k(\pi)\) satisfies \(B_k-D(\bar\pi_k)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize a proximal retained-cut upper model, append an exact supergradient cut, accept sufficient actual improvement, and stop using the unregularized bundle gap.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is proper, upper-semicontinuous, and concave on nonempty closed convex \(\Pi\).
Every evaluation supplies an exact value and exact supergradient cut.
A center cut is retained, the proximal subproblem is attained, and \(0<t_{\min}\le t_k\le t_{\max}<\infty\).
\(B_k\) is finite whenever the stopping test is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\le\widehat D_{k+1}\le\widehat D_k,\qquad B_k-D(\bar\pi_k)\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow D^*-D(\bar\pi_k)\le\varepsilon.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat D_k(\pi)=\min_{i\in I_k}\{\alpha_i+(g^i)^{\mathsf T}\pi\}\), let \(\Pi\) be closed and convex, and let \(t_k>0\). A feasible \(\pi_k^+\) maximizes \(\widehat D_k(\pi)-\|\pi-\bar\pi_k\|_2^2/(2t_k)\) if and only if there are coefficients \(\mu_i\ge0\), supported on \[A_k(\pi_k^+)=\{i:\alpha_i+(g^i)^{\mathsf T}\pi_k^+=\widehat D_k(\pi_k^+)\},\] with \(\sum_i\mu_i=1\), such that \[\sum_{i\in A_k(\pi_k^+)}\mu_i g^i-\frac{1}{t_k}(\pi_k^+-\bar\pi_k)\in N_\Pi(\pi_k^+).\]

\(t_k>0\), and the proximal bundle maximum is attained.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column-generation specialization connecting block pricing solutions to valid bundle cuts for a concave Lagrangian dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[D(\pi)=b^{\mathsf T}\pi+\sum_{s=1}^S\inf_{x_s\in X_s}(c_s-A_s^{\mathsf T}\pi)^{\mathsf T}x_s.\] If every infimum is attained at \(x_s^i\) for \(\pi=\pi^i\), then \[g^i=b-\sum_{s=1}^S A_sx_s^i\] is a supergradient of \(D\) at \(\pi^i\), and \[D(\pi)\le D(\pi^i)+(g^i)^{\mathsf T}(\pi-\pi^i)\quad\text{for every }\pi.\] Thus block pricing evaluates the dual and supplies a valid affine upper cut for the bundle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solutions of the block pricing problems produce the coupling-residual supergradient and hence a valid upper bundle cut for the concave dual objective.

assumptions_latex: Predicted and realized improvements use a common concave-maximization convention.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value invariant induced by serious-step center acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If realized improvement is \(a_k=D(\pi^{k+1})-D(\bar\pi_k)\), predicted improvement satisfies \(p_k>0\), and the center moves only when \(a_k\ge\eta p_k\) with \(\eta\in(0,1)\), then every accepted center satisfies \(D(\bar\pi_{k+1})>D(\bar\pi_k)\). A null step leaves the center and its evaluated dual value unchanged.

Reference-Center Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Serious-step management of a proximal stabilization center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar\pi_k\) be the current center, \(\pi^{k+1}\) a trial multiplier, \(p_k>0\) the model-predicted improvement, and \(a_k\) the realized dual improvement after pricing. For a fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), set \(\bar\pi_{k+1}=\pi^{k+1}\) when \(a_k\geq\eta p_k\) and otherwise set \(\bar\pi_{k+1}=\bar\pi_k\). After a serious step, the proximal weight may be relaxed; after a null step, retain the center, add the new cut, and strengthen localization according to safeguarded parameter bounds.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The center changes exactly on a serious step satisfying \(a_k\geq\eta p_k\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_\rho=1/\rho\ne1\), so penalized-dual optimality does not imply unpenalized restricted-dual optimality.

notation.meaning: Maximizer of the quadratically penalized dual objective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary preventing a penalized stabilization subproblem from serving by itself as a master-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A maximizer of \(D(\pi)-\frac{\rho}{2}\|\pi-\bar\pi\|_2^2\) need not maximize \(D\). On \([0,1]\), let \(D(\pi)=\pi\), \(\bar\pi=0\), and \(\rho>1\). The unique penalized maximizer is \(\pi_\rho=1/\rho\), whereas the unique maximizer of \(D\) is \(1\). Consequently, penalized-subproblem optimality alone cannot certify master optimality; termination requires an independently valid full-master dual bound and the applicable primal-dual gap test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal-penalty solution can differ from the restricted-dual optimizer, so its optimality cannot by itself certify master optimality.

Penalty Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic proximal stabilization of a restricted-master dual iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the concave restricted-master dual objective \(D_k:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\), a center \(\bar\pi_k\), and \(\rho_k>0\), compute \[\pi_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\pi}\left\{D_k(\pi)-\frac{\rho_k}{2}\|\pi-\bar\pi_k\|_2^2\right\}.\] Use \(\pi_k\) for pricing. If pricing returns a column with reduced cost below \(-\varepsilon\), add it and optionally update \(\bar\pi_{k+1}\); otherwise, when exact pricing certifies every reduced cost at least \(-\varepsilon\), output the current restricted-master solution as \(\varepsilon\)-optimal for the full master under the usual column-generation duality assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize the restricted-master dual with a quadratic penalty around a center, price at the stabilized multiplier, and stop after exact pricing finds no sufficiently improving column.

children.title: Smoothing Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Restricted-master stabilization through smoother dual response structure.

assumptions_latex: \(D:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\) is proper, upper-semicontinuous, and concave.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_\mu\ge D\), the envelopes are nondecreasing in \(\mu\), and \(D_\mu(\pi)\to D(\pi)\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\) for \(\pi\in\operatorname{dom}D\).

notation.meaning: Concave Moreau envelope with smoothing parameter \(\mu\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic approximation properties of the concave Moreau envelope used for dual smoothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[D_\mu(\pi)=\sup_u\left\{D(u)-\frac{1}{2\mu}\|u-\pi\|_2^2\right\},\qquad \mu>0.\] Then \(D_\mu(\pi)\ge D(\pi)\). If \(0<\mu_1<\mu_2\), then \(D_{\mu_1}(\pi)\le D_{\mu_2}(\pi)\), and \[\lim_{\mu\downarrow0}D_\mu(\pi)=D(\pi)\] at every \(\pi\in\operatorname{dom}D\). Thus finite smoothing is an upper approximation of the concave dual objective, and its bias vanishes as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The concave Moreau envelope lies above the original dual objective, increases with the smoothing parameter, and converges pointwise to the original objective as smoothing vanishes.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Approximation and Vanishing-Smoothing Limit
Smoothing Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moreau smoothing of a polyhedral restricted-master dual objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper upper-semicontinuous concave dual objective \(D_k\) and \(\mu>0\), define its concave Moreau envelope by \[D_{k,\mu}(\pi)=\sup_{u\in\mathbb{R}^m}\left\{D_k(u)-\frac{1}{2\mu}\|u-\pi\|_2^2\right\}.\] If the maximizer \(u_\mu(\pi)\) is unique, then \(D_{k,\mu}\) is differentiable and \[\nabla D_{k,\mu}(\pi)=\frac{u_\mu(\pi)-\pi}{\mu}.\] A smoothing-stabilized step updates the dual center using this gradient and performs pricing with the associated multiplier \(u_\mu(\pi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace the nonsmooth dual objective by its concave Moreau envelope, update through the envelope gradient, and price using the associated proximal multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(D_k\) is proper, upper semicontinuous, and concave.
The displayed proximal maximizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{k,\mu}\) is differentiable with \(\nabla D_{k,\mu}(\pi)=(u_\mu(\pi)-\pi)/\mu\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The concave Moreau-envelope formulas are internally consistent and representation is a plausible knowledge kind, but no cited source supports its interpretation as a column-generation stabilization mechanism or the stated pricing step.

children.title: Primal-Dual Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization using coupled primal information and dual information.

assumptions_latex: \(X_k\) and \(\Pi\) are nonempty convex sets.
\(L_k\) is convex in \(x\) and concave in \(\pi\).
\(\tau_k>0\), \(\sigma_k>0\), and a saddle point of \(\Phi\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized saddle point is characterized by the displayed inequalities and is unique.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unambiguous saddle-point formulation and uniqueness condition for coupled primal-dual stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\Phi(x,\pi)=L_k(x,\pi)+\frac{1}{2\tau_k}\|x-\bar x_k\|_2^2-\frac{1}{2\sigma_k}\|\pi-\bar\pi_k\|_2^2.\] A pair \((x_k,\pi_k)\in X_k\times\Pi\) is a regularized saddle point exactly when \[\Phi(x_k,\pi)\le\Phi(x_k,\pi_k)\le\Phi(x,\pi_k)\quad\forall(x,\pi)\in X_k\times\Pi.\] If such a saddle point exists under the stated convex-concave and positive-parameter assumptions, it is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupled stabilization is defined by the saddle inequalities, and any attained saddle is unique under positive primal and dual quadratic regularization.
knowledge_statements.title: Well-Posed Regularized Primal-Dual Saddle Characterization
Primal-Dual Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled proximal regularization of restricted-master primal and dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_k(x,\pi)\) be the restricted-master Lagrangian, with closed convex primal set \(X_k\) and closed convex dual set \(\Pi\). Given \((\bar x_k,\bar\pi_k)\) and positive parameters \(\tau_k,\sigma_k\), compute a regularized saddle point \[ (x_k,\pi_k)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X_k}\operatorname*{argmax}_{\pi\in\Pi}\left\{L_k(x,\pi)+\frac{1}{2\tau_k}\|x-\bar x_k\|_2^2-\frac{1}{2\sigma_k}\|\pi-\bar\pi_k\|_2^2\right\}. \] Price with \(\pi_k\), add improving columns, and update both centers from \((x_k,\pi_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularize both sides of the restricted-master saddle problem, price at the resulting dual point, and update the primal and dual centers together.
assumptions_latex: \(X_k\) and \(\Pi\) are nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(L_k\) is convex in \(x\) and concave in \(\pi\).
\(\tau_k>0\) and \(\sigma_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_k,\pi_k)\) is the coupled regularized saddle point used for reoptimization and pricing.
