knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pooling Changes the Restricted Master but Not the Full Column Universe
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural distinction between temporary active-set removal and permanent deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\) be the full column universe, \(A_k\subseteq\mathcal U\) the active set, and \(P_k\subseteq\mathcal U\setminus A_k\) an exactly reconstructible pool. Moving \(j\in A_k\) to \(P_k\) restricts the current master to \(A_k\setminus\{j\}\), which may raise its value or make it infeasible, but leaves \(\mathcal U\) and the full-master optimum unchanged. Any global pricing certificate must still cover every column in \(\mathcal U\), including pooled columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pooling may weaken the restricted master but does not change the full master when pooled columns remain in the priced universe.
assumptions_latex: Each pooled column retains its exact objective and constraint coefficients.
Full pricing ranges over \(\mathcal U\), or an equivalent pool scan plus new-column oracle covers \(\mathcal U\).
The restricted and full problems are minimization problems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A_k\setminus\{j\})\ge v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A_k),\qquad v_{\mathrm{full}}(\mathcal U)\text{ is unchanged},
knowledge_statements.title: Pooling Changes the Restricted Master but Not the Full Column Universe

assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon\le\delta<1\).
The pooling rule treats every variable with value at most \(\delta\) as inactive without a feasibility-core safeguard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal F(\{0,1\})\ne\varnothing\quad\text{but}\quad\mathcal F(\{0\})=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Required positive weight of the pooled column

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of pooling based solely on a positive primal-activity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<\varepsilon\le\delta<1\). Consider \[\min 0\quad\text{s.t.}\quad \lambda_0+\lambda_1=1,\quad \lambda_1=\varepsilon,\quad \lambda_0,\lambda_1\ge0.\] Its unique feasible solution has \(\lambda_1=\varepsilon\le\delta\). A rule declaring \(\lambda_j\le\delta\) inactive can therefore select column 1, but removing it forces \(0=\varepsilon\) and makes the restricted master infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive activity tolerance can classify a small but feasibility-essential column as inactive, and pooling it can destroy restricted feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tolerance-Based Inactivity Can Hide a Feasibility-Core Column
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Based Inactivity Can Hide a Feasibility-Core Column

assumptions_latex: The restricted master has an attained optimum \(\bar\lambda\).
\(\bar\lambda_j=0\) exactly.
All other variables and constraints are unchanged when column \(j\) is removed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A\setminus\{j\})=v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A)<+\infty.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the candidate column variable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Current-iteration safety of pooling a column that is zero in a retained optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar\lambda\) be an optimal solution of a feasible minimization restricted master over active set \(A\), with \(\bar\lambda_j=0\). Removing column \(j\) leaves the restriction of \(\bar\lambda\) feasible with the same objective value. Because the reduced feasible set is contained in the old one, its optimal value is also no smaller, so the two values are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A column exactly zero in a retained optimum can be removed without changing current restricted-master feasibility or value.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Zero Activity Permits Current-Master Removal
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Zero Activity Permits Current-Master Removal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact state transition that retains selected active columns outside the restricted master without mixing identifiers and stored records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\) be the column-identifier universe, \(A_k,P_k\subseteq\mathcal U\) be disjoint active and pooled sets, and \(S_k:P_k\to\mathcal D\) store reconstruction records. For an admitted set \(J_k\subseteq A_k\), define \[A_{k+1}=A_k\setminus J_k,\qquad P_{k+1}=P_k\cup J_k.\] Preserve \(S_k(j)\) for \(j\in P_k\) and store a record \(S_{k+1}(j)\) reproducing the canonical data of every \(j\in J_k\). The admission rule is external to this transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pooling moves identifiers from the active set to a disjoint pooled set while storing exact reconstruction records in a separate map.
assumptions_latex: Column identifiers are unique in \(\mathcal U\).
\(A_k\cap P_k=\varnothing\).
Every newly stored record passes the exact reconstruction certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_{k+1}\cap P_{k+1}=\varnothing,\qquad A_{k+1}\cup P_{k+1}=A_k\cup P_k.

notation.meaning: Map from pooled identifiers to reconstruction records

knowledge_statements.title: Type-Consistent Column-Pooling Transition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable coefficient-integrity certificate for exact column storage in a pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D(j)=(a_j,c_j,\ell_j,u_j,\eta_j)\) contain every canonical master datum of column \(j\), let \(s_j\) be its pool record, and let \(R\) be the deterministic reconstruction map. The record is integrity-valid exactly when \[R(s_j)=D(j)\] componentwise. Under this equality, inserting the reconstruction produces the original variable bounds, objective coefficient, master-column coefficients, and required metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pooled record is exact precisely when reconstruction reproduces every canonical master datum componentwise.
assumptions_latex: Column identifiers are unique.
The canonical record contains every column-specific datum used by the restricted master.
Equality is exact for the stored representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R(s_j)=D(j).

notation.meaning: Canonical full-master data of column j

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Pooled-Column Reconstruction Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admission, capacity, eviction, and deletion semantics for an exact reconstruction cache.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After solving a feasible restricted master over active columns \(A_k\), retain an optimal solution \(\bar\lambda\). Choose an admitted set \[J_k\subseteq\{j\in A_k\setminus C_k:\bar\lambda_j=0\},\] where \(C_k\) is any protected initialization or feasibility-core set. Verify exact reconstruction records for \(J_k\), then move their identifiers from the active set to the pool. If the pool exceeds capacity \(M\), evict records using a fixed deterministic priority. Eviction deletes only cached data: each evicted column remains in the full admissible universe and must remain covered by exact pricing. Thus admission preserves the current restricted-master optimum, while capacity control changes only future reuse cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pool only exactly zero columns outside a protected core, verify reconstruction, and treat eviction as cache deletion rather than removal from the priced universe.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master has an attained feasible optimum \(\bar\lambda\).
The protected set \(C_k\) remains active.
Every admitted record passes exact reconstruction, and \(M\) is a nonnegative integer.
Exact pricing continues to cover every admissible column, including evicted identifiers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A_k\setminus J_k)=v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A_k),\qquad |P_{k+1}|\le M,\qquad \mathcal U\text{ is unchanged}.

notation.meaning: Protected active initialization or feasibility core

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Preserving Bounded Column-Pool Policy
Column Pooling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retention of inactive generated columns outside the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an active index set \(A_k\) and a disjoint pool \(P_k\). After solving the restricted master, move any eligible inactive column \(j\in A_k\) to the pool by \[A_{k+1}=A_k\setminus\{j\},\qquad P_{k+1}=P_k\cup\{(a_j,c_j,\eta_j)\},\] where \(a_j\) is its master coefficient vector, \(c_j\) its objective coefficient, and \(\eta_j\) its lifecycle metadata. Pooling removes the variable from reoptimization but preserves sufficient data to reconstruct it exactly; it does not alter the full master’s column universe.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move eligible inactive columns from the restricted master into a disjoint store while retaining all coefficients and metadata needed for exact reconstruction.
assumptions_latex: Each stored record uniquely identifies a full-master column.
The active set and pool are disjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_{k+1}\cap P_{k+1}=\varnothing\), and every pooled column remains exactly reconstructible.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Column pooling is appropriately algorithmic, but no source supports the policy. Moreover, A_k contains indices while P_k is updated with tuple records, so the asserted disjointness A_{k+1} cap P_{k+1}=emptyset is ill-typed unless the pool is indexed consistently.

children.title: Column Reactivation
children.top_down_role: Return of retained columns to the active restricted master.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reactivation Need Not Improve the Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact transfer and a sibling policy predicting usefulness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact reconstruction and transfer alone do not guarantee strict objective improvement or positive use of the reactivated column. If an old optimal solution remains optimal after extension with \(\lambda_j=0\), then \[v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A_k\cup\{j\})=v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A_k),\] and an expanded-master optimum may still satisfy \(\lambda_j=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Returning a column to the master can leave both the optimum and that column's value unchanged.
assumptions_latex: An old optimal solution remains optimal for the expanded restricted master when extended with \(\lambda_j=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A_k\cup\{j\})=v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A_k)\quad\text{and an optimum may have }\lambda_j=0.

notation.meaning: Variable associated with the reactivated column

knowledge_statements.title: Reactivation Need Not Improve the Master

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity and Feasibility Under Exact Reactivation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of returning an unchanged pooled column to a minimization restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k\) be the active column set of a feasible minimization restricted master and let \(j\notin A_k\) be a pooled column reconstructed with its original coefficients and nonnegative variable. The expanded master over \(A_k\cup\{j\}\) contains every old feasible solution by assigning \(\lambda_j=0\). Consequently it remains feasible and \[v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A_k\cup\{j\})\le v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A_k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact reactivation preserves feasibility and cannot worsen a minimization restricted-master value.
assumptions_latex: The old restricted master is feasible.
The reactivated column has its original full-master data.
Its variable is nonnegative and may be set to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal F(A_k)\subseteq\mathcal F(A_k\cup\{j\}),\qquad v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A_k\cup\{j\})\le v_{\mathrm{RMP}}(A_k).

notation.meaning: Restricted-master feasible set embedded in the full variable space
Restricted-master optimal value for active set A

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity and Feasibility Under Exact Reactivation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type-consistent transfer of selected retained columns back to the active restricted master; eligibility is owned by the reentry-criteria sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k,P_k\subseteq\mathcal U\) be disjoint active and pooled identifier sets, let \(S_k\) store integrity-valid pool records, and choose \(J_k\subseteq P_k\) by an external reentry policy. Verify \(R(S_k(j))=D(j)\) for every \(j\in J_k\), then set \[A_{k+1}=A_k\cup J_k,\qquad P_{k+1}=P_k\setminus J_k.\] Insert each reconstructed column once and reoptimize the expanded restricted master. Solver-specific basis or state restoration is optional and does not alter the mathematical transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After verifying stored data, reactivation moves selected identifiers from the pool to the active master and reoptimizes; reentry selection is separate.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\cap P_k=\varnothing\).
Every selected record reconstructs the original column data exactly.
Duplicate active identifiers are rejected.
Reactivated variables may be assigned zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_{k+1}\cap P_{k+1}=\varnothing,\qquad A_{k+1}\cup P_{k+1}=A_k\cup P_k.

notation.meaning: Reconstructed master data for pooled column j

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Column-Reactivation Transition
Column Reactivation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact transfer of a retained column back into the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given active set \(A_k\), pool \(P_k\), current dual multiplier \(\pi_k\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), select a pooled column \(j\) satisfying the prescribed reentry predicate. Reconstruct its variable and coefficients, then set \[A_{k+1}=A_k\cup\{j\},\qquad P_{k+1}=P_k\setminus\{j\}.\] Warm-start and reoptimize the restricted master over \(A_{k+1}\). If no pooled column satisfies the predicate, leave both sets unchanged. Reactivation itself creates no new full-master column and must preserve the stored column’s original objective and constraint coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select an eligible pooled column, reconstruct it without changing its coefficients, return it to the active master, and warm-start reoptimization.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\cap P_k=\varnothing\).
Every pooled record is exactly reconstructible.
The reentry predicate is evaluated at the current master state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(j\in A_{k+1}\), \(j\notin P_{k+1}\), and its full-master data are unchanged.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The transfer operation matches column reactivation and algorithm is the correct role, but the decisive reentry predicate and warm-start behavior are delegated to unspecified policy and have no supporting citation.

children.title: Pool-Reentry Criteria
children.top_down_role: Structural signals governing when retained columns become relevant again.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pool Exhaustion Is Not Pricing Exhaustion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits the certificate obtained by testing only retained pooled columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_k\subseteq\mathcal C\) be the retained pool and let \(\bar c_j(\pi_k)\) be the complete reduced cost of column \(j\) for a minimization master. Then \[\min_{j\in P_k}\bar c_j(\pi_k)\ge-\varepsilon\] certifies only that no pooled column satisfies the reentry threshold. It implies \(\min_{j\in\mathcal C}\bar c_j(\pi_k)\ge-\varepsilon\) only if the pool is exhaustive or a valid lower bound for every omitted column is at least \(-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure to find an improving pooled column is not a global pricing certificate unless the pool is exhaustive or omitted columns have valid reduced-cost bounds.
assumptions_latex: P_k\subseteq\mathcal C.
\bar c_j(\pi_k)\text{ is evaluated under one consistent minimization-master convention}.
\varepsilon\ge0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{j\in P_k}\bar c_j\ge-\varepsilon\not\Rightarrow\min_{j\in\mathcal C}\bar c_j\ge-\varepsilon\quad\text{when }P_k\subsetneq\mathcal C.

notation.meaning: complete reduced cost of column j

knowledge_statements.title: Pool Exhaustion Is Not Pricing Exhaustion
Pool-Reentry Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost and feasibility predicate for reactivating a pooled column.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization master with equality-row multiplier \(\pi_k\), a pooled column \(j\) with objective coefficient \(c_j\) and master vector \(a_j\) satisfies reduced-cost reentry at tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) when \[j\in P_k,\qquad \bar c_j(\pi_k):=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi_k< -\varepsilon.\] If the master has additional dualized rows or variable bounds, their dual contributions must be included in \(\bar c_j\). The column may reenter only if its stored data remain valid and it is not already represented by an equivalent active column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid pooled column may reenter a minimization master when its complete current reduced cost is below the negative tolerance and no equivalent active column exists.
assumptions_latex: The master is posed as a minimization problem.
\(\pi_k\) is dual-feasible for the solved restricted master.
\(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar c_j(\pi_k)<-\varepsilon\) makes column \(j\) eligible for pool reentry.

notation.meaning: complete reduced cost of column j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the appropriate knowledge kind, and the displayed reduced-cost test is standard for the stated equality-form minimization convention. A source is still required, especially because additional rows, bounds, and duplicate equivalence are only described informally and can change the complete reduced-cost expression.

children.title: Column Lifecycle Control System
children.top_down_role: Control of inactive, redundant, or repeatedly generated columns.

children.title: Column Deletion
children.top_down_role: Removal of columns judged unnecessary for the active or retained representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for preserving the current restricted-master optimum under deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^\star\) be an optimal restricted-master solution over \(A_k\). If \(D_k\subseteq\{j\in A_k:x_j^\star=0\}\), then retaining every column in the support of \(x^\star\) leaves \(x^\star\) feasible after deleting \(D_k\). Therefore the reduced restricted master has the same optimal value. This certifies only the current solve, not permanent dispensability after later master changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting columns that are zero in a retained optimal solution preserves the current restricted-master value, but not their future dispensability.
assumptions_latex: The current restricted master is a minimization problem over \(A_k\).
\(x^\star\) is an optimal restricted-master solution.
Every column with \(x_j^\star\ne0\) is retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v(A_k\setminus D_k)=v(A_k).

notation.meaning: Restricted-master value over column set A

knowledge_statements.title: Current-Optimum Preservation Certificate
Column Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe removal of dispensable columns from a restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After reoptimization, choose a deletion set \(D_k\subseteq A_k\) containing only nonbasic columns whose values are zero within tolerance and whose removal preserves a designated feasible core \(F_k\subseteq A_k\). Set \[A_{k+1}=A_k\setminus D_k,\qquad F_k\subseteq A_{k+1}.\] Each deleted column is either stored in a reconstructible pool or remains generable by an exact pricing oracle. Reoptimize over \(A_{k+1}\). Deletion changes the restricted master but not the definition of the full master, and it cannot support termination unless pricing also checks omitted columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete only inactive columns while preserving a feasible core and recoverability; omitted columns must still be covered by pooling or exact pricing.
assumptions_latex: The current restricted master has a designated feasible core \(F_k\).
Every deleted column is recoverable or regenerable.
Termination uses exact pricing over omitted columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced master remains feasible, while the full-master column universe is unchanged.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits an algorithm leaf, but no source supports the deletion safeguards. Merely naming F_k a feasible core does not formally state that the master restricted to F_k is feasible, which is needed for the feasibility conclusion.

children.title: Column Aging
children.top_down_role: Tracking prolonged column inactivity as a retention signal.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Long Inactivity Does Not Imply Future Uselessness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive failure of interpreting column age as a permanent deletion certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min\sum_j c_j\lambda_j\quad\text{s.t.}\quad\sum_j\lambda_j=1,\quad\sum_j a_j\lambda_j=0,\quad\lambda\ge0.\] Initially let columns \(A=(a,c)=(0,0)\) and \(J=(1,0)\) be present. The unique feasible solution has \(\lambda_A=1\) and \(\lambda_J=0\), so \(J\) can remain inactive through arbitrarily many resolves. After adding \(N=(-1,-2)\), the optimum is \(\lambda_J=\lambda_N=1/2\), \(\lambda_A=0\), with value \(-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A column can remain zero for arbitrarily long and become essential after another column is added.
assumptions_latex: Columns are represented by their coupling and objective coefficients.
The restricted master is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_J^{\mathrm{old}}=0\quad\text{but}\quad\lambda_J^{\mathrm{new}}=\tfrac12.

notation.meaning: Initially active, aged, and subsequently added columns

knowledge_statements.title: Long Inactivity Does Not Imply Future Uselessness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy-neutral definition of consecutive inactivity age; the activity predicate must be declared by the implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a Boolean activity predicate \(A_j^k\) for column \(j\) after restricted-master solve \(k\). Define \(q_j^0=0\) and \[q_j^{k+1}=\begin{cases}0,&A_j^k\text{ is true},\\q_j^k+1,&A_j^k\text{ is false}.\end{cases}\] Thus \(q_j^{k+1}\) is the number of consecutive completed solves through iteration \(k\) in which the declared activity predicate failed. Primal-value, basis-status, and reduced-cost predicates define distinct aging variants and must not be interchanged implicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column age counts consecutive failures of an explicitly declared activity predicate; different activity predicates define different aging variants.
assumptions_latex: Each newly introduced column has age zero.
The activity predicate is evaluated once per completed restricted-master solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_j^{k+1}=\max\{t\ge0:A_j^k,A_j^{k-1},\ldots,A_j^{k-t+1}\text{ are all false}\}.

notation.meaning: Declared activity predicate for column j at solve k

knowledge_statements.title: Predicate-Based Column Age
Column Aging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration counter measuring persistent inactivity of an active column.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each active column \(j\) an age \(q_j^k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\). After restricted-master iteration \(k\), with primal value \(x_j^k\) and activity tolerance \(\delta\ge0\), update \[q_j^{k+1}=\begin{cases}0,&x_j^k>\delta,\\ q_j^k+1,&x_j^k\le\delta.\end{cases}\] A column becomes eligible for pooling or deletion when \(q_j^{k+1}\ge Q\), where \(Q\ge1\) is a chosen age threshold, subject to feasibility-core and recoverability safeguards. Aging alone does not certify that a column is globally dispensable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reset a column’s age when active and increment it when negligible; reaching a threshold permits lifecycle review but does not itself justify irreversible deletion.
assumptions_latex: \(q_j^0=0\) for each newly generated column.
\(\delta\ge0\) and \(Q\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_j^{k+1}\ge Q\) is an eligibility signal, not an optimality certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counter update is a plausible column-aging algorithm, but it is an implementation-specific convention with no citation. The domain and nonnegativity of x_j^k should also be made explicit for the activity test.

children.title: Duplicate Column Control
children.top_down_role: Recognition and handling of repeatedly generated equivalent columns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example showing that coefficient matching without cost equality is unsound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x_1+(1-\varepsilon)x_2:x_1+x_2=1,\ x_1,x_2\ge0\}\) with \(0<\varepsilon<1\). The columns have identical constraint coefficients but different costs. Merging them while retaining only column 1 gives value \(1\), whereas the full master has value \(1-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Columns with identical constraint coefficients but different costs are not duplicates; merging them changes the optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon<1\).
The erroneous policy ignores the objective-coefficient difference.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_{\mathrm{merged}}=1\ne1-\varepsilon=v_{\mathrm{full}}.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Approximate-Merge Counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact duplicate relation for nonnegative unrestricted-above linear-master columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a linear restricted master whose generated variables satisfy \(x_j\ge0\) with no individual upper bounds, two columns are exact duplicates when their complete master coefficient vectors, objective coefficients, and all metadata determining row or block membership are identical. Such variables may be replaced by one variable equal to their sum without changing the represented feasible set or objective values. Any differing bound, cost, coefficient, or membership datum prevents this certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Columns are exact duplicates only when every master-relevant coefficient, cost, domain, and membership datum agrees.
assumptions_latex: The compared generated variables are nonnegative and have no individual upper bounds.
The record includes every coefficient and metadata item affecting the master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z\sim z'\Longrightarrow\text{merging their variables by summation preserves the master feasible set and objective}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Master-Column Equivalence
Duplicate Column Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical equivalence test preventing repeated active master columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a column record be \(z_j=(a_j,c_j,b_j)\), comprising its master coefficient vector, objective coefficient, and bound or block metadata. With canonicalization map \(\kappa\), a candidate \(z\) is a duplicate of an active or pooled column exactly when \[\kappa(z)=\kappa(z_j)\quad\text{for some }j\in A_k\cup P_k.\] Duplicate control rejects the candidate or merges its metadata without adding another master variable. If floating-point data are compared approximately, the chosen tolerances must preserve all coefficients relevant to feasibility, objective value, and block identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalize every candidate and reject or merge it when an equivalent active or pooled record already exists, preserving feasibility, cost, and block identity.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa(z)=\kappa(z')\) only for master-equivalent column records.
The lookup covers both active and pooled records.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No accepted candidate duplicates an equivalence class already represented in \(A_k\cup P_k\).

notation.meaning: all retained active and pooled columns

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits duplicate control, but no source supports the canonicalization policy. The assumption only says equal canonical forms imply master equivalence; the claimed exact duplicate test also requires every intended equivalent pair to receive the same canonical form.

children.title: Master-Basis Reoptimization Cross-Index
children.top_down_role: Boundary to basis updates, warm starts, degeneracy handling, and numerical LP reoptimization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of appending columns on an existing restricted-master basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) with a feasible basis \(B\). Appending columns preserves the old basic feasible solution by assigning every new variable value zero. If \(B\) was optimal before insertion, it remains optimal for the enlarged master exactly when every appended column has nonnegative reduced cost \[\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}B^{-\mathsf T}c_B\ge0.\] Thus insertion preserves primal feasibility but can destroy dual feasibility and basis optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding columns leaves the old basic solution feasible, but a negative reduced cost makes its basis nonoptimal for the enlarged master.
assumptions_latex: \text{The master is an equality-form minimization LP with nonnegative variables}.
B\text{ is a feasible basis before insertion}.
B\text{ is optimal for the pre-insertion master when applying the optimality equivalence}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_B=B^{-1}b\text{ remains feasible, and }B\text{ remains optimal}\iff\bar c_j\ge0\text{ for every appended }j.

notation.meaning: cost vector of the basic variables
reduced cost of an appended column

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Preserving Column Insertion
Master-Basis Reoptimization Cross-Index
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic interface between column insertion and simplex-basis reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a restricted master in equality form \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), let \(B\) be a nonsingular basis matrix with basic costs \(c_B\). Its reoptimization state is represented by \[x_B=B^{-1}b,\qquad \pi=B^{-\mathsf T}c_B,\qquad \bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi.\] A newly inserted column \(a_j\) is transformed as \(d_j=B^{-1}a_j\). Warm-start reoptimization retains \(B\) when it remains valid; a pivot replaces one basic column using \(d_j\). Degeneracy handling and numerical refactorization belong to the LP-basis solver interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent the warm start by a nonsingular master basis, its basic solution and dual multiplier; transform inserted columns through the basis before pivoting.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is an equality-form linear program.
\(B\) is a nonsingular submatrix of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((B^{-1}b,B^{-\mathsf T}c_B,B^{-1}a_j)\) supplies the algebraic state required for basis reoptimization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The basis formulas are standard and representation fits this cross-index topic, but the record has no inspectable citation for simplex warm starts, pivots, or basis reoptimization.

children.title: Column-Generation Degradation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Geometric, oracle, and numerical causes of slow or unreliable master progress.

children.title: Early-Phase Dual Instability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Unstable prices and slow early identification of useful columns.

children.title: Dual Oscillation
children.top_down_role: Unstable movement of restricted-master prices across generation rounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Oscillation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed diagnostic for unstable restricted-master dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given dual iterates \(\pi_0,\pi_1,\ldots\), window length \(W\ge2\), scale \(s_k:=\max\{1,\|\pi_k\|_2\}\), and threshold \(\theta>0\), declare windowed dual oscillation at iteration \(k\ge W\) when \[\max_{k-W<i\le k}\frac{\|\pi_i-\pi_{i-1}\|_2}{s_{i-1}}>\theta\quad\text{and}\quad \|\pi_k-\pi_{k-W}\|_2<\min_{k-W<i\le k}\|\pi_i-\pi_{i-1}\|_2.\] The first inequality detects large successive motion; the second detects return toward an earlier multiplier rather than sustained displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual oscillation is diagnosed when recent multiplier steps are large but the current multiplier returns closer to its window-start value than any individual step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed predicate flags recurrent, nonprogressive motion of the dual sequence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predicate is an uncited, parameter-dependent diagnostic rather than an established characterization of dual oscillation. Its first comparison is normalized while the return comparison is unnormalized, so its behavior is also scale-dependent despite the stated normalization.

children.title: Heading-In Delay
children.top_down_role: Slow early identification of productive price regions and useful columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Heading-In Delay
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Early iterations with improving columns but insufficient bound progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_k\) be the valid restricted-master lower bound for a minimization problem, let \(r_k<0\) be the most negative reduced cost returned by exact pricing, and choose \(T\ge1\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(\eta>0\). A heading-in delay of length \(T\) occurs at iteration \(k\ge T\) when \[r_i\le-\varepsilon\ \text{ for every }i=k-T+1,\ldots,k,\qquad L_k-L_{k-T}\le\eta.\] Thus improving columns are repeatedly available while the certified bound changes by at most \(\eta\); the condition is diagnostic and does not imply incorrectness or nonconvergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heading-in delay occurs when exact pricing repeatedly finds meaningful improving columns but the valid master bound advances by no more than a chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The full problem is a minimization problem.
Each \(L_i\) is a valid comparable lower bound.
Pricing is exact over the diagnostic window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent negative reduced costs together with \(L_k-L_{k-T}\le\eta\) diagnose delayed early progress.

notation.meaning: minimum reduced cost returned by pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary is appropriate for heading-in delay, but the proposed diagnostic has no source. In ordinary minimization column generation, the restricted-master objective is an upper bound, not automatically a lower bound; the construction and validity of L_k therefore must be specified and supported before the criterion can be trusted.

children.title: Early-Progress Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Signals distinguishing unstable price movement from delayed entry into a productive regime.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Raw Dual-Motion Diagnostics Are Representation Dependent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits interpretation of multiplier-distance components in early-progress diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an equality row \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\), replacing it by \(t a_i^{\mathsf T}x=t b_i\) with \(t>0\) leaves the primal feasible set unchanged and maps a corresponding dual coordinate to \(\pi_i/t\), while preserving the product contributing to every reduced cost. Consequently, thresholds based on raw norms \(\|\pi_k-\pi_{k-1}\|\) can change under an equivalent row scaling. Moreover, when the restricted-master dual optimum is nonunique, selecting different optimal multipliers can create apparent motion without a change in master value or pricing information. Such a threshold diagnoses intrinsic instability only after row scaling, the norm, and the dual-solution selection rule are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Raw changes in master dual vectors are not representation-invariant; equivalent row scaling or switching among optimal dual solutions can create or suppress an oscillation signal.
assumptions_latex: \text{The rescaled equality replaces, rather than supplements, the original row}.
\text{Compared dual vectors use the coordinate system and selection rule declared by the diagnostic}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\pi_k-\pi_{k-1}\|\text{-based thresholds are not intrinsic without fixed scaling and dual selection}.

notation.meaning: dual coordinate associated with the original equality row

knowledge_statements.title: Raw Dual-Motion Diagnostics Are Representation Dependent
Early-Progress Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A windowed diagnostic for unstable early column-generation progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For iterations \(k=0,\ldots,K\), let \(z_k\) be the restricted-master objective and \(\pi_k\) an optimal master dual vector; for \(k=1,\ldots,K\), let \(r_k^*\) be the minimum exact reduced cost returned by pricing. Given an integer \(W\) with \(1\le W\le K\) and tolerances \(\delta_z,\delta_\pi,\delta_r>0\), declare early progress unstable over the last \(W\) iterations when
\[
|z_K-z_{K-W}|\le\delta_z,\qquad \max_{K-W<k\le K}\|\pi_k-\pi_{k-1}\|>\delta_\pi,\qquad \min_{K-W<k\le K}r_k^*<-\delta_r.
\]
This diagnostic records objective stagnation and substantial dual variation while exact pricing finds at least one materially improving column in the window.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Early progress is diagnosed as unstable when the master objective stagnates, dual solutions vary substantially, and exact pricing finds at least one materially negative reduced cost during the diagnostic window.
assumptions_latex: \(z_k\) and \(\pi_k\) are computed consistently for \(k=0,\ldots,K\).
\(r_k^*\) is obtained by exact pricing for \(k=1,\ldots,K\).
\(W\) is an integer satisfying \(1\le W\le K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The diagnostic is triggered when \(|z_K-z_{K-W}|\le\delta_z\), \(\max_{K-W<k\le K}\|\pi_k-\pi_{k-1}\|>\delta_\pi\), and \(\min_{K-W<k\le K}r_k^*<-\delta_r\).

notation.meaning: Restricted-master dual vector at iteration k.
Minimum exact reduced cost at iteration k.
Number of iterations in the diagnostic window.

children.title: Degeneracy-Driven Tailing-Off Boundary
children.top_down_role: Slow late-stage closure and weak progress along degenerate master faces.

children.title: Column-Generation Tailing-Off
children.top_down_role: Slow late-stage improvement in restricted-master objectives or bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Tailing-Off
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic progress criterion for late-stage column-generation stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_k\) be the monotone restricted-master bounds converging to \(z_*\), and define the remaining gap \(g_k=|z_k-z_*|\). Column generation tails off along an infinite index set \(I\) when \(g_k>0\) and
\[
\lim_{\substack{k\to\infty\\k\in I}}\frac{|z_{k+1}-z_k|}{g_k}=0.
\]
Thus individual master improvements become negligible relative to the unresolved gap. This condition describes degradation rather than nonconvergence: \(z_k\) may still converge to \(z_*\), but no uniform positive fraction of the remaining gap is removed per iteration along \(I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tailing-off occurs when successive bound improvements become negligible compared with the remaining optimality gap, even though the bounds may still converge.
assumptions_latex: \(z_k\to z_*\) monotonically.
\(g_k>0\) on the index set \(I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty,\,k\in I}|z_{k+1}-z_k|/g_k=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed ratio-limit definition is mathematically coherent and fits the failure-boundary leaf, but it is a particular formalization of tailing-off rather than a universally standard definition. A direct column-generation source is required.

children.title: Restricted-Master Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Weak progress associated with alternative master solutions on degenerate faces.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degeneracy Does Not Imply Multiple Optima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates restricted-master basis degeneracy from primal nonuniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min\{0:x_1=1,\ x_2=0,\ x_1,x_2\ge0\}.\] Its constraint matrix is \(I_2\), so its only feasible point and hence its unique primal optimum is \((1,0)\). The unique basis \(B=I_2\) nevertheless has basic vector \(x_B=(1,0)\), which contains a zero component. Thus its optimal basis is degenerate despite uniqueness of the feasible point and optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted master can have a degenerate optimal basis even when its feasible point and primal optimum are unique.
assumptions_latex: \text{The LP is in equality standard form}.
\text{Basis degeneracy means that at least one basic variable is zero}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{basis degeneracy}\not\Rightarrow\text{multiple primal optima}.
knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy Does Not Imply Multiple Optima
Restricted-Master Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal degeneracy of an optimal basis of a linear restricted master in standard form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the restricted master
\[
\min\{c_J^{\mathsf T}\lambda:A_J\lambda=b,\ \lambda\ge0\},
\]
where \(A_J\) has full row rank and \(B\subseteq J\) indexes a nonsingular square basis matrix \(A_B\). The basic solution associated with \(B\) has \(\lambda_B=A_B^{-1}b\) and \(\lambda_j=0\) for \(j\notin B\). A feasible basis \(B\) is degenerate when at least one component of \(\lambda_B\) is zero. An optimal restricted-master basis is degenerate when it is feasible and optimal and has a zero basic variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal restricted-master basis is degenerate when its associated optimal basic feasible solution has at least one zero basic variable.
assumptions_latex: \(A_J\) has full row rank.
\(A_B\) is square and nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible basis \(B\) is degenerate exactly when \((A_B^{-1}b)_i=0\) for some basic index \(i\).

notation.meaning: Basis selected from the restricted columns.

children.title: Degeneracy-Driven Slowdown
children.top_down_role: Links master degeneracy to repeated columns with limited incremental value.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Driven Slowdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of guaranteed objective progress under degenerate master pivots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In a primal-simplex restricted master, let an entering column have reduced cost \(\bar c_j<0\), direction \(d=B^{-1}a_j\), and ratio-test step
\[
\alpha=\min_{i:d_i>0}\frac{(\lambda_B)_i}{d_i}.
\]
The objective change is \(\alpha\bar c_j\). If a minimizing row has \((\lambda_B)_i=0\), then \(\alpha=0\), so an improving column can cause a basis change without changing the master objective. Repeated zero-step pivots therefore admit arbitrarily many column-generation iterations with no positive objective improvement; without a nondegeneracy or progress condition, no uniform per-iteration decrease follows from \(\bar c_j<0\) alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a degenerate master solution, a negative-reduced-cost column may enter with zero step, permitting repeated basis changes without objective improvement.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is solved by primal-simplex pivots.
The entering column satisfies \(\bar c_j<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the ratio test yields \(\alpha=0\), then \(\alpha\bar c_j=0\), and strict per-pivot progress fails.

notation.meaning: Reduced cost of the entering column.
Basic direction induced by the entering column.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A zero simplex step and zero objective change are standard, but repeated zero-step pivots do not by themselves establish arbitrarily many column-generation iterations because pivots within one restricted-master solve are not necessarily separate column-generation iterations. A direct source and a more carefully scoped iteration claim are needed.

children.title: Pricing Reliability Bottleneck
children.top_down_role: Expensive or poorly informed pricing that dominates computation.

children.title: Pricing Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Pricing workloads that dominate column-generation runtime.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A measurable computational bottleneck in the column-generation pricing stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For iteration \(k\), let \(T_k^{P}\) be total pricing time and \(T_k^{M}\) restricted-master solution time, including all pricing blocks attempted before the next master update. For a threshold \(\rho\in(0,1)\), pricing is a \(\rho\)-bottleneck over iterations \(I\) when
\[
\frac{\sum_{k\in I}T_k^{P}}{\sum_{k\in I}(T_k^{P}+T_k^{M})}\ge\rho.
\]
If pricing blocks run in parallel, \(T_k^{P}\) denotes elapsed critical-path time rather than the sum of processor times. The condition is computational and does not itself imply incorrect reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing is a bottleneck when it consumes at least a chosen fraction of total master-and-pricing elapsed time over a specified iteration set.
assumptions_latex: All measured times use the same elapsed-time convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pricing-time fraction over \(I\) is at least \(\rho\).

notation.meaning: Elapsed pricing time at iteration k.
Elapsed restricted-master solution time at iteration k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The timing ratio is internally precise and fits a condition leaf, but it is an operationally chosen bottleneck metric with a user-selected threshold. A performance-diagnostics source or explicit standard-field rationale is required.

children.title: Pricing Miscalibration
children.top_down_role: Poorly informed pricing that returns unhelpful or incorrectly prioritized columns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Miscalibration caused by approximate solution of the pricing problem even when the current master dual vector is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a fixed current dual vector \(\pi\), let \(v=\inf_{p\in P}\bar c_\pi(p)\). If pricing returns a feasible \(\widehat p\in P\), its oracle suboptimality is \(\delta=\bar c_\pi(\widehat p)-v\ge0\). For tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the returned pricing value is \(\varepsilon\)-miscalibrated when \(\delta>\varepsilon\). In particular, an improving column is hidden when \(v<0\le\bar c_\pi(\widehat p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with the correct dual vector, an approximate pricing solve is miscalibrated when its returned reduced cost exceeds the true pricing infimum beyond tolerance and may miss a negative minimum.
assumptions_latex: \widehat p\in P
v=\inf_{p\in P}\bar c_\pi(p)>-\infty
Pricing and the comparison minimum use the same current dual vector \(\pi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta=\bar c_\pi(\widehat p)-v\ge0;\quad v<0\le\bar c_\pi(\widehat p)\text{ is a false nonimprovement report.}

notation.meaning: True pricing infimum at the current dual vector.
Feasible column returned by the approximate oracle.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Oracle Suboptimality Miscalibration
Pricing Miscalibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mismatch between reported and true reduced costs in approximate pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a column \(a
_j\) with cost \(c_j\), let the true master dual vector be \(\pi\) and let pricing use \(\widehat\pi\), producing \(\widehat r_j=c_j-\widehat\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\) instead of \(r_j=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\). Given tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), pricing is miscalibrated on a candidate set \(S\) when
\[
\sup_{j\in S}|\widehat r_j-r_j|=\sup_{j\in S}|(\widehat\pi-\pi)^{\mathsf T}a_j|>\varepsilon.
\]
A sign-changing miscalibration occurs when some \(j\in S\) satisfies \(r_j<0\le\widehat r_j\) or \(\widehat r_j<0\le r_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing is miscalibrated when reduced costs computed from an approximate or stale dual differ from true reduced costs beyond tolerance, possibly reversing their signs.
assumptions_latex: Column costs and vectors use the same normalization in true and approximate pricing.
\(S\) is the candidate set being assessed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Miscalibration holds when \(\sup_{j\in S}|\widehat r_j-r_j|>\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: True reduced cost of column j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost error identity and sign-change condition are correct, and the knowledge kind fits the leaf. No source supports this particular definition of pricing miscalibration.

children.title: Bottleneck-Induced Mispricing
children.top_down_role: Accuracy losses or stale guidance arising from constrained pricing effort.

assumptions_latex: \(L\) is a valid lower bound on the reduced-cost infimum over the entire column universe.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\ge-\varepsilon\ \Longrightarrow\ \forall j\in\mathcal U,\ r_\pi(j)\ge-\varepsilon.

notation.meaning: Certified global lower bound returned by pricing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate under which incomplete pricing effort supports an approximate or exact pricing conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_\pi^\star=\inf_{j\in\mathcal U}r_\pi(j)\). If a truncated pricing procedure returns a rigorous global lower bound \(L\le r_\pi^\star\), then \(L\ge-\varepsilon\) certifies \(r_\pi(j)\ge-\varepsilon\) for every \(j\in\mathcal U\). In particular, \(L\ge0\) certifies full-master dual feasibility. The best inspected reduced cost is an upper bound on \(r_\pi^\star\) and cannot provide this certificate by itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incomplete pricing is certifying only when it supplies a global lower bound on the best possible reduced cost; an inspected incumbent is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Lower-Bound Certificate for Truncated Pricing
knowledge_statements.title: Global Lower-Bound Certificate for Truncated Pricing

assumptions_latex: The pricing search terminates after inspecting \(S=\{1\}\).
Both columns belong to the admissible full universe.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{j\in S}r_\pi(j)=0\quad\text{while}\quad\min_{j\in\mathcal U}r_\pi(j)=-1.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example of an improving column outside the inspected pricing region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U=\{1,2\}\) and, at the current dual vector, let \(r_\pi(1)=0\) and \(r_\pi(2)=-1\). If an effort cap permits inspection only of \(S=\{1\}\), the truncated search reports no negative reduced cost even though column 2 is improving.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A capped current-dual search can inspect a zero-reduced-cost column and miss an uninspected negative-reduced-cost column.
knowledge_statements.title: Current-Dual Effort-Cap Mispricing Example

assumptions_latex: \(S\subsetneq\mathcal U\).
Reduced costs are evaluated using the current dual vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{j\in S}r_\pi(j)\ge0\ \not\Rightarrow\ \min_{j\in\mathcal U}r_\pi(j)\ge0.

notation.meaning: Subset inspected before the pricing effort cap is reached
Reduced cost of column j at the current dual vector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Current-dual mispricing caused by an effort cap that searches only part of the admissible column universe.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal U\) be the admissible column universe, \(S\subsetneq\mathcal U\) the subset inspected under an effort cap, and \(r_\pi(j)\) the current-dual reduced cost. Then \(\min_{j\in S}r_\pi(j)\ge0\) does not imply \(\min_{j\in\mathcal U}r_\pi(j)\ge0\). Exhaustion of the capped region is therefore not a full-pricing certificate unless an additional bound covers \(\mathcal U\setminus S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative reduced costs on an effort-capped subset do not rule out an improving column elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted Pricing Search Does Not Certify Full Pricing
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Pricing Search Does Not Certify Full Pricing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint current-dual certificate when pricing uses stale information and returns only a rigorous global solve bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_{\pi}(j)=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\), let pricing use stale dual \(\pi'\), and suppose it returns \(L'\le\inf_{j\in\mathcal U}r_{\pi'}(j)\). If \(|(\pi-\pi')^{\mathsf T}a_j|\le E\) for every \(j\in\mathcal U\), then \[\inf_{j\in\mathcal U}r_{\pi}(j)\ge L'-E.\] Hence \(L'-E\ge-\varepsilon\) certifies that every current-dual reduced cost is at least \(-\varepsilon\); \(L'-E\ge0\) certifies current full-master dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a uniform dual-staleness error from a rigorous stale-dual pricing lower bound yields a valid current-dual pricing certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(r_{\pi}(j)=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\) for every admissible column.
\(L'\) is a valid global lower bound on the stale-dual pricing infimum.
The uniform drift bound holds over the entire column universe.
\(E,\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L'-E\le\inf_{j\in\mathcal U}r_{\pi}(j).

notation.meaning: Uniform reduced-cost error bound from dual drift

knowledge_statements.title: Combined Staleness-and-Truncation Pricing Certificate
Bottleneck-Induced Mispricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost sign failure caused by delayed or truncated pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose pricing uses a stale dual vector \(\pi_{k-d}\) because iteration-\(k\) pricing is delayed or truncated. For column \(a_j\), the stale and current reduced costs satisfy
\[
\widehat r_{j,k}-r_{j,k}=(\pi_k-\pi_{k-d})^{\mathsf T}a_j,
\qquad
|\widehat r_{j,k}-r_{j,k}|\le\|\pi_k-\pi_{k-d}\|_*\|a_j\|.
\]
If \(r_{j,k}<0\) and \((\pi_k-\pi_{k-d})^{\mathsf T}a_j\ge-r_{j,k}\), then \(\widehat r_{j,k}\ge0\), so the bottleneck hides an improving column. Any reliable sign decision therefore requires an error bound strictly smaller than the magnitude of the relevant negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delayed pricing can hide an improving column when dual drift creates an error at least as large as that column’s negative reduced-cost margin.
assumptions_latex: Pricing at iteration \(k\) uses \(\pi_{k-d}\) with \(d\ge1\).
The primal and dual norms are paired.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \((\pi_k-\pi_{k-d})^{\mathsf T}a_j\ge-r_{j,k}>0\), then \(r_{j,k}<0\le\widehat r_{j,k}\).

notation.meaning: Stale dual vector used by pricing.
Reduced cost computed with the stale dual.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stale-dual identity, norm bound, and sign-flip condition are correct. Direct support is needed for attributing stale pricing to a bottleneck and for the claimed reliability boundary in an asynchronous or truncated-pricing setting.

children.title: False Termination under Inexact Pricing
children.top_down_role: Premature stopping when approximate pricing misses existing improving columns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric strengthening of the immutable two-column example, showing that an uncertified pricing miss has no finite worst-case gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(M>0\), consider \(\min\{-M\lambda_2:\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1,\ \lambda\ge0\}\), initially restricted to column \(1\). The restricted optimum and its dual multiplier are zero, while the omitted column has reduced cost \(-M\) and the full-master optimum is \(-M\). An inexact oracle inspecting only column \(1\) reports minimum reduced cost zero; if that report triggers termination, the returned objective gap is \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling the missed column produces false termination with an arbitrarily large objective gap.
assumptions_latex: Termination accepts an uncertified no-improvement report from a search that omits column \(2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_{\mathrm{RMP}}-z_{\mathrm{MP}}=M,\text{ and hence no finite worst-case gap bound follows from the report alone.}

notation.meaning: Arbitrary positive cost and gap scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrarily Large False-Termination Gap
False Termination under Inexact Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-column master exhibiting premature stopping after an inexact pricing miss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the full master
\[
\min\{0\lambda_1-\lambda_2:\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1,\ \lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\}.
\]
Start with only column \(1\). The restricted master has value \(0\) and dual multiplier \(\pi=0\). The omitted column has true reduced cost \(r_2=-1-\pi=-1\), so adding it yields the full-master optimum \(-1\). An inexact pricing oracle that examines only column \(1\) reports minimum reduced cost \(0\). A stopping rule accepting that report terminates at value \(0\), although an improving column exists and the optimality gap equals \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pricing oracle that misses an omitted column of reduced cost −1 can certify zero reduced cost and stop one unit above the true optimum.
assumptions_latex: Termination relies solely on the inexact oracle reporting no negative reduced cost.
The initial restricted master contains only column \(1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates at value \(0\) although the full-master optimum is \(-1\).

notation.meaning: Weights of the existing and omitted columns.
Dual multiplier for the convexity equation.
True reduced cost of the omitted column.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-column counterexample is self-contained, mathematically correct, and appropriately classified as a counterexample, but the evidence contract requires a source or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Benders Decomposition Interface
children.top_down_role: Projection architecture organized around complicating variables, a master representation, and subordinate value information.

children.title: Complicating-Variable Partition
children.top_down_role: Selection of coordinating variables whose fixation exposes an easier subordinate problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Complicating-Variable Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders partition of master variables from subordinate variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the optimization problem
\[
\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+d^{\mathsf T}y:x\in X,\ y\in Y,\ Ax+By\ge b\},
\]
a complicating-variable partition designates \(x\) as the master block and \(y\) as the subordinate block when, for every fixed \(x\in X\), the residual problem
\[
\inf\{d^{\mathsf T}y:y\in Y,\ By\ge b-Ax\}
\]
belongs to a class that can be solved or dualized more directly than the original joint problem. The partition is structural: fixing \(x\) must remove the couplings assigned to the master while leaving a well-defined subordinate feasibility-and-value problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complicating variables are the master variables whose fixation removes coupling and exposes a tractable subordinate optimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) specify the admissible master and subordinate domains.
Fixing \(x\) leaves a well-defined subordinate problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The blocks \(x\) and \(y\) form a complicating-variable partition with \(x\) coordinating the subordinate problem.

children.title: Subordinate Value-Function Representation
children.top_down_role: The subordinate optimization value viewed over master decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Subordinate Value-Function Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real subordinate value function over master decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(x\in X\), define the subordinate value function
\[
Q(x)=\inf\{d^{\mathsf T}y:y\in Y,\ By\ge b-Ax\}.
\]
Use the extended-real conventions \(Q(x)=+\infty\) when the subordinate constraints are infeasible and \(Q(x)=-\infty\) when the subordinate objective is unbounded below. Then the joint problem is represented exactly as
\[
\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(c^{\mathsf T}x+Q(x)\bigr).
\]
When the original problem has an attained finite optimum, any minimizing \(x^*\) together with a subordinate minimizer attaining \(Q(x^*)\) forms an optimal joint solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Master Epigraph Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear Benders optimality-cut representation for a feasible bounded subordinate LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
Q(x)=\min\{d^{\mathsf T}y:By\ge b-Ax,\ y\ge0\},
\qquad
P=\{\pi\ge0:B^{\mathsf T}\pi\le d\}.
\]
If the subordinate problem is feasible with finite value and strong duality holds for every considered \(x\), then
\[
Q(x)=\max_{\pi\in P}\pi^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax).
\]
Consequently its epigraph is
\[
\{(x,\theta):x\in X,\ \theta\ge\pi^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\ \text{for every }\pi\in P\}.
\]
If \(P\) is a polyhedron whose relevant maximum is attained at an extreme point, it suffices to impose the inequalities for its extreme points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong LP duality represents the subordinate epigraph by Benders optimality cuts indexed by dual-feasible points, or by relevant extreme points.

Linear-programming strong duality holds.
The extreme-point reduction is used only when a relevant dual maximum is attained at an extreme point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}Q=\{(x,\theta):\theta\ge\pi^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\text{ for all }\pi\in P\}\) on \(X\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Structure of the Recourse Epigraph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural consequence of the linear Benders epigraph representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On a polyhedral domain where the subordinate LP is feasible and finite,
\[
Q(x)=\max_{\pi\in P}\pi^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax).
\]
Thus \(Q\) is convex polyhedral. When the relevant maxima are attained at extreme points,
\[
Q(x)=\max_{\pi\in E(P)}\pi^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax),
\]
so the recourse value is piecewise affine and its epigraph is the intersection of the corresponding halfspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite linear-recourse value function is a convex polyhedral, piecewise-affine maximum of dual extreme-point supports.

knowledge_statements.title: Master Feasibility Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-ray representation of Benders master feasibility cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(x\), consider the subordinate system \(By\ge b-Ax\), \(y\ge0\), and define the cone
\[
R=\{r\ge0:B^{\mathsf T}r\le0\}.
\]
Farkas' alternative gives
\[
\exists y\ge0:\ By\ge b-Ax
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
r^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\le0\ \text{for every }r\in R.
\]
Hence the master-feasible set is represented by
\[
\{x\in X:r^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\le0\ \text{for every }r\in R\}.
\]
When \(R\) is polyhedral, it suffices to impose one feasibility cut for each extreme ray of \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Farkas’ alternative represents subordinate feasibility by Benders cuts indexed by the extreme rays of a dual recession cone.
assumptions_latex: The subordinate feasibility system is linear.
The extreme-ray reduction assumes the cone \(R\) is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Subordinate feasibility is equivalent to \(r^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\le0\) for every \(r\in R\).

notation.meaning: Master decision whose subordinate feasibility is tested.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound and monotonicity property of valid finite Benders master refinements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L_k\) be the finite master optimum when the master contains only valid point and ray cuts. Every feasible solution of the full projected problem satisfies those cuts, hence
\[
L_k\le z^*.
\]
If cuts are retained and \(P_k\subseteq P_{k+1}\), \(R_k\subseteq R_{k+1}\), then
\[
L_k\le L_{k+1}\le z^*.
\]
This interpretation requires each finite master to be feasible and bounded below; an otherwise free recourse epigraph variable therefore needs a valid initial lower bound or sufficient cuts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global optimality-gap certificate obtained from transferred Benders master and incumbent bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If a valid bounded Benders master has value \(L\), and a master decision \(\hat x\) with a recourse-feasible response \(\hat y\) has full objective value
\[
U=c^{\mathsf T}\hat x+q^{\mathsf T}\hat y,
\]
then
\[
L\le z^*\le U,
\qquad 0\le U-z^*\le U-L.
\]
Thus \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality. A subproblem primal value transfers to \(U\) only with full master and recourse feasibility, while a master value transfers to \(L\) only when the master is bounded and every installed cut is valid.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination of Exact Status-Conditioned Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination of exact linear status-conditioned Benders refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E_P\) be the finite set of relevant dual extreme points and \(E_R\) the finite set of extreme rays. Suppose every nonterminal exact refinement selects a violated extreme-point or extreme-ray cut. A previously stored cut cannot be violated by the current master solution, so every strict refinement adds a new member of \(E_P\cup E_R\). Consequently at most
\[
|E_P|+|E_R|
\]
strict refinement iterations occur, followed by at most one certification iteration. When no feasibility cut is violated and the exact recourse value is no greater than the master epigraph estimate, the master solution is globally optimal. This conclusion does not extend without additional safeguards to uncertified statuses, invalid cuts, non-extreme oracle outputs, cut deletion permitting repetition, or inexact separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact linear Benders refinement using extreme-point and extreme-ray oracles terminates finitely because every nonterminal iteration adds a previously absent cut from finite families.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal Dual Face and Cut Tightness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and tightness characterization for linear-recourse optimality cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q(x)=\max_{\pi\in D}\pi^\top(h-Tx)\) and a trial point \(\bar x\) with finite attained recourse dual value, every \(\pi\in D\) gives a valid cut \(\theta\ge\pi^\top(h-Tx)\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact normalized separation oracle for the linear extreme-ray feasibility-cut family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\{r\in\mathbb R_+^m:W^{\mathsf T}r\le0\}\), choose \(e\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\), and solve
\[
\sigma(\bar x)=\max\{r^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x):r\in C,\ e^{\mathsf T}r=1\}.
\]
If the normalized slice is empty, then \(C=\{0\}\). Otherwise, \(\sigma(\bar x)>0\) exactly when recourse at \(\bar x\) is infeasible, and any optimizer \(\bar r\) supplies the violated valid cut \(\bar r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0\). If \(\sigma(\bar x)\le0\), all ray inequalities hold. Without normalization, positive-violation maximization over the homogeneous cone is unbounded.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible Recourse Does Not Ensure a Finite Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundedness boundary within the complete-recourse regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Nonemptiness of \(Y(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) removes the need for feasibility cuts but does not ensure that \(Q(x)=\inf\{q^\top y:y\in Y(x)\}\) is finite. For example, let \(Y(x)=\{y\in\mathbb R:y\ge0\}\) for every \(x\) and let \(q=-1\). Recourse is feasible everywhere, but \(Q(x)=\inf_{y\ge0}(-y)=-\infty\). A finite-valued optimality-cut system therefore additionally requires subordinate boundedness or an equivalent dual-feasibility condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete feasibility eliminates feasibility cuts, but a separate boundedness condition is needed for finite recourse values and meaningful optimality cuts.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y(x)\ne\varnothing\ \forall x\in X\quad\not\Longrightarrow\quad Q(x)>-\infty\ \forall x\in X.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Recourse Does Not Ensure a Finite Value

assumptions_latex: The master domain is \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and recourse constraints are \(Wy\ge h-Tx\) with \(y\ge0\).
The recourse objective is bounded below for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under complete recourse, the Benders master needs optimality cuts but no feasibility cuts on \(X\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard complete-recourse condition in two-stage linear optimization
