knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete recourse relative to the prescribed master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(Y(x)=\{y\ge0:Wy\ge h-Tx\}\). The model has complete recourse on \(X\) precisely when
\[
Y(x)\ne\varnothing\qquad\text{for every }x\in X.
\]
Equivalently, every feasibility-cut inequality satisfies
\[
r^\top(h-Tx)\le0\qquad\text{for every }x\in X\text{ and every }r\in C,
\]
where \(C=\{r\ge0:W^\top r\le0\}\). Thus the effective domain of \(Q\) contains \(X\), and no master point in \(X\) can be removed by a recourse feasibility cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete recourse means every master-feasible decision admits a feasible subordinate solution, so feasibility cuts are redundant on the master domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Complete-Recourse Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is appropriate for this regime leaf, and the local definition correctly expresses recourse feasibility for every x in X. A source is needed both for the equivalence with redundant feasibility cuts and to confirm whether this taxonomy uses 'complete recourse' for what is often called 'relatively complete recourse.'

children.title: Incomplete-Recourse Regime
children.top_down_role: Models requiring simultaneous approximation of subordinate feasibility and value.

assumptions_latex: The master domain is \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(Y(x)=\{y\ge0:Wy\ge h-Tx\}\).
The recourse objective is bounded below whenever \(Y(x)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Incomplete recourse requires simultaneous outer approximation of \(\operatorname{dom}Q\) and lower approximation of \(Q\) on that domain.

notation.meaning: Effective domain of the recourse value.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: incomplete recourse is failure of universal recourse feasibility and necessitates feasibility and value cuts
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incomplete linear recourse over the master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The model has incomplete recourse on \(X\) when
\[
\operatorname{dom}Q=\{x\in X:Y(x)\ne\varnothing\}\subsetneq X.
\]
Its projected feasible domain is
\[
\operatorname{dom}Q=\{x\in X:r^\top(h-Tx)\le0\text{ for every }r\in C\},
\]
where \(C=\{r\ge0:W^\top r\le0\}\). Accordingly, a Benders master must enforce feasibility cuts to approximate \(\operatorname{dom}Q\) and optimality cuts to approximate the finite values \(Q(x)\) on that domain. A master decision outside \(\operatorname{dom}Q\) cannot furnish a primal incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incomplete recourse occurs when some master-feasible decisions lack subordinate feasibility, requiring feasibility cuts in addition to value-function optimality cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete-Recourse Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition fits the incomplete-recourse regime, and the feasibility-domain description is plausible under the stated boundedness assumption. No Benders or Farkas source with a specific locator supports the projected-domain equality and the asserted simultaneous need for feasibility and optimality cuts.

children.title: Benders Convergence Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Termination regimes and global certificates obtained from master and subordinate bounds.

children.title: Polyhedral Finite-Termination Regime
children.top_down_role: Finite generation behavior associated with polyhedral subordinate representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Generators Do Not Suffice Without Cut Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp algorithmic boundary for finite termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize the master objective \(\theta\) over \(x\in[-1,1]\) for \(Q(x)=|x|\), whose exact cuts are \(\theta\ge x\) and \(\theta\ge-x\). If the master retains only the most recently generated cut, then with \(\theta\ge x\) it selects \(x=-1\) and generates \(\theta\ge-x\); after dropping the first cut it selects \(x=1\) and regenerates \(\theta\ge x\). The process can cycle despite having only two generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite cut family does not ensure finite termination if generated cuts are discarded.
assumptions_latex: The master minimizes \theta and retains only its newest cut.
Each one-cut master is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x_k)_{k\ge0}=(-1,1,-1,1,\ldots)\quad\text{is possible despite only two exact generators.}
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Generators Do Not Suffice Without Cut Retention

assumptions_latex: The master domain is nonempty and the full linear optimization problem has a finite optimum attained by some feasible solution.
The relevant dual polyhedron and Farkas cone have finitely many extreme-point and extreme-ray generators.
Each iteration solves the master and subproblem exactly and adds a previously absent violated generator cut unless the stopping test holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact Benders method terminates after finitely many distinct generator additions with an optimality certificate.

notation.meaning: Number of relevant dual extreme points.
Number of relevant Farkas extreme rays.
Master lower and incumbent upper bounds.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite generation plus exact separation yields classical finite termination of linear Benders decomposition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-generation theorem for polyhedral linear Benders decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N_P<\infty\) be the number of relevant dual extreme points and \(N_R<\infty\) the number of relevant feasibility-ray generators. Since every nonterminal iteration adds a violated cut absent from the current master, at most \(N_P+N_R\) such generator additions can occur. Once no violated feasibility or optimality cut exists, the master epigraph equals the recourse epigraph at its optimizer. The master objective is then a valid lower bound \(L_k\), the recovered feasible solution gives an upper bound \(U_k\), and exactness yields \(L_k=U_k\), certifying global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finitely many relevant polyhedral generators and exact solves, each nonterminal iteration adds a new cut, so Benders terminates finitely at a zero-gap optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Finite-Termination Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Theorem is the correct mathematical role for the finite-termination claim. The exact hypotheses needed for finite termination and the claimed bound of at most N_P+N_R generator additions require authoritative confirmation; no relevant citation is supplied, and the local inventory does not support this theorem.

children.title: Nonpolyhedral Asymptotic Regime
children.top_down_role: Convergence behavior for nonpolyhedral subordinate value functions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonpolyhedral boundary illustrated by a smooth convex value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)=x^2\) on \([-1,1]\). Its supporting affine function at \(t\) is \(\ell_t(x)=2tx-t^2\), and \(Q(x)-\ell_t(x)=(x-t)^2\). For any finite \(T\subset[-1,1]\), choose \(x\notin T\); then \(\max_{t\in T}\ell_t(x)<Q(x)\). Consequently no finite family of supporting cuts represents the epigraph of \(Q\) exactly on the whole interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic value function cannot be represented exactly on an interval by finitely many tangent cuts.
assumptions_latex: \ell_t\text{ is the affine support of }Q\text{ at }t
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall T\subset[-1,1]\text{ finite},\qquad \max_{t\in T}(2tx-t^2)\not\equiv x^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Supporting-Cut Representation Can Fail

assumptions_latex: The master domain \(X\) is compact, and the proper closed convex recourse value \(Q\) is finite on \(X\).
At every trial point, exact separation returns a valid affine support of \(Q\) that is tight there.
Master problems are solved globally and generated cuts are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lower bounds approach the optimum and every accumulation point of incumbent-optimal iterates is globally optimal, although finite termination need not occur.

notation.meaning: Piecewise-affine lower model at iteration k.
Optimal value of the full problem.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: compact cutting-plane convergence for closed convex value functions with exact supporting separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact supporting-cut convergence for a compact nonpolyhedral convex master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_k\) be the maximum of all affine supports generated through iteration \(k\). Then \(Q_k\le Q_{k+1}\le Q\), so the master values \(L_k=\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+Q_k(x)\}\) form a nondecreasing sequence bounded above by \(v^\star=\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+Q(x)\}\). Under the stated exact-separation and compactness assumptions, \(L_k\to v^\star\), and any accumulation point of a sequence whose true objective values converge to the bounds is optimal. Because a nonpolyhedral epigraph may require infinitely many supports, equality \(L_k=v^\star\) need not occur at any finite iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact supporting cuts produce increasing lower bounds converging to the optimum on a compact domain, but a nonpolyhedral value function may require infinitely many cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonpolyhedral Asymptotic Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement asserts a convergence theorem rather than a general principle. More importantly, whether compactness, closed convexity, exact tight separation, global master solution, and cut retention suffice for all stated convergence and accumulation-point conclusions depends on the precise cutting-plane theorem. An authoritative locator is required before a reliable replacement can be formulated.

children.title: Benders Lower-Upper Bound Certificate
children.top_down_role: Progress and stopping certification from master bounds and recovered feasible solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility Requirement for an Upper Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on interpreting a candidate objective as a Benders upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite objective value of a master or partially recovered candidate is not an upper bound unless the candidate is feasible for the full minimization problem. For example, in \(\min\{x:x\ge1\}\), the infeasible candidate \(x=0\) has value \(0<v^\star=1\), so treating it as an upper bound can create a false stopping certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only a fully feasible incumbent supplies an upper bound; an infeasible candidate may have an objective below the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
The reported candidate is not certified feasible for all original constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\notin\mathcal X\;\Longrightarrow\;F(x_k)\text{ is not certified to satisfy }F(x_k)\ge v^\star.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Requirement for an Upper Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-so-far bound bookkeeping for a finite minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given valid iteration bounds \(L_j\le v^\star\le U_j\), define \(\underline L_k=\max_{0\le j\le k}L_j\) and \(\overline U_k=\min_{0\le j\le k}U_j\). Then \(\underline L_k\le v^\star\le\overline U_k\), \((\underline L_k)\) is nondecreasing, \((\overline U_k)\) is nonincreasing, and \(\overline U_k-\underline L_k\le U_k-L_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best-so-far bounds remain valid, move monotonically inward, and give a gap no worse than the current raw gap.
assumptions_latex: v^\star\in\mathbb R
L_j\le v^\star\le U_j\quad(0\le j\le k)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \underline L_k\le v^\star\le\overline U_k,\qquad \overline U_k-\underline L_k\le U_k-L_k.

notation.meaning: Best certified lower bound through iteration k
Best certified upper bound through iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Best-Bound Envelopes

assumptions_latex: The master relaxation supplies a valid lower bound \(L_k\) on the finite optimum \(v^\star\).
A recovered full-feasible solution supplies an upper bound \(U_k\ge v^\star\).
The requested absolute tolerance is \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(L_k\le v^\star\le U_k\) and \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\) certify \(\varepsilon\)-optimality of the incumbent.

notation.meaning: Objective value of the best certified feasible incumbent.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary lower-upper bound certificate for minimization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-gap certificate for a finite minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), retain the master optimum \(L_k\) and the objective value \(U_k\) of the best recovered full-feasible solution. Their validity gives
\[
L_k\le v^\star\le U_k.
\]
Therefore the incumbent's suboptimality satisfies
\[
0\le U_k-v^\star\le U_k-L_k.
\]
If \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\), the incumbent is certified \(\varepsilon\)-optimal. For a relative tolerance \(\rho\ge0\), a scale-explicit alternative is \(U_k-L_k\le\rho\max\{1,|U_k|\}\). The certificate is valid only when both bounds include every declared subproblem and master inexactness allowance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid master lower bound and feasible-incumbent upper bound enclose the optimum; their gap directly certifies absolute or scaled relative optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Lower-Upper Bound Certificate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate is exactly the correct content kind, and the absolute-gap implication is elementary and correctly stated. Nonetheless, the record supplies no source locator, and the particular relative-gap scaling by max{1,|U_k|} is a convention that should be sourced or explicitly scoped rather than presented as canonical.

children.title: Inexact Benders Certification Regimes
children.top_down_role: Qualified convergence information under controlled subordinate error.

children.title: Subproblem Accuracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Controlled levels of subordinate solution accuracy used during decomposition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-independent primal–dual accuracy measure for an inexact subordinate minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(d_k\) be a verified lower bound on the finite subordinate optimum \(Q(x_k)\), and let \(u_k\) be the objective value of a subordinate-feasible point. Then \(d_k\le Q(x_k)\le u_k\), and \(\delta_k=u_k-d_k\) certifies both \(0\le u_k-Q(x_k)\le\delta_k\) and \(0\le Q(x_k)-d_k\le\delta_k\). Hence \(\delta_k\le\eta_k\) is independently checkable, whereas an unquantified solver status does not establish \(\eta_k\)-accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible subordinate value and a verified lower bound bracket the true subproblem value; their gap is a checkable accuracy certificate.
assumptions_latex: Q(x_k)\in\mathbb R
d_k\le Q(x_k)\text{ is independently verified}
u_k\text{ comes from a subordinate-feasible point}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_k\le Q(x_k)\le u_k,\qquad \max\{u_k-Q(x_k),Q(x_k)-d_k\}\le\delta_k.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Subproblem Gap

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), a recourse oracle returns certified bounds \(\ell_k\le Q(x_k)\le u_k\).
The oracle error is \(\delta_k=u_k-\ell_k\ge0\), and any returned cut is globally valid despite inexact solution.
The desired final accuracy is \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed, vanishing, and summable error schedules support respectively error-floor, asymptotic, and accumulated-error-controlled certification regimes.

notation.meaning: Certified lower and upper recourse bounds.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: certified oracle gaps distinguish fixed, vanishing, and summable inexactness schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy schedules for certified inexact recourse oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fixed-accuracy regime satisfies \(\delta_k\le\bar\delta\) and generally permits certification only to a tolerance containing the nonzero error floor \(\bar\delta\). A vanishing-accuracy regime satisfies \(\delta_k\to0\) and is appropriate for asymptotic exactness. A summable regime satisfies \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\delta_k<\infty\) and controls accumulated oracle error in convergence arguments. For finite \(\varepsilon\)-termination, the algorithm must allocate subproblem and master errors so that the reported corrected gap, including all certified residual allowances, is at most \(\varepsilon\); an unquantified solver status is not an accuracy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified subproblem gaps may be fixed, vanish, or be summable; the global stopping gap must explicitly include the resulting error allowance.
knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Accuracy Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is a reasonable kind for classifying accuracy regimes, but the consequences attributed to fixed, vanishing, and summable errors vary across inexact Benders and cutting-plane algorithms. The assumptions do not identify a specific variant or propagation constants, and no authoritative locator supports the combined claim.

children.title: Cut Reliability Certification
children.top_down_role: Qualification of cuts produced from approximate subordinate information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reliability certificate for an affine cut produced by an inexact linear or convex recourse solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)=\inf_y\{q(y):y\in Y(x)\}\). Suppose verifiably dual-feasible data yield an affine function \(\ell_k(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), and a subordinate primal-feasible point at \(x_k\) has value \(u_k\). Then \(\theta\ge\ell_k(x)\) is globally valid and \(0\le Q(x_k)-\ell_k(x_k)\le u_k-\ell_k(x_k)\). Thus \(u_k-\ell_k(x_k)\le\eta_k\) certifies \(\eta_k\)-tightness at the trial point without weakening global validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual feasibility certifies global cut validity, while a subordinate primal–dual gap certifies local tightness error.
assumptions_latex: \ell_k(x)\le Q(x)\text{ on }X\text{ follows from verifiable dual feasibility}
u_k\text{ is the value of a subordinate-feasible point at }x_k
Q(x_k)\in\mathbb R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell_k\le Q\text{ on }X,\qquad 0\le Q(x_k)-\ell_k(x_k)\le u_k-\ell_k(x_k).

notation.meaning: Feasible subordinate objective value at the trial point

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Recourse Cut Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trial-Point Agreement Does Not Certify Global Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between local agreement and a globally reliable cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[-1,1]\), let \(Q(x)=x^2\) and \(\ell(x)=2x\). Although \(\ell(0)=Q(0)=0\), one has \(\ell(x)>Q(x)\) for every \(x\in(0,1)\). Hence agreement, or a small error, at the trial point alone does not certify \(\ell\le Q\) on the master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut can agree exactly with the value function at the trial point yet overestimate it elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: \ell(x)=2x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell(0)=Q(0),\qquad \ell(x)>Q(x)\quad(0<x<1).
knowledge_statements.title: Trial-Point Agreement Does Not Certify Global Validity
Cut Reliability Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certifies globally valid or uniformly error-bounded inexact Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(Q:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be the subordinate value function, and let \(\ell(x)=\alpha+g^\top x\). A reliability certificate with tolerance \(\eta\geq0\) is verifiable data establishing \(\ell(x)\leq Q(x)+\eta\) for every \(x\in X\). Consequently, \(\ell(x)-\eta\leq Q(x)\) on \(X\), so the corrected inequality \(\theta\geq\ell(x)-\eta\) is valid for the epigraph of \(Q\). When \(\eta=0\), the original inequality \(\theta\geq\ell(x)\) is globally valid, though it need not be tight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified uniform overestimation error makes the downward-corrected cut globally valid; zero error certifies validity of the original cut but not necessarily tightness.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\operatorname{dom}Q\)
\(\eta\geq0\)
The supplied certificate is independently verifiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\ell(x)-\eta\leq Q(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in X.\]

notation.meaning: Proposed affine Benders lower estimator before correction

children.title: Error-Aware Termination Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Certification limits imposed by residual subordinate error.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nominal Gap Can Hide Certified Bound Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of termination based on an uncorrected reported gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{x:x\ge0\}\), let \(z^\star=0\) and use the feasible incumbent \(\widehat x=1\). Report \(\widehat L=\widehat U=0\), \(\delta_L=0\), and \(\delta_U=1\). The certified enclosure \(\widehat L-\delta_L\le z^\star\le\widehat U+\delta_U\) holds and \(F(\widehat x)\le\widehat U+\delta_U\), but the nominal gap is zero while the corrected gap and actual incumbent error are both one. Thus the nominal gap alone cannot certify any tolerance below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero reported gap can conceal a positive certified error allowance and positive incumbent suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: \widehat L-\delta_L\le z^\star\le\widehat U+\delta_U
\widehat x\text{ is feasible and }F(\widehat x)\le\widehat U+\delta_U
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat U-\widehat L=0\quad\text{but}\quad F(\widehat x)-z^\star=(\widehat U+\delta_U)-(\widehat L-\delta_L)=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Nominal Gap Can Hide Certified Bound Error
Error-Aware Termination Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Termination test accounting for certified errors in reported upper and lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization problem with objective \(F\), feasible set \(\mathcal X\), and finite optimal value \(z^*=\inf_{x\in\mathcal X}F(x)\). Suppose \(\widehat L,\widehat U\in\mathbb R\) and \(\delta_L,\delta_U\geq0\) satisfy \(\widehat L-\delta_L\leq z^*\leq\widehat U+\delta_U\), and suppose a feasible incumbent \(\widehat x\in\mathcal X\) satisfies \(F(\widehat x)\leq\widehat U+\delta_U\). For \(\varepsilon\geq0\), termination is justified when \((\widehat U+\delta_U)-(\widehat L-\delta_L)\leq\varepsilon\); then \(F(\widehat x)-z^*\leq\varepsilon\). Equivalently, \(\widehat U-\widehat L\leq\varepsilon-\delta_L-\delta_U\), which can hold only if the right-hand side is nonnegative whenever the reported gap is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Terminate when the reported gap plus both certified errors is within tolerance, provided a feasible incumbent is bounded by the corrected upper bound; that incumbent is then epsilon-optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(z^*=\inf_{x\in\mathcal X}F(x)\in\mathbb R\)
\(\widehat L-\delta_L\leq z^*\leq\widehat U+\delta_U\)
\(\widehat x\in\mathcal X\) and \(F(\widehat x)\leq\widehat U+\delta_U\)
\(\delta_L,\delta_U,\varepsilon\geq0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(\widehat U-\widehat L)+\delta_U+\delta_L\leq\varepsilon\;\Longrightarrow\;F(\widehat x)-z^*\leq\varepsilon.\]

notation.meaning: Objective and feasible set of the minimization problem

children.title: Continuous Benders Model Regimes
children.top_down_role: Benders interfaces distinguished by subordinate geometry and block multiplicity.

children.title: Classical Linear Benders Interface
children.top_down_role: Linear subordinate duality and polyhedral projection, with discrete-master specialization cross-indexed elsewhere.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact single-subproblem linear Benders procedure at the continuous interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use a master minimizing \(c^\top x+\theta\) over \(x\in X\), a well-posed lower-bounded \(\theta\), and accumulated valid cuts. At its solution \((x^k,\theta^k)\), solve the linear subordinate problem exactly. If it is infeasible, add a violated feasibility cut from a certified recession ray. If it is feasible and \(\theta^k<Q(x^k)\), add an optimality cut from a dual optimum. Stop when the subordinate problem is feasible and \(\theta^k=Q(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical linear Benders alternates exact master and subordinate solves, adding a feasibility-ray or optimality cut until the epigraph gap closes.
assumptions_latex: Master and subordinate problems are solved exactly.
Generated dual points and rays satisfy their defining constraints.
The master is well posed and every retained cut is globally valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{At termination, }(x^k,\theta^k)\text{ satisfies the exact subordinate feasibility and epigraph conditions.}

notation.meaning: Exact subordinate value at the tested master point

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Linear Benders Cutting-Plane Loop

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality of a valid master lower bound and an assembled feasible objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x^k,\theta^k)\) minimize the current valid-cut master with value \(L_k=c^\top x^k+\theta^k\). If the subordinate problem at \(x^k\) is feasible with finite value and \(\theta^k=Q(x^k)\), then \(c^\top x^k+Q(x^k)=L_k\). The left side is a feasible full-problem value and \(L_k\) is a valid lower bound, so both equal \(z^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing the exact subordinate epigraph gap makes the assembled feasible value equal the master lower bound and certifies global optimality.
assumptions_latex: (x^k,\theta^k)\text{ is optimal for the current master.}
All master cuts are globally valid.
Q(x^k)\text{ is finite and attained when a full primal solution is required.}
\theta^k=Q(x^k)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k=c^\top x^k+Q(x^k)=z^\star.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Benders Termination Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination for a Finite Linear Benders Cut Universe
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence under exact separation from finitely many complete point and ray generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume a finite set of dual extreme-point and extreme-ray cuts completely represents subordinate optimality and feasibility over the master domain. If each master is solved exactly, every nonterminal iteration adds a new violated cut from this set, and duplicate cuts are not inserted, then only finitely many nonterminal cut-addition iterations occur. Termination yields either the optimality certificate or infeasibility of the valid complete master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact linear Benders terminates finitely when a finite complete cut universe is separated without duplicates.
assumptions_latex: A finite point-and-ray cut set completely represents subordinate optimality and feasibility over the master domain.
Every nonterminal iteration adds a previously absent violated cut from that set.
Master and subordinate separation problems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The number of nonterminal cut-addition iterations is at most the size of the finite complete cut set.}
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination for a Finite Linear Benders Cut Universe
Classical Linear Benders Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear recourse value represented by subordinate dual points and recession rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(W\in\mathbb R^{p\times m}\), \(T\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(q\in\mathbb R^m\). Define \(Q(x)=\inf\{q^\top y:Wy\geq h-Tx,\ y\in\mathbb R_+^m\}\). Whenever this primal problem is feasible with finite value, linear-programming strong duality gives \(Q(x)=\max\{\pi^\top(h-Tx):W^\top\pi\leq q,\ \pi\in\mathbb R_+^p\}\). Every dual-feasible \(\pi\) yields the globally valid optimality cut \(\theta\geq\pi^\top(h-Tx)\). Moreover, every \(r\in\mathbb R_+^p\) satisfying \(W^\top r\leq0\) yields the necessary feasibility inequality \(r^\top(h-Tx)\leq0\); its violation excludes an infeasible master point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a dimensionally specified linear subordinate problem, dual-feasible points generate optimality cuts and nonnegative dual recession rays generate necessary feasibility cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(W\in\mathbb R^{p\times m}\), \(T\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(q\in\mathbb R^m\)
Linear-programming strong duality applies whenever the subordinate primal is feasible with finite value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q(x)=\max_{\pi\in\mathbb R_+^p,\,W^\top\pi\leq q}\pi^\top(h-Tx),\qquad r\in\mathbb R_+^p,\ W^\top r\leq0\;\Longrightarrow\;r^\top(h-Tx)\leq0\ \text{whenever the primal is feasible}.\]

children.title: Convex Nonlinear Subproblem Regime
children.top_down_role: Subordinate problems supporting globally valid dual information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual certificate for convex subordinate optimality and cut tightness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q(x)=\inf_y\{f(y):g_i(y)+a_i^\top x\le0\}\), suppose \(\bar y\) is feasible at \(\bar x\), \(\bar\lambda\ge0\), complementary slackness holds, and there exist \(u\in\partial f(\bar y)\) and \(v_i\in\partial g_i(\bar y)\) satisfying \(u+\sum_i\bar\lambda_i v_i=0\). Under a convex constraint qualification, \((\bar y,\bar\lambda)\) is primal-dual optimal and its dual cut is tight at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex KKT conditions certify subordinate optimality and tightness of the multiplier cut.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every \(g_i\) are proper closed convex functions.
\(\bar y\) is feasible at \(\bar x\).
A convex constraint qualification sufficient for KKT necessity and strong duality holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q(\bar x)=f(\bar y)=d(\bar\lambda,\bar x),\qquad d(\bar\lambda,x)\le Q(x)\ \text{for all }x.
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Tightness Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes unconditional weak-duality validity from qualification-dependent tightness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\lambda\ge0\), weak duality gives \(d(\lambda,x)\le Q(x)\). If the subordinate problem at \(\bar x\) has a positive duality gap or the dual supremum is not attained, no available multiplier need satisfy \(d(\lambda,\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\). Thus multiplier cuts may remain globally valid without being tight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak duality preserves validity, but a duality gap or nonattainment can prevent cut tightness.
assumptions_latex: \(d(\lambda,x)\) is defined as the global Lagrangian infimum.
\(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d(\lambda,x)\le Q(x),\quad d(\lambda,\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\ \text{is not guaranteed without zero gap and attainment}.
knowledge_statements.title: Validity–Tightness Boundary
Convex Nonlinear Subproblem Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex subordinate structure under which dual multipliers produce global Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)=\inf_y\{f(y):g_i(y)+a_i^\top x\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), where \(f\) and every \(g_i\) are proper closed convex functions. For any \(\lambda\geq0\), define \(d(\lambda,x)=\inf_y\{f(y)+\sum_i\lambda_i(g_i(y)+a_i^\top x)\}\). Weak duality gives \(d(\lambda,x)\leq Q(x)\) globally. If Slater's condition holds at \(\bar x\) and \(\bar\lambda\) is dual optimal there, then \(d(\bar\lambda,\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\), so \(\theta\geq d(\bar\lambda,x)\) is a globally valid supporting Benders cut tight at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity and strong duality make an optimal subordinate multiplier produce a globally valid cut that is tight at the generating point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g_i\) are proper closed convex functions.
Slater's condition holds for the subordinate problem at \(\bar x\).
A dual optimum \(\bar\lambda\geq0\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d(\bar\lambda,x)\leq Q(x)\ \text{for all }x,\qquad d(\bar\lambda,\bar x)=Q(\bar x).\]

notation.meaning: Dual-optimal multiplier at the generating point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly uses weak duality for global validity and strong duality at the generating point for tightness, and its content kind fits the regime leaf. No supporting citation or standard-field rationale is supplied.

children.title: Nonconvex Subproblem Validity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of global cut validity or exactness under merely local subordinate solutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes a global nonconvex Lagrangian bound from information obtained at a local subordinate solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonconvex subordinate problem, \(d(\lambda,x)=\inf_y L(y,\lambda;x)\) remains a global lower bound when the infimum is taken over the full subordinate domain. Evaluating or differentiating \(L\) only at a locally minimizing or stationary \(\bar y\) does not compute \(d\). Consequently local KKT conditions alone certify neither global branch-cut validity nor tightness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally minimized Lagrangian remains a valid bound, whereas a local KKT solution does not certify a globally valid or tight cut.
assumptions_latex: The subordinate problem may be nonconvex.
The dual function uses the global Lagrangian infimum.
\(\lambda\ge0\) for inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d(\lambda,x)\le Q(x),\qquad \text{local stationarity alone does not imply global validity or tightness}.
knowledge_statements.title: Global-Dual versus Local-Branch Information
Nonconvex Subproblem Validity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local subordinate stationary point can generate a derivative cut that is not globally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(Q(x)=\min_{y\in\mathbb R}\{(y^2-1)^2+xy\}\) for \(x\in[-1,1]\). At \(\bar x=0\), \(\bar y=1\) is a local and global minimizer with value zero, and differentiating this branch gives the affine candidate \(\ell(x)=x\). For every \(x>0\), however, evaluating the subordinate objective at \(y=-1\) gives \(Q(x)\leq-x<x=\ell(x)\). Thus a cut derived from one local solution branch need not underestimate the global nonconvex value function, even when that solution is globally optimal at the generating point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut from one locally selected nonconvex solution branch can overestimate the global value immediately away from its generating point.
assumptions_latex: The candidate cut uses the local branch through \((\bar x,\bar y)=(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q(x)\leq-x<\ell(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in(0,1].\]

notation.meaning: Affine candidate obtained from a local solution branch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit example supports the stated failure phenomenon, and counterexample is the correct content kind. It nevertheless lacks cited evidence or an explicitly marked standard-field rationale.

children.title: Single-Cut Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Combined subordinate information maintained in one master approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Cut Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One master epigraph variable aggregates all subordinate value components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S p_sQ_s(x)\), where \(p_s\geq0\) and \(\sum_s p_s=1\). If \(\ell_{s,k}(x)\leq Q_s(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), then \(\ell_k(x)=\sum_s p_s\ell_{s,k}(x)\leq Q(x)\). Single-cut Benders uses one epigraph variable \(\theta\) and appends \(\theta\geq\ell_k(x)\) at iteration \(k\). The resulting master is a valid lower approximation of the original objective, but it does not retain separate epigraph restrictions for individual subordinate components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted sum of component cuts gives one valid aggregate cut for a single master epigraph variable.
assumptions_latex: \(p_s\geq0\) and \(\sum_{s=1}^S p_s=1\)
\(\ell_{s,k}(x)\leq Q_s(x)\) for all \(s\) and \(x\in X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\theta\geq\sum_{s=1}^S p_s\ell_{s,k}(x)\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Nonnegative weighted aggregation preserves lower-estimator validity, and representation fits the leaf. No relevant citation is supplied.

children.title: Multi-Cut Benders Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Disaggregated subordinate value approximations maintained in the master.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational multi-cut loop for independent subordinate value components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), solve the valid master containing separate variables \(\theta_s\), evaluate or separate every subordinate component at \(x^k\), and append each violated valid inequality \(\theta_s\ge\ell_{s,k}(x)\). Update a feasible incumbent and reoptimize. The master value \(LB_k\) and incumbent value \(UB_k\) certify \(LB_k\le v^\star\le UB_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multi-cut Benders inserts violated component cuts separately and terminates using a master-incumbent gap.
assumptions_latex: The master contains all required first-stage and feasibility restrictions.
Each \(\ell_{s,k}\) is a globally valid lower estimator.
Component separation is exact at the trial point.
A feasible incumbent supplies \(UB_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: LB_k\le v^\star\le UB_k,\qquad UB_k-LB_k\le\varepsilon\Rightarrow\text{the incumbent is }\varepsilon\text{-optimal}.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Cut Iteration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-termination regime for exact multi-cut Benders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the master has finitely many relevant candidates, every component has finitely many relevant optimality and feasibility cuts, exact separation adds a new violated cut whenever the gap is nonzero, and duplicate cuts are suppressed, only finitely many candidate/cut discoveries are possible. The method therefore terminates finitely with infeasibility or a zero-gap optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite candidate and component-cut families imply finite termination under exact separation and duplicate suppression.
assumptions_latex: The relevant master candidate set is finite.
Every component has a finite relevant cut family.
Master and subordinate problems are solved exactly.
A nonterminal iteration adds a previously absent violated cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Exact multi-cut Benders terminates after finitely many distinct candidate/cut discoveries.}
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Polyhedral Termination
Multi-Cut Benders Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate epigraph variables preserve subordinate component cuts in disaggregated form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\in\mathbb N\), let \(Q(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S p_sQ_s(x)\) with \(p_s\geq0\), and suppose \(\ell_{s,k}(x)\leq Q_s(x)\) for every component \(s\), generated index \(k\), and \(x\in X\). A multi-cut master introduces variables \(\theta_s\) and imposes \(\theta_s\geq\ell_{s,k}(x)\) for every generated pair \((s,k)\), while using \(\sum_{s=1}^S p_s\theta_s\) as the recourse approximation. For any fixed generated index \(k\), the component inequalities imply the corresponding aggregate inequality \(\sum_{s=1}^S p_s\theta_s\geq\sum_{s=1}^S p_s\ell_{s,k}(x)\). Thus disaggregation retains componentwise restrictions that imply their weighted aggregate counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multi-cut Benders maintains a separate lower epigraph model for each subordinate component; nonnegative weighted summation of those restrictions implies the corresponding aggregate cut.
assumptions_latex: \(S\in\mathbb N\)
\(Q(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S p_sQ_s(x)\) with \(p_s\geq0\)
\(\ell_{s,k}(x)\leq Q_s(x)\) for every \(s,k\) and \(x\in X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\left[\theta_s\geq\ell_{s,k}(x)\ \text{for }s=1,\ldots,S\right]\Longrightarrow\sum_{s=1}^S p_s\theta_s\geq\sum_{s=1}^S p_s\ell_{s,k}(x).\]

children.title: Adaptive Cut Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Dynamic grouping and separation of subordinate cut families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strengthening of a partitioned Benders master under cut-preserving refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P'\) refine \(\mathcal P\). If every refined block retains the component cuts used to form each corresponding coarse-block inequality, summing refined-block inequalities reproduces every coarse inequality. Hence the refined master lower model satisfies \(L_{\mathcal P'}(x)\ge L_{\mathcal P}(x)\). The one-block and singleton partitions recover single-cut and multi-cut models, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut-preserving partition refinement strengthens the lower model, with single-cut and multi-cut as the extreme partitions.
assumptions_latex: \(p_s\ge0\) for every component.
Each \(\ell_{s,r}\) is a valid lower estimator of \(Q_s\).
\(\mathcal P'\) refines \(\mathcal P\).
The compared masters retain the same underlying component cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{\mathcal P'}(x)\ge L_{\mathcal P}(x)\quad\text{for every }x.
knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Refinement Dominance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Master-Preservation Test for Aggregation Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical certificate for changing a partition or compressing cut history without changing the current master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k\) and \(\widetilde M_k\) be the master feasible sets before and after a partition, merge, or history-compression operation. The operation preserves the current master exactly if \[M_k\subseteq\widetilde M_k\quad\text{and}\quad\widetilde M_k\subseteq M_k.\] Equivalently, the old and new systems imply one another. Under this equality and an unchanged objective, all master objective values and optimizer sets are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An aggregation change preserves the current master exactly when the old and new systems imply one another.
assumptions_latex: Both systems use the same master-variable domain and objective.
All implication tests are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_k=\widetilde M_k.

notation.meaning: Master feasible set before the aggregation change
Master feasible set after the aggregation change

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Master-Preservation Test for Aggregation Changes

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unsafe History Compression Can Decrease the Master Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of monotone lower-bound progress when a nonimplied aggregate cut is discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0\}\) and let a master minimizing \(\theta\) contain \(\theta\ge1\) and \(\theta\ge0\). Its value is \(1\). If a compression step deletes \(\theta\ge1\) while retaining only \(\theta\ge0\), the new value is \(0\). Both rows can be valid lower estimators when \(Q(0)\ge1\), but the reported lower bound decreases because the deleted row was not implied by the retained system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting a nonimplied aggregate cut can weaken the master even when every retained cut remains valid.
assumptions_latex: The master minimizes \(\theta\) over \(X=\{0\}\).
The true subordinate value satisfies \(Q(0)\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{\mathrm{after}}=0<1=L_{\mathrm{before}}.

notation.meaning: Master bounds before and after compression

assumptions_latex: \(S<\infty\).
Every split produces nonempty blocks and strictly refines the current partition.
No merge or coarsening operation occurs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{split}}\le S-|\mathcal P_0|.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial bound on aggregation changes for a split-only adaptive policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P_0\) partition \(\{1,\ldots,S\}\). If every partition-changing iteration replaces at least one block by two or more nonempty blocks and no iteration merges blocks, then \(|\mathcal P_k|\) strictly increases at each change and never exceeds \(S\). Hence at most \(S-|\mathcal P_0|\) partition-changing iterations occur before the singleton partition is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A split-only adaptive aggregation policy changes its partition at most S minus the initial number of blocks times.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Bound on Strict Split-Only Refinement
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Bound on Strict Split-Only Refinement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adaptive Aggregation State and Transition Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical state for changing subordinate-component partitions while preserving cut provenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S=\{1,\ldots,q\}\), let \(\mathsf A_k=(\mathcal P_k,(H_{s,k})_{s\in S})\), where \(\mathcal P_k\) partitions \(S\) and \(H_{s,k}\) is a finite retained library of valid component minorants \(\ell_{s,r}\le Q_s\). For every \(B\in\mathcal P_k\), introduce \(\theta_B\) and impose \[\theta_B\ge\sum_{s\in B}p_s\ell_{s,r_s}(x)\qquad\text{for every }(r_s)_{s\in B}\in\prod_{s\in B}H_{s,k}.\] A split or merge changes \(\mathcal P_k\) while retaining the component libraries and reconstructing the new block rows from them. An old row may be deleted without changing the current master only when it is implied by the reconstructed system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The adaptive state is a component partition plus provenance-preserving component cut libraries from which each aggregate master is reconstructed.
assumptions_latex: \(p_s\ge0\) for every component.
Every stored \(\ell_{s,r}\) is a valid lower estimator of \(Q_s\).
Each retained library is finite at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P_k\text{ remains a partition of }S\quad\text{and every reconstructed aggregate row is valid}.

notation.meaning: Retained cut library for component s
Epigraph variable for current block B

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Aggregation State and Transition Semantics

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Exactness after Eventual Singleton Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence inheritance for split-only adaptive aggregation in a finite polyhedral Benders regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume finitely many subordinate components, each with a finite complete family of Benders cuts, and assume the complete multi-cut master is feasible with finite attained optimum. Suppose an exact adaptive method never deletes a nonimplied cut, performs only partition refinements, reaches the singleton partition after finitely many refinements, and thereafter adds a violated component cut whenever one exists. Then only finitely many distinct cuts can be added; after finitely many master solves no component cut is violated, and the current solution solves the complete multi-cut master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finite component cut families, cut preservation, and eventual singleton refinement, adaptive aggregation finitely reaches the exact multi-cut master optimum.
assumptions_latex: The component set and every complete component-cut family are finite.
The complete multi-cut master is feasible and has a finite attained optimum.
Master and separation problems are solved exactly.
Only strict refinements occur, the singleton partition is eventually reached, and nonimplied cuts are never discarded.
Whenever a component cut is violated, at least one such cut is added.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K<\infty:\quad x^K\text{ solves the complete multi-cut master and no component cut is violated}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Exactness after Eventual Singleton Refinement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition Refinement Dominance and Equality Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corrected comparison of partitioned masters under retained component-cut provenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P'\) refine \(\mathcal P\), and let both masters be constructed from the same retained component minorants. Every coarse aggregate row obtained by summing aligned component rows is implied by the corresponding refined rows, so the refined lower model cannot be weaker: \(L_{\mathcal P'}(x)\ge L_{\mathcal P}(x)\). If every block master contains the full Cartesian product of the same component-cut libraries, then both models equal \(\sum_s p_s\max_{r\in H_s}\ell_{s,r}(x)\), and refinement gives equality rather than strict strengthening.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut-preserving refinement cannot weaken an aligned aggregate model; with full cross-product component histories, all partitions induce the same lower model.
assumptions_latex: \(p_s\ge0\) for every component.
\(\mathcal P'\) refines \(\mathcal P\).
Both masters use the same retained component minorants and preserve every compared coarse implication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{\mathcal P'}(x)\ge L_{\mathcal P}(x),\quad\text{with equality under full Cartesian-product reconstruction}.

notation.meaning: Lower model induced by partition P

knowledge_statements.title: Partition Refinement Dominance and Equality Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete adaptive partition policy using component-cut slope heterogeneity and exact projected-master preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an evaluated point \(x^k\), choose an active slope \(g_{s,k}\) for each component model and define \(h_k(B)=\max_{s,t\in B}\|g_{s,k}-g_{t,k}\|_*\). If \(h_k(B)>\tau_{\mathrm{split}}\), replace \(B\) by nonempty groups from a fixed deterministic clustering rule, requiring every output group to have diameter at most \(\tau_{\mathrm{split}}\). Blocks \(B,C\) are merge-eligible only if \(h_k(B\cup C)\le\tau_{\mathrm{merge}}\), where \(0\le\tau_{\mathrm{merge}}\le\tau_{\mathrm{split}}\), and reconstruction from retained component libraries leaves the induced epigraph in the common variables \((x,\sum_B\theta_B)\) unchanged. Retain all component-cut provenance through either transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split slope-heterogeneous blocks and merge only similar blocks whose reconstructed projected master is exactly unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Every retained component cut is a valid minorant with recorded component provenance.
The clustering rule is deterministic and produces a genuine refinement when invoked.
Projected-master equality for a merge is tested exactly.
\(0\le\tau_{\mathrm{merge}}\le\tau_{\mathrm{split}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P_{k+1}\text{ is a partition, reconstructed cuts remain valid, and every accepted merge preserves the induced master lower model}.

notation.meaning: Active-slope heterogeneity of aggregation block B

knowledge_statements.title: Heterogeneity-Triggered Split and Certified-Merge Policy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Exactness under Master-Preserving Partition Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exactness in a finite polyhedral regime allowing splits and merges that preserve the induced master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume finitely many components and a finite complete family \(\mathcal C\) of component cuts. Suppose every partition transition preserves the induced master lower model, no nonimplied cut is discarded, and exact separation adds a previously nonimplied member of \(\mathcal C\) whenever one exists at the current master optimizer. Then only finitely many strict model enlargements occur. After at most \(|\mathcal C\setminus\mathcal C_0|\) enlargements, no complete-family cut is violated and the current solution solves the complete multi-cut master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Master-preserving splits and merges do not prevent finite exactness when the complete cut family is finite and separation is productive.
assumptions_latex: The complete union of component-cut families \(\mathcal C\) is finite.
Every partition change preserves the induced master lower model in common master variables.
Nonimplied cuts are never discarded.
Master optimization and separation are exact.
At a nonexact master optimizer, separation adds a previously nonimplied violated cut from \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{strict\ enlargements}}\le|\mathcal C\setminus\mathcal C_0|,\qquad x^K\text{ solves the complete multi-cut master}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Exactness under Master-Preserving Partition Changes
Adaptive Cut Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamically partitions subordinate components between aggregate and disaggregate master models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input component functions \(Q_s\), weights \(p_s\), an initial partition \(\mathcal P_0\) of \(\{1,\ldots,S\}\), and a stopping tolerance. At iteration \(k\), solve a master having one epigraph variable \(\theta_B\) per block \(B\in\mathcal P_k\). Evaluate all subordinate components at \(x^k\), construct valid cuts \(\ell_{s,k}\), and append \(\theta_B\geq\sum_{s\in B}p_s\ell_{s,k}(x)\). Split blocks whose prescribed heterogeneity or violation test is met, and optionally merge blocks only while retaining all implied valid aggregate cuts. Stop under a certified gap test and output the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method repeatedly solves a partitioned master, adds block-aggregate cuts, and changes component groups using specified split and merge tests.
assumptions_latex: Every generated \(\ell_{s,k}\) is a valid lower estimator of \(Q_s\).
Every \(\mathcal P_k\) is a partition of \(\{1,\ldots,S\}\).
The stopping test uses certified upper and lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\theta_B\geq\sum_{s\in B}p_s\ell_{s,k}(x)\quad\text{for each }B\in\mathcal P_k.\]

children.title: Pareto-Optimal Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Nondominated cut selection among alternative subordinate dual solutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core-point auxiliary optimization over the dual-optimal face at the current master decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex, let \(x^c\in\operatorname{ri}(X)\), and suppose
\[Q(x)=\max_{u\in U}u^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\]
is finite on \(X\). For a trial point \(\bar x\), define
\[U(\bar x)=\{u\in U:u^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)=Q(\bar x)\}.\]
If the auxiliary problem
\[\max_{u\in U(\bar x)}u^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx^c)\]
attains a solution \(u^*\), then \(\theta\ge {u^*}^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\) is tight at \(\bar x\) and Pareto-optimal over \(X\) relative to the cut family generated by \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing over the current dual-optimal face at a relative-interior core point selects a tight Pareto-optimal Benders cut.
assumptions_latex: X is convex and x^c\in\operatorname{ri}(X).
Q(x)=\max_{u\in U}u^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx) is finite on X.
U(\bar x) is nonempty and the auxiliary maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \theta\ge {u^*}^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\text{ is tight at }\bar x\text{ and Pareto-optimal over }X.

notation.meaning: Relative-interior core point of the master domain.
Dual-optimal face at the trial decision.
Auxiliary optimizer defining the selected cut.

knowledge_statements.title: Magnanti–Wong Pareto-Cut Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the general Pareto guarantee for auxiliary-point selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the auxiliary point is on the relative boundary of \(X\), maximizing candidate-cut value only at that point need not establish Pareto optimality: two valid cuts may agree there while one dominates the other elsewhere on \(X\). Thus auxiliary optimality at a boundary point alone is not a nondominance certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A boundary auxiliary point can fail to distinguish a dominated cut from its dominator, so the general guarantee requires a relative-interior core point.
assumptions_latex: Dominance is tested over the entire master domain X.
The auxiliary point is not required to lie in \operatorname{ri}(X).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^c\notin\operatorname{ri}(X)\;\Longrightarrow\;\text{auxiliary-point optimality alone need not imply Pareto optimality}.

notation.meaning: Auxiliary point used to compare cuts.
Master domain on which dominance is tested.
