Pareto-Optimal Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondominance of valid affine lower cuts over the master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and let \(\mathcal C\) be a family of affine functions valid for \(Q\), so \(\ell(x)\leq Q(x)\) for all \(x\in X\) and \(\ell\in\mathcal C\). A cut \(\theta\geq\ell(x)\) is Pareto-optimal relative to \((X,\mathcal C)\) if no \(\widetilde\ell\in\mathcal C\) satisfies \(\widetilde\ell(x)\geq\ell(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and \(\widetilde\ell(x_0)>\ell(x_0)\) for at least one \(x_0\in X\). Thus no admissible valid cut dominates it throughout the master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Benders cut is Pareto-optimal when no other admissible valid cut is everywhere at least as strong and somewhere strictly stronger.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\operatorname{dom}Q\)
Every \(\ell\in\mathcal C\) satisfies \(\ell\leq Q\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\nexists\,\widetilde\ell\in\mathcal C:\ \widetilde\ell\geq\ell\ \text{on }X\ \text{and }\ \widetilde\ell(x_0)>\ell(x_0)\ \text{for some }x_0\in X.\]

notation.meaning: Admissible family of valid affine cuts
Affine lower estimator defining the cut

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nondominance definition matches the leaf and plain text, but no inspectable source supports the selected admissible-family formulation.

children.title: Facet-Multiplicity Cut Generation Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Cut families targeting stronger projected geometry or several refinements per stage.

children.title: Facet-Oriented Cut Generation
children.top_down_role: Cut selection aimed at strong projected master geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact facet selection when a finite complete facet description is explicitly available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given nonzero facet normals \(a_i\), select \[i^\star\in\arg\max_{i\in I}\frac{a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar z-b_i}{\lVert a_i\rVert_*}.\] If the maximum is positive, return \(a_{i^\star}^{\mathsf T}z\le b_{i^\star}\); otherwise certify \(\bar z\in P\). Positive rescaling of an inequality leaves its normalized score unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over a complete facet list, maximizing normalized violation returns a violated facet or certifies membership.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{z:a_i^{\mathsf T}z\le b_i,\ i\in I\}\) has a finite complete facet description.
\(a_i\ne0\) for every \(i\).
\(\lVert\cdot\rVert_*\) is a norm on the normal space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{i\in I}\frac{a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar z-b_i}{\lVert a_i\rVert_*}>0\iff \bar z\notin P.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum Normalized Facet-Violation Selection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted Candidate Families Need Not Contain a Violated Facet
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on claims that a restricted dual or facet family necessarily separates every exterior trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be a proper subfamily of the facet inequalities of \(P\). A point \(\bar z\notin P\) need not violate any member of \(\mathcal C\). For \(P=[0,1]^2\), \(\mathcal C=\{x_1\ge0,\ x_1\le1\}\), and \(\bar z=(1/2,2)\), every inequality in \(\mathcal C\) is satisfied although \(\bar z\notin P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incomplete candidate family may contain no violated facet for an exterior point.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is not assumed to contain every facet inequality of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar z\notin P\ \not\Rightarrow\ \exists C\in\mathcal C\text{ violated by }\bar z.

notation.meaning: Restricted family of candidate facet cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Candidate Families Need Not Contain a Violated Facet

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of a Violated Facet Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence guarantee for separation using a complete facet description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{z\in\mathbb R^d:a_i^{\mathsf T}z\le b_i,\ i\in I\}\) be a nonempty full-dimensional polyhedron whose displayed inequalities form a complete irredundant facet description. For every \(\bar z\notin P\), some \(i\in I\) satisfies \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar z>b_i\), and that inequality defines a facet of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every exterior point violates a facet in a complete irredundant facet description.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is nonempty and full-dimensional.
The displayed system is a complete irredundant facet description.
\(\bar z\notin P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists i\in I:\ a_i^{\mathsf T}\bar z>b_i\quad\text{and}\quad\dim\{z\in P:a_i^{\mathsf T}z=b_i\}=d-1.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence of a Violated Facet Inequality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facet certification for projected epigraphs that may be lower-dimensional in the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron with relative dimension \(r\ge1\), and let \(a^{\mathsf T}z\le b\) be valid for \(P\). For \(F=\{z\in P:a^{\mathsf T}z=b\}\), the inequality defines a facet of \(P\) if and only if \(\dim F=r-1\). Equivalently, \(F\) contains \(r\) affinely independent points and some point of \(P\) satisfies \(a^{\mathsf T}z<b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid inequality defines a facet of a possibly lower-dimensional polyhedron exactly when its equality face has relative codimension one.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty polyhedron with \(r=\dim P\ge1\).
\(a^{\mathsf T}z\le b\) is valid for \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is a facet of }P\iff\dim F=\dim P-1.

notation.meaning: Equality face exposed by the candidate cut

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Dimensional Facet Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact facet generation when a finite dual-derived inequality family completely represents a full-dimensional projected polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{z:a(u)^{\mathsf T}z\le b(u),\ u\in U\}\), where \(U\) is finite. Remove zero, duplicate up to positive scaling, and redundant inequalities. If \(P\) is nonempty and full-dimensional, every remaining inequality defines a facet of \(P\). Enumerating the remaining family and maximizing normalized violation therefore returns a violated facet whenever \(\bar z\notin P\), and otherwise certifies \(\bar z\in P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduce a finite complete dual cut family to an irredundant description, then separate over its facet rows.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is finite and its inequalities represent \(P\) exactly.
\(P\) is nonempty and full-dimensional.
Redundancy and positive-scaling equivalence are tested exactly.
Every retained normal is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar z\notin P\iff\exists u\in U_{\mathrm{irr}}:\ a(u)^{\mathsf T}\bar z>b(u),\qquad \dim\{z\in P:a(u)^{\mathsf T}z=b(u)\}=\dim(P)-1.

notation.meaning: Indices remaining in the irredundant inequality description
Projected polyhedron represented by the dual-derived inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Complete Dual-Family Facet Extraction
Facet-Oriented Cut Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selects dual-derived cuts whose equality faces are facets of a polyhedral epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{(x,\theta):x\in X,\ \theta\geq Q(x)\}\) be a full-dimensional polyhedron and let a subordinate dual face parameterize valid inequalities \(a(u)^\top x-\theta\leq b(u)\). Given a trial point, select a dual-feasible extreme point \(u\) whose inequality is violated there. Retain it as facet-oriented only after verifying that its equality set in \(P\) contains \(\dim(P)\) affinely independent points, equivalently that the exposed face has dimension \(\dim(P)-1\). Append the certified facet inequality to the master; otherwise retain it merely as a valid nonfacet cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate a violated dual cut and classify it as facet-defining only after an affine-rank test on its equality face.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a full-dimensional polyhedron.
The dual parameterization produces inequalities valid for \(P\).
Equality points or an equivalent exact face-dimension oracle are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\dim\{z\in P:a(u)^\top x-\theta=b(u)\}=\dim(P)-1.\]

notation.meaning: Polyhedral epigraph of the subordinate value function
Dual extreme point indexing a cut

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine-rank criterion correctly characterizes a facet of a full-dimensional polyhedron, but the asserted dual selection procedure and availability of a violated dual extreme point require a specialized source and more precise algorithmic conditions.

children.title: Multiple-Cut Generation
children.top_down_role: Generation of several master refinements during a decomposition stage.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Cut Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adds several independently valid Benders inequalities during one master iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At master iterate \(x^k\), solve the relevant subordinate dual problems and obtain a finite index set \(J_k\) of certified dual points or rays. For every \(j\in J_k\), form its associated valid optimality cut \(\theta_j\geq\ell_j(x)\) or feasibility cut \(r_j(x)\leq0\). Remove duplicates and cuts failing the prescribed violation threshold, then append every remaining inequality before resolving the master. Stop when the certified optimality gap meets tolerance; otherwise repeat. Validity is preserved because each appended inequality is certified separately, independently of how many are generated together.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, generate, filter, and simultaneously append several separately certified optimality or feasibility cuts before resolving the master.
assumptions_latex: Every retained dual point or ray has a validity certificate.
\(J_k\) is finite at every iteration.
Termination uses certified master and incumbent bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal M_{k+1}=\mathcal M_k\cap\bigcap_{j\in J_k}\{z:C_j(z)\leq0\}.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic generate-filter-append scheme fits the algorithm leaf, but the subordinate dual systems, cut indexing, violation threshold, and convergence conditions are not specialized or sourced sufficiently to establish a particular multiple-cut algorithm.

children.title: Strength–Multiplicity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance between individual cut strength and the volume of generated refinements.

knowledge_statements.title: Strength–Multiplicity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal relaxation dominance of disaggregated cuts, balanced against increased master size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonnegative weights \(p_s\), component cuts \(\theta_s\geq\ell_s(x)\) imply the aggregate inequality \(\sum_s p_s\theta_s\geq\sum_s p_s\ell_s(x)\). The converse generally fails because an aggregate inequality permits one component's deficit to be offset by another component's surplus. Hence, with identical component information, the disaggregated multi-cut master projects to a relaxation no weaker than the corresponding single-cut master. This strength requires up to \(S\) epigraph variables and component inequalities per generation round instead of one aggregate variable and inequality, so relaxation dominance alone does not determine computational time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregated cuts dominate their aggregate counterpart as a relaxation, but enlarge the master and therefore need not reduce total runtime.
assumptions_latex: \(p_s\geq0\) for \(s=1,\ldots,S\)
The aggregate and disaggregated masters use the same component cut functions \(\ell_s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bigcap_{s=1}^S\{\theta_s\geq\ell_s(x)\}\subseteq\left\{\sum_{s=1}^S p_s\theta_s\geq\sum_{s=1}^S p_s\ell_s(x)\right\}.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated inclusion establishes disaggregated relaxation dominance for nonnegative weights, and the runtime qualification is appropriately cautious. No supporting citation or explicit standard-field rationale is provided.

children.title: Supplementary Benders Cut Family
children.top_down_role: Supplementary master refinements derived from subordinate relaxations or known structure.

children.title: Subproblem-Relaxation Cuts
children.top_down_role: Master refinements obtained from relaxed subordinate models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invalidity from an Upper Recourse Surrogate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure when the subordinate surrogate is not a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0\}\), \(Q(0)=0\), and \(R(0)=1\). The support \(\theta\ge1\) is valid for \(\operatorname{epi}_X R\) but excludes \((0,0)\in\operatorname{epi}_X Q\). Hence convexity of \(R\) alone does not ensure a valid supplementary Benders cut; the global lower-bound relation \(R\le Q\) is essential to the general guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex surrogate above exact recourse can produce a support that cuts off an exact epigraph point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (0,0)\in\operatorname{epi}_X Q\quad\text{but}\quad(0,0)\notin\{(x,\theta):\theta\ge1\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Invalidity from an Upper Recourse Surrogate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric ordering induced by increasingly tight subordinate lower relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(R_1(x)\le R_2(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), then
\[\operatorname{epi}_X Q\subseteq\operatorname{epi}_X R_2\subseteq\operatorname{epi}_X R_1.\]
Thus the ideal epigraph of the tighter lower relaxation \(R_2\) is no weaker than that of \(R_1\). Every affine minorant of either relaxation is valid for \(\operatorname{epi}_XQ\), although an individual support of \(R_2\) need not dominate every support obtained from \(R_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pointwise tighter lower recourse relaxation has a smaller, stronger ideal epigraph, but individual supporting cuts remain only partially ordered.
assumptions_latex: R_1(x)\le R_2(x)\le Q(x) for all x\in X.
All epigraphs use the same master domain X.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{epi}_X Q\subseteq\operatorname{epi}_X R_2\subseteq\operatorname{epi}_X R_1.

notation.meaning: Epigraph restricted to the master domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordering of Subproblem-Relaxation Epigraphs
Subproblem-Relaxation Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid Benders cuts obtained from convex lower relaxations of the recourse function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the master domain and \(Q:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) the exact recourse value. Suppose a relaxed subproblem defines a proper convex function \(R\) satisfying \(R(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). For any \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}R\) and \(g\in\partial R(\bar x)\), the inequality \[\theta\ge R(\bar x)+g^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\] is valid for every \((x,\theta)\) satisfying \(x\in X\) and \(\theta\ge Q(x)\). Thus a supporting cut from the relaxation may strengthen the master without excluding any exact epigraph point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every supporting hyperplane of a convex lower relaxation of recourse is a valid Benders master cut.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is proper and convex on \(X\).
\(R(x)\le Q(x)\) for all \(x\in X\).
\(g\in\partial R(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\ge R(\bar x)+g^{\mathsf T}(x-\bar x)\) is valid for \(\operatorname{epi}_X Q\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex supporting-hyperplane argument is mathematically standard and the property role fits the cut-family leaf, but the record supplies no inspectable source for its Benders interpretation or stated relaxation setting.

children.title: Structure-Derived Valid-Inequality Cuts
children.top_down_role: Supplementary refinements obtained from known model structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Derived Valid-Inequality Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility condition for inequalities derived from known recourse or linking structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\{(x,\theta):x\in X,\ \theta\ge Q(x)\}\) be the exact Benders epigraph. A structure-derived inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x+b\theta\ge d\) is an admissible supplementary cut precisely when \[a^{\mathsf T}x+b\theta\ge d\qquad\text{for every }(x,\theta)\in E.\] In particular, validity may be established from linking constraints, conservation identities, variable bounds, or a valid projection of the subproblem formulation. Adding any collection of such inequalities to a relaxation of \(E\) preserves all feasible solutions of the original decomposed problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structure-derived inequality is admissible exactly when it holds throughout the exact recourse epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the master domain.
\(Q:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is the exact recourse function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x+b\theta\ge d\) may be added without removing any point of \(E\).

notation.meaning: Exact recourse epigraph over the master domain.
Coefficients and right-hand side of the supplementary inequality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly characterizes validity over the exact epigraph and fits the leaf, but the examples involving projections, linking constraints, and preservation in the decomposed model have no cited source.

children.title: Supplementary Cut Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of auxiliary cuts with the represented master projection.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity criterion for supplementary cuts enforced globally or on a recorded master localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be the master space, \(E\subseteq Z\) the exact Benders set, \(D\subseteq Z\) the domain on which cuts \(h_j(z)\le0\) are enforced, and \(H_j=\{z:h_j(z)\le0\}\). The cuts are compatible on \(D\) if and only if \(E\cap D\subseteq\bigcap_j H_j\). Global compatibility is the special case \(D=Z\). Consequently, whenever \(E\cap D\ne\varnothing\), compatible cuts cannot make the localized exact model infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A supplementary cut must contain every exact point in the domain where it is enforced; global validity is the full-domain special case.
assumptions_latex: Each cut is defined on the master space.
The enforcement domain \(D\) is recorded explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\cap D\subseteq\bigcap_jH_j.

notation.meaning: Exact Benders feasible set or epigraph.
Domain on which the supplementary cuts are enforced.
Halfspace or feasible set of supplementary cut j.

knowledge_statements.title: Global and Local Supplementary-Cut Compatibility

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Validity Does Not Imply Global Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing that a locally valid supplementary cut cannot be enforced outside its recorded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\{(x,\theta):0\le x\le1,\ \theta\ge x\}\), let \(D=\{(x,\theta):x\le1/2\}\), and consider \(\theta\ge2x-1/2\). For every point of \(E\cap D\), \(\theta\ge x\ge2x-1/2\), so the cut is compatible on \(D\). The exact point \((1,1)\in E\) violates the cut, so enforcing it outside \(D\) removes an exact point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut can be valid on a localization but invalid globally, so its enforcement domain is part of its validity record.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\cap D\subseteq\{\theta\ge2x-1/2\}\quad\text{but}\quad E\nsubseteq\{\theta\ge2x-1/2\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Validity Does Not Imply Global Compatibility
Supplementary Cut Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint validity and consistency requirements for supplementary cuts in a Benders master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\{(x,\theta):x\in X,\ \theta\ge Q(x)\}\), and let supplementary cuts be \(h_j(x,\theta)\le0\) for \(j\in J\). They are compatible with the exact Benders model when \[E\subseteq\bigcap_{j\in J}\{(x,\theta):h_j(x,\theta)\le0\}.\] They are compatible with a restricted master domain \(D\) when additionally \(E\cap D\ne\varnothing\) whenever the corresponding exact localized problem is feasible. Under these conditions, adding the cuts neither removes an exact feasible epigraph point nor creates a false infeasibility certificate within the intended localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Supplementary cuts must contain the exact epigraph and remain consistent with any legitimate master localization.
assumptions_latex: Each \(h_j\) is defined on the master-variable space.
\(D\) is the currently intended master localization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented master preserves every exact epigraph point relevant to \(D\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits, but the additional localization clause is not formulated clearly enough to distinguish global cut validity from validity restricted to D. A source is needed to determine the intended compatibility criterion and correct quantification.

children.title: Benders Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Regularization families controlling unstable or weakly informed master movement.

children.title: Localized Benders Master Family
children.top_down_role: Master models localized around reference decisions or controlled objective levels.

children.title: Regularized Benders Masters
children.top_down_role: Master localization through penalties around reference decisions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: The Penalized Master Value Is Not a Global Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates stabilized candidate selection from global Benders bound certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[L_k=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x),\qquad \widehat L_k=\inf_{x\in X}\left\{m_k(x)+\tfrac12\lVert x-z_k\rVert_{H_k}^2\right\}.\] If \(m_k\le F\) on \(X\), then \(L_k\le F^\star\), but \(\widehat L_k\le F^\star\) need not hold. For \(X=\mathbb R\), \(F(x)=m_k(x)=x^2\), \(z_k=1\), and \(H_k=[1]\), one has \(F^\star=L_k=0\) and \(\widehat L_k=1/3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unregularized master supplies the global lower bound; the penalized optimum generally does not.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k(x)\le F(x)\) for all \(x\in X\).
\(H_k\succeq0\), and both infima are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\le F^\star,\qquad \widehat L_k\not\le F^\star\text{ in general}.
knowledge_statements.title: The Penalized Master Value Is Not a Global Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness of a Positive-Definite Regularized Master Candidate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness of the proximal Benders-master candidate, conditional on attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X\) is convex, \(m_k\) is convex on \(X\), \(H_k\succ0\), and the minimum is attained, then \[x_k^+\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{m_k(x)+\tfrac12\lVert x-z_k\rVert_{H_k}^2\right\}\] is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite quadratic penalty makes an attained convex regularized-master solution unique.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and convex.
\(m_k\) is proper and convex on \(X\).
\(H_k\succ0\), and the displayed minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lvert\arg\min_{x\in X}\{m_k(x)+\tfrac12\lVert x-z_k\rVert_{H_k}^2\}\rvert=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness of a Positive-Definite Regularized Master Candidate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order Certificate for a Regularized Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate for an exact convex quadratic regularized-master solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, let \(m_k\) be proper lower-semicontinuous convex, and let \(H_k\succeq0\). Under the stated subdifferential qualification, \(x_k^+\in X\) minimizes \(m_k(x)+\tfrac12\lVert x-z_k\rVert_{H_k}^2\) if and only if \[0\in\partial m_k(x_k^+)+H_k(x_k^+-z_k)+N_X(x_k^+).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact optimality balances a model subgradient, proximal displacement, and feasible-set normal.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(m_k\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(H_k\succeq0\).
\(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}m_k)\cap\operatorname{ri}(X)\ne\varnothing\), and the minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k^+\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{m_k(x)+\tfrac12\lVert x-z_k\rVert_{H_k}^2\right\}\iff0\in\partial m_k(x_k^+)+H_k(x_k^+-z_k)+N_X(x_k^+).

notation.meaning: Convex normal cone of X at x

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Certificate for a Regularized Master

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-oracle proximal Benders iteration with serious/null center updates and bound-preserving stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\le F\) be the current convex Benders model on \(X\), let \(z_k\in X\) be an evaluated center, and let \(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_k\le\rho_{\max}\). Compute \[x_k^+\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\|x-z_k\|_2^2\right\}.\] Evaluate \(F(x_k^+)\), append a valid affine minorant to obtain \(m_{k+1}\), and set \(p_k=m_k(z_k)-m_k(x_k^+)\). For \(\eta\in(0,1)\), set \(z_{k+1}=x_k^+\) when \(p_k>0\) and \(F(z_k)-F(x_k^+)\ge\eta p_k\); otherwise set \(z_{k+1}=z_k\). Choose \(\rho_{k+1}\) within its safeguards, no larger after a serious step and no smaller after a null step. If \(p_k\le0\), retain the center and use the appended cut as model repair. Maintain \(U_k\) as the best evaluated feasible value and \(L_k=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\); stop only when \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a proximal master, add the oracle cut, accept sufficient actual improvement as a serious step, and stop using the unregularized master bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and each displayed minimization is attained.
\(F\) is proper, closed, and convex on \(X\); evaluated values are exact and finite.
Every oracle affine minorant is globally valid, so \(m_k\le F\).
\(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_k\le\rho_{\max}<\infty\) and \(0<\eta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\le F^*\le U_k,\qquad U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow U_k-F^*\le\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Serious–Null-Step Regularized Benders Cycle

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semidefinite Regularization Need Not Select a Unique Candidate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp uniqueness boundary for convex regularized Benders masters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R^2\), \(m_k(x)=0\), \(z_k=0\), and \(H_k=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\). Then \[\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{m_k(x)+\tfrac12\|x-z_k\|_{H_k}^2\right\}=\{(0,t):t\in\mathbb R\}.\] Thus positive semidefiniteness alone does not guarantee a unique regularized-master candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular quadratic regularizer can leave an entire feasible direction unpenalized, so positive semidefiniteness alone does not guarantee uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(m_k\) are convex.
\(H_k\succeq0\) is singular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_k\succeq0\ \not\Rightarrow\ \left|\arg\min_{x\in X}\{m_k(x)+\tfrac12\|x-z_k\|_{H_k}^2\}\right|=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Regularization Need Not Select a Unique Candidate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Cut-Addition Bound for Polyhedral Regularized Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional finite bound for an exact retained-cut regularized master with a finite complete cut family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(F=\max_{j\in J}\ell_j\) on \(X\), where \(J\) is finite. If every generated cut is retained and every iteration with \(U_k-L_k>\varepsilon\) adds a previously absent member of \(J\), then at most \(|J\setminus I_0|\) such nonterminal iterations occur. Consequently a subsequent unrestricted-gap test must satisfy \(U_K-L_K\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Productive separation over a finite complete cut family bounds the number of nonterminal cut additions.
assumptions_latex: \(F=\max_{j\in J}\ell_j\) on \(X\) for a finite affine family \(J\).
Master and oracle computations are exact, and all generated cuts are retained.
Whenever \(U_k-L_k>\varepsilon\), a previously absent cut from \(J\) is added.
A finite feasible incumbent is maintained and \(L_k=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{nonterminal}}\le |J\setminus I_0|.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Cut-Addition Bound for Polyhedral Regularized Benders

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simplex Dual of an Unconstrained Quadratic Regularized Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-cut dual representation of an unconstrained positive-definite regularized Benders master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{\alpha_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x\}\), where \(I\) is finite, and let \(H\succ0\). With \(\Delta_I=\{\mu\in\mathbb R_+^I:\sum_i\mu_i=1\}\) and \(\bar g(\mu)=\sum_i\mu_i g_i\), \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{m(x)+\tfrac12\|x-z\|_H^2\right\}=\max_{\mu\in\Delta_I}\left\{\sum_i\mu_i\alpha_i+\bar g(\mu)^{\mathsf T}z-\tfrac12\|\bar g(\mu)\|_{H^{-1}}^2\right\}.\] For every dual maximizer \(\mu^*\), the unique primal minimizer is \(x^*=z-H^{-1}\bar g(\mu^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite unconstrained quadratic regularized master has a simplex dual whose aggregate cut slope determines the unique primal candidate.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and nonempty.
\(H\succ0\).
Each stored cut is affine and finite on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*=z-H^{-1}\sum_{i\in I}\mu_i^*g_i\quad\text{and primal and dual values agree}.

notation.meaning: Aggregate slope of the stored cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Dual of an Unconstrained Quadratic Regularized Master

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dual of a positive-definite finite-cut regularized Benders master over a closed convex master set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x)=\max_{i\in I}\{\alpha_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x\}\), let \(I\) be finite and nonempty, let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(H\succ0\). Define \(\phi(x)=\delta_X(x)+\tfrac12\|x-z\|_H^2\), \(\Delta_I=\{\mu\ge0:\sum_i\mu_i=1\}\), and \(\bar g(\mu)=\sum_i\mu_i g_i\). Then \[\min_{x\in X}\left\{m(x)+\tfrac12\|x-z\|_H^2\right\}=\max_{\mu\in\Delta_I}\left\{\sum_i\mu_i\alpha_i-\phi^*(-\bar g(\mu))\right\}.\] For any dual maximizer \(\mu^*\), the unique primal minimizer satisfies \[x^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{\bar g(\mu^*)^{\mathsf T}x+\tfrac12\|x-z\|_H^2\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained finite-cut quadratic master has a simplex dual expressed through the conjugate of the feasible-set quadratic; the aggregate cut slope determines the unique primal candidate.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and nonempty.
\(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(H\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{x\in X}\{m(x)+\tfrac12\|x-z\|_H^2\}=\max_{\mu\in\Delta_I}\{\sum_i\mu_i\alpha_i-\phi^*(-\bar g(\mu))\}.

notation.meaning: Convex indicator of the master set X.
Convex conjugate of the feasible-set quadratic function.
Aggregate slope of the stored cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Finite-Cut Regularized-Master Dual
Regularized Benders Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal stabilization of a convex Benders cutting-plane master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a closed convex master set \(X\), cuts \(\theta\ge\alpha_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x\) for \(i\in I_k\), a reference point \(z_k\in X\), and \(\rho_k>0\), compute \[(x_{k+1},\theta_{k+1})\in\arg\min_{x\in X,\theta}\left\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\theta+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\lVert x-z_k\rVert_2^2:\theta\ge\alpha_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x,\ i\in I_k\right\}.\] Evaluate the subproblem at \(x_{k+1}\), append violated valid cuts, and update \(z_k\) according to the serious/null-step rule. Stop when the incumbent upper bound minus the unregularized master lower bound meets the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularized master minimizes the cutting-plane model plus a proximal penalty around a reference point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
All stored cuts are valid lower bounds on recourse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_{k+1},\theta_{k+1})\) is the next stabilized master candidate.

notation.meaning: Indices of cuts active in the master model.

children.title: Level Benders Masters
children.top_down_role: Master localization through controlled objective-level regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard level-set localization of a convex Benders cutting-plane master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\) be a proper lower-semicontinuous convex lower model on a nonempty closed convex set \(X\), let \(L_k=\inf_Xm_k\), and let \(U_k>L_k\) be an incumbent upper bound. Choose \(\lambda_k\in(0,1)\), set \(\ell_k=L_k+\lambda_k(U_k-L_k)\), and compute \[x_{k+1}=\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{\tfrac12\lVert x-z_k\rVert_2^2:m_k(x)\le\ell_k\right\}.\] Evaluate the true subordinate problem at \(x_{k+1}\), update cuts and bounds, and repeat until the prescribed valid bound-gap test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A level Benders master projects a reference point onto a cutting-plane level set strictly between the current lower and upper bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(m_k\) is a proper lower-semicontinuous convex lower model with finite \(L_k\).
\(U_k>L_k\) and \(0<\lambda_k<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k<\ell_k<U_k\text{ and the level projection is well posed}.
knowledge_statements.title: Level Benders Master

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint and infeasibility boundaries for hard level localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(L=\inf_Xm<U\) and \(\ell=L+\lambda(U-L)\), every \(0<\lambda<1\) gives \(L<\ell<U\). At \(\lambda=0\), the level set may be empty when the infimum is not attained. At \(\lambda=1\), the constraint may remain feasible but loses strict localization below the incumbent bound. Every \(\ell<L\) yields an empty level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interior level parameters give feasible strict localization; the lower endpoint may be unattained, and the upper endpoint loses strict localization.
assumptions_latex: \(L=\inf_Xm\in\mathbb R\) and \(U>L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0<\lambda<1\Rightarrow L<\ell<U;\qquad \ell<L\Rightarrow C_\ell=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Current lower and incumbent upper bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Level-Parameter Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and Uniqueness of the Level Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posedness of the Euclidean level-stabilized master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(m:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with finite \(L=\inf_Xm\). For every \(\ell>L\), the set \(C_\ell=\{x\in X:m(x)\le\ell\}\) is nonempty, closed, and convex. Hence every \(z\in\mathbb R^n\) has a unique Euclidean projection onto \(C_\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A level strictly above the finite model infimum gives a nonempty closed convex set with a unique Euclidean projection.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(m\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(L=\inf_Xm\in\mathbb R\) and \(\ell>L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\,P_{C_\ell}(z).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the level set.

knowledge_statements.title: Existence and Uniqueness of the Level Projection
Level Benders Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-set stabilization of a convex Benders cutting-plane master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x+\max_{i\in I_k}(\alpha_i+g_i^{\mathsf T}x)\), let \(L_k=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\), and let \(U_k\) be an incumbent upper bound. Choose \(\lambda_k\in(0,1)\) and set \(\ell_k=L_k+\lambda_k(U_k-L_k)\). Given a reference point \(z_k\), compute \[x_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\left\{\frac12\lVert x-z_k\rVert_2^2:m_k(x)\le\ell_k\right\}.\] Evaluate recourse at \(x_{k+1}\), update cuts and bounds, and stop when \(U_k-L_k\) is within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A level master projects a reference point onto a cutting-plane level set between current lower and upper bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(m_k(x)\) is a valid lower model of the objective.
\(L_k<U_k\) and \(0<\lambda_k<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) is the next level-stabilized candidate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The level-projection algorithm is coherent and appropriately classified, but no source supports the exact level convention, feasibility assumptions, or Benders specialization.

children.title: Localization Regime Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice among stabilization regimes based on master behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Localization Regime Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection rule balancing model reliability, movement control, and bound progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_k\le f^\star\le U_k\) be valid bounds and \(G_k=U_k-L_k\). Select a localization parameter so that the localized master contains at least one point whose cutting-plane value does not exceed \(L_k+\lambda G_k\), where \(\lambda\in(0,1)\). For a level master this means choosing the level \(\ell_k=L_k+\lambda G_k\); for a proximal or trust-region master it means adjusting the penalty or radius until the predicted decrease is a prescribed positive fraction of \(G_k\). A regime failing this feasibility-and-progress test must be relaxed before accepting its candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose localization tightly enough to control movement but loosely enough to preserve a model point promising fixed-fraction gap reduction.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\) and \(U_k\) are valid finite bounds.
The cutting-plane model is a valid objective lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The chosen localization admits a candidate with predicted decrease proportional to \(G_k\).

notation.meaning: Fixed level or progress fraction in \((0,1)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits regime selection, but the claimed common fixed-fraction progress test for level, proximal, and trust-region masters is not established. In particular, predicted decrease is not defined uniformly across the regimes. A source is needed before selecting a reliable formulation.

children.title: Trust-Region Benders
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood control for successive master decisions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-definedness boundary for ratio-based acceptance in trust-region Benders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(p_k=m_k(z_k)-m_k(x_k^+)\) and \(a_k=F(z_k)-F(x_k^+)\). The agreement ratio \(r_k=a_k/p_k\) has its intended reduction interpretation only when \(p_k>0\). A complete update rule must handle \(p_k\le0\) separately, for example by rejection, model repair, or a distinct certified stopping test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Actual-to-predicted acceptance requires positive predicted reduction; zero or negative prediction needs an explicit fallback.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k(z_k),m_k(x_k^+),F(z_k),F(x_k^+)\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_k\text{ is a reduction-agreement ratio only if }p_k>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Agreement-Ratio Domain and Fallback Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Restricted Master Value Need Not Be a Global Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-bound interface for a trust-region Benders master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[L_k=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x),\qquad L_k^{\mathrm{TR}}=\inf_{x\in X\cap B(z_k,\Delta_k)}m_k(x).\] If \(m_k\le F\) on \(X\), then \(L_k\le F^\star\) and \(L_k\le L_k^{\mathrm{TR}}\), but \(L_k^{\mathrm{TR}}\le F^\star\) need not hold. For \(F=m_k=x^2\), \(X=\mathbb R\), \(z_k=2\), and \(\Delta_k=1/2\), one has \(F^\star=L_k=0\) and \(L_k^{\mathrm{TR}}=9/4\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trust-region master selects a local candidate; the unrestricted master is required for a guaranteed global lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k(x)\le F(x)\) for all \(x\in X\).
\(z_k\in X\), \(\Delta_k>0\), and both infima are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\le F^\star,\qquad L_k^{\mathrm{TR}}\not\le F^\star\text{ in general}.
knowledge_statements.title: A Restricted Master Value Need Not Be a Global Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimality System for a Convex Trust-Region Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for the localized master subproblem, independent of the acceptance policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be closed and convex, \(m_k\) proper lower-semicontinuous convex, and use a Euclidean trust region. Under the stated qualification, a feasible \(x_k^+\) minimizes \(m_k\) over \(X\cap B(z_k,\Delta_k)\) if and only if there exist \(g_k\in\partial m_k(x_k^+)\), \(v_k\in N_X(x_k^+)\), and \(\lambda_k\ge0\) such that \[g_k+v_k+\lambda_k(x_k^+-z_k)=0,\qquad \lambda_k(\lVert x_k^+-z_k\rVert_2-\Delta_k)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subgradient balance, normal-cone feasibility, and complementary trust-region activity certify the localized solve.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(m_k\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(\Delta_k>0\).
There exists \(x\in\operatorname{ri}(X)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}m_k)\) with \(\lVert x-z_k\rVert_2<\Delta_k\), and the minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k^+\in\arg\min\{m_k(x):x\in X,\ \lVert x-z_k\rVert_2\le\Delta_k\}.

notation.meaning: Normal-cone vector for the master domain

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality System for a Convex Trust-Region Master

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-oracle trust-region Benders iteration with model repair and unrestricted-bound stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\le F\) on closed convex \(X\), let \(z_k\in X\), and let \(0<\Delta_k\le\Delta_{\max}\). Compute \[x_k^+\in\arg\min\{m_k(x):x\in X,\ \|x-z_k\|\le\Delta_k\},\] evaluate \(F(x_k^+)\), and append a valid global minorant to obtain \(m_{k+1}\). Put \(p_k=m_k(z_k)-m_k(x_k^+)\) and \(a_k=F(z_k)-F(x_k^+)\). For \(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\), accept \(z_{k+1}=x_k^+\) when \(p_k>0\) and \(a_k/p_k\ge\eta_1\); otherwise retain \(z_{k+1}=z_k\). Shrink \(\Delta_k\) when \(p_k\le0\) or the ratio is below \(\eta_1\); enlarge it only when the trial is accepted with ratio at least \(\eta_2\) and the trust-region boundary is active; otherwise retain it, always enforcing \(0<\Delta_{k+1}\le\Delta_{\max}\). For \(p_k\le0\), the appended cut is the model-repair action. Maintain the best evaluated feasible value \(U_k\) and \(L_k=\inf_{x\in X}m_k(x)\), and stop only when \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a localized master, repair it with every oracle cut, update the center and radius using agreement, and stop using the unrestricted master bound.
assumptions_latex: Every localized master is attained.
Every oracle cut is a valid global minorant of \(F\), and evaluated values are exact and finite.
\(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\), and radius updates preserve \(0<\Delta_k\le\Delta_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_k\le F^*\le U_k,\qquad U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow U_k-F^*\le\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Safeguarded Trust-Region Benders Cycle

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Cut-Addition Bound for Polyhedral Trust-Region Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional finite bound for retained-cut trust-region Benders with a finite complete cut family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\max_{j\in J}\ell_j\) on \(X\) for a finite affine family \(J\). If every cut is retained, stopping uses the unrestricted master bound, and every iteration with \(U_k-L_k>\varepsilon\) adds a previously absent cut from \(J\), then at most \(|J\setminus I_0|\) such nonterminal iterations occur, independently of the accepted-radius trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Productive separation over a finite complete family bounds nonterminal cut additions despite trust-region localization.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and \(F=\max_{j\in J}\ell_j\) on \(X\).
Localized masters and separation are exact, and all generated cuts are retained.
Whenever \(U_k-L_k>\varepsilon\), a previously absent cut from \(J\) is added.
The lower bound is computed from the unrestricted master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{nonterminal}}\le |J\setminus I_0|.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Cut-Addition Bound for Polyhedral Trust-Region Benders
Trust-Region Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Neighborhood control for successive convex Benders master decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a reference point \(z_k\in X\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and valid Benders model \(m_k\), compute \[x_{k+1}\in\arg\min\{m_k(x):x\in X,\ \lVert x-z_k\rVert\le\Delta_k\}.\] Evaluate the exact objective \(F(x_{k+1})\) and form the agreement ratio \[r_k=\frac{F(z_k)-F(x_{k+1})}{m_k(z_k)-m_k(x_{k+1})}\] whenever the denominator is positive. Accept \(x_{k+1}\) as the new reference when \(r_k\) exceeds the acceptance threshold; otherwise retain \(z_k\). Enlarge, retain, or shrink \(\Delta_k\) according to prescribed ratio thresholds, append new Benders cuts, and stop by the global bound gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trust-region Benders restricts each master decision near a reference point and updates the radius using actual-versus-predicted improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k(x)\le F(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
\(z_k\in X\) and \(\Delta_k>0\).
Ratio thresholds and a zero-denominator fallback are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns an accepted reference sequence and valid global Benders bounds.
