children.title: Benders Reference-Point Management
children.top_down_role: Reference-point mechanisms supporting stronger cut selection.

children.title: Core-Point Management
children.top_down_role: Selection and maintenance of core reference points for cut generation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Core-Point Initialization by a Relative Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite initialization of a relative-interior core point from feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d=\dim(\operatorname{aff}X)\). If \(x^0,\ldots,x^d\in X\) are affinely independent and span \(\operatorname{aff}X\), then every barycenter \(z=\sum_{i=0}^d\lambda_ix^i\) with \(\lambda_i>0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\) belongs to \(\operatorname{ri}X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive barycenter of feasible points spanning the master's affine hull initializes a core point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and convex.
The feasible points are affinely independent and span \(\operatorname{aff}X\).
All barycentric weights are positive and sum to one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z\in\operatorname{ri}X.
knowledge_statements.title: Core-Point Initialization by a Relative Simplex

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization and invariant update of a qualitative core point for a fixed convex master set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be nonempty and convex. Initialize \(z_0\in\operatorname{ri}X\). Given \(x_{k+1}\in X\) and \(\gamma_k\in(0,1)\), update \[z_{k+1}=(1-\gamma_k)z_k+\gamma_kx_{k+1}.\] Then \(z_{k+1}\in\operatorname{ri}X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict convex average of a relative-interior core point and any feasible master point remains a core point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and convex.
\(z_k\in\operatorname{ri}X\), \(x_{k+1}\in X\), and \(0<\gamma_k<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_{k+1}\in\operatorname{ri}X.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Interior Core-Point Maintenance
Core-Point Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maintaining a relative-interior point for Pareto-strengthened Benders cut generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty convex master set and choose \(z_0\in\operatorname{ri}X\). After obtaining any master-feasible point \(x_{k+1}\in X\), select \(\gamma_k\in(0,1)\) and update \[z_{k+1}=(1-\gamma_k)z_k+\gamma_k x_{k+1}.\] Then \(z_{k+1}\in\operatorname{ri}X\), so it remains eligible as a core point for auxiliary Pareto-optimal-cut selection. If numerical tolerances or changing master restrictions make relative-interior membership uncertain, replace the update by a projection or analytic-center computation that explicitly restores a positive relative-interior margin before using the point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexly averaging a relative-interior core point with a feasible point preserves an eligible core point for cut strengthening.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and convex.
\(z_k\in\operatorname{ri}X\) and \(x_{k+1}\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{k+1}\in\operatorname{ri}X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-interior averaging property is standard and the algorithm role fits core-point management. No source supports its Pareto-Benders use or the proposed projection or analytic-center restoration rule.

children.title: Interior-Point Management
children.top_down_role: Use of interior reference points within stabilized cut selection.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-programming construction and certificate for a quantitatively interior point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the normalized-margin assumptions, solve \[\max_{x,\delta}\ \delta\quad\text{s.t.}\quad Cx=d,\quad a_i^{\mathsf T}x+\delta\lVert a_i\rVert_2\le b_i\ \forall i,\quad0\le\delta\le1.\] The optimum satisfies \(\delta^*>0\) exactly when a point strictly satisfies every displayed genuine inequality relative to the affine hull. Any optimizer with \(\delta^*>0\) is in \(\operatorname{ri}D\) and carries a certified normalized margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing the smallest normalized slack constructs an interior reference point and reports its certified margin.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions of the Normalized Interior-Margin Condition hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta^*>0\Rightarrow x^*\in\operatorname{ri}D.

notation.meaning: Optimal normalized margin, capped at one.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum Normalized-Slack Interior Point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative relative-interiority condition for a polyhedral localized master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Cx=d\}\ne\varnothing\), with \(\operatorname{aff}D=\{x:Cx=d\}\). Assume every inequality normal \(a_i\ne0\) and no displayed inequality is identically active on \(D\). A point \(z\) has normalized margin \(\delta>0\) when \[Cz=d,\qquad a_i^{\mathsf T}z\le b_i-\delta\lVert a_i\rVert_2\quad\forall i.\] Such a point belongs to \(\operatorname{ri}D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point satisfying the affine hull and a positive normalized slack from every genuine inequality boundary is quantitatively interior.
assumptions_latex: \(D\ne\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{aff}D=\{x:Cx=d\}\).
Every \(a_i\ne0\), and no displayed inequality is identically active on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z\in\operatorname{ri}D.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Interior-Margin Condition

assumptions_latex: \(A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(b_k\in\mathbb{R}^p\), \(C_k\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\), and \(d_k\in\mathbb{R}^q\).
\(D_k=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_kx\le b_k,\ C_kx=d_k\}\) is nonempty and \(\operatorname{aff}D_k=\{x:C_kx=d_k\}\).
Every row \((A_k)_{i\cdot}\) is nonzero, and no inequality \((A_kx)_i\le(b_k)_i\) is identically active on \(D_k\).
\(\delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maintained point satisfies \(z_k\in\operatorname{ri}D_k\) and has normalized slack at least \(\delta_k\) from every inequality boundary in the stated representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative relative-interiority requirements for stable reference points in a polyhedral localized Benders master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(b_k\in\mathbb{R}^p\), \(C_k\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\), and \(d_k\in\mathbb{R}^q\), and define \(D_k=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_kx\le b_k,\ C_kx=d_k\}\). Assume \(D_k\ne\varnothing\), \(\operatorname{aff}D_k=\{x:C_kx=d_k\}\), every row of \(A_k\) is nonzero, and no inequality represented by a row of \(A_k\) is identically active on \(D_k\). A reference point \(z_k\) has normalized interior margin \(\delta_k>0\) when \[C_kz_k=d_k,\qquad (A_kz_k)_i\le (b_k)_i-\delta_k\lVert(A_k)_{i\cdot}\rVert_2\quad\text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}.\] Interior-point management constructs or updates \(z_k\) to satisfy this condition and rechecks it whenever the constraints defining \(D_k\) change. Under the stated representation assumptions, such a point belongs to \(\operatorname{ri}D_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a reference point satisfying the affine-hull equations and a prescribed normalized positive slack from every genuine inequality boundary, and recheck the margin whenever the localized master changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Management

children.title: Reference-Point Quality Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cut-quality sensitivity to stale, poorly centered, or weak reference points.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary References Can Miss Dominating Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete loss of reference-point discrimination at the relative boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[0,1]\), let \(Q(x)=x\), \(\ell_1(x)=0\), and \(\ell_2(x)=x\). Both cuts are valid, and \(\ell_2\ge\ell_1\) on \(X\), strictly on \((0,1]\). At the boundary reference \(z=0\), however, \(\ell_1(z)=\ell_2(z)=0\); every interior reference \(z\in(0,1)\) distinguishes them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dominated cut can tie its dominating alternative at a boundary reference even though every interior point separates them.
assumptions_latex: Selection compares candidates only through their values at one reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell_1(0)=\ell_2(0),\qquad \ell_2(x)>\ell_1(x)\ \forall x\in(0,1].

notation.meaning: Reference point used for cut comparison.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary References Can Miss Dominating Cuts

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reference Quality Affects Strength, Not Pre-Certified Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between reference-dependent cut selection and independent cut validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every candidate \(\ell_j\) is independently certified to satisfy \(\ell_j(x)\le Q(x)\) for all \(x\in X\). Selecting among them using any reference \(z\), even \(z\notin X\), cannot invalidate the selected inequality on \(X\). An infeasible, boundary, stale, or poorly centered reference may nevertheless eliminate a dominance guarantee, fail to distinguish candidates, or select a weak cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A poor reference can weaken cut selection but cannot invalidate a candidate cut whose global validity was established independently.
assumptions_latex: Every candidate cut is independently certified as a global lower estimator on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell_{j(z)}(x)\le Q(x)\ \forall x\in X,\quad\text{while dominance need not hold}.

notation.meaning: Cut index selected using reference z.

knowledge_statements.title: Reference Quality Affects Strength, Not Pre-Certified Validity
Reference-Point Quality Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure modes caused by infeasible, boundary, or poorly centered reference points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the master set and let a cut-selection procedure require a core point in \(\operatorname{ri}X\). If \(z\notin X\), auxiliary cut selection need not preserve the intended validity or dominance interpretation. If \(z\in\operatorname{rbd}X\), objectives evaluated at \(z\) may fail to distinguish cuts that differ only away from the minimal face containing \(z\); consequently Pareto-strengthening guarantees requiring a core point can fail. A safe quality boundary is therefore \[z\in\operatorname{ri}X\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{dist}(z,\operatorname{rbd}X)\ge\delta>0\] in the affine hull whenever a positive margin is computationally meaningful.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infeasible references are unusable, while boundary references can destroy cut discrimination; a positive relative-interior margin is the safe regime.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty convex master set.
The strengthening rule evaluates candidate cuts at a reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Core-point guarantees should be asserted only for \(z\in\operatorname{ri}X\), preferably with positive boundary margin.

notation.meaning: Relative boundary of the master set.
Reference point used by cut selection.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the claim that an infeasible reference can compromise cut validity is not generally justified: reference-point selection may affect dominance without affecting validity when candidate cuts are already valid. The distance condition also needs explicit affine-hull conventions. A Pareto-cut source is required to determine the correct failure statement.

children.title: Benders Cut-Subproblem Control Interface
children.top_down_role: Computational control of growing cut collections and multiple subordinate solves.

children.title: Cut Pool Lifecycle Management
children.top_down_role: Retention and active-set control for previously generated cuts.

children.title: Cut Pool Construction
children.top_down_role: Organization of retained cuts outside the active master set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of a persistent valid-cut repository using explicit canonicalization and domain metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent every nontrivial generated cut \(g\) by normalized data \(N(g)\) and a recorded validity domain \(D_g\). After rejecting cuts without established validity, form \(U_k=P_k\cup G_k\) and identify entries only when their normalized inequalities and validity domains agree. Let \(P_{k+1}\) contain one representative of each resulting equivalence class, with merged provenance and activity metadata. A stored cut \(g\) is eligible for a current master domain \(M_k\) only if \(M_k\subseteq D_g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate, normalize, deduplicate, and annotate old and generated cuts, retaining one traceable representative per equivalence class.
assumptions_latex: The normalization map is defined on every retained nontrivial cut.
Each retained cut has an established validity domain.
Equality or tolerance semantics for normalized data and domains are fixed before the update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{k+1}=\operatorname{Rep}\big((P_k\cup G_k)/\!\sim\big),\qquad g\text{ eligible on }M_k\Rightarrow M_k\subseteq D_g.

notation.meaning: Canonical normalized data for cut g.
Recorded validity domain of cut g.
Equality of normalized inequality and validity-domain data.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonicalized Cut-Pool Update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set relation between a valid persistent pool and the subset currently enforced.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a pool of cuts \(h_i(z)\le0\), let \(A\subseteq P\), and define \(F(S)=\{z\in M:h_i(z)\le0\ \forall i\in S\}\). Then \(F(P)\subseteq F(A)\). If every cut in \(P\) is valid for an exact set \(E\subseteq M\), then \(E\subseteq F(P)\subseteq F(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full valid pool defines a tighter relaxation than any active subset, while both retain every exact feasible point.
assumptions_latex: A\subseteq P.
Every cut in P is valid for E when exact-set containment is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\subseteq F(P)\subseteq F(A).

notation.meaning: Region obtained by enforcing cut set S.

knowledge_statements.title: Pool–Active-Set Relaxation Relation
Cut Pool Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of a persistent pool of valid Benders cuts and metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the cut pool as \(P_0=\varnothing\). At iteration \(k\), solve selected subproblems at the candidate \(x_k\) and generate a finite set \(G_k\) of globally valid cuts. Canonicalize coefficients, discard numerically null inequalities, and merge duplicates up to a prescribed scaling tolerance. Set \[P_{k+1}=P_k\cup G_k,\] attaching to each retained cut its creation iteration, source subproblem, violation at \(x_k\), most recent active iteration, and validity domain. Only cuts whose validity domain contains the current master domain are eligible for activation. Output the updated pool and its metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build the pool by validating, normalizing, deduplicating, and annotating generated cuts before making them eligible for a master.
assumptions_latex: Every generated cut has a recorded validity domain.
Coefficient and violation tolerances are fixed.
Only globally valid or domain-compatible cuts enter the pool.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{k+1}\) is a deduplicated repository of valid, traceable cuts.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits cut-pool construction, but the normalization, duplicate-merging, metadata, tolerance, and domain-eligibility policies are implementation-specific and uncited. The displayed set union also does not by itself express the preceding canonicalization and merge operations.

children.title: Active Cut Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection of pooled cuts for current master enforcement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness condition when only a working subset of retained valid cuts is enforced.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be a family of valid master cuts and \(A_k\subseteq\mathcal C\) the active subset. For a minimization master, \(v(A_k)\le v(\mathcal C)\). If an exact separation oracle at an active-master optimizer \(z_k\) either returns a violated cut in \(\mathcal C\) or certifies that none exists, then the latter certificate implies that \(z_k\) satisfies every cut in \(\mathcal C\). If \(\mathcal C\) exactly represents the intended master set, such termination is feasible for that set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial activation preserves a valid lower bound, and exact separation restores full-cut feasibility at termination.
assumptions_latex: Every cut in \mathcal C is valid.
The active master is solved globally.
Separation over \mathcal C is exact at the termination candidate.
Exact intended-master feasibility is concluded only when \mathcal C represents that set exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v(A_k)\le v(\mathcal C),\qquad \operatorname{sep}_{\mathcal C}(z_k)=\varnothing\Rightarrow z_k\models\mathcal C.

notation.meaning: Minimization-master value with cut set S.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation Sufficiency Under Partial Activation

assumptions_latex: Every cut in \(P_k\) is valid on the current master domain.
The materially violated set \(V_k\), mandatory set \(M_k\), scoring rule, and feasibility tolerance are fixed before selection.
The integer budget satisfies \(B_k\ge |V_k\cup M_k|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected set satisfies \(V_k\cup M_k\subseteq A_k\subseteq P_k\) and \(|A_k|\le B_k\).

notation.meaning: Persistent pool of cuts valid on the current master domain.
Cuts activated in the current master.
Materially violated cuts and mandatory cuts, respectively.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selecting a budget-feasible working subset from a persistent pool of valid Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a valid cut pool \(P_k\), a candidate \((x_k,\theta_k)\), and an integer budget \(B_k>0\), let \(V_k\subseteq P_k\) be the cuts violated beyond the feasibility tolerance and let \(M_k\subseteq P_k\) be the mandatory cuts. Assume \(B_k\ge |V_k\cup M_k|\). Assign a fixed score to each cut in \(P_k\setminus(V_k\cup M_k)\), for example using normalized violation, recent activity, and age. Initialize \(A_k=V_k\cup M_k\), then add highest-scoring remaining cuts until no more cuts can be added without making \(|A_k|>B_k\). Solve the next master using \(A_k\). A cut omitted from \(A_k\) remains in \(P_k\) and may be reactivated later.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activate every materially violated or mandatory cut, requiring the budget to accommodate them, and fill the remaining capacity with the highest-scoring pool cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Active Cut Selection

children.title: Cut Aging Policies
children.top_down_role: Age-based treatment of persistently inactive cuts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistent reset, increment, protection, and deletion rule for an age-managed cut pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_k\) be the finite pool, \(H_k\subseteq P_k\) the protected cuts, \(G_k\) newly generated cuts, and \(a_i^k\) each stored cut's age. Under a fixed activity test, set \(a_i^{k+1}=0\) when cut \(i\) is active or materially violated at the current candidate and set \(a_i^{k+1}=a_i^k+1\) otherwise. For maximum age \(A\), update \[P_{k+1}=H_k\cup\{i\in P_k\setminus H_k:a_i^{k+1}\le A\}\cup G_k,\] assigning age zero to new cuts. Thus protection, rather than age, controls deletion of every cut in \(H_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reset useful cuts, increment inactive ones, delete only over-age unprotected cuts, and retain the protected set explicitly.
assumptions_latex: P_k and G_k are finite.
Activity and violation use a fixed scaling convention and tolerance.
Every protected cut is identified before the update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_k\cup G_k\subseteq P_{k+1}.
knowledge_statements.title: Protected Cut-Aging Update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of deleting a cut solely because it remains slack at sampled master solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=[0,1]\) and \(Q(x)=\max\{0,x-1/2\}\), represented by \(C_1:\theta\ge0\) and \(C_2:\theta\ge x-1/2\). At every repeatedly sampled point \((x,\theta)=(0,0)\), \(C_2\) is slack by \(1/2\) and can acquire arbitrary age. Deleting it admits \((1,0)\), although \(Q(1)=1/2\). Hence inactivity on the observed history is not a redundancy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut can remain inactive throughout the sampled history while still being necessary elsewhere in the master domain.
assumptions_latex: The aging rule observes only the stated sampled points.
Deletion is based solely on consecutive inactivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_2\text{ is historically inactive but nonredundant on }M.

notation.meaning: Exact value function in the example.

knowledge_statements.title: Inactivity Does Not Imply Redundancy
Cut Aging Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-based aging rule for a finite Benders cut pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_k\) be the cut pool at iteration \(k\), and let \(a_i^k\in\mathbb N_0\) denote the age of cut \(i\). Given an activity tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\) and maximum age \(A\in\mathbb N\), set \(a_i^{k+1}=0\) if cut \(i\) is binding within \(\varepsilon\) at the current master solution or separates that solution by more than \(\varepsilon\); otherwise set \(a_i^{k+1}=a_i^k+1\). Retain all indispensable feasibility cuts and define \(P_{k+1}=\{i\in P_k:a_i^{k+1}\le A\}\cup G_k\), where \(G_k\) contains newly generated cuts. Stop aging when the decomposition termination test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reset active or violated cuts to age zero, increment inactive cuts, and discard over-age cuts except protected feasibility cuts; always add newly generated cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k\) is finite at every iteration.
Cut activity and violation are evaluated under a fixed scaling convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{k+1}=\{i\in P_k:a_i^{k+1}\le A\}\cup G_k\), with indispensable feasibility cuts protected.

notation.meaning: age of cut i at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this Benders-specific aging policy. Moreover, the displayed update can delete an indispensable feasibility cut whose age exceeds A, contradicting the stated protection rule; a corrected formulation must explicitly union the protected set.

children.title: Retention–Turnover Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance between historical cut retention and active-set turnover.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic effect of enforcing more valid cuts and the absence of a universal runtime ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization master with valid active cut sets \(A\subseteq B\), let \(F(A),F(B)\) be the corresponding feasible regions and \(v(A),v(B)\) their optimal values. Then \(F(B)\subseteq F(A)\) and \(v(A)\le v(B)\). Enforcing more valid cuts therefore cannot weaken the master lower bound, but it increases or preserves the number of master rows. No universal runtime ordering follows: a larger master can cost more per solve, while its tighter relaxation can reduce later decomposition iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: More active valid cuts tighten a minimization master, but exchange higher per-solve burden for a potentially smaller iteration count.
assumptions_latex: A\subseteq B and every cut in B is valid.
Both masters share the same objective and base domain.
Both optimal values are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(B)\subseteq F(A),\qquad v(A)\le v(B).
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Strength–Master-Size Tradeoff
Retention–Turnover Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-budget selection principle balancing useful retained cuts against pool renewal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite candidate pool \(P_k\), assign each cut \(i\) a predicted utility \(u_i^k\ge0\), retention cost \(c_i>0\), and turnover penalty \(d_i^k\ge0\). Under budget \(B>0\), a retention decision is any \(R_k\subseteq P_k\) satisfying \(\sum_{i\in R_k}c_i\le B\). The scalarized policy selects \(R_k\) to maximize \(\sum_{i\in R_k}u_i^k-\lambda\sum_{i\in R_k}d_i^k\), with \(\lambda\ge0\). Increasing retention can preserve useful master information but consumes capacity that could admit new cuts; varying \(B\) or \(\lambda\) traces this explicit retention–turnover tradeoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A budgeted cut pool should retain cuts by predicted benefit net of retention or turnover penalties; its budget and penalty weight control preservation versus renewal.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k\) is finite and the scores are fixed during the selection step.
Cuts required for master validity are selected independently or assigned mandatory retention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{R\subseteq P_k}\{\sum_{i\in R}u_i^k-\lambda\sum_{i\in R}d_i^k:\sum_{i\in R}c_i\le B\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalarized policy is an unsupported local construction. Charging d_i^k to retained cuts does not clearly model turnover, and the formulation contains no explicit decision or capacity term for admitting new cuts.

children.title: Cut Comparison-Scaling Calculus
children.top_down_role: Comparison and numerical scaling of alternative valid cuts.

children.title: Cut Dominance Screening
children.top_down_role: Comparison of alternative cuts for redundant or inferior master refinement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP-dual certificate for dominance of affine epigraph cuts on a polyhedral master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=\{x:Ax\le d\}\ne\varnothing\), \(C_i:\theta\ge\alpha_i+\beta_i^{\mathsf T}x\), and \(C_j:\theta\ge\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}x\). Put \(c_0=\alpha_i-\alpha_j\) and \(c=\beta_i-\beta_j\). If \(\inf_{x\in M}c^{\mathsf T}x\) is finite and LP strong duality holds, then \(C_i\) dominates \(C_j\) on \(M\) if and only if there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=-c\) and \(c_0-d^{\mathsf T}\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a polyhedral master domain, affine-cut dominance has a nonnegative LP-multiplier certificate.
assumptions_latex: M is nonempty.
The dominance-test LP has a finite optimum and satisfies strong duality.
Both cuts use the same epigraph orientation and coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_i\succeq_M C_j\iff\exists\lambda\ge0:\ A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=-(\beta_i-\beta_j),\ (\alpha_i-\alpha_j)-d^{\mathsf T}\lambda\ge0.

notation.meaning: Cut i dominates cut j throughout M.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Dominance Certificate
Cut Dominance Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dominance test for affine lower-bounding cuts over a master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the master domain and consider valid cuts \(C_i:\theta\ge\alpha_i+\beta_i^{\mathsf T}x\) and \(C_j:\theta\ge\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}x\). Cut \(C_i\) dominates \(C_j\) on \(M\) precisely when \(\alpha_i+\beta_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}x\) for every \(x\in M\). Equivalently, \(\inf_{x\in M}[(\alpha_i-\alpha_j)+(\beta_i-\beta_j)^{\mathsf T}x]\ge0\). If this condition holds, deleting \(C_j\) leaves the master feasible region defined by the pair unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One affine Benders cut dominates another when its lower bound is everywhere at least as large on the master domain; the dominated cut can then be removed.
assumptions_latex: Both cuts are valid on the same nonempty master domain \(M\).
Both inequalities use the same epigraph orientation and variable scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_i\) dominates \(C_j\) if and only if \(\inf_{x\in M}[(\alpha_i-\alpha_j)+(\beta_i-\beta_j)^{\mathsf T}x]\ge0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dominance condition and deletion consequence are mathematically precise for affine epigraph cuts on a common domain, and the content kind fits, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Cut Normalization
children.top_down_role: Numerical scaling conventions used for cut comparison or enforcement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariance and uniqueness induced by positive homogeneous normalization of an oriented affine inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s\) be positive on nonzero cut data and satisfy \(s(ta,tb)=t s(a,b)\) for every \(t>0\). Define \(N(a,b)=(a,b)/s(a,b)\). Then \(N(ta,tb)=N(a,b)\). Moreover, \(N(a_1,b_1)=N(a_2,b_2)\) if and only if \((a_2,b_2)=t(a_1,b_1)\) for some \(t>0\). Thus \(N\) selects one representative from each positive-scaling class of oriented cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive homogeneous normalization is invariant to positive rescaling and selects one representative from each oriented cut ray.
assumptions_latex: s(a,b)>0 and s(ta,tb)=t s(a,b) for every t>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N(ta,tb)=N(a,b),\qquad N(a_1,b_1)=N(a_2,b_2)\iff(a_2,b_2)=t(a_1,b_1)\text{ for some }t>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Invariant Canonical Representative
Cut Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive homogeneous normalization of affine inequalities before numerical comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a nontrivial cut as \(a^{\mathsf T}z\ge b\), where \((a,b)\ne(0,0)\). For a chosen positive homogeneous scale \(s(a,b)>0\), its normalized representation is \(\bar a^{\mathsf T}z\ge\bar b\), where \((\bar a,\bar b)=(a,b)/s(a,b)\). Typical choices are \(s(a,b)=\|a\|_2\) when \(a\ne0\), or \(s(a,b)=\|(a,b)\|_2\). Because division is by a positive scalar, the normalized and original cuts define the same halfspace; normalization only fixes a representative for comparison and tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize a nonzero cut by dividing every coefficient and its right-hand side by one positive homogeneous scale, preserving the represented halfspace.
assumptions_latex: The cut coefficient pair is nonzero.
The selected scale is finite, positive, and applied to both sides.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{z:a^{\mathsf T}z\ge b\}=\{z:\bar a^{\mathsf T}z\ge\bar b\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalization definition is mathematically sound, but no source is supplied. The eventual sourced version should also state explicitly that s(ta,tb)=t s(a,b) for every t>0.

children.title: Scaling-Sensitive Dominance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of dominance assessment under inconsistent or ill-conditioned scaling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical boundary of coefficient-only normalization when the cut normal approaches zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For cut data \((a,b)\) normalized by \(s(a,b)=\|a\|\), the map \(N(a,b)=(a/\|a\|,b/\|a\|)\) is undefined at \(a=0\) and is not uniformly bounded as \(\|a\|\downarrow0\). In one dimension, \(N(\varepsilon,1)=(1,1/\varepsilon)\), whose right-hand side diverges as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Using \(\|(a,b)\|\) avoids division by \(\|a\|\) alone but does not eliminate all floating-point conditioning concerns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalizing only by the cut normal is undefined at a zero normal and ill-conditioned near one.
assumptions_latex: \varepsilon>0.
The chosen scale is s(a,b)=\|a\|.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{0<\varepsilon\le1}\|N(\varepsilon,1)\|=+\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Zero Normalizer Instability
Scaling-Sensitive Dominance Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of coefficientwise approximate dominance tests without scale invariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a numerical screening rule declare cuts \(a_1^{\mathsf T}z\ge b_1\) and \(a_2^{\mathsf T}z\ge b_2\) equivalent whenever \(\|(a_1,b_1)-(a_2,b_2)\|_\infty\le\tau\), for fixed \(\tau>0\). This rule is not invariant under positive rescaling: the identical halfspaces \(z_1\ge1\) and \(\varepsilon z_1\ge\varepsilon\) have coefficient distance \(1-\varepsilon\), whereas their common rescaling by \(\delta>0\) has distance \(\delta(1-\varepsilon)\). Thus the decision can cross the tolerance boundary solely through scaling. Dominance tolerances must therefore be applied after a common normalization or through a scale-invariant geometric test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Raw coefficient tolerances can change their verdict when equivalent cuts are rescaled. Normalize cuts or use a scale-invariant geometric dominance test.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon<1\), \(\delta>0\), and \(\tau>0\).
The screening rule compares unnormalized coefficient vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicate \(\|(a_1,b_1)-(a_2,b_2)\|_\infty\le\tau\) is not invariant under common positive rescaling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly exhibits the failure of an absolute coefficient tolerance under positive rescaling, and failure_boundary is the appropriate kind. An inspectable numerical-screening source is still required.

children.title: Subproblem Evaluation Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Concurrent or prioritized evaluation of independent subordinate blocks.

children.title: Parallel Subproblem Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Concurrent evaluation of independent subordinate blocks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: All-block synchronous evaluation of conditionally independent Benders subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Q(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S p_sQ_s(x)\) with \(p_s\ge0\). At iteration \(k\), broadcast the same master point \(x^k\) and solve all conditionally independent block subproblems concurrently. Each worker returns a globally valid block cut \(\ell_s^k\le Q_s\), or its block feasibility certificate. After the barrier, add the individual certificates or the aggregate cut \(\ell^k=\sum_s p_s\ell_s^k\), and then update the master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Broadcast one master point, evaluate every independent block concurrently, collect globally valid certificates, and refine the master after all required responses arrive.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S p_sQ_s(x)\) with \(p_s\ge0\).
Conditional on \(x^k\), the block subproblems have no shared subordinate decisions or residual cross-block constraints.
Every returned cut or feasibility certificate is globally valid for its block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell^k(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S p_s\ell_s^k(x)\le Q(x)\quad\forall x.

notation.meaning: Common master point evaluated in round k.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Parallel Benders Evaluation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating parallel independent evaluation from a coupled subordinate solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Parallel block solves are equivalent to separate serial solves at a common \(x^k\) only when each block's feasible set, objective, and certificate are determined without subordinate variables or mutable state shared with another block. If a constraint \(H_{rs}(y_r,y_s,x^k)\le0\) remains, separate block optima are not certificates for the joint subordinate problem unless an additional valid decomposition or coordination construction is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual cross-block constraints place the subordinate problem outside the independent parallel-evaluation regime.
assumptions_latex: All workers evaluate the same master point \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_{rs}(y_r,y_s,x^k)\le0\text{ involving two blocks precludes uncoordinated independent certification.}

notation.meaning: Constraint coupling subordinate blocks r and s.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Independence Boundary
Parallel Subproblem Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous parallel evaluation of separable Benders subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the recourse function decomposes as \(Q(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S p_sQ_s(x)\). At master iteration \(k\), broadcast \(x^k\) to workers and evaluate all independent subproblems \(Q_s(x^k)\) concurrently. Worker \(s\) returns either valid cut data \((\alpha_s^k,\beta_s^k)\) satisfying \(Q_s(x)\ge\alpha_s^k+(\beta_s^k)^{\mathsf T}x\), or a valid feasibility certificate. After all required returns arrive, aggregate available optimality cuts using the weights \(p_s\), add the resulting cut or cuts to the master, and compute \(x^{k+1}\). Terminate when the prescribed feasibility and bound-gap tests hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Broadcast one master point, solve independent scenario or block subproblems concurrently, aggregate their valid certificates, refine the master, and repeat until termination.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(x^k\), the \(S\) subproblems share no decision variables.
Each worker returns a valid optimality cut or feasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Concurrent evaluation yields the same collection of block certificates as independent serial evaluation at \(x^k\).

children.title: Selective Subproblem Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Prioritized evaluation of a subset of subordinate blocks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prioritized subset evaluation with a precise bounded-coverage condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), choose a nonempty set \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,S\}\), evaluate only those blocks at \(x^k\), add every valid returned cut, and retain previously generated globally valid cuts. A bounded-coverage schedule satisfies \(\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+T-1}S_t=\{1,\ldots,S\}\) for every \(k\) and some \(T\in\mathbb N\). Equivalently, each block is omitted for at most \(T-1\) consecutive iterations. Termination requires current evaluation of every relevant block or valid bounds covering every omitted contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate selected blocks first, enforce bounded coverage, and do not terminate without current evidence or certified bounds for omitted blocks.
assumptions_latex: Every retained cut is globally valid on the master domain.
The bounded-coverage condition holds for some finite \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall s,k\ \exists t\in\{k,\ldots,k+T-1\}:s\in S_t.
knowledge_statements.title: Fair Selective Subproblem Evaluation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Current-point certificate permitting selected blocks to remain unevaluated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\sum_s p_sQ_s\) with \(p_s\ge0\), and fix \(\bar x\). Let \(E\) be evaluated exactly. If \(L_s(\bar x)\le Q_s(\bar x)\) for every block and \(0\le Q_s(\bar x)-L_s(\bar x)\le\Delta_s\) for every \(s\notin E\), then \[0\le Q(\bar x)-\sum_s p_sL_s(\bar x)\le\sum_{s\notin E}p_s\Delta_s.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitted blocks are safely skipped at a candidate only when their certified weighted error is within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(p_s\ge0\) for every block.
Evaluated blocks are exact at \(\bar x\).
Every omitted block has a valid current-point error bound \(\Delta_s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{s\notin E}p_s\Delta_s\le\varepsilon\Rightarrow Q(\bar x)-\sum_sp_sL_s(\bar x)\le\varepsilon.

notation.meaning: Blocks evaluated at the candidate point.
Certified error bound for an omitted block.

knowledge_statements.title: Omitted-Block Error Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure of subset-only current-point certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_1(x)=0\), \(Q_2(x)=x\), and \(Q=Q_1+Q_2\) on \([0,1]\). At \(\bar x=1\), evaluating only block 1 returns zero although \(Q(\bar x)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An evaluated subset can appear exact while an omitted block contributes positive error.
assumptions_latex: Only block 1 is evaluated at \(\bar x=1\).
No bound for block 2 is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncertified Omission Falsifies Aggregate Tests
Selective Subproblem Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fair subset scheduling for block-separable Benders refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), choose a nonempty index set \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,S\}\) using predicted violation, uncertainty, or elapsed time since evaluation. Evaluate only the subproblems in \(S_k\) at \(x^k\), add every returned valid cut, and retain all previously valid cuts from unevaluated blocks. Require bounded coverage: for some \(T\in\mathbb N\), \(\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+T-1}S_t=\{1,\ldots,S\}\) for every \(k\). A global termination certificate may be issued only after every block has been evaluated at the candidate point, or after valid blockwise bounds certify the omitted evaluations unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate promising subproblems first, but enforce bounded coverage and require current evidence from every relevant block before certifying global termination.
assumptions_latex: Every generated block cut is globally valid on the master domain.
The scheduler satisfies bounded coverage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No block remains unevaluated for more than \(T-1\) consecutive scheduling windows, and termination requires a complete valid certificate.

children.title: Subproblem Scheduling Granularity
children.top_down_role: Block grouping and evaluation frequency within coordinated execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Scheduling Granularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition-based definition of scheduling units for decomposed subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\{1,\ldots,S\}\) index elementary subproblems. A scheduling granularity is a partition \(\mathcal G=\{G_1,\ldots,G_m\}\) of \(I\) into nonempty groups; each group \(G_j\) is dispatched and synchronized as one task. The finest granularity is \(\{\{1\},\ldots,\{S\}\}\), while the coarsest is \(\{I\}\). In the local runtime model \(T(G)=h+\sum_{s\in G}t_s\), where \(h\ge0\) is per-task overhead and \(t_s\ge0\) is the computation time of subproblem \(s\). For \(P\in\mathbb N\) identical workers, let \(\mathcal A_1,\ldots,\mathcal A_P\) partition \(\mathcal G\) into the groups assigned to the workers. The modeled makespan is \(\max_{p\in\{1,\ldots,P\}}\sum_{G\in\mathcal A_p}T(G)\). Finer partitions expose more concurrency but incur the overhead \(h\) more often.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scheduling granularity partitions elementary subproblems into nonempty dispatch units. Smaller units expose more concurrency and load-balancing opportunities but incur dispatch and synchronization overhead more often.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\{1,\ldots,S\}\) is finite and \(S\in\mathbb N\).
The displayed runtime model assumes additive computation times \(t_s\ge0\) and fixed per-task overhead \(h\ge0\).
Each group in \(\mathcal G\) is dispatched exactly once to one of \(P\in\mathbb N\) identical workers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partition \(\mathcal G\) determines the \(m\) available scheduling units and contributes total modeled dispatch overhead \(mh\).

notation.meaning: task groups assigned to worker p

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Neither Extreme Granularity Uniformly Minimizes Makespan
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp overhead–parallelism examples under the accepted seed runtime model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(T(G)=h+\sum_{s\in G}t_s\), let \(S=P\ge2\). If \(h=0\) and \(t_s=1\), singleton groups have makespan \(1\), while the single group has makespan \(S\). Conversely, if \(P=1\) and \(h>0\), singleton groups have makespan \(\sum_st_s+Sh\), while the single group has makespan \(\sum_st_s+h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fine tasks win with abundant workers and no overhead; one coarse task wins on one worker with positive task overhead.
assumptions_latex: Runtime follows the accepted seed model \(T(G)=h+\sum_{s\in G}t_s\).
Each group is dispatched exactly once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Neither the finest nor coarsest partition minimizes makespan in every parameter regime.}
knowledge_statements.title: Neither Extreme Granularity Uniformly Minimizes Makespan

children.title: Subproblem Staleness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Reliability limits for master updates based on delayed subordinate information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delay definition and admissibility boundary for asynchronously returned Benders information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a block-s return accepted at master iteration \(k\) was generated from \(x^{\tau_{s,k}}\), define its delay by \(d_{s,k}=k-\tau_{s,k}\). A bounded-staleness regime requires \(0\le d_{s,k}\le D\) for every accepted return and some fixed \(D\in\mathbb N_0\). A delayed cut may refine the current master only when it remains globally valid; current-point termination additionally requires a fresh evaluation or a valid current-point error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound accepted delays, require global cut validity, and do not treat stale tightness as current-point certification.
assumptions_latex: Accepted returns identify the generating iteration \(\tau_{s,k}\).
Every delayed cut used for refinement is globally valid on the unchanged master domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le k-\tau_{s,k}\le D.

notation.meaning: Iteration whose master point generated the return.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Staleness Acceptance Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stale Tightness Is Not Current Tightness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal valid-but-nontight stale-cut example.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)=x^2\) on \([0,1]\). The supporting cut \(\ell(x)=0\) is exact at \(x^0=0\) and globally valid, but at \(x^1=1\) it has error \(Q(1)-\ell(1)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact old cut can stay valid while failing to certify the current value.
assumptions_latex: The cut was generated at \(x^0=0\).
The current point is \(x^1=1\).

notation.meaning: Supporting cut generated at the old point.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Tightness Is Not Current Tightness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cut Age Does Not Destroy Global Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of algebraic validity from freshness-dependent accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\ell(x)\le Q_s(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), and neither \(Q_s\) nor \(X\) changes, then the inequality remains valid at every later master point regardless of its generation time. Delay affects current-point tightness, reported values, violation estimates, and progress logic—not the inequality's validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally valid cut remains valid indefinitely under an unchanged model, although it may become very loose.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell\le Q_s\) globally on \(X\).
The block model and master domain are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell(x^k)\le Q_s(x^k)\quad\text{at every later }x^k\in X.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Age Does Not Destroy Global Validity
Subproblem Staleness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-delay admissibility condition for asynchronously returned Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a cut received at master iteration \(k\) have been generated from the earlier point \(x^{\tau_{s,k}}\) for block \(s\), where \(0\le\tau_{s,k}\le k\). Its delay is \(d_{s,k}=k-\tau_{s,k}\). A bounded-staleness schedule requires a constant \(D\in\mathbb N_0\) such that \(d_{s,k}\le D\) for every accepted return. A stale cut may refine the current master only if it remains globally valid for all master points. It may not alone certify current block optimality or termination; such certification requires evaluation at the candidate point or a separate valid error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept delayed cuts only within a fixed delay bound and only when globally valid; stale evaluations alone cannot certify optimality at the current master point.
assumptions_latex: Each accepted cut is globally valid despite being generated at an earlier point.
Accepted delays are uniformly bounded by \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le k-\tau_{s,k}\le D\), and stale returns are refinement information rather than current-point termination certificates.

notation.meaning: iteration whose master point generated the returned block cut
