children.title: Benders Refinement Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Modeling and numerical phenomena yielding invalid, weak, excessive, or unstable master refinement.

children.title: Benders Cut Strength-Loss Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Alternative subordinate certificates providing little new master strength.

children.title: Weak Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Valid cuts providing little improvement to the master approximation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact consequence of cut dominance for the current master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\ell_1(x)\le\ell_2(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), then \(\theta\ge\ell_2(x)\) implies \(\theta\ge\ell_1(x)\) on \(X\). Removing the first cut leaves the master feasible set and objective value unchanged. Small violation or inactivity at one point does not establish this implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-domain domination certifies redundancy; small impact at one iterate does not.
assumptions_latex: The two cuts are valid on the same domain \(X\).
The dominating cut remains in the master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell_1\le\ell_2\text{ on }X\Longrightarrow C_1\text{ is redundant in the presence of }C_2.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Redundancy Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical master-domain comparison of valid Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For valid epigraph cuts \(C_i:\theta\ge\ell_i(x)\) on \(X\), \(C_1\) is dominated by \(C_2\) when \(\ell_1(x)\le\ell_2(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), with strict inequality somewhere on \(X\). A valid cut is Pareto-optimal relative to the comparison class when no other valid cut dominates it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dominated cut is everywhere no stronger than another valid cut; a Pareto-optimal cut has no such dominator.
assumptions_latex: Both affine cuts are valid on the same master domain \(X\).
Both cuts use the epigraph orientation \(\theta\ge\ell_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_2\text{ dominates }C_1\iff \ell_2\ge\ell_1\text{ on }X\text{ and }\ell_2>\ell_1\text{ somewhere on }X.

notation.meaning: Affine right-hand side of cut i.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominated and Pareto-Optimal Benders Cuts
Weak Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational weakness criterion based on normalized separation at the generating point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C:\theta\ge\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\) be a valid Benders cut generated at the current master point \((x^k,,\theta^k)\). With positive scale \(s(C)>0\), define its normalized separation by \(\sigma_k(C)=[\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x^k-\theta^k]_+/s(C)\). Relative to a prescribed threshold \(\varepsilon_{m weak}>0\), call \(C\) weak at iteration \(k\) when \(0<\sigma_k(C)\le\varepsilon_{m weak}\). Such a cut is valid and separating, but it removes only a small normalized margin at the point that triggered it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weak cut is valid and separating but has normalized violation no larger than a chosen weakness threshold at its generating master point.
assumptions_latex: The cut is valid on the full master domain.
The positive scale \(s(C)\) is fixed consistently across compared cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is weak at iteration \(k\) exactly when \(0<\sigma_k(C)\le\varepsilon_{\rm weak}\).

notation.meaning: normalized separation produced by cut C

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The operational threshold definition is not shown to be a recognized meaning of weak Benders cuts, and no source is supplied. The generating point also contains the malformed expression \(x^k,,\theta^k\).

children.title: Nearly Parallel Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Successive cuts carrying largely redundant directional information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dominance test at the zero-angle limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(a_2=\lambda a_1\) with \(\lambda>0\). Then \[\{z:a_2^{\mathsf T}z\ge b_2\}\subseteq\{z:a_1^{\mathsf T}z\ge b_1\}\iff b_2/\lambda\ge b_1.\] Equality gives identical halfspaces; strict inequality gives a tighter parallel halfspace whenever the relevant boundaries meet the ambient domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positively parallel cuts, dominance is determined by the scaled offsets, not direction alone.
assumptions_latex: The cuts share the orientation \(a_i^{\mathsf T}z\ge b_i\).
\(a_1,a_2\ne0\) and \(a_2=\lambda a_1\) for \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{z:a_2^{\mathsf T}z\ge b_2\}\subseteq\{z:a_1^{\mathsf T}z\ge b_1\}\iff b_2/\lambda\ge b_1.

notation.meaning: Positive scaling between the oriented normals.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance of Exactly Parallel Cuts

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Oriented Near Parallelism of Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-invariant angular predicate for nonzero cut normals in a common inequality orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write two cuts in the common orientation \(a_i^{\mathsf T}z\ge b_i\), with \(a_i,a_j\ne0\). For \(\varepsilon_{\angle}\in[0,1)\), call them nearly parallel in the same direction when \[1-\frac{a_i^{\mathsf T}a_j}{\lVert a_i\rVert_2\lVert a_j\rVert_2}\le\varepsilon_{\angle}.\] Antiparallel normals are not identified under this oriented convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two commonly oriented cuts are nearly parallel when the cosine of their nonzero normals is close to one.
assumptions_latex: Both normals are nonzero.
Both inequalities use a common orientation and variable scaling.
\(\varepsilon_{\angle}\in[0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 1-\frac{a_i^{\mathsf T}a_j}{\lVert a_i\rVert_2\lVert a_j\rVert_2}\le\varepsilon_{\angle}.
knowledge_statements.title: Oriented Near Parallelism of Benders Cuts
Nearly Parallel Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Angular redundancy condition for normalized Benders cut normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write two nontrivial cuts in common orientation as \(a_i^{\mathsf T}z\ge b_i\) and \(a_j^{\mathsf T}z\ge b_j\), with \(a_i,a_j\ne0\). For an angular tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\angle}\in[0,1)\), the cuts are nearly parallel when \(1-|a_i^{\mathsf T}a_j|/(\|a_i\|_2\|a_j\|_2)\le\varepsilon_{\angle}\). If orientation must agree, replace the absolute value by \(a_i^{\mathsf T}a_j\) and require it to be positive. Near parallelism concerns directions only; it does not imply dominance, which additionally depends on offsets and the master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two cuts are nearly parallel when their normalized normals have cosine magnitude close to one. This angular test alone does not establish dominance.
assumptions_latex: Both cut normals are nonzero.
Both cuts use a common variable scaling and inequality orientation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(1-|a_i^{\mathsf T}a_j|/(\|a_i\|_2\|a_j\|_2)\le\varepsilon_{\angle}\) is the nearly-parallel predicate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed Benders-specific predicate. Using an absolute cosine treats antiparallel normals as nearly parallel even though, under a fixed inequality orientation, they describe opposing directions; the intended oriented or unoriented convention must be fixed.

children.title: Degenerate Cut Families
children.top_down_role: Alternative subordinate certificates yielding indistinguishable or marginal refinements.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact test for alternative certificates producing the same master refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\operatorname{aff}(X)=x_0+V\) and \(\ell_i(x)=\alpha_i+\beta_i^{\mathsf T}x\). Then \[\ell_1|_X=\ell_2|_X\iff (\beta_1-\beta_2)^{\mathsf T}v=0\ \forall v\in V\quad\text{and}\quad \ell_1(x_0)=\ell_2(x_0).\] If \(X\) is full-dimensional, this is equivalent to \(\alpha_1=\alpha_2\) and \(\beta_1=\beta_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two cuts are indistinguishable exactly when their affine functions agree on the master domain.
assumptions_latex: The two cuts share the same epigraph orientation.
The master domain has affine hull \(x_0+V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell_1|_X=\ell_2|_X\iff (\beta_1-\beta_2)\perp V\text{ and }\ell_1(x_0)=\ell_2(x_0).

notation.meaning: Linear space parallel to the affine hull of the master domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Indistinguishable-Cut Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicity of subordinate certificates as the source of alternative Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a fixed master point \(\bar x\), let \(D^\star(\bar x)\) be the optimal face of the subordinate dual and let each \(u\in D^\star(\bar x)\) induce \(\ell_u(x)=\alpha(u)+\beta(u)^{\mathsf T}x\). Every such cut is tight at \(\bar x\). Multiple optimal certificates may induce distinct supporting cuts, but certificate multiplicity alone does not imply distinct cuts because \(u\mapsto(\alpha(u),\beta(u))\) need not be injective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate subordinate dual can supply many optimal certificates; they may generate different cuts or the same cut.
assumptions_latex: \(D^\star(\bar x)\) is nonempty.
Every \(u\in D^\star(\bar x)\) induces a valid affine Benders estimator tight at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |D^\star(\bar x)|>1\text{ permits, but does not guarantee, distinct induced cuts}.

notation.meaning: Optimal subordinate-dual face at the generating point.
Affine cut induced by certificate u.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Certificate Degeneracy
Degenerate Cut Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-deficient or duplicate cut families that provide little independent refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For normalized cuts \(a_i^{\mathsf T}z\ge b_i\), \(i=1,,\ldots,m\), form the row matrix \(A=[a_1^{\mathsf T};,\ldots;a_m^{\mathsf T}]\). The family is directionally degenerate when \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\), and numerically degenerate at tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) when the smallest singular value associated with the row span satisfies \(\sigma_{\min}(A),\le\varepsilon\). Exact duplicate positive-scaled cuts are a special case after normalization. Adding such cuts can increase master size without adding comparable independent normal directions; rank deficiency alone, however, does not imply logical redundancy because distinct offsets can define distinct parallel supporting halfspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut family is degenerate when normalized normals are rank deficient or nearly so. This signals little directional diversity, though differing offsets may still matter.
assumptions_latex: All cut normals are expressed under one variable scaling and normalization.
The rank or singular-value test is applied to nonzero normals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\) characterizes exact directional degeneracy, while \(\sigma_{\min}(A)\le\varepsilon\) marks numerical degeneracy.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement contains malformed comma sequences and no supporting source. The phrase 'smallest singular value associated with the row span' is ambiguous and can exclude the zero singular values that detect rank deficiency; numerical degeneracy also requires a scale-aware singular-value convention.

children.title: Combined Strength-Loss Regimes
children.top_down_role: Interactions among weakness, directional redundancy, and degeneracy.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), the Benders master uses affine lower estimators \(\ell_j(x)=\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}x\) of the recourse function \(Q\) on a master domain \(X\).
A reference scale \(L>0\) and tolerances \(\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_a,\varepsilon_d>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is present precisely when all three displayed inequalities hold for a nonempty cut family.

notation.meaning: Normalized cut violation at the current master point
Normalized angular separation of two cut normals

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic intersection of weak, nearly parallel, and degenerate Benders cut behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cut family \(J_k\) is in a combined strength-loss regime at iteration \(k\) if there exists a nonempty subset \(I_k\subseteq J_k\) such that \[\max_{j\in I_k}s_j^k\leq\varepsilon_s,\qquad \max_{i,j\in I_k}a_{ij}\leq\varepsilon_a,\qquad \sigma_{\min}(B_{I_k})\leq\varepsilon_d,\] where \(B_{I_k}\) has normalized rows \(\beta_j^{\mathsf T}/\|\beta_j\|\). Thus the selected cuts simultaneously have small local violations, nearly coincident normal directions, and a numerically rank-deficient normal matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combined strength loss occurs when a nonempty cut family is simultaneously weak at the incumbent, nearly parallel, and numerically rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Combined Strength-Loss Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the failure-regime leaf, but its conjunction of violation, angular, and singular-value thresholds is nonstandard and uncited. It also requires nonzero cut normals, and the use of absolute inner products treats antiparallel normals as equivalent without justification.

children.title: Benders Master Progress Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Unstable coordinating decisions and slow late-stage bound closure.

children.title: Benders Master Oscillation
children.top_down_role: Unstable movement among coordinating master decisions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: False-positive boundary for definitions based only on master-solution movement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every relevant master has distinct tied optima \(a\ne b\), and the selection rule alternates \(x^{2j}=a\), \(x^{2j+1}=b\). Then \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|=\|a-b\|>0\), although the master objective is unchanged. Persistent movement alone therefore does not certify adverse bound behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver can alternate between tied master optima without adverse objective or bound behavior.
assumptions_latex: a\ne b
a\text{ and }b\text{ are tied optima for every relevant master}
x^{2j}=a,\quad x^{2j+1}=b
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x^{k+1}-x^k\|=\|a-b\|>0\quad\text{without adverse objective movement}.
knowledge_statements.title: Iterate Movement Without Adverse Progress

assumptions_latex:
The master iterates satisfy \(x^k\in X\subset\mathbb R^n\), where \(X
eq\varnothing\).
Two disjoint closed regions \(U,V\subset X\) have separation \(\operatorname{dist}(U,V)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The master oscillates between separated regions while the certified optimality gap fails to contract geometrically.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational definition for persistent two-region oscillation of Benders master solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Benders master oscillation occurs if there exist disjoint closed sets \(U,V\subset X\), an index \(k_0\), and infinitely many indices \(k\geq k_0\) such that \(x^k\in U\) and \(x^{k+1}\in V\), or \(x^k\in V\) and \(x^{k+1}\in U\), while \[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{g_{k+1}}{g_k}=1\] along indices with \(g_k>0\). The positive set separation excludes harmless movement among nearby master optima.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Master oscillation is persistent alternation between separated regions while the certified gap has asymptotic contraction factor one.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Master Oscillation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The container and definition role fit, but the separated-region and asymptotic-gap criterion is an uncited operational definition. A specialized source is needed to establish that this is the intended Benders notion and to specify the indices on which the gap ratio is evaluated.

children.title: Benders Master Tailing-Off
children.top_down_role: Slow late-stage closure of the master-subproblem bound gap.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sublinear Gap Closure Without Uniform Linear Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence separating convergence to zero from eventual geometric contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g_k=(k+1)^{-1}\), \(g_k\downarrow0\) and \(g_{k+1}/g_k=(k+1)/(k+2)\to1\). Thus convergence of a positive gap does not imply an eventual uniform contraction factor below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sequence 1/(k+1) closes to zero but has asymptotic contraction factor one.
assumptions_latex: g_k=\frac{1}{k+1}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g_k\downarrow0,\qquad \frac{g_{k+1}}{g_k}\to1.
knowledge_statements.title: Sublinear Gap Closure Without Uniform Linear Contraction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rate boundary excluding ratio-one gap behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(0<g_{k+1}\le qg_k\) for every \(k\ge k_0\), where \(0\le q<1\), then \(g_k\le g_{k_0}q^{k-k_0}\) and \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}g_{k+1}/g_k\le q<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eventual uniform geometric contraction rules out asymptotic contraction factor one.
assumptions_latex: 0<g_{k+1}\le qg_k\quad(k\ge k_0)
0\le q<1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g_k\le g_{k_0}q^{k-k_0},\qquad \limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{g_{k+1}}{g_k}\le q<1.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Geometric Closure Boundary

assumptions_latex: The Benders procedure maintains valid bounds \(L_k\leq z^\star\leq U_k\) with gaps \(g_k=U_k-L_k>0\).
The gap sequence is nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method exhibits tailing-off exactly when \(g_k\to0\) but its asymptotic linear contraction factor equals one.

notation.meaning: Valid lower and upper bounds after iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic gap-based definition, independent of wall-clock implementation details.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Benders master tailing-off is the asymptotic regime characterized by \[g_k\longrightarrow0,\qquad \limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{g_{k+1}}{g_k}=1.\] Equivalently, convergence continues, but no uniform factor \(q<1\) and index \(k_0\) satisfy \(g_{k+1}\leq qg_k\) for every \(k\geq k_0\). This condition distinguishes slow terminal progress from finite stagnation at a positive gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tailing-off means the valid Benders gap converges to zero without any eventual uniform linear contraction factor below one.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Master Tailing-Off

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Under the stated positive, nonincreasing gap assumptions, the displayed condition and its uniform-contraction reformulation are consistent. However, identifying this exact asymptotic condition with Benders tailing-off requires a specific source.

children.title: Oscillation-Induced Slowdown
children.top_down_role: Late-stage degradation associated with unstable master movement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Oscillation Alone Does Not Establish Slowdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary requiring an additional link between master movement and progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Alternation of master iterates is compatible with a gap sequence satisfying \(g_{k+1}=qg_k\) for fixed \(q\in(0,1)\). Under those conditions \(g_k=q^kg_0\), so the movement observation alone cannot imply tailing-off or vanishing relative progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Master alternation is logically compatible with geometric gap closure; an additional causal mechanism is required.
assumptions_latex: x^{2j}=a,\quad x^{2j+1}=b,\quad a\ne b
g_{k+1}=qg_k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g_k=q^kg_0,\qquad g_{k+1}/g_k=q<1.
knowledge_statements.title: Oscillation Alone Does Not Establish Slowdown

assumptions_latex: The master iterates alternate infinitely often between closed sets \(U,V\) with \(\operatorname{dist}(U,V)>0\).
Every cut generated at a point of either set improves the master lower bound by at most \(\delta_k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\delta_k\to0\) along oscillating iterations, then per-iteration lower-bound progress vanishes along that subsequence.

notation.meaning: Master lower bound after iteration k
Upper bound on the improvement produced at iteration k
Indices at which an inter-region transition occurs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slowdown mechanism caused by repeatedly refining separated regions with diminishing cut impact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_{UV}\) be the infinite set of iterations at which the master solution moves between \(U\) and \(V\). If valid cut addition gives \[0\leq L_{k+1}-L_k\leq\delta_k\qquad(k\in K_{UV})\] and \(\delta_k\to0\) along \(K_{UV}\), then \[L_{k+1}-L_k\longrightarrow0\qquad(k\in K_{UV}).\] Hence persistent separated-region oscillation, coupled with diminishing local cut impact, forces an infinite subsequence of vanishing master-bound improvements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When alternating regions receive cuts of diminishing impact, lower-bound improvement vanishes along the oscillating subsequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Oscillation-Induced Slowdown

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property matches the slowdown leaf and the implication is mathematically immediate from the stated bound, but the claimed Benders oscillation mechanism and its interpretation lack supporting evidence.

children.title: Benders Master Congestion Regimes
children.top_down_role: Excessive cut accumulation overwhelming master reoptimization.

children.title: Benders Master Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion of the master through accumulated refinement cuts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing that retention alone does not force indefinite master growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If all retained cuts belong to a finite universe \(\mathcal C\), with \(|\mathcal C|=N\), and duplicates are not inserted, then \(J_k\subseteq\mathcal C\) and \(|J_k|\le N\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite universe of distinct cuts caps master growth even when every generated cut is retained.
assumptions_latex: |\mathcal C|=N<\infty
J_k\subseteq\mathcal C
Duplicate cuts are not inserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |J_k|\le N\quad\text{for every }k.

notation.meaning: Finite universe of distinct admissible cuts

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Cut-Universe Growth Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-count growth indexed separately by iterations and actual cut additions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J_k\) be the retained cuts after iteration \(k\), and let \(a_k\) count distinct cuts added through iteration \(k\). If cuts are never deleted, then \(J_k\subseteq J_{k+1}\) and \(|J_k|=|J_0|+a_k\). Thus \(|J_k|\to\infty\) exactly when \(a_k\to\infty\); if every iteration adds at least one distinct cut, then \(|J_k|\ge |J_0|+k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without deletion, master size equals its initial size plus the number of distinct retained additions; iteration-linear growth requires an addition every iteration.
assumptions_latex: No retained cut is deleted or aggregated away.
\(a_k\) counts distinct cuts inserted after initialization through iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |J_k|=|J_0|+a_k;\qquad a_k\to\infty\Longleftrightarrow |J_k|\to\infty.

notation.meaning: Number of distinct post-initialization cut additions through iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Retained-Cut Cardinality Growth

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), the master contains all retained Benders cuts indexed by \(J_k\).
At least one new cut is retained at infinitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without cut deletion or aggregation, the master description grows unboundedly and has at least \(|J_0|+k\) retained cuts after \(k\) additions.

notation.meaning: Indices of cuts retained in the master at iteration k
Master feasible region after iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone constraint growth when every generated Benders cut is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If cuts are never deleted or aggregated, then \(J_k\subseteq J_{k+1}\) and \[M_k=\{(x,\theta):x\in X,\ \theta\geq\ell_j(x)\ \text{for every }j\in J_k\}.\] If at least one new cut is added at each iteration, then \(|J_k|\geq|J_0|+k\). Consequently the number of master inequalities, and therefore the explicit master input size, grows at least linearly with the number of Benders iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retaining every new Benders cut makes the explicit master constraint count grow at least linearly with the iteration count.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Master Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the master-growth leaf and is correct if every indexed iteration adds at least one retained cut. The assumptions instead say this occurs only at infinitely many iterations, while the statement asserts the stronger bound after every iteration; the iteration/addition indexing and an implementation source are needed.

children.title: Benders Cut Congestion
children.top_down_role: Computational burden from excessive or redundant active cuts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe compression of a Benders cut pool using exact implication certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) index cuts \(\theta\ge\ell_j(x)\) on \(X\). Suppose that for every \(j\in D\subseteq J\), some retained \(i\in J\setminus D\) satisfies \(\ell_j(x)\le\ell_i(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Then \[\mathcal M(J)=\mathcal M(J\setminus D),\qquad \mathcal M(S):=\{(x,\theta):x\in X,\ \theta\ge\ell_j(x)\ \forall j\in S\}.\] Thus deleting \(D\) preserves all master objective values, optimizer sets, and lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cuts dominated everywhere by retained cuts can be deleted without changing the master.
assumptions_latex: All cuts share the same master domain and epigraph orientation.
Each deleted cut has a retained full-domain dominator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M(J)=\mathcal M(J\setminus D).

notation.meaning: Master feasible set induced by cut set S.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance-Based Congestion Pruning

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Current Inactivity Is Not a Deletion Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for activity-only pruning of a congested cut pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[0,1]\), consider \(\ell_1(x)=x\) and \(\ell_2(x)=1-x\). At \(x=0\), the cut \(\theta\ge\ell_1(x)\) is weaker than \(\theta\ge\ell_2(x)\), but at \(x=1\) it is uniquely stronger. Hence inactivity at one master solution does not certify safe permanent deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A currently inactive cut may be strongest elsewhere, so activity alone cannot justify permanent deletion.
assumptions_latex: Both displayed epigraph cuts are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Inactivity at one master point does not imply global redundancy}.
knowledge_statements.title: Current Inactivity Is Not a Deletion Certificate

assumptions_latex: The master retains affine cuts \(\ell_j(x)=\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}x\) indexed by \(J_k\).
Activity and angular tolerances \(\varepsilon_v,\varepsilon_a>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Congestion occurs when the fraction of retained cuts that are inactive or directionally redundant tends to one.

notation.meaning: Cuts active within tolerance at the master solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational congestion predicate based on inactivity and near-duplicate cut directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(A_k=\{j\in J_k:|\theta^k-\ell_j(x^k)|\leq\varepsilon_v\}\). Let \(R_k\) contain each \(j\in J_k\) for which some earlier \(i\in J_k\) satisfies \(1-|\beta_i^{\mathsf T}\beta_j|/(\|\beta_i\|\|\beta_j\|)\leq\varepsilon_a\). Benders cut congestion is the regime \[|J_k|\to\infty,\qquad \frac{|(J_k\setminus A_k)\cup R_k|}{|J_k|}\to1.\] Thus almost all stored cuts are inactive at the incumbent or nearly duplicate an existing normal direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut congestion occurs when the master grows while almost every retained cut is inactive or directionally redundant.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Cut Congestion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the congestion leaf, but the proposed limiting fraction is an uncited diagnostic. “Earlier” is not formalized, and the angular expression is undefined for zero-normal cuts.

children.title: Master Reoptimization Saturation
children.top_down_role: Runtime degradation when repeated solution of the expanded master dominates progress.

assumptions_latex: The master solution time at iteration \(k\) is \(T_k>0\), and the valid lower-bound improvement is \(\Delta_k=L_{k+1}-L_k\geq0\).
The retained master size satisfies \(|J_k|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reoptimization saturation holds when certified lower-bound improvement per unit master-solve time tends to zero.

notation.meaning: Time required to reoptimize the iteration-k master

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implementation-sensitive saturation criterion using progress per unit master reoptimization time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Master reoptimization saturation is the regime in which \[|J_k|\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad \frac{\Delta_k}{T_k}\longrightarrow0.\] If additionally \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}T_k>0\), saturation follows whenever \(\Delta_k\to0\); if \(T_k\to\infty\), it may occur even with nonvanishing absolute improvements. The definition measures certified optimization progress per unit time and therefore depends on the solver, hardware, and retained master formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reoptimization saturates when a growing master yields asymptotically zero certified bound improvement per unit solve time.
knowledge_statements.title: Master Reoptimization Saturation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the saturation leaf and its conditional observations are mathematically consistent. The progress-per-time definition is solver- and hardware-dependent and needs an inspectable performance or Benders implementation source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Master Size Does Not Imply Reoptimization Saturation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected abstract sequence that is not shown to arise from a valid Benders execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proposed numerical sequences \(|J_k|=k\), \(T_k=1\), and \(\Delta_k=1\) imply \(\Delta_k/T_k=1\), but no Benders model or valid bound sequence realizing them is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The abstract sequences show only arithmetic independence, not a realizable Benders counterexample.
assumptions_latex: |J_k|=k
T_k=1
\Delta_k=1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Delta_k/T_k=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Master Size Does Not Imply Reoptimization Saturation

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf should own measured degradation of repeated master reoptimization. Benders Master Growth and Benders Cut Congestion were excluded as structural sibling pathologies. The central metric remains materially ambiguous, so publication is deferred.

children.title: Invalid Cuts from Local or Inexact Solves
children.top_down_role: Loss of global master validity when subordinate certificates are unreliable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual-Feasibility Certificate for Inexact Optimality Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe use of a nonoptimal subordinate dual point in linear Benders decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q(x)=\min\{q^\top y:Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge0\}\), any computed \(\widehat\pi\ge0\) satisfying \(W^\top\widehat\pi\le q\) is dual feasible. Weak duality gives \(\widehat\pi^\top(h-Tx)\le Q(x)\) wherever the subordinate primal is feasible with finite value, so \(\theta\ge\widehat\pi^\top(h-Tx)\) is globally valid even if \(\widehat\pi\) is not dual optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonoptimal dual solution still gives a valid Benders cut when dual feasibility is certified.
assumptions_latex: \widehat\pi\ge0
W^\top\widehat\pi\le q
Q(x)\text{ is finite at the considered master points}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\pi^\top(h-Tx)\le Q(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Feasibility Certificate for Inexact Optimality Cuts

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity test for a feasibility cut obtained from an approximate ray computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Wy\ge h-Tx\), \(y\ge0\), a computed vector \(\widehat r\) certifies \(\widehat r^\top(h-Tx)\le0\) only when \(\widehat r\ge0\) and \(W^\top\widehat r\le0\). Without these cone conditions, Farkas' implication does not certify global validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate feasibility ray is safe only after its dual-cone conditions are certified.
assumptions_latex: Wy\ge h-Tx
y\ge0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat r\ge0,\ W^\top\widehat r\le0\Longrightarrow[\text{subordinate feasibility}\Rightarrow\widehat r^\top(h-Tx)\le0].
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Feasibility-Ray Requirement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restoring exact validity from a certified uniform overestimation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an affine estimator \(\widehat\ell\) satisfies \(\widehat\ell(x)\le Q(x)+\varepsilon\) for every \(x\in X\), with \(\varepsilon\ge0\), then \(\widehat\ell(x)-\varepsilon\le Q(x)\) on \(X\). Hence \(\theta\ge\widehat\ell(x)-\varepsilon\) is exactly valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a certified uniform error bound converts an epsilon-valid estimator into an exactly valid cut.
assumptions_latex: \widehat\ell(x)\le Q(x)+\varepsilon\quad\text{for every }x\in X
\varepsilon\ge0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\ell(x)-\varepsilon\le Q(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in X.
knowledge_statements.title: Correction of Uniformly Epsilon-Valid Cuts
Invalid Cuts from Local or Inexact Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-validity boundary for cuts produced by local or insufficiently accurate subordinate solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, a Benders optimality cut is globally valid exactly when \(\ell_k(x)\leq Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). A merely local subordinate solution, or an inexact dual vector lacking a certified dual-feasible bound, need not satisfy this inequality. If some \(\bar x\in X\) obeys \(\ell_k(\bar x)>Q(\bar x)\), then \((\bar x,Q(\bar x))\in\operatorname{epi}Q\) violates \(\theta\geq\ell_k(x)\). Consequently, the master approximation is invalid and can remove a globally optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally or inexactly derived cut is unsafe whenever it exceeds the global recourse value somewhere, because it can exclude a true optimum.
assumptions_latex: For each master point \(x\in X\), the true recourse value is the global infimum \(Q(x)=\inf_{y\in Y(x)}f(x,y)\).
A generated optimality cut \(\ell_k\) is accepted into a minimization master as a claimed global lower estimator of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\ell_k(\bar x)>Q(\bar x)\) at any feasible \(\bar x\), the cut is invalid and may exclude the true epigraph and a global optimum.

notation.meaning: Cut derived from a subordinate certificate
Epigraph of the true recourse function

children.title: Poor Complicating-Variable Partitioning
children.top_down_role: Partitions leaving hard subproblems or an ineffective master projection.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partition Quality Is Not an Exactness Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating computationally poor partitioning from an inexact reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a declared master block \(x\in X\), define \(Q(x)=\inf\{f(x,y):y\in Y(x)\}\) using extended-real values. Then \(\inf_{x\in X,\,y\in Y(x)}f(x,y)=\inf_{x\in X}Q(x)\), independently of the difficulty of evaluating \(Q\). Thus a computationally poor partition need not destroy exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact partial minimization preserves the model for any partition; poor partitioning is computational rather than automatically mathematical failure.
assumptions_latex: Q(x)=\inf\{f(x,y):y\in Y(x)\}
Extended-real values record infeasibility or unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\in X,\,y\in Y(x)}f(x,y)=\inf_{x\in X}Q(x).

notation.meaning: Exact subordinate value function induced by the partition

knowledge_statements.title: Partition Quality Is Not an Exactness Condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Solver-Independent Ordering of Exact Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Problem-dependent tradeoff between subordinate tractability and master effectiveness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact choices of complicating variables can induce the same global optimum while differing in subordinate dimension, integrality, conditioning, and master description. Without a specified solver, cut family, tolerances, and cost model, exactness yields no universal ordering by total work or convergence speed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact Benders partitions cannot be ranked universally without a solver and performance model.
assumptions_latex: Each partition represents its induced value function exactly.
No subordinate solver, cut family, tolerance protocol, or computational cost model is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Exactness alone implies no universal computational ordering of the partitions.}
knowledge_statements.title: No Solver-Independent Ordering of Exact Partitions

assumptions_latex: A formulation is partitioned into master variables \(x\in X\) and subordinate variables \(y\in Y(x)\).
The subordinate value function is \(Q(x)=\inf_{y\in Y(x)}f(x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partition is poor when it fails either tractable-subproblem or informative-projection requirements.

notation.meaning: Complicating variables retained in the master
Variables assigned to the subordinate problem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural failure boundary balancing subordinate tractability against master informativeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Relative to a specified subordinate solver class \(\mathcal S\) and master cut class \(\mathcal C\), a partition is poor if at least one of the following holds: the problem defining \(Q(x)\) is outside \(\mathcal S\) for some reachable \(x\); or distinct relevant points \(x,x'\in X\) cannot be separated to the required tolerance by cuts in \(\mathcal C\) derived from \(Q\). The first failure leaves hard subordinate problems; the second produces an ineffective master projection even when subordinate solves are tractable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition is poor if subordinate problems remain outside the intended solver class or available cuts cannot distinguish relevant master decisions.
knowledge_statements.title: Poor Complicating-Variable Partitioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the leaf, but “reachable,” “relevant,” “required tolerance,” and separation by a cut class are not formally defined. A problem-class-specific source is needed before a reliable mathematical boundary can be selected.

children.title: Lagrangian-Dantzig-Wolfe Bound Correspondence
children.top_down_role: The shared bound structure behind coupling relaxation and block convexification.

children.title: Lagrangian Bound View
children.top_down_role: Bound interpretation arising from relaxation of coupling constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Bound View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional separable minimization with coupling equalities dualized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite block index set. Dualizing \(\sum_{i\in I}A_i x_i=b\) with \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) gives the separable dual function \[q(\lambda)=\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_{i\in I}\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i-\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_i x_i\bigr).\] The Lagrangian bound for the minimization problem is \[z_{\mathrm{LD}}=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}q(\lambda)\leq z^\star.\] Each evaluation of \(q\) decomposes by block, and weak duality does not require the sets \(X_i\) to be convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing the coupling equality yields a sum of independent block infima; maximizing this dual function gives a valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The block index set \(I\) is finite; each \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) is nonempty; \(A_i\in\mathbb R^{m\times n_i}\), \(c_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
The primal block problem \(z^\star=\inf\{\sum_{i\in I}c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i:\sum_{i\in I}A_i x_i=b,\ x_i\in X_i\}\) has a finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrangian bound is \(z_{\mathrm{LD}}=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}q(\lambda)\) and satisfies \(z_{\mathrm{LD}}\leq z^\star\).

source_refs.source_title: Practical Methods of Optimization

children.title: Dantzig-Wolfe Bound View
children.top_down_role: Bound interpretation arising from block convexification.

knowledge_statements.title: Dantzig-Wolfe Bound View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise convexification view of the Dantzig-Wolfe lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite block index set. For the block problem \(\inf\{\sum_{i\in I}c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i:\sum_{i\in I}A_i x_i=b,\ x_i\in X_i\}\), the Dantzig-Wolfe relaxation has value \[z_{\mathrm{DW}}=\min\left\{\sum_{i\in I}c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i:\sum_{i\in I}A_i x_i=b,\ x_i\in\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\right\}.\] Equivalently, each \(x_i\) is represented as a convex combination of points in \(X_i\). This convexified minimization problem satisfies \(z_{\mathrm{DW}}\leq z^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dantzig-Wolfe replaces every block set by its convex hull, producing a convexified master whose optimum lower-bounds the original minimum.
assumptions_latex: The block index set \(I\) is finite; each \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) is nonempty and compact; \(A_i\in\mathbb R^{m\times n_i}\), \(c_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
The original block problem is feasible and has finite optimal value \(z^\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Dantzig-Wolfe bound is the optimum over blockwise convex hulls and satisfies \(z_{\mathrm{DW}}\leq z^\star\).

children.title: Bound-Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural settings supporting matching bounds across the two views.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional compact-block regime for Lagrangian-Dantzig-Wolfe bound equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite block index set and define \[z^\star=\min\left\{\sum_{i\in I}c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i:\sum_{i\in I}A_i x_i=b,\ x_i\in X_i\right\}.\] Let \(z_{\mathrm{LD}}\) be the bound obtained by Lagrangian relaxation of the coupling equality, and let \(z_{\mathrm{DW}}\) be the bound obtained by replacing every \(X_i\) with \(\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\). Under the stated compactness, feasibility, and finiteness assumptions, \[z_{\mathrm{LD}}=z_{\mathrm{DW}}\leq z^\star.\] Equality with \(z^\star\) additionally requires the blockwise convexification to have no relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For compact finite-dimensional blocks, dualizing the coupling constraints and convexifying each block produce the same lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The block index set \(I\) is finite; each \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) is nonempty and compact; \(A_i\in\mathbb R^{m\times n_i}\), \(c_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
The blockwise convexified problem is feasible and has finite value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrangian-dual and Dantzig-Wolfe relaxation bounds coincide: \(z_{\mathrm{LD}}=z_{\mathrm{DW}}\leq z^\star\).

notation.meaning: Lagrangian dual bound obtained by dualizing coupling equalities

children.title: Bound-Correspondence Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Modeling regimes where the two bound constructions cease to align.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Domain-Only Convexification Can Break Bound Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by convexifying a block domain while reevaluating the original nonlinear cost at averaged points instead of convexifying the resource-cost epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the block data \(X=\{-1,1\}\), \(f(x)=x^2\), and coupling equation \(x=0\). The optimized Lagrangian value is \[d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R}\min_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+\lambda x\bigr)=1.\] The cost-bearing Dantzig-Wolfe master has \(\alpha_-,\alpha_+\ge0\), \(\alpha_-+\alpha_+=1\), \(-\alpha_-+\alpha_+=0\), and objective \(\alpha_-f(-1)+\alpha_+f(1)\), hence value \(z_{\mathrm{DW}}=1\). Replacing only \(X\) by \([-1,1]\) and evaluating \(f\) at the averaged point gives \(z_{\mathrm{domain\text{-}only}}=0\). Therefore bound correspondence requires convexification of the joint resource-cost epigraph, equivalently cost-bearing columns, rather than domain-only convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying only the domain and reevaluating a nonlinear cost at averaged points can yield a different value from both Lagrangian relaxation and the correct cost-column master.
assumptions_latex: x=0\text{ is the coupling equation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^*=z_{\mathrm{DW}}=1\ne0=z_{\mathrm{domain\text{-}only}}.

notation.meaning: Value after convexifying only the block domain

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Only Convexification Can Break Bound Correspondence

assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and the block objectives and coupling maps are linear.
\(\varphi\) is proper and \(b\in\operatorname{dom}\varphi\).
The Lagrangian multiplier ranges over all of \(\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_{\mathrm{LD}}=\varphi^{**}(b)\leq \varphi(b)=z_{\mathrm{DW}},\qquad z_{\mathrm{LD}}=z_{\mathrm{DW}}\iff\varphi^{**}(b)=\varphi(b).

notation.meaning: Lower-semicontinuous convex closure of the resource-value function

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact criterion separating the unrestricted Lagrangian bound from the complete block-convexification value at the required coupling resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the convexified resource-value function \[\varphi(r)=\inf\left\{\sum_{i\in I}c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i:\sum_{i\in I}A_i x_i=r,\ x_i\in\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\right\}.\] If \(\varphi\) is proper, the complete Dantzig-Wolfe value is \(z_{\mathrm{DW}}=\varphi(b)\), whereas the unrestricted Lagrangian bound is \(z_{\mathrm{LD}}=\varphi^{**}(b)\). Consequently, \(z_{\mathrm{LD}}=z_{\mathrm{DW}}\) exactly when \(\varphi(b)=\varphi^{**}(b)\); lower semicontinuity of \(\varphi\) at \(b\) is sufficient. If \(\varphi^{**}(b)<\varphi(b)\), correspondence fails by that strict amount.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bounds agree at the required resource exactly when the convexified resource-value function equals its lower-semicontinuous convex closure there; a closure gap produces a strict bound gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Function Closedness Boundary

assumptions_latex: The primal problem is \(\min\{x:x\in\{0,1\},\ 1-x\le 0\}\).
The Lagrangian multiplier is restricted to \(0\le\lambda\le\bar\lambda<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\bar\lambda}=\bar\lambda<1=z_{\mathrm{DW}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure caused by restricting multipliers while retaining all Dantzig-Wolfe columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Relax \(1-x\le 0\) with \(\lambda\in[0,\bar\lambda]\). The restricted Lagrangian bound is \[d_{\bar\lambda}=\max_{0\le\lambda\le\bar\lambda}\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}\bigl(x+\lambda(1-x)\bigr)=\max_{0\le\lambda\le\bar\lambda}\min\{\lambda,1\}=\bar\lambda.\] The complete Dantzig-Wolfe master over columns \(x=0\) and \(x=1\), including the original constraint, has value \(z_{\mathrm{DW}}=1\). Thus bound correspondence requires the full multiplier domain of the relaxed coupling constraints; restricted multipliers can produce a strictly weaker bound even when the column set is complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting the Lagrangian multiplier below one yields bound bar-lambda, whereas the complete Dantzig-Wolfe convexification yields one; hence the usual bound correspondence fails.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Correspondence Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample and bound calculations are mathematically consistent, and failure_boundary fits the terminal container, but no inspectable source supports the named correspondence boundary.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(R\) are finite subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\).
\(P=\operatorname{conv}(V)+\operatorname{cone}(R)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\{\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_vv+\sum_{r\in R}\mu_rr:\lambda\ge0,\ \mu\ge0,\ \sum_v\lambda_v=1\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) belongs to \(P\) exactly when there exist coefficients \(\lambda_v\ge0\) for \(v\in V\) and \(\mu_r\ge0\) for \(r\in R\) satisfying \[\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_v=1,\qquad x=\sum_{v\in V}\lambda_vv+\sum_{r\in R}\mu_rr.\] Consequently, replacing \(x\in P\) by these equations gives an extended formulation whose projection onto the \(x\)-space is precisely \(P\). In block decomposition, each \(v\) or \(r\) is a Dantzig-Wolfe column and the linking constraints act on its projected image.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedron represented by its points and rays is exactly the projection of the corresponding nonnegative column-weight formulation.

By the finite-dimensional alternative for linear inequalities, \[x\in\operatorname{proj}_x Q\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad u^T(h-Tx)\le0\quad\text{for every }u\in U.\] Hence elimination of the subordinate variable \(y\) produces a row description in the retained \(x\)-space. Extreme rays of the polyhedral cone \(U\) suffice, and each resulting inequality is a Benders feasibility cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating a nonnegative subordinate block yields exactly the family of Farkas inequalities indexed by the dual cone; its extreme rays generate Benders feasibility cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Duality Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic polarity interface between a column-generated cone and its valid-row description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the closed convex cone \(K\), bipolar duality gives \[K=K^{**}=\{z\in\mathbb R^d:\langle u,z\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }u\in K^*\}.\] Consequently, when a homogenized Dantzig-Wolfe formulation represents feasible points through generators of \(K\), the corresponding valid homogeneous rows are indexed by \(K^*\). A Benders row formulation containing all those inequalities imposes exactly the same cone-membership condition. If \(K\) is polyhedral, finite generator descriptions exist for both \(K\) and \(K^*\), with lineality represented explicitly where present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed convex cone, membership is equivalent to satisfaction of every inequality indexed by its dual cone. Thus complete column and valid-row formulations of the same homogenized cone are dual descriptions, with lineality handled explicitly in polyhedral finite representations.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
\(K^*=\{u\in\mathbb R^d:\langle u,z\rangle\ge0\ \forall z\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z\in K\iff\langle u,z\rangle\ge0\) for every \(u\in K^*\).

children.title: Projection-Duality Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of the row-column correspondence across model regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite exact column and row descriptions for a closed nonpolyhedral cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2:t\ge\|x\|_2\}\). This closed self-dual second-order cone has infinitely many extreme rays and admits no finite generating-ray description. Its self-duality likewise precludes a finite exact description by homogeneous linear inequalities. Thus conic polarity remains exact, but finite Dantzig-Wolfe column and Benders row descriptions require additional structure such as polyhedrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order cone has exact conic polarity but neither a finite ray description nor a finite homogeneous linear-inequality description.
assumptions_latex: K=\{(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2:t\ge\|x\|_2\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ has neither a finite generating-ray description nor a finite homogeneous halfspace description.}
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Generation Boundary Outside Polyhedral Geometry

assumptions_latex: \(C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x>0,\ y\ge1/x\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x C=(0,\infty)\neq[0,\infty)=\overline{\operatorname{proj}_x C}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonpolyhedral projection need not be closed, so closed-halfspace dual descriptions may recover only its closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \(C\) is closed and convex, but its projection onto the first coordinate is \(\operatorname{proj}_x C=(0,\infty)\), which is not closed. Every closed halfspace containing this projection also contains \(0\), so the intersection of all such halfspaces is \([0,\infty)=\overline{\operatorname{proj}_x C}\), not the projection itself. Therefore an exact column-versus-row projection duality based on closed polar or separating inequalities requires an appropriate closedness condition; without it, the row description can identify only the closure of the column projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex set can have a nonclosed projection; then closed separating inequalities describe the projection's closure rather than the projection itself.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Duality Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The closed convex example and its nonclosed projection are correct, and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but the record supplies no source for the projection-closedness boundary.

children.title: Pricing-Oracle View
children.top_down_role: Generated-variable interpretation of block optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Oracle View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduced-cost pricing and its stopping condition for a minimization master with nonnegative columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the reduced cost \(\bar c_\pi(v)=c(v)-\pi^Ta(v)\). A pricing oracle returns a minimizer of \[\min_{v\in V}\bar c_\pi(v).\] If the minimum is negative, the returned \(v\) violates the full-master dual inequality \(\pi^Ta(v)\le c(v)\) and is eligible to enter the restricted master. If the minimum is nonnegative, every such inequality holds, so \(\pi\) is feasible for the dual of the full column master. This equivalence presumes exact optimization over the complete admissible column set \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing minimizes reduced cost over all admissible columns. A negative result identifies a dual-violating candidate column, while a nonnegative minimum certifies full-master dual feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The full master is \(\min\{\sum_{v\in V}c(v)\lambda_v:\sum_{v\in V}a(v)\lambda_v=b,\ \lambda\ge0\}\).
\(\pi\in\mathbb R^m\) is a candidate multiplier for the equality constraints.
The displayed pricing minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{v\in V}\{c(v)-\pi^Ta(v)\}\ge0\iff \pi^Ta(v)\le c(v)\) for every \(v\in V\).

\(r(v)=c(v)-\pi^Ta(v)\), and the oracle returns \(\hat v\in V\) satisfying \(r(\hat v)\le r_*+\delta\).
\(\delta\ge0\), and the additive guarantee has the displayed minimization direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r(\hat v)<0\Rightarrow r_*<0,\qquad r(\hat v)\ge\delta\Rightarrow r_*\ge0.

notation.meaning: Infimum reduced cost over all admissible columns
Admissible column returned by the approximate oracle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Improvement and exhaustion conclusions available from an additively approximate reduced-cost minimization oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_*:=\inf_{v\in V}r(v)\), where \(r(v)=c(v)-\pi^Ta(v)\), and suppose an oracle returns \(\hat v\in V\) satisfying \(r(\hat v)\le r_*+\delta\) for \(\delta\ge0\). Since \(r_*\le r(\hat v)\), the guarantee gives \[r(\hat v)-\delta\le r_*\le r(\hat v).\] Hence \(r(\hat v)<0\) is an improving-column certificate, and \(r(\hat v)\ge\delta\) certifies \(r_*\ge0\) and therefore full pricing exhaustion. If \(0\le r(\hat v)<\delta\), the oracle output alone is inconclusive: the true infimum may be negative or nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive pricing guarantee brackets the true minimum between the returned reduced cost minus the tolerance and the returned reduced cost. A negative return certifies improvement, a return at least equal to the tolerance certifies exhaustion, and the intervening band is inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.title: Additively Inexact Pricing Outcomes

knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Oracle View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of the full-master dual region by an attained reduced-cost minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\pi\in\mathbb R^m\), compute \(v^*\in\arg\min_{v\in V}\{c(v)-\pi^Ta(v)\}\). If \(c(v^*)-\pi^Ta(v^*)<0\), then the inequality \(a(v^*)^Tz\le c(v^*)\), which is valid for every \(z\in D\), separates \(\pi\) from \(D\). If the minimum is nonnegative, then \(\pi\in D\). Thus exact attained pricing returns either a verifiable separating row indexed by \(v^*\) or a membership certificate for the full-master dual feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With an attained exact pricing minimum, a negative-reduced-cost column indexes an inequality separating the tested dual point; a nonnegative minimum certifies membership in the full dual region.
assumptions_latex: The dual feasible set is \(D=\{z\in\mathbb R^m:z^Ta(v)\le c(v)\ \forall v\in V\}\).
The pricing oracle optimizes exactly over the complete set \(V\), and its minimum is attained.
The tested point is \(\pi\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\notin D\iff\min_{v\in V}\{c(v)-\pi^Ta(v)\}<0\).

The oracle returns \(\hat v\in V\) satisfying \(s(\hat v)\ge s_*(\pi)-\delta\) for \(\delta\ge0\).

Inequality index returned by the approximate oracle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation and membership conclusions available from an additively approximate violation-maximization oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{z:a(v)^Tz\le c(v)\ \forall v\in V\}\), define \(s_*(\pi)=\sup_{v\in V}\{a(v)^T\pi-c(v)\}\), and suppose an oracle returns \(\hat v\) satisfying \(s(\hat v)\ge s_*(\pi)-\delta\), where \(s(v)=a(v)^T\pi-c(v)\) and \(\delta\ge0\). Then \[s(\hat v)\le s_*(\pi)\le s(\hat v)+\delta.\] If \(s(\hat v)>0\), the inequality indexed by \(\hat v\) separates \(\pi\) from \(D\). If \(s(\hat v)+\delta\le0\), then \(s_*(\pi)\le0\) and \(\pi\in D\). When \(s(\hat v)\le0<s(\hat v)+\delta\), neither conclusion follows from this output alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive observed violation supplies a separating inequality, while a returned violation plus its additive error no greater than zero certifies membership. The intervening tolerance band is inconclusive.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Separation Outcomes

children.title: Oracle Transformation
children.top_down_role: Translation between pricing-oriented and separation-oriented access.

assumptions_latex: An exact pricing oracle minimizes \(c(v)-\pi^Ta(v)\) over every \(v\in V\).
The full dual region is \(D=\{\pi:\pi^Ta(v)\le c(v)\ \forall v\in V\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pricing call implements an exact membership-or-separation oracle for \(D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct pricing-to-separation transformation for an implicitly constrained master dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(\pi\in\mathbb R^m\). Call the pricing oracle to obtain \[\rho=\min_{v\in V}\{c(v)-\pi^Ta(v)\},\qquad v^*\in\arg\min_{v\in V}\{c(v)-\pi^Ta(v)\}.\] If \(\rho<0\), output the separating inequality \(a(v^*)^Tz\le c(v^*)\). Otherwise output \(\pi\in D\). The first output is valid for every \(z\in D\) and violated by \(\pi\); the second follows because \(c(v)-\pi^Ta(v)\ge0\) for every \(v\in V\). Termination occurs after one exact pricing call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One exact pricing call becomes a separation call: return the violated column inequality when reduced cost is negative, otherwise certify dual membership.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Transformation

assumptions_latex: The transformation requires an attained reduced-cost minimizer to return a separating column.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{v\in V}\bigl(c(v)-a(v)\bigr)=-1<0,\qquad \operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in V}\bigl(c(v)-a(v)\bigr)=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Full dual region indexed by all admissible columns

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an argmin-based one-call transformation when the reduced-cost infimum is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=(0,1)\), \(a(v)=1\), and \(c(v)=v\). The full dual region is \[D=\{\pi\in\mathbb R:\pi\leq v\ \forall v\in(0,1)\}=(-\infty,0].\] At \(\pi=1\), \[\inf_{v\in V}\{c(v)-\pi a(v)\}=\inf_{0<v<1}(v-1)=-1<0,\] but the infimum has no minimizer in \(V\). Thus a pricing interface required to return an exact optimum-attaining column is undefined, and the argmin-based one-call pricing-to-separation transformation cannot be invoked. Producing a violated inequality instead requires an approximate witness or a different oracle contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative reduced-cost infimum need not be attained, so a transformation requiring an optimal pricing column can fail even though violated dual inequalities exist.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Attainment Boundary

assumptions_latex: A tolerance oracle may report exhaustion whenever every returned reduced cost is at least \(-\delta\), where \(\delta>0\).
The complete column set contains a column with reduced cost \(-\varepsilon\), where \(0<\varepsilon<\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tolerance report does not imply exact dual feasibility or exact master optimality.

notation.meaning: Magnitude of an undetected negative reduced cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate pricing yields approximate separation only; exact exhaustion cannot be inferred.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a tolerance oracle is permitted to declare no improving column when the best reduced cost is at least \(-\delta\). If the complete master contains a column \(v\) with \(c(v)-\pi^Ta(v)=-\varepsilon\) for \(0<\varepsilon<\delta\), that declaration is compatible with an actually violated dual inequality \(\pi^Ta(v)\le c(v)\). Hence it certifies at most \(c(v)-\pi^Ta(v)\ge-\delta\) for all columns, not exact membership in \(D\). Pricing-separation correspondence therefore preserves exact certificates only with exact or suitably error-controlled oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tolerance larger than an undetected negative reduced cost can produce a false exact-exhaustion claim; only approximate dual feasibility is then certified.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Correspondence Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tolerance counterexample correctly distinguishes approximate from exact dual feasibility, and failure_boundary fits the container, but no source supports the approximate-oracle boundary.

Multipliers \(\lambda\) have the sign restrictions dictated by the coupling constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality-coupled problem, define \[q(\lambda)=-\lambda^Tb+\sum_i\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\lambda^TA_ix_i\bigr).\] A certificate consists of \(\lambda\) together with verifiable block-optimality certificates establishing each displayed infimum. For every primal-feasible block tuple, the coupling terms cancel, so weak duality gives \(q(\lambda)\le p^*\). Thus the evaluated scalar \(q(\lambda)\) is a global lower bound. For inequality couplings, the same conclusion requires the corresponding multiplier sign restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sign-feasible multiplier plus certified block minima yields a computable Lagrangian value that globally lower-bounds the original minimization optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Bound Certificates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global lower bound assembled from certified, possibly inexact block lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact block minimizers are unnecessary if each block supplies a rigorous lower estimate \(\ell_i\le\inf_{x_i\in X_i}(f_i(x_i)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_ix_i)\). Then \[L(\lambda,\ell)=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_i\ell_i\le q(\lambda)\le p^*.\] If certified errors satisfy \(0\le q_i(\lambda)-\ell_i\le\delta_i\), the resulting bound loses at most \(\sum_i\delta_i\) relative to \(q(\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified lower estimates of the block Lagrangian infima can replace exact block solutions; their sum remains a global lower bound with additive certified error.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier \(\lambda\) obeys all sign restrictions induced by relaxed inequality constraints.
Each \(\ell_i\) has an independently verifiable certificate that it does not exceed the corresponding block infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_i\ell_i\le q(\lambda)\le p^*.

notation.meaning: Certified lower estimate of block i's Lagrangian infimum

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximate Primal Block Values Need Not Be Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating upper estimates of block infima from valid Lagrangian lower-bound evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible approximate block point generally gives an upper estimate of the block infimum, not a lower estimate. For the uncoupled one-block problem \(\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}x^2=0\), the feasible approximate point \(x=1\) has value \(1\). Substituting \(1\) for the infimum would assert the false lower bound \(1\le p^*=0\). Thus an approximate primal block value is admissible in a dual-bound certificate only with global-optimality or rigorous lower-bound evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible approximate block objective cannot be inserted into a Lagrangian lower bound without rigorous lower-bound evidence.
assumptions_latex: A block solver returns only a feasible point and its objective value, without a global-optimality or lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{feasible approximate block values do not necessarily produce a valid global dual lower bound}.

children.title: Oracle-Exhaustion Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence that no missing column, cut, or subordinate response can improve the master.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Exhaustion Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality certificate combining restricted-master strong duality with exhaustive pricing and separation checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\hat x\) and \(\pi\) be primal- and dual-optimal solutions of the restricted minimization master with common attained value \(z_{\mathrm{restricted}}\). Exact pricing exhaustion establishes every full-master dual inequality at \(\pi\). Exact separation exhaustion establishes every missing full-master primal inequality at \(\hat x\). Hence \(\hat x\) is feasible for the full primal, and \(\pi\), extended by zero multipliers for omitted valid rows when necessary, is feasible for the full dual. Weak duality then gives \[z_{\mathrm{full}}\le z_{\mathrm{restricted}}=c^T\hat x=b^T\pi\le z_{\mathrm{full}},\] with the inequality directions interpreted for the stated minimization primal-dual pair. Therefore \(z_{\mathrm{restricted}}=z_{\mathrm{full}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted-master primal-dual equality, full-column pricing exhaustion, and full-row separation exhaustion provide full-primal and full-dual feasible solutions of equal value, certifying complete-master optimality.
assumptions_latex: The restricted minimization master has attained primal and dual optima \(\hat x\) and \(\pi\) with equal value \(z_{\mathrm{restricted}}\).
Every full-master dual inequality induced by an admissible missing column is satisfied by \(\pi\).
Every full-master primal inequality induced by an omitted valid row is satisfied by \(\hat x\).
The full primal and dual obey weak duality, and omitted-row dual multipliers may be extended by zero with their required signs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{restricted}}=z_{\mathrm{full}}\).

For example, \(\mathcal C=\{1,2\}\), \(S=\{1\}\), \(\bar c_1(\pi)=0\), and \(\bar c_2(\pi)=-1\). Therefore unsuccessful heuristic search is not an exhaustion certificate unless accompanied by a valid global oracle bound or exhaustive exact search. The analogous limitation applies to searching only a subset of possible separating rows.

children.title: Primal-Dual Gap Certificates
children.top_down_role: Stopping information obtained by combining feasible solutions and valid bounds.

assumptions_latex: The primal problem has value \(p^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\), and weak duality holds: \(d(y)\le p^*\) for every dual-feasible \(y\).
The reported point \(\hat x\in X\) is primal feasible and \(\hat y\) is dual feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le f(\hat x)-p^*\le G(\hat x,\hat y)\), so \(G(\hat x,\hat y)\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality of \(\hat x\).

notation.meaning: Primal-dual gap at a feasible pair.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality certificate for a minimization problem, independent of the particular block-generation mechanism.

source_refs.locator: 3 Primal-dual splitting methods p. 69
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\), and let \(d(y)\) be a dual objective satisfying \(d(y)\le p^*\) for every dual-feasible \(y\). Given a primal-feasible \(\hat x\) and dual-feasible \(\hat y\), define the primal-dual gap by \[G(\hat x,\hat y)=f(\hat x)-d(\hat y).\] Then weak duality gives \[0\le f(\hat x)-p^*\le G(\hat x,\hat y).\] Consequently, the feasible pair together with evaluations of \(f(\hat x)\) and \(d(\hat y)\) is a verifiable certificate; the stopping test \(G(\hat x,\hat y)\le\varepsilon\) certifies absolute \(\varepsilon\)-optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible primal solution and a valid dual bound certify that their objective gap bounds the primal suboptimality; a gap at most epsilon is an epsilon-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Gap Certificates

source_witnesses.locator: 3 Primal-dual splitting methods p. 69
source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-normalized stopping certificate from a feasible primal value and a finite valid dual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=f(\hat x)\) be the value of a primal-feasible point and let \(L=d(\hat y)\) be a finite valid dual lower bound, so \(L\le p^*\le U\). For a declared scale \(s>0\), define \(G_{\mathrm{rel}}=(U-L)/s\). Then \(G_{\mathrm{rel}}\le\varepsilon\) implies \(0\le U-p^*\le\varepsilon s\). The symmetric choice \(s=\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}\) is always positive; normalization by \(|U|\) or \(|L|\) alone is undefined when the selected denominator is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual gap divided by a declared positive scale gives a relative stopping certificate; one-sided normalization can fail at zero.
assumptions_latex: L=d(\hat y)\le p^*\le f(\hat x)=U
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{U-L}{s}\le\varepsilon\quad\Longrightarrow\quad0\le U-p^*\le\varepsilon s.

notation.meaning: Relative primal-dual gap under the declared scale

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Primal-Dual Gap Certificate

children.title: Finite Polyhedral Generation
children.top_down_role: Finitely representable master refinement in polyhedral settings.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(R\) are finite and \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R\) has no unrepresented lineality.
Each successful exact call returns a previously absent improving member of \(V\cup R\).
A call that returns no improving generator certifies exhaustion over all of \(V\cup R\).
The initial master contains \(V_0\subseteq V\) and \(R_0\subseteq R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{success}}\le |V\setminus V_0|+|R\setminus R_0|,
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicate-free exact generation for a pointed polyhedron represented by finitely many points and rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}V+\operatorname{cone}R\), where finite sets \(V\) and \(R\) contain every admissible point and ray generator used by an exact restricted master. If each successful call returns a member of \(V\cup R\) absent from the master, then at most \(|V\setminus V_0|+|R\setminus R_0|\) successful calls occur. If a call returning no improving generator is an exact exhaustion certificate, termination requires at most one additional terminal call after the last successful addition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite point-and-ray representation gives a finite duplicate-free bound on successful generation and, with an exact exhaustion test, finite termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Point-and-Ray Generation Bound

assumptions_latex: The generated domain is a nonempty polytope \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\}\).
Each exact generation call returns a previously absent improving vertex whenever the current restricted master is not optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(N\) distinct vertices can be generated, and exact termination occurs after finitely many successful generation calls.

notation.meaning: Polyhedral domain generated by finitely many vertices.
Number of vertices in the fixed representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded polyhedral generation with an exact oracle and duplicate exclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\}\) be the domain underlying an exact column, atom, or block-generation method. Suppose every successful oracle call returns a vertex not already present in the restricted master, and returns no improving vertex only when the restricted master is globally optimal. After \(k\) successful calls, the master contains \(k\) distinct members of the finite set \(\{v^1,\ldots,v^N\}\). Hence there are at most \(N\) successful generation calls, and the method reaches an exact stopping certificate after finitely many calls. The sharper bound is \(N-|V_0|\) when the initial master contains \(|V_0|\) distinct vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact generation over a polytope can add only finitely many distinct vertices, so duplicate-free generation terminates after at most the number of initially absent vertices.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Polyhedral Generation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-cardinality argument and complexity-bound role fit the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the generation assumptions or finite-termination conclusion.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
Each \(V_k\) is finite, \(V_k\subseteq V_{k+1}\), and \(V_k\subset K\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical inner-refinement model for a compact nonpolyhedral generated domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact and convex, let \(V_k\subset K\) be finite with \(V_k\subseteq V_{k+1}\), and define \(K_k=\operatorname{conv}V_k\). Then each \(K_k\) is a polytope and \(K_k\subseteq K_{k+1}\subseteq K\). The refinement exhausts \(K\) exactly when \(\overline{\bigcup_kK_k}=K\), equivalently when the union of the generated inner hulls is dense in \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonpolyhedral generation uses nested finite inner polytopes whose closed union must fill the target domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Finite-Master Refinement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Euclidean Disk Requires Infinitely Many Generated Atoms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical compact nonpolyhedral example precluding exact finite point generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\|x\|_2\le1\}\). For every nonempty finite set \(V\subset D\), \(\operatorname{conv}V\) is a polygon and is strictly contained in \(D\). Moreover, for every nonzero \(c\), minimizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(D\) has the unique solution \(-c/\|c\|_2\); varying \(c\) exposes infinitely many distinct boundary points. Hence no finite generated atom set represents \(D\) exactly, although nested finite hulls may converge to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite inner master of the disk is polygonal, while varying linear objectives exposes infinitely many distinct atoms.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is the closed Euclidean unit disk.
Restricted domains are convex hulls of nonempty finite generated point sets contained in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall V\subset D\text{ nonempty and finite},\quad \operatorname{conv}V\ne D.

assumptions_latex: The generated domain is the Euclidean disk \(D=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\|x\|_2\le1\}\).
A restricted master uses the convex hull of finitely many oracle-generated points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite generated set equals \(D\); therefore finite exact generation is unavailable in general, although approximation may converge asymptotically.

notation.meaning: Restricted domain after finitely many generated points.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete compact nonpolyhedral boundary showing why exact generation can require infinitely many atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\|x\|_2\le1\}\). For every finite collection \(v^1,\ldots,v^k\in D\), the restricted domain \(P_k=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^k\}\) is a polygon and therefore satisfies \(P_k\ne D\). Moreover, minimizing \(c^\top x\) over \(D\) for nonzero \(c\) returns \(-c/\|c\|_2\), so varying oracle directions can expose infinitely many distinct boundary points. Thus an atom-generation scheme cannot represent this domain exactly after finitely many generated atoms in general; finite masters may approach the required value or domain only asymptotically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Euclidean disk has infinitely many exposed points, while every finite generated master is polygonal; exact finite representation therefore fails in general.
