children.title: Generation-Regime Transition Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural changes separating finite generation from asymptotic refinement.

assumptions_latex: \(V\subset\mathbb R^n\) is finite.
\(P\) is a nonempty unbounded polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\ne\operatorname{conv}V;\qquad P=\operatorname{conv}V'+\operatorname{cone}R+L\ \text{for suitable finite }V',R\text{ and lineality space }L.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualification required when extending compact finite point generation to unbounded polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite set \(V\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(\operatorname{conv}V\) is bounded. Hence no unbounded polyhedron is representable by finite point generation alone. A nonempty polyhedron instead admits a finite Minkowski-Weyl form \(P=\operatorname{conv}V'+\operatorname{cone}R+L\), where finite point and ray sets encode the pointed part and \(L\) is its lineality subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite points alone never represent an unbounded polyhedron; recession rays and any lineality must also be encoded.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Point-Generation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional transition boundary for compact convex point generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex. There exists a finite set \(V\subseteq K\) such that \(K=\operatorname{conv}V\) if and only if \(K\) is a polytope. Consequently, a compact nonpolyhedral convex set has no exact representation by finitely many generated points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty compact convex set is exactly finitely point-generated if and only if it is a polytope.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
Generation uses the convex hull of finitely many points of \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists V\subseteq K,\ |V|<\infty,\ K=\operatorname{conv}V\iff K\text{ is a polytope}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Point Generation–Polytope Equivalence

assumptions_latex: The domain \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
Exact generation means finding a finite set \(V\subset K\) with \(K=\operatorname{conv}V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact finite generation is possible if and only if \(K\) is a polytope; otherwise unrestricted exact representation requires infinitely many generated points.

notation.meaning: Compact convex domain to be generated.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric boundary between exact finite and generally asymptotic point generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty compact convex set \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\), define exact finite generation as the existence of a finite set \(V\subset K\) such that \(K=\operatorname{conv}V\). The generation regime satisfies \[K\text{ is exactly finitely generated}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad K\text{ is a polytope}.\] Thus polyhedrality is the transition boundary: on the polyhedral side, a finite vertex set can support exact termination under an exhaustive exact oracle; on the nonpolyhedral side, no finite point set represents \(K\), so unrestricted exact representation generally requires infinitely many generated points, even when finite approximations converge in objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact convex domain admits exact finite point generation exactly when it is a polytope; nonpolyhedral domains generally require asymptotic generation.
knowledge_statements.title: Generation-Regime Transition Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-generation equivalence is precise for compact convex subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and condition fits the transition-boundary leaf. It lacks an inspectable convex-geometry citation.

children.title: Subproblem Solution Cost

assumptions_latex: Every local cost uses the same declared computational model.
Each returned local solution has a valid, comparably defined certificate at its stated tolerance.
Blocks are independent and processors are unit-rate and contention-free for the ideal parallel formula.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparable cost accounting for exact, inexact, cold-started, and warm-started subordinate solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_{i,t}(\varepsilon_{i,t};s_{i,t})\) be the work required by a declared local solver, initialized from state \(s_{i,t}\), to return a point with a declared certified local residual or objective gap at most \(\varepsilon_{i,t}\). For independent block solves, sequential work is \(\sum_iC_{i,t}(\varepsilon_{i,t};s_{i,t})\), and ideal contention-free elapsed work with one unit-rate processor per block is \(\max_iC_{i,t}(\varepsilon_{i,t};s_{i,t})\). Exact and cold-start cases are represented by requiring zero tolerance when attainable and by using the declared cold state, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subproblem costs are comparable only after fixing the local certificate, tolerance, solver, initialization state, and computational model.

assumptions_latex: The accelerator can execute at most one block solve at a time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E=2>1=\max_iC_i.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose two mathematically independent block solves each require one unit of exclusive accelerator time, so each isolated cost is \(C_1=C_2=1\). If both require the same accelerator, they execute serially and elapsed time is \(2>\max\{C_1,C_2\}=1\), even with zero communication cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent mathematical blocks need not run in maximum block time when they contend for one exclusive resource.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Resource Parallel-Cost Failure

assumptions_latex: Iteration \(t\) solves \(B\) independent block subproblems.
An exact solve of block \(i\) at iteration \(t\) costs \(C_{i,t}\) operations in the stated computational model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sequential subproblem work is \(S_t=\sum_{i=1}^B C_{i,t}\), while ideal fully parallel elapsed work is bounded by \(\max_i C_{i,t}\) plus coordination overhead.

notation.meaning: Cost of solving block i at iteration t.
Total sequential subproblem cost at iteration t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric work bound for independent exact block solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), suppose decomposition requires exact solutions of \(B\) independent block subproblems, with block \(i\) costing \(C_{i,t}\) operations under a fixed computational model. The sequential subproblem work is \[S_t=\sum_{i=1}^{B}C_{i,t},\] and cumulative work through iteration \(T\) is \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}S_t\). With one processor per block and no resource contention, the ideal parallel elapsed cost is \(\max_{1\le i\le B}C_{i,t}\) plus communication and synchronization overhead. These expressions count subproblem solution only and exclude restricted-master reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Per iteration, sequential block-solution cost is the sum of block costs; ideal parallel elapsed cost is their maximum plus coordination overhead.
knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Solution Cost

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sequential sum and ideal parallel maximum are coherent under the stated independence and no-contention model, and complexity_bound fits the leaf. No source supports this decomposition cost model.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\cup U=\{1,\ldots,B\}\) and \(Q\cap U=\varnothing\).
Each \(L_i\) is a valid lower bound on the minimum reduced cost over the entire skipped block.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound for block i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage condition for exhaustion without exactly repricing every block in the current round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_i=\inf_{x\in X_i}r_i(x)\), and partition the blocks into queried blocks \(Q\) and unqueried blocks \(U\). If exact pricing establishes \(\rho_i\ge0\) for every \(i\in Q\), and valid lower bounds \(L_i\le\rho_i\) satisfy \(L_i\ge0\) for every \(i\in U\), then \(\rho_i\ge0\) for every block. Without complete coverage by exact queries or valid bounds, selective pricing does not certify exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selective pricing certifies exhaustion only when every skipped block has a valid nonnegative lower bound on its minimum reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Selective Block-Pricing Exhaustion Certificate

assumptions_latex: \(Q_t\ne\varnothing\), and queried calls use declared certified tolerances.
Queried blocks are independent, use one unit-rate processor each, and incur no resource contention in the ideal parallel model.

notation.meaning: certified tolerance requested from block i in round t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-round accounting for selective block pricing with certified approximate calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If round \(t\) queries \(Q_t\subseteq\{1,\ldots,B\}\), and block \(i\in Q_t\) is solved to certified tolerance \(\delta_{i,t}\) at cost \(P_{i,t}(\delta_{i,t})\), sequential pricing work is \(\sum_{i\in Q_t}P_{i,t}(\delta_{i,t})\). With independent calls and one contention-free unit-rate processor per queried block, ideal elapsed cost is \(\max_{i\in Q_t}P_{i,t}(\delta_{i,t})\). Neither expression supplies a coverage certificate for blocks outside \(Q_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selective approximate pricing charges only queried blocks, but lower work does not itself certify global coverage.
knowledge_statements.title: Selective and Approximate Pricing Cost

assumptions_latex: Only block 1 is queried, and no valid lower bound is available for block 2.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_1=0\ge0\quad\text{but}\quad\min_i\rho_i=-1<0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of exhaustion inference under incomplete block coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two singleton pricing blocks with reduced costs \(r_1=0\) and \(r_2=-1\). A schedule querying only block 1 observes a nonnegative minimum, while the global minimum is \(\min\{0,-1\}=-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative result in a queried block does not exclude a negative-reduced-cost object in a skipped block.
knowledge_statements.title: Unqueried Improving Block
Pricing-Oracle Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric cost and exhaustion test for exhaustive blockwise exact pricing in a minimization column-generation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), let the restricted-master dual solution induce a reduced-cost function \(r_{i,t}:X_i\to\mathbb R\) for every block \(i\in\{1,\ldots,B\}\), where the sets \(X_i\) contain all eligible objects. Suppose exact pricing computes \(\rho_{i,t}=\min_{x\in X_i}r_{i,t}(x)\) at cost \(P_{i,t}\), using the convention that negative reduced cost is improving. Sequential pricing work is \[P_t=\sum_{i=1}^{B}P_{i,t}.\] With one contention-free processor per block, ideal parallel elapsed cost is \(\max_{1\le i\le B}P_{i,t}\) plus coordination overhead. Exhaustive exact pricing certifies that no improving object exists precisely when \(\rho_{i,t}\ge0\) for every block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive exact block pricing costs the sum of block-oracle costs sequentially and certifies that no improving object exists when every minimum reduced cost is nonnegative under the stated convention.
assumptions_latex: There are \(B\ge1\) blocks, and \(X_i\) contains every object eligible for generation from block \(i\).
The current restricted-master dual solution defines \(r_{i,t}:X_i\to\mathbb R\), with negative reduced cost designated as improving.
Each pricing problem is solved exactly at cost \(P_{i,t}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sequential pricing work is \(P_t=\sum_{i=1}^{B}P_{i,t}\), and \(\rho_{i,t}\ge0\) for all \(i\in\{1,\ldots,B\}\) certifies exhaustion of improving objects.

notation.meaning: Set of all eligible objects in block i.
Reduced cost of object x in block i at iteration t.
Exact-pricing cost for block i at iteration t.
Minimum reduced cost in block i at iteration t.

children.title: Oracle Cost-Dominance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where oracle work dominates total decomposition runtime.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Cost-Dominance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational dominance predicate under an additive nonnegative work model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(O_t\), \(M_t\), and \(H_t\) be nonnegative oracle, restricted-master, and residual work at iteration \(t\), and let \(W_t=O_t+M_t+H_t\). Under the declared convention that one component dominates when its cost is at least the combined cost of all remaining components, iteration \(t\) is oracle-dominant exactly when \[O_t\ge M_t+H_t.\] If \(W_t>0\), this is equivalent to \(O_t/W_t\ge1/2\). Over iterations \(t\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\), cumulative oracle dominance is defined by \[\sum_{t=1}^{T}O_t\ge\sum_{t=1}^{T}(M_t+H_t).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the declared additive-work convention, oracle cost dominates an iteration when it is at least the combined master and residual cost; cumulative dominance uses the analogous summed condition.
assumptions_latex: For each iteration \(t\), the costs \(O_t\), \(M_t\), and \(H_t\) are nonnegative.
Total work is modeled additively as \(W_t=O_t+M_t+H_t\).
Dominance means costing at least as much as all remaining components combined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Oracle dominance is equivalent to \(O_t\ge M_t+H_t\), or to \(O_t/W_t\ge1/2\) when \(W_t>0\).

notation.meaning: Total modeled work at iteration t.

children.title: Oracle Cost Amortization
children.top_down_role: Reuse or distribution of oracle effort across master iterations.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is symmetric positive definite and identical in every call.
The cached factorization and stated operation costs use one fixed computational model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_T^{\mathrm{reuse}}=F_H+TS_H,\qquad C_T^{\mathrm{fresh}}=T(F_H+S_H).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition-oracle reuse for unconstrained strongly convex quadratic calls with a fixed Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(t=1,\ldots,T\), let \(x_t=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\{\tfrac12x^\top Hx+d_t^\top x\}\), where \(H\succ0\) is fixed while \(d_t\) may depend on the current master multiplier. Factoring \(H=LL^\top\) once at cost \(F_H\) and solving with the factors at cost \(S_H\) per call gives total work \(F_H+TS_H\), compared with \(T(F_H+S_H)\) if the same factorization is rebuilt for every call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed quadratic-oracle Hessian permits one factorization to be reused across changing multiplier-dependent linear terms.
knowledge_statements.title: Invariant-System Factorization Amortization

assumptions_latex: The implementation reuses a factorization of \(H_1\) without an update representing \(H_2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for cached linear-algebra state after oracle data change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A factorization cached for \(H\) remains an exact direct-solve mechanism only while the coefficient matrix is \(H\), unless an exact update is applied. For scalar quadratic calls with \(H_1=1\), \(H_2=2\), and \(d=-2\), reuse of \(H_1^{-1}\) on the second call returns \(x=2\), although the second call's exact minimizer is \(x=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reusing a factorization after the oracle system matrix changes can return the wrong oracle solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Cached-Factorization Validity Boundary

assumptions_latex: A reusable oracle computation costs \(F\), and each of \(T\) subsequent queries costs \(q_t\).
Without reuse, query \(t\) would cost \(c_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reuse is amortizing exactly when \(F+\sum_tq_t<\sum_tc_t\), with average reused cost \((F+\sum_tq_t)/T\).

notation.meaning: Marginal cost of reused query t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic amortized accounting for reusable oracle setup, preprocessing, or cached state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a sequence of \(T\) oracle calls shares preprocessing, factorization, or cached state built once at cost \(F\). If reused query \(t\) costs \(q_t\), total oracle work is \[C_T^{\mathrm{reuse}}=F+\sum_{t=1}^{T}q_t,\qquad \bar C_T^{\mathrm{reuse}}=\frac{F+\sum_{t=1}^{T}q_t}{T}.\] If independently solving query \(t\) costs \(c_t\), reuse yields a strict amortized saving exactly when \(F+\sum_tq_t<\sum_tc_t\). For constant costs \(q_t=q<c=c_t\), this occurs when \(T>F/(c-q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reusable oracle setup is worthwhile when its one-time cost plus marginal query costs is below the cost of solving all queries independently.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Cost Amortization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The amortized accounting and constant-cost break-even inequality are correct, and complexity_bound fits the leaf. No source or instantiated reuse mechanism supports applying this generic model to decomposition oracles.

children.title: Restricted-Master Growth-Cost Coupling
children.top_down_role: Complexity caused by repeated solution of expanding restricted masters.

children.title: Restricted-Master Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion of the restricted master through generated columns or cuts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite admissible universe with novelty-producing generation; repeated regeneration is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(|\mathcal U|=N\), the initial master contains \(n_0\) distinct objects from \(\mathcal U\), and every successful generation event adds at least one never-previously-generated object, then at most \(N-n_0\) successful events occur and at most \(N\) distinct objects are ever generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite object universe bounds distinct master growth and the number of novelty-producing generation events.
assumptions_latex: \(|\mathcal U|=N<\infty\).
The initial master contains \(n_0\) distinct members of \(\mathcal U\).
Each successful event adds a never-previously-generated member of \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_{\mathrm{success}}\le N-n_0.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Universe Saturation Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact size dynamics when generated objects may be removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If iteration \(t\) adds \(b_t\) objects and then deletes \(d_t\) objects, where \(0\le d_t\le n_{t-1}+b_t\), then \[n_t=n_{t-1}+b_t-d_t=n_0+\sum_{s=1}^t(b_s-d_s).\] Consequently \(0\le n_t\le n_0+\sum_{s=1}^t b_s\). Bounded additions do not make \((n_t)\) monotone when deletion is permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With deletion, master size equals additions minus deletions and need not grow monotonically.
assumptions_latex: The master has size \(n_{t-1}\) before iteration \(t\).
Iteration \(t\) adds \(b_t\ge0\) and then deletes \(0\le d_t\le n_{t-1}+b_t\) objects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: n_t=n_0+\sum_{s=1}^t(b_s-d_s),\qquad 0\le n_t\le n_0+\sum_{s=1}^t b_s.
knowledge_statements.title: Deletion-Aware Master-Size Recurrence

assumptions_latex: The initial restricted master contains \(n_0\) generated objects.
Iteration \(t\) retains all existing objects and adds \(b_t\ge0\) new ones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The master size is \(n_t=n_0+\sum_{s=1}^tb_s\), hence \(n_t\le n_0+bt\) whenever \(b_s\le b\).

notation.meaning: Number of objects added at iteration t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone master growth without column, cut, or block deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n_0\) be the initial number of generated objects in a restricted master, and let iteration \(t\) add \(b_t\ge0\) distinct objects while deleting none. Then the exact growth identity is \[n_t=n_0+\sum_{s=1}^{t}b_s.\] If at most \(b\) objects are added per iteration, then \(n_t\le n_0+bt\); if exactly one object is added at every successful generation iteration, then \(n_t=n_0+t\). The bound counts retained columns, cuts, atoms, or blocks and does not include auxiliary rows or variables introduced by a particular master formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without deletion, restricted-master size equals its initial size plus all generated objects and grows at most linearly when per-iteration additions are bounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The growth identity and linear bound are correct under retention and bounded additions, and complexity_bound fits the leaf. The record has no inspectable source.

children.title: Master Reoptimization Cost
children.top_down_role: Computational workload of repeatedly solving the evolving master.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional cumulative bound for state-dependent reoptimization costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_t=R(n_t,S_{t-1},\Delta_t,\varepsilon_t)\) be the work of reoptimization \(t\). If \(R_t\le M(n_t)\) for a nondecreasing envelope \(M\) and \(n_t\le n_T\), then \[C_T^{\mathrm{master}}=\sum_{t=1}^T R_t\le\sum_{t=1}^T M(n_t)\le T M(n_T).\] If also \(n_t\le n_0+bt\) and \(M(n)\le an^p\), then \(C_T^{\mathrm{master}}\le a\sum_{t=1}^T(n_0+bt)^p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State-dependent reoptimization work admits the familiar final-size bound only when a declared nondecreasing size envelope bounds every incremental solve.
assumptions_latex: There are \(T\) reoptimizations.
\(R_t\le M(n_t)\) for a declared nondecreasing envelope \(M\).
The retained sizes satisfy \(n_t\le n_T\).
The polynomial-envelope conclusion additionally assumes \(n_t\le n_0+bt\) and \(M(n)\le an^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_T^{\mathrm{master}}\le T M(n_T),
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Bound for Incremental Reoptimization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Size Alone Does Not Bound Reoptimization Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on conclusions obtainable from a row or column count alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A count \(n\) of master rows, columns, or retained objects does not by itself bound reoptimization work. Equal-dimensional instances can have arbitrarily large coefficient encoding length, and work also depends on the computational model, solver, requested accuracy, numerical conditioning, and retained state. Consequently, no solver-independent complexity bound follows from \(n\) alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Master dimension alone gives no universal complexity bound because encoding, solver, accuracy, conditioning, and retained state also determine work.
assumptions_latex: \(n\) records only a declared combinatorial dimension.
Coefficient encoding length, computational model, solver, and accuracy are unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No universal upper bound }C\le f(n)\text{ follows from master dimension alone.}
knowledge_statements.title: Size Alone Does Not Bound Reoptimization Complexity
Master Reoptimization Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric cumulative bound separating restricted-master size from solver-dependent optimization cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M(n)\) denote the work required by a specified solver and accuracy criterion to optimize a restricted master of size \(n\). If the successive master sizes are \(n_1,\ldots,n_T\), cumulative reoptimization work is \[C_T^{\mathrm{master}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}M(n_t).\] If \(n_t\) is nondecreasing and \(M\) is nondecreasing, then \[C_T^{\mathrm{master}}\le T M(n_T).\] If additionally \(n_t\le n_0+bt\) and \(M(n)\le an^p\) for constants \(a,b,p\ge0\), then \[C_T^{\mathrm{master}}\le a\sum_{t=1}^{T}(n_0+bt)^p.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative restricted-master work is the sum of solver costs at successive master sizes and is at most the number of reoptimizations times the final-size cost under monotone growth and cost.
assumptions_latex: There are \(T\ge1\) reoptimizations with master sizes \(n_1,\ldots,n_T\).
The cost function \(M(n)\) uses a fixed solver, accuracy criterion, and computational model.
Both \(n_t\) and \(M(n)\) are nondecreasing for the stated final-size bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cumulative work is \(C_T^{\mathrm{master}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}M(n_t)\le T M(n_T)\).

notation.meaning: Cost of optimizing a restricted master of size n.

children.title: Warm-Start Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Reoptimization cost variation under changes to the retained master state.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility of transferred LP states under pure column addition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the old master \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and the augmented master \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+d^{\mathsf T}w:Ax+Dw=b,\ x,w\ge0\}\), every old primal-feasible \(x\) extends to the feasible point \((x,0)\). An old dual-feasible \(y\) remains feasible exactly when \(D^{\mathsf T}y\le d\). Thus column addition preserves the old primal point but can invalidate the old dual state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Appending columns preserves an old primal solution by zero extension, while the old dual remains feasible only if all new reduced costs are nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: The new master only appends nonnegative variables \(w\).
The transferred vectors are feasible for the old primal and dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x,0)\text{ is primal feasible, and }y\text{ is dual feasible iff }D^{\mathsf T}y\le d.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Preserved, Dual-Sensitive Column Warm Start
Warm-Start Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-ratio characterization comparing warm and cold reoptimization; no universal warm-start improvement is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For restricted master \(t\), let \(M(n_t)>0\) be its cold-start reoptimization cost under a fixed solver and stopping criterion, and let \(W_t\ge0\) be its cost when initialized with the preceding solver state \(z_{t-1}\). Define \[R_t=\frac{W_t}{M(n_t)}.\] The warm start saves work when \(R_t<1\), is cost-neutral when \(R_t=1\), and is harmful when \(R_t>1\). Thus the ratio measures observed sensitivity to the transferred state but supplies no unconditional complexity improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The warm-start sensitivity ratio compares warm and cold reoptimization costs; values below one indicate savings, while values above one indicate harmful initialization.
assumptions_latex: The cold-start cost satisfies \(M(n_t)>0\) for restricted master \(t\).
The warm-start cost \(W_t\ge0\) is measured for the same master, solver, stopping criterion, and computational model.
The warm start uses a preceding solver state \(z_{t-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(R_t=W_t/M(n_t)\), warm starting saves work if \(R_t<1\), is neutral if \(R_t=1\), and is harmful if \(R_t>1\).

notation.meaning: Cold-start reoptimization cost at master size n_t.
Transferred solver state from the preceding master.
Ratio of warm-start cost to cold-start cost.

children.title: Growth–Cost Feedback
children.top_down_role: Runtime interaction between master expansion and repeated solution effort.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterfactual downstream cost attributable to retaining one generated object.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an object increases retained size by one at reoptimizations \(t=s,\ldots,\ell\), then, holding the remaining trajectory fixed, its marginal master-cost burden is \[\Delta C_{s:\ell}=\sum_{t=s}^{\ell}[M(n_t+1)-M(n_t)].\] If \(M\) is nondecreasing, this burden is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An object's marginal retention cost is the sum of its size-induced cost increments over every reoptimization during its lifetime.
assumptions_latex: The counterfactual trajectory without the selected object has sizes \(n_t\).
All trajectory components other than the selected object's presence are held fixed.
\(M\) is nondecreasing for the nonnegativity conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Delta C_{s:\ell}=\sum_{t=s}^{\ell}[M(n_t+1)-M(n_t)]\ge0.

notation.meaning: Last reoptimization retaining the selected object.
Counterfactual size without the selected object.

knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Retention Burden

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Growth–cost feedback with additions, deletions, aggregation, compression, or purging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If iteration \(t\) adds \(a_t\ge0\) counted objects and removes or consolidates the equivalent of \(d_t\ge0\) counted objects, then \[n_t=n_{t-1}+a_t-d_t=n_0+\sum_{s=1}^t(a_s-d_s),\qquad C_T=\sum_{t=1}^T[O_t+M(n_t)].\] The retain-all formula is the special case \(d_t=0\). Thus gross generation and retained-master growth differ whenever objects are deleted, purged, replaced, aggregated, or compressed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Current master size equals initial size plus additions minus effective removals; retain-all cumulative growth is only the zero-removal case.
assumptions_latex: \(n_t\) counts the retained representation after active-set management.
Reoptimization at retained size \(n\) costs \(M(n)\), and iteration \(t\) has oracle cost \(O_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: n_t=n_0+\sum_{s=1}^t(a_s-d_s),\qquad C_T=\sum_{t=1}^T[O_t+M(n_t)].

notation.meaning: Effective objects removed at iteration t.
Retained master size after iteration t.
Reoptimization cost at retained size n.

knowledge_statements.title: Managed Active-Set Growth–Cost Accounting

assumptions_latex: Master size obeys \(n_t=n_0+\sum_{s=1}^t b_s\).
Reoptimization at size \(n\) costs \(M(n)\), and iteration \(t\) incurs oracle cost \(O_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Total work through \(T\) is \(\sum_{t=1}^T[O_t+M(n_0+\sum_{s=1}^t b_s)]\), explicitly coupling generation to all later master costs.

notation.meaning: Master cost as a function of size.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive work representation exposing the downstream cost of present generation decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose iteration \(t\) adds \(b_t\ge0\) retained objects, so \(n_t=n_0+\sum_{s=1}^{t}b_s\). If oracle work is \(O_t\) and reoptimizing a master of size \(n\) costs \(M(n)\), then cumulative work through \(T\) is represented by \[C_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left[O_t+M\!\left(n_0+\sum_{s=1}^{t}b_s\right)\right].\] Hence an object generated at iteration \(s\) affects not only \(O_s\) but every later master term \(M(n_t)\) for \(t\ge s\). This is the growth-cost feedback coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generated objects enlarge every later restricted master, so current generation decisions create downstream reoptimization costs as well as immediate oracle costs.
knowledge_statements.title: Growth–Cost Feedback

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive representation correctly exposes how retained additions enter later master-size arguments, and representation fits the feedback leaf. An algorithm-specific source is needed to substantiate the modeled feedback beyond bookkeeping.

children.title: Distributed Coordination Cost Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coordination overhead in parallel or distributed decomposition.

children.title: Decomposition Communication Cost
children.top_down_role: Data-transfer overhead between coordinating and subordinate processes.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Communication Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate message and payload complexity for synchronous block coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the communication graph be \(G=(V,E)\), and suppose round \(k\) transmits one \(d_k\)-scalar vector in each direction along every edge. After \(K\) rounds, the number of directed messages is \(2K|E|\), the scalar payload is \(2|E|\sum_{k=1}^{K}d_k\), and, with \(b\) bytes per scalar, the payload volume is \(2b|E|\sum_{k=1}^{K}d_k\). Thus constant-dimensional coordination has communication complexity \(O(K|E|d)\); computation distributed across blocks does not remove this coordination cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: K synchronous neighbor-exchange rounds communicate 2K|E| messages and 2|E| times the summed vector dimensions in scalar payload.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is fixed during the run.
Each edge carries one vector in both directions per round.
Protocol overhead and retransmission are excluded.

notation.meaning: vector dimension communicated in round k

children.title: Decomposition Synchronization Cost
children.top_down_role: Waiting and coordination overhead across parallel workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Synchronization Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-delay cost for synchronous decomposition iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iteration \(k\), let worker \(i\) require local time \(t_{ik}\), and let a global barrier cost \(s_k\). A synchronous decomposition method cannot complete that iteration before its slowest required worker arrives; consequently its coordination time through \(K\) iterations is \[T_{\mathrm{sync}}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\left(\max_{1\le i\le p}t_{ik}+s_k\right).\] Relative to the perfectly balanced baseline \(\sum_k p^{-1}\sum_i t_{ik}\), the synchronization penalty is the sum of the straggler imbalance and barrier costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronous runtime sums the slowest worker time and barrier overhead at every iteration, exposing both load imbalance and explicit synchronization penalties.
assumptions_latex: Every iteration requires results from all \(p\) workers.
Worker computations within an iteration run concurrently.
Communication not included in \(s_k\) is accounted for separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{sync}}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}(\max_i t_{ik}+s_k)\).

notation.meaning: worker i computation time in iteration k

children.title: Latency-Dominated Regimes
children.top_down_role: Distributed settings where communication delay dominates local optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Latency-Dominated Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion identifying coordination latency as the dominant wall-clock expense.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose one coordination round performs local computation of duration \(c\), sends \(m\) messages of payload \(q\) bytes, and has critical-path communication time \(n_{\ell}\ell+q_{\mathrm{cp}}/B\), where \(\ell\) is per-message startup latency and \(B\) is bandwidth. For a prescribed dominance factor \(\gamma\ge 1\), the round is latency-dominated when \[n_{\ell}\ell\ge \gamma\left(c+\frac{q_{\mathrm{cp}}}{B}\right).\] In this regime, batching messages or reducing coordination rounds can improve time more than reducing payload or local arithmetic by the same relative amount.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regime is latency-dominated when critical-path message startup time exceeds computation plus bandwidth time by a chosen factor.
assumptions_latex: The affine communication model \(\ell+q/B\) applies.
Critical-path message startups do not overlap completely.
\(\gamma\ge1\) is fixed before classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(n_{\ell}\ell\ge\gamma(c+q_{\mathrm{cp}}/B)\) characterizes latency dominance.

source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods
source_refs.locator: 1.3.5 Concurrency and Communication Tradeoffs p. 68

children.title: Asynchrony Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance between reduced waiting and increased information staleness.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchrony Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock criterion balancing synchronization removal against extra asynchronous updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an accuracy criterion \(\varepsilon\). Suppose a synchronous run reaches it after \(K_s(\varepsilon)\ge 1\) iterations in elapsed time \(T_s\), and an asynchronous run with maximum information delay \(\tau\) reaches it after \(K_a(\varepsilon,\tau)\ge 1\) completed updates in elapsed time \(T_a\). Define the effective elapsed-time increments \(t_s=T_s/K_s(\varepsilon)\) and \(t_a=T_a/K_a(\varepsilon,\tau)\). The asynchronous run improves time to accuracy exactly when \[K_a(\varepsilon,\tau)t_a<K_s(\varepsilon)t_s.\] Equivalently, \[\frac{K_a(\varepsilon,\tau)}{K_s(\varepsilon)}<\frac{t_s}{t_a}.\] Thus the observed reduction in effective time per completed update must exceed the update-count inflation associated with delayed information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchrony improves wall-clock time when its effective time saved per completed update outweighs the additional updates required under delayed information.
assumptions_latex: Both runs use the same accuracy criterion \(\varepsilon\).

children.title: Oracle Accuracy-Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: The balance between approximate subordinate work and reliable global certification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy-cost interface for an inexact subordinate pricing oracle that supplies certified bounds on the infimum reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a restricted-master dual point, let \(r_*:=\inf_{a\in\mathcal A}r(a)\). Suppose a pricing call requested at tolerance \(\delta\ge0\), with modeled cost \(C(\delta)\), returns certified bounds \(L_\delta\le r_*\le U_\delta\) satisfying \(U_\delta-L_\delta\le\delta\). Then \(U_\delta<0\) certifies the existence of a negative-reduced-cost object, whereas \(L_\delta\ge-\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-feasibility of the reduced-cost inequalities. If \(U_\delta\ge0\) and \(L_\delta< -\varepsilon\), the interval certifies neither conclusion; a tighter call may be required, but decisiveness additionally requires the certified bounds to tighten around \(r_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified upper and lower bounds from inexact pricing prove improvement or epsilon reduced-cost feasibility; an interval straddling both thresholds is inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: \(L_\delta\le r_*\le U_\delta\) are valid certified bounds.
\(U_\delta-L_\delta\le\delta\) for the requested tolerance \(\delta\ge0\).
\(C(\delta)\) measures work under a fixed pricing implementation and computational model.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\) is the declared reduced-cost feasibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_\delta<0\Rightarrow r_*<0,\qquad L_\delta\ge-\varepsilon\Rightarrow r_*\ge-\varepsilon.

notation.meaning: infimum reduced cost over all admissible generated objects
certified interval containing the infimum reduced cost
modeled work of the pricing call

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Inexact Pricing Interval

assumptions_latex: Every call returns a certified interval of width at most its requested tolerance.
\(C(\delta)\) is a valid worst-case cost bound under one fixed oracle implementation and computational model.
\(\delta_0>0\), \(\bar\delta>0\), and \(0<\beta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W(\bar\delta)\le\sum_{j=0}^{J}C(\delta_0\beta^j),\qquad J=\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{\log(\delta_0/\bar\delta)}{\log(1/\beta)}\right\rceil\right\}.

notation.meaning: first refinement index guaranteed to reach the target width

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost of tightening a certified subordinate oracle geometrically until a target interval width is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use tolerances \(\delta_j=\delta_0\beta^j\) with \(0<\beta<1\). The first index guaranteed to satisfy \(\delta_j\le\bar\delta\) is \(J=\max\{0,\lceil\log(\delta_0/\bar\delta)/\log(1/\beta)\rceil\}\), and total refinement work through that call is at most \(\sum_{j=0}^{J}C(\delta_0\beta^j)\). Reaching the target width does not guarantee a decisive sign test when the true reduced cost lies at or sufficiently near a certification threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric tolerance tightening has an explicit cumulative call-cost bound, but arbitrarily narrow intervals can remain inconclusive at a decision threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Accuracy-Refinement Cost

assumptions_latex: No certified one-sided or two-sided relation between \(\widetilde r\) and \(r_*\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde r\ge0\ \not\Rightarrow\ r_*\ge0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between an approximate oracle value and a reliable exhaustion certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the true minimum reduced cost be \(r_*=-1\). An approximate oracle may return \(\widetilde r=0\) without contradicting any declared guarantee when no error bound is supplied, so this output cannot establish \(r_*\ge0\). More generally, an approximate value alone certifies neither improvement nor exhaustion unless its error model yields an appropriate valid one-sided bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cheap approximate oracle output is not a stopping certificate without a valid error bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncertified Approximation Cannot Prove Exhaustion

assumptions_latex: \(C_k(\delta)=a_k\delta^{-p}\).
A valid coordinating theorem bounds accumulated oracle error by \(\sum_k w_k\delta_k\le\eta\).

notation.meaning: cost coefficient of oracle call k
certified sensitivity weight of call k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form allocation of a certified additive error budget under common power-law subordinate costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_k>0\), \(w_k>0\), \(p>0\), and \(\eta>0\). For \(C_k(\delta_k)=a_k\delta_k^{-p}\), the problem \[\min_{\delta_k>0}\sum_{k=1}^K a_k\delta_k^{-p}\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{k=1}^K w_k\delta_k\le\eta\] has the unique solution \[\delta_k^*=\frac{\eta\,(a_k/w_k)^{1/(p+1)}}{\sum_{j=1}^K a_j^{1/(p+1)}w_j^{p/(p+1)}}.\] The error budget is active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For common power-law oracle costs, the optimal conditional error allocation balances marginal work against each call's certified sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Power-Law Oracle-Budget Allocation
Oracle Accuracy-Cost Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy scheduling for inexact subordinate oracles used by a coordinating method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At call \(k\), let an oracle return a value within additive error \(\delta_k\ge0\) at cost \(C_k(\delta_k)\), with \(C_k\) nonincreasing in \(\delta_k\). If the coordinating certificate weights oracle errors by \(w_k\ge0\), then an oracle budget \(\eta\) is respected whenever \[\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_k\delta_k\le\eta.\] The least modeled subordinate work compatible with that certificate is therefore \[\inf_{\delta_k\ge0}\left\{\sum_{k=1}^{K}C_k(\delta_k):\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_k\delta_k\le\eta\right\}.\] Reliable certification requires charging every inexact call to this error budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose per-call oracle tolerances by minimizing total subordinate cost subject to the weighted error allowance in the global certificate.
assumptions_latex: Oracle errors enter the certificate additively with known weights.
Each \(C_k(\delta)\) is a valid worst-case call cost.
The global error allowance is \(\eta\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\sum_k C_k(\delta_k)\) subject to \(\sum_k w_k\delta_k\le\eta\) expresses the accuracy-cost allocation.

notation.meaning: additive error of oracle call k
cost as a function of requested accuracy

children.title: Decomposition Route Taxonomy

children.title: Constraint-Relaxation Route
children.top_down_role: Lagrangian coordination for models whose coupling rows obstruct otherwise tractable blocks.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative-Interior Qualification for Exact Constraint Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit finite-dimensional qualification for the equality-coupled convex route.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_i(f_i+\delta_{X_i})(x_i)\), let \(A(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_iA_ix_i\), and suppose \(F\) is proper, closed, and convex with finite primal value at \(b\). If \[b\in\operatorname{ri}\bigl(A(\operatorname{dom}F)\bigr),\] then the Lagrangian dual has no value gap and an optimal multiplier exists: \[p^*=\max_{\lambda}\left[-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_i\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_ix_i\bigr)\right].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Membership of the coupling right-hand side in the relative interior of the attainable coupling image gives zero duality gap and dual attainment.
assumptions_latex: \(F=\sum_i(f_i+\delta_{X_i})\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The primal value at \(b\) is finite.
\(b\in\operatorname{ri}(A(\operatorname{dom}F))\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*=\max_{\lambda}g(\lambda).

notation.meaning: Indicator function of block set X_i.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Interior Qualification for Exact Constraint Relaxation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite nonconvex example showing that separable relaxation need not recover the primal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min\{f(x):x\in\{0,1,2\},\ x=1\},\qquad f(0)=f(2)=0,\quad f(1)=1.\] The primal value is \(p^*=1\). Its Lagrangian dual function is \[g(\lambda)=\min\{-\lambda,1,\lambda\},\] so \(d^*=\sup_\lambda g(\lambda)=0<p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A three-point nonconvex problem has primal value one and Lagrangian-dual value zero.
assumptions_latex: The domain is \(\{0,1,2\}\).
The coupling equality is \(x=1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Constraint-Relaxation Gap
Constraint-Relaxation Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex Lagrangian decomposition obtained by dualizing coupling equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[p^*=\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^{m}A_ix_i=b\right\}.\] Dualizing only the coupling equality gives the separable dual function \[g(\lambda)=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_ix_i\bigr).\] Weak duality gives \(g(\lambda)\le p^*\). If the block problems are proper convex programs and a standard relative-interior constraint qualification holds, then \(p^*=\sup_{\lambda}g(\lambda)\), so multiplier coordination recovers the primal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing coupling rows separates the blocks; under convexity and a relative-interior qualification, maximizing the resulting dual recovers the primal value.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_i\) is nonempty and convex, and each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The primal value is finite.
A feasible point satisfies the applicable relative-interior qualification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^r}g(\lambda)\), with blockwise evaluation of \(g\).

notation.meaning: block contribution to the coupling equality

children.title: Column-Reformulation Route
children.top_down_role: Dantzig-Wolfe and column generation when local convexification has exploitable structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Reformulation Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dantzig-Wolfe representation for bounded polyhedral block sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each bounded polytope satisfy \(X_i=\operatorname{conv}\{v_{ij}:j\in J_i\}\). Then the block-angular linear program \[\min\left\{\sum_i c_i^{\mathsf T}x_i:\sum_i A_ix_i=b,\ x_i\in X_i\right\}\] is equivalent to the master formulation \[\min_{\theta}\left\{\sum_{i,j}(c_i^{\mathsf T}v_{ij})\theta_{ij}:\sum_{i,j}A_iv_{ij}\theta_{ij}=b,\ \sum_j\theta_{ij}=1,\ \theta_{ij}\ge0\right\}.\] Column generation restricts the sets \(J_i\) and uses block pricing to find a column with negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent each block point as a convex combination of its vertices, yielding a master problem whose missing variables are generated by block pricing.
assumptions_latex: Every \(X_i\) is a nonempty bounded polytope.
The objective and coupling constraints are linear.
All vertices conceptually belong to \(J_i\), though only subsets need be stored.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original block-angular program and the full convexity master have equal feasible images and equal optimal values.

notation.meaning: vertex j of block polytope i

children.title: Value-Function Projection Route
children.top_down_role: Benders decomposition when fixing coordinating variables exposes informative subordinate problems.

assumptions_latex: Every master and subordinate problem is solved exactly.
At every queried coordinating point, the subordinate problem is either infeasible or has a finite attained optimum.
The subordinate oracle returns a valid Farkas ray or an optimal dual solution as appropriate.
The master contains the declared coordinating-variable constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No violated feasibility cut and }z^k\ge\phi(x^k)\text{ certify optimality of the complete projected formulation.}

notation.meaning: master epigraph variable for the subordinate value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical exact master-subproblem loop for linear value-function projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a master containing accumulated feasibility cuts \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0\) and optimality cuts \(z\ge\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\). Solve it at \((x^k,z^k)\), then solve the subordinate problem. If the subordinate problem is infeasible, add a cut from a Farkas ray. If it has finite value \(\phi(x^k)>z^k\), add a cut from an optimal dual vector. If it is feasible and \(z^k\ge\phi(x^k)\), the globally solved restricted master solution is optimal for the complete projected formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the restricted projected master, query the subordinate problem, add a feasibility or optimality cut when violated, and stop when the epigraph estimate is valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Benders Cutting-Plane Loop

assumptions_latex: \(W\), \(h\), and \(T\) are finite-dimensional real data.
The subordinate feasibility system is \(Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Farkas certificate for the linear subordinate feasibility system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d(x)=h-Tx\) and \(K=\{r:r\ge0,\ W^{\mathsf T}r\le0\}\). The system \(Wy\ge d(x),\ y\ge0\) is feasible if and only if \(r^{\mathsf T}d(x)\le0\) for every \(r\in K\). Hence any \(r\in K\) with \(r^{\mathsf T}d(\bar x)>0\) certifies infeasibility at \(\bar x\), and \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0\) is a valid Benders feasibility cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector in the dual recession cone certifies subordinate infeasibility and generates an exact feasibility cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Subproblem Feasibility-Ray Certificate

assumptions_latex: The relevant subordinate dual polyhedron and feasibility cone have finite extreme-point and extreme-ray cut families.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated finite extreme-cut assumptions, the exact Benders loop terminates after finitely many cut additions with an optimal projected-master solution or a master infeasibility conclusion. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The value-function projection route is operational when fixing \(x\) leaves a tractable subordinate problem whose oracle either returns an affine lower support of a finite subordinate value or separates \(x\) from the value function's effective domain. For a linear subordinate problem, an optimal dual solution supplies the support and a dual recession ray supplies the domain-separating feasibility cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The route applies when fixed coordinating decisions expose tractable subordinate solves that return value supports or feasibility-domain separators.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-Function Route Applicability

assumptions_latex: The subordinate problem is the minimization LP \(\inf\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi(\bar x)=-\infty\text{ is outside the finite-valued optimality-cut and infeasibility-ray dichotomy.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the canonical two-branch linear Benders oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the subordinate problem is feasible but unbounded below at \(\bar x\), then no optimal dual vector exists and a Farkas feasibility ray is not the appropriate response, because the subordinate constraint system is feasible. The canonical feasibility-cut or finite-optimality-cut loop therefore requires a modeling assumption excluding this case or a separate mechanism that detects and handles primal improving recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible but unbounded subordinate problem is neither a feasibility-cut case nor a finite optimality-cut case and must be excluded or handled separately.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Subproblem Boundary
Value-Function Projection Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders value-function representation for a linear subordinate problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For coordinating variable \(x\), define \[\phi(x)=\inf\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge0\}.\] Whenever this subordinate linear program is feasible with finite value, linear-programming duality gives \[\phi(x)=\sup\{\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx):W^{\mathsf T}\pi\le q,\ \pi\ge0\}.\] Hence minimizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x+\phi(x)\) can be projected into variables \((x,z)\) by imposing \(z\ge\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\) for every dual-feasible \(\pi\). Extreme rays additionally supply feasibility cuts when the subordinate problem is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subordinate optimal value is the supremum of dual affine functions, producing Benders optimality cuts and, when needed, feasibility cuts.
assumptions_latex: The subordinate problem is a finite-dimensional linear program.
Strong duality applies whenever its value is finite.
The admissible coordinating set for \(x\) is specified separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(x)=\sup_{\pi\ge0,\,W^{\mathsf T}\pi\le q}\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\) on its finite domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Row Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation-driven row addition inside a restricted row-column master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input finite active row and column sets \((R_0,C_0)\), a separation tolerance \(\varepsilon_r\), and a master containing only \(R_k\times C_k\). At iteration \(k\), solve the restricted master and obtain its candidate \(z_k\). Invoke a valid separation oracle over the full row family \(R\). If it returns \(r_k\in R\) with violation \(v(r_k,z_k)>\varepsilon_r\), set \(R_{k+1}=R_k\cup\{r_k\}\) and retain \(C_{k+1}=C_k\); otherwise declare the row side certified and pass \(z_k\) to column pricing or joint termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the current hybrid master, add a globally valid violated row, and certify the row side when no violation exceeds tolerance.

Every generated row is valid for all full-master columns.
The restricted master is solved to its prescribed accuracy.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pricing-driven column addition inside a restricted row-column master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input active sets \((R_0,C_0)\), pricing tolerance \(\varepsilon_c\), and a restricted master on \(R_k\times C_k\). The oracle minimizes reduced cost over the full column family.
Each new column has coefficients for every active row.

children.title: Joint Generation Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of row and column refinement within a shared master.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite covering-form LP with exact current-state separation and pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{x\ge0}\left\{\sum_{j\in C}c_jx_j:\sum_{j\in C}a_{rj}x_j\ge b_r\ (r\in R)\right\}\] and its dual. Let \((x^k,y^k)\) be an optimal primal-dual pair for the restriction to \(R_k\times C_k\). If exact separation verifies every row in \(R\) at \(x^k\), and exact pricing verifies every dual column inequality in \(C\) at \(y^k\), then zero extension makes \(x^k\) and \(y^k\) full primal- and dual-feasible. Their equal restricted objectives certify full-LP optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous exhaustive row and column checks extend a restricted primal-dual optimum to a full-LP optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) and \(C\) are finite.
The restricted master has an optimal primal-dual pair \((x^k,y^k)\).
Every coefficient \(a_{rj}\) is defined on \(R\times C\).
Separation and pricing are exact and use the current pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^k\text{ and }y^k\text{ extend to globally optimal full-LP solutions}.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Joint Row-Column Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial augmentation bound, excluding solve and oracle cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(R\) and \(C\) are finite, generated rows and columns are retained, and every nonterminal iteration adds at least one previously inactive object, then \[K_{\mathrm{aug}}\le |R\setminus R_0|+|C\setminus C_0|.\] With exact terminating oracles, simultaneous exhaustion is therefore reached after finitely many augmentations whenever each required restricted master is solvable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite retained row and column universes bound the number of augmenting iterations by the number of initially inactive objects.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) and \(C\) are finite.
Generated objects are retained.
Every nonterminal iteration adds a previously inactive row or column.
Required restricted masters are solvable.

Joint Generation Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinated stopping and updates for simultaneous row and column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize finite \((R_0,C_0)\). At iteration \(k\), solve the restricted master, run full-family separation and pricing, and obtain maximum row violation \(v_k\) and minimum reduced cost \(\rho_k\). Add every selected row with violation exceeding \(\varepsilon_r\) and every selected column with reduced cost below \(-\varepsilon_c\), then re-solve. Stop only when \[v_k\le\varepsilon_r\quad\text{and}\quad \rho_k\ge-\varepsilon_c.\] The output consists of the master candidate, its active-set dual variables, and both oracle reports; failure of either test requires continued generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint coordination solves, separates, and prices repeatedly; termination requires simultaneous row-feasibility and column-reduced-cost certificates.
assumptions_latex: Separation and pricing range over their respective full families.
Generated rows and columns are mutually evaluable.
The restricted master supplies valid primal and dual candidates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination requires \(v_k\le\varepsilon_r\) and \(\rho_k\ge-\varepsilon_c\) simultaneously.

children.title: Hybrid Compatibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limits on combining generated rows with generated columns.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation and pricing reports are tied to the state actually tested.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V(z)=\sup_{r\in R}v(r,z)\) and \(P(u)=\inf_{c\in C}\bar c(c;u)\). A report \(V(z)\le\varepsilon_r\) certifies only \(z\), and \(P(u)\ge-\varepsilon_c\) certifies only \(u\). If a row or column update and reoptimization changes the state to \((z',u')\), neither report transfers without an additional inheritance theorem. Both oracles must therefore be rerun at the current state before joint termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle reports generally become stale when reoptimization changes the primal or dual state.
assumptions_latex: Separation tests \(V(z)=\sup_{r\in R}v(r,z)\).

knowledge_statements.title: State-Specific Oracle-Certificate Boundary
Hybrid Compatibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by incompatible row and column universes or one-sided stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Hybrid row-column generation requires a well-defined coefficient for every pair in the full Cartesian family \(R\times C\), and termination requires valid full-family separation and pricing. Without both conditions, restricted-master optimality is not a global certificate. For example, consider the matrix game \[\min_{x\in\Delta_2}\max_{r\in\{1,2\}}(Ax)_r,\qquad A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.\] Starting with only row \(1\) and column \(1\) yields restricted value \(0\), while the full value is \(1/2\). Thus stopping after only active-set checks gives a false certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rows and columns must be mutually evaluable and searched globally; otherwise a restricted master can appear optimal while missing the true worst row or improving column.
assumptions_latex: The example uses probability simplex \(\Delta_2\).
The restricted master initially contains only the first row and first column.
No full-family separation or pricing certificate is available at premature stopping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restricted value \(0\) differs from the full value \(1/2\), demonstrating failure of one-sided active-set certification.

children.title: Linear Programming Generation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Delayed-column simplex, basis reoptimization, row generation, and LP numerical mechanics retain their LP primary home.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Programming Generation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates LP generation mechanics from general continuous Lagrangian-block decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the minimization-form linear program \(\min\{\sum_{j\in K}c_jx_j:\sum_{j\in K}a_jx_j=b,\ x_j\geq 0\}\), where \(K\) is the full column index set. Let \(J\subseteq K\) index the current restricted master, and let \(y\) be a dual solution satisfying \(a_j^{\mathsf T}y\leq c_j\) for every \(j\in J\). Column pricing evaluates \[\rho_J=\inf_{j\in K\setminus J}(c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y).\] If the pricing oracle returns a column attaining a negative reduced cost, that column may be added; if it certifies \(\rho_J\geq0\), no omitted column improves the restricted LP under this convention. Analogously, a row oracle may add a violated linear constraint. A method lies on the linear-programming generation side of the boundary when these augmentations preserve an LP that is reoptimized by simplex or another LP solver, without an essential integrality, stochastic-information, or monotone-operator mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A method remains LP generation when pricing adds negative-reduced-cost columns, separation adds violated linear rows, and every augmented restricted problem remains an LP handled by LP reoptimization.
assumptions_latex: The full model is a minimization-form linear program with full column index set \(K\).
The restricted master and every generated augmentation preserve linearity.
The pricing oracle returns a negative-reduced-cost column when prescribed or certifies that no such column exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method is classified on the linear-programming generation side of the specialization boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Decomposition Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies decomposition whose correctness essentially depends on discrete feasibility or search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the feasible set contain an essential discrete restriction \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\times\mathbb R^q\). A decomposition crosses into the mixed-integer specialization when its finite correctness or global optimality requires branching, integrality-valid cuts, discrete subproblem certificates, or logical inference not implied by continuous convex duality. Thus branch-and-price and branch-cut-and-price are mixed-integer methods because generated columns or cuts are embedded in a search tree; integer Benders and logic-based Benders are mixed-integer methods when their master decisions or subproblem deductions depend essentially on discreteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decomposition is mixed-integer-specialized when global correctness requires branching, integrality-valid cuts, discrete certificates, or logic beyond continuous convex duality.
assumptions_latex: At least one decision block is constrained to a nonconvex discrete set.
Removing the discrete mechanism can admit a point outside the discrete feasible set or lose global optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method belongs beyond the continuous Lagrangian-block boundary and in mixed-integer decomposition.

notation.meaning: numbers of integer and continuous coordinates

children.title: Stochastic Decomposition Boundary
children.top_down_role: L-shaped methods, stochastic multi-cuts, nested Benders, and scenario-tree specialization retain their stochastic-programming primary home.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Random Labels Alone Do Not Create a Stochastic Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative side of the stochastic-specialization boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Q_s(x)=Q(x)\) for every scenario label \(s\), with \(p_s\ge0\), \(\sum_s p_s=1\), and no scenario-indexed decisions or nonanticipativity constraints. Then \[\sum_s p_sQ_s(x)=Q(x).\] Thus duplicating one deterministic subordinate problem under weighted scenario labels does not create a stochastic information structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted scenario labels alone do not make an otherwise identical deterministic decomposition stochastic-specialized.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_s=Q\) for every scenario label \(s\).
\(p_s\ge0\) and \(\sum_sp_s=1\).
No scenario-adapted decisions or nonanticipativity constraints occur.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_sp_sQ_s(x)=Q(x),\quad\text{so scenario labels alone do not imply stochastic specialization}.
knowledge_statements.title: Random Labels Alone Do Not Create a Stochastic Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive classification contract assigning information-dependent decomposition methods to stochastic programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A decomposition is stochastic-specialized when correctness of its model, cuts, recursion, feasibility, or convergence essentially depends on a probability law or filtration, including conditional recourse, probability-weighted expectations, nonanticipativity among decisions sharing an information history, or scenario-tree nesting. L-shaped expectation cuts, stochastic multi-cuts, and nested Benders recursion therefore have their primary home in stochastic programming. Removable random labels do not satisfy this criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decomposition crosses the stochastic boundary when stochastic information structure is mathematically essential rather than cosmetic.
assumptions_latex: Classification is based on the information structure required for mathematical correctness, not randomized computation or random naming alone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{essential dependence on stochastic information structure}\Longrightarrow\text{stochastic-programming primary home}.

notation.meaning: Random information observed through stage t

knowledge_statements.title: Essential Stochastic-Information Boundary
Stochastic Decomposition Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates scenario and information-structure methods from deterministic block decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let decisions be adapted to a filtration \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^T\), and let the objective or constraints depend on random data \(\xi\). A decomposition crosses into the stochastic-programming specialization when its validity requires conditional recourse, scenario probabilities, nonanticipativity, or scenario-tree nesting. The two-stage form \[\min_x\; c^{\mathsf T}x+\mathbb E[Q(x,\xi)]\] is stochastic-specialized when cuts approximate scenario recourse functions or their expectation. Consequently, L-shaped methods, stochastic multi-cuts, nested Benders methods, and scenario-tree decompositions retain their stochastic primary home even when their subproblems admit Lagrangian interpretations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A method is stochastic-specialized when its cuts or recursion essentially use probabilities, conditional recourse, nonanticipativity, or scenario-tree information.
assumptions_latex: Random data affect the objective, constraints, or feasible recourse decisions.
Feasible policies must respect the stated information filtration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method lies on the stochastic-programming side of the decomposition boundary.

notation.meaning: recourse value after first-stage decision x

The illustrative two-stage model also leaves the domains of x and c and the definition of Q implicit. A specific stochastic-programming source is required before selecting the reliable formulation.

children.title: Operator-Splitting Boundary

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Splitting Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies methods governed primarily by resolvent fixed-point iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be maximally monotone operators on a real Hilbert space \(H\), consider \(0\in A(x)+B(x)\), and let \(\gamma>0\). A method lies on the operator-splitting side of the boundary when its defining iteration is a fixed-point map constructed from separate evaluations of the resolvents \(J_{\gamma A}=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}\) and \(J_{\gamma B}=(I+\gamma B)^{-1}\), or from such resolvent evaluations together with an explicit evaluation of a stated cocoercive component. This classification applies when convergence is formulated through averaged or nonexpansive operator theory rather than through a master problem and Lagrangian block-value cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A method is operator-splitting-specialized when its core fixed-point iteration separately evaluates component resolvents, possibly with a forward step for a stated cocoercive component, and its convergence is governed by operator theory.
assumptions_latex: The inclusion is posed on a real Hilbert space \(H\).
The operators \(A\) and \(B\) are maximally monotone.
The stepsize satisfies \(\gamma>0\), and every component evaluation used by the splitting map is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Resolvent-based fixed-point methods retain their operator-splitting specialization.

notation.meaning: resolvent of the scaled operator gamma A

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed-Optimization Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates mathematical block decomposition from algorithms constrained by agent topology and local information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let agents \(i\in V\) communicate over a graph \(G=(V,E)\), with agent \(i\) initially knowing only local data defining \(f_i\) and its incident communication links. An optimization method crosses into the distributed specialization when each update must be computable from local state, local data, and messages received from neighbors, and when convergence depends on connectivity, mixing, delays, or other network assumptions. Merely solving independent blocks in parallel under a globally accessible coordinator does not satisfy this distributed-information condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimization is distributed-specialized when updates use only local data and neighbor messages and convergence materially depends on network properties.
assumptions_latex: Each agent has restricted initial access to problem data.
Communication is constrained by the graph or an explicitly time-varying network.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Network-constrained local-information methods retain their distributed-optimization primary home.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus-Specific Topics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted graph-consensus representation of a separable convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected undirected graph, let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, and let each \(f_i:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex. Then the centralized problem has the consensus representation \[\inf_{x\in H}\sum_{i\in V}f_i(x)=\inf_{(x_i)_{i\in V}\in H^{|V|}}\left\{\sum_{i\in V}f_i(x_i):x_i=x_j\text{ for every }\{i,j\}\in E\right\}.\] Because \(G\) is connected, the edge equalities are equivalent to global agreement of all local copies. Whenever minimizers exist, a centralized minimizer \(x^\star\) corresponds to the lifted minimizer \(x_i^\star=x^\star\) for every \(i\in V\), and every lifted minimizer has this form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a connected undirected graph, the centralized infimum of a sum equals the infimum over local copies constrained to agree across every edge; when minimizers exist, they correspond through identical local copies.
assumptions_latex: The graph \(G=(V,E)\) is connected and undirected.
The decision space \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
Each local objective \(f_i:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Edgewise agreement is equivalent to global agreement, so the lifted and centralized problems have equal optimal values and corresponding minimizers whenever those minimizers exist.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp graph-connectivity boundary for interpreting edgewise equality as one global consensus constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be an oriented incidence matrix of a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\). The constraint \((D^{\mathsf T}\otimes I_H)x=0\) forces the local copies \(x_i\) to be equal within each connected component. It forces one common value over all vertices if and only if \(G\) is connected. If \(G\) is disconnected, assigning distinct constants to two components gives zero edge-consensus residual but violates global consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Edge equalities imply agreement only within connected components; connectedness is necessary and sufficient for them to certify global consensus.

children.title: Communication-Centric Topics

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Centric Topics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines resource accounting that distinguishes communication-centric analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an algorithm executed by agents on a communication network and an accuracy parameter \(\varepsilon>0\), let \(R(\varepsilon)\), \(M(\varepsilon)\), and \(B(\varepsilon)\) denote, respectively, the communication rounds, transmitted messages, and transmitted bits required to produce an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate output under a stated error criterion and protocol model. An analysis is communication-centric when at least one communication quantity is an explicit resource measure and cannot be inferred solely from the number of local arithmetic iterations. Algorithms with identical local update counts may therefore have different communication costs because of topology, synchronization, batching, compression, or message precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive accuracy tolerance epsilon, communication-centric analysis explicitly measures rounds, messages, or bits under a stated network and protocol model; local iteration counts alone need not determine these costs.
assumptions_latex: The accuracy parameter satisfies \(\varepsilon>0\).
The communication protocol, network model, and accuracy criterion are specified.
Local computation and inter-agent transmission are accounted for separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Communication performance is stated using one or more of \(R(\varepsilon)\), \(M(\varepsilon)\), and \(B(\varepsilon)\), together with the applicable network and protocol model.

notation.meaning: positive target accuracy under the stated error criterion
communication rounds required for epsilon accuracy
